choices.text: Raise the temperature to flatten the distribution so that low-probability tokens are selected more often.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Raise the Top K value significantly to greatly increase the number of candidate tokens the model considers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the maximum number of tokens so that the model writes the same content longer and in more detail.

exam-aif-c01-54.explanation: When the temperature is low, the probability distribution becomes sharper and high-probability tokens are mainly selected, so responses are more consistent. Raising the temperature flattens the distribution, so low-probability tokens are drawn more often and variation increases. Raising Top K increases the number of candidates and actually increases diversity. The maximum number of tokens is only an upper limit on length and has nothing to do with the consistency of wording.

exam-aif-c01-55.prompt: A legal information company operates a knowledge base of statute documents. When it searches with short chunks, the results match the query exactly, but the model lacks surrounding context and its answers are thin. The company also wants to reduce re-indexing costs because there are many documents. It wants to keep search precision while passing broader context to the model. Which chunking strategy is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hierarchical chunking: search with small child chunks and pass them to the model after replacing them with larger parent chunks

choices.label: B
choices.text: In fixed-size chunking, shrink the chunks much smaller and remove the overlap.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No chunking: treat each document as a single chunk and embed the entire document.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keep the default chunking of about 300 tokens and only reduce the number of search results.

exam-aif-c01-55.explanation: Hierarchical chunking searches precisely with child chunks and then replaces the results with broader parent chunks before passing them to the model, so it provides both precision and context. Making the chunks smaller reduces the context even further. Without chunking, the entire document becomes a single vector and search precision drops. Default chunking is a unit of about 300 tokens that respects sentence boundaries, so it has no effect of expanding context.

exam-aif-c01-56.prompt: An AI service team will run a two-week load test on a specific Amazon Bedrock model before launching a new chatbot. Fixed throughput is needed only during this period, and the team wants to cancel immediately when the test ends. The usage plan after the test is undecided, so long-term commitments must be avoided. Considering cost, which configuration is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Purchase Provisioned Throughput with a 6-month commitment to receive the hourly discount.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Purchase Provisioned Throughput with a 1-month commitment and delete it right after two weeks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use only batch inference jobs without reserving throughput, in place of the fixed throughput requirement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Purchase Provisioned Throughput with no commitment and delete it when the test ends.

exam-aif-c01-56.explanation: If fixed throughput is needed, Provisioned Throughput is the answer, and the no-commitment option can be deleted at any time, so it meets the requirement to cancel after two weeks. Hourly charges continue until it is deleted, so do not forget to delete it. The 1-month and 6-month commitments cannot be deleted until the term ends, so they conflict with the constraint of avoiding long-term commitments. Batch inference does not reserve throughput, so it does not meet the fixed throughput requirement.

exam-aif-c01-57.prompt: A marketing team wants to create product promotional images by entering only a text description, without a separate photo shoot. During the adoption review, a request came up that the whole team should understand how models such as Stable Diffusion work. Which statement BEST explains the basic principle by which a diffusion model generates images?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It predicts the next word as a probability based on the preceding words and context and attaches the words one after another.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It generates images by learning the process of adding noise and removing it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It finds the image closest to the input description in a repository and returns a copy of it as is.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It cuts an image into small pieces and then reassembles them in the original order to increase the resolution.

exam-aif-c01-57.explanation: A diffusion model generates images by learning the process of adding noise and removing it. Predicting the next word as a probability and attaching the words in sequence is the approach of language models that generate text. Finding a stored image and copying it is search, not generating a new image. The explanation of reassembling pieces has nothing to do with the generation principle of a diffusion model.

exam-aif-c01-58.prompt: A fintech company is choosing a candidate model for a generative AI app. Before deployment, it must check how often the candidate model produces responses containing stereotypes about occupations or gender, and there is no time for people to read each response. What is the MOST appropriate way to score the model responses with an evaluation prompt dataset?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Estimate response bias by aggregating the number of InvokeModel calls with AWS CloudTrail.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Register occupation and gender in the Guardrails denied topics as a substitute for evaluation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Score the responses with a judge model and a stereotyping metric in an Amazon Bedrock evaluation job.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scan Amazon S3 for sensitive information with Amazon Macie and use the results as a bias metric.

exam-aif-c01-58.explanation: The judge model method in Amazon Bedrock evaluations has a built-in metric that scores whether a response contains stereotypes, so candidate models can be compared before deployment using an evaluation dataset. AWS CloudTrail leaves only a record of invocations and does not score response content. Guardrails denied topics is a feature that blocks specific topics at runtime, not an evaluation that measures a model's bias. Amazon Macie is a service that finds sensitive data in Amazon S3, so it has nothing to do with stereotypes in responses.

exam-aif-c01-59.prompt: An online bookstore wants to put personalized recommended book lists in its app based on users' purchase and click history. The history data is already accumulated in Amazon S3, but the company has no staff to build a recommendation algorithm itself and the launch schedule is tight. It needs the method with the LEAST operational overhead. What should it choose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Implement a collaborative filtering algorithm from scratch in Amazon SageMaker and host it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Analyze review sentiment with Amazon Comprehend and show the highest-scoring books to everyone.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Build an Amazon Lex chatbot that asks users directly about their preferred genres.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Upload the interaction data to Amazon Personalize and build a recommendation model.

exam-aif-c01-59.explanation: The managed service that creates personalized recommendations from interaction data between users and items is Amazon Personalize, and you do not have to build the algorithm yourself. Implementing it directly in Amazon SageMaker is possible, but it has the largest development and operational burden. Showing the same books to everyone based on review sentiment scores is not personalization. Asking genres through a chatbot is not recommendation based on history.

exam-aif-c01-60.prompt: Internal HR policy documents are revised every week, and answers to employee questions must cite the source documents. The documents are in Amazon S3, and the HR team wants revisions to be reflected immediately. The development team has only two people, so it wants to reflect the latest content without retraining the model. Which approach has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fine-tune the model with the policy documents every time they are revised, purchase new Provisioned Throughput, and delete the previous model.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Paste the entire policy text as is into the prompt of every request and pass it to the model.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Register policy clauses in the guardrail word filter so that those clauses appear in responses.

choices.label: D
choices.text: RAG that ingests and embeds the Amazon S3 documents with an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base and passes the search results to the model

exam-aif-c01-60.explanation: The documents change frequently and source citation is needed, so RAG using a knowledge base is appropriate. The documents are split into chunks and embedded into a vector index, the chunks closest to the question are passed to the model, and no retraining is needed. Fine-tuning has to be repeated with every revision, so its cost and operations are large. Putting the entire policy in the prompt causes length limit and cost problems. The word filter is for blocking and is not a feature for providing knowledge.

exam-aif-c01-61.prompt: A fintech company is comparing two binary classification models. The classification threshold for production is still being discussed with the business team and has not been decided. The company therefore wants to first see how well the models distinguish positives from negatives regardless of the threshold. Which metric is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AUC: a value that represents the ability to give higher scores to positive examples regardless of the threshold

choices.label: B
choices.text: Compare only a single value, the overall accuracy calculated assuming a threshold of 0.5, between the two models.

choices.label: C
choices.text: RMSE: looks at the average size of the error between predictions and actual values in continuous value prediction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use only the recall calculated at one specific threshold as the model selection criterion.

exam-aif-c01-61.explanation: AUC does not depend on the score threshold and measures the ability to give positives higher scores than negatives, so it is suitable for a comparison where the threshold is undecided. A value near 0.5 is at the level of random guessing, and the closer to 1, the better. The accuracy at a threshold of 0.5 or the recall at a specific threshold changes when the threshold changes. RMSE is a metric for regression models.

exam-aif-c01-62.prompt: A customer service chatbot keeps writing unnecessary sentences even after it finishes its answer, so response time is long and token costs are rising. The prompt has been set to make the chatbot output a delimiter string "### END" at the end of the answer. The company wants generation to stop the moment this string is output, to reduce unnecessary token generation. Which inference setting is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lower the temperature value close to 0 to reduce the randomness of the output so that the answer comes out in the same form every time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set the Top K value to 1 to limit the next-token candidates to one.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Specify the string "### END" in the stop sequences so that generation stops when that string is generated.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fix the response length (max tokens) at the minimum allowed value to cut the response short.

exam-aif-c01-62.explanation: If you specify a delimiter string in the stop sequences, the model stops producing tokens after it generates that string, so it meets the requirement to stop immediately at a specific string. Lowering the temperature only reduces randomness and does not stop at a specific string. Setting Top K to 1 only reduces the number of candidates, and the stopping point stays the same. Fixing the response length at the minimum would cut the answer off midway regardless of the delimiter string, which breaks normal answers.

exam-aif-c01-63.prompt: In an advertising company's slogan generation app, feedback said that the results were too scattered, so the Top P value was lowered from 0.9 to 0.5. The person in charge must explain to the team how this change affects the responses. In terms of the candidate pool from which the model selects the next token, which statement describes the effect of this change MOST accurately?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The top 50% of cumulative probability is added, so the candidate range widens and low-probability tokens are selected often.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The number of next-token candidates is fixed at exactly 50, so the size of the candidate pool becomes the same.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only candidates within the top 50% of cumulative probability are considered, so the candidate range narrows and diversity decreases.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The maximum length of generated responses is cut in half, so only shorter slogans are produced.

exam-aif-c01-63.explanation: Top P is a value that cuts off candidates based on cumulative probability, so lowering it leaves only the most likely candidates, which makes responses more conservative and reduces diversity. The explanation that the candidate range widens has the direction reversed. Fixing the candidates to a set number is the behavior of Top K, and with Top P the number of candidates differs for each token. The response length is determined by a separate length parameter.

exam-aif-c01-64.prompt: A credit card company is evaluating a credit card fraud detection model. The loss from missing an actual fraudulent transaction is much greater than the cost of suspecting a legitimate transaction and sending the customer a confirmation text message. Fraud is only a tiny fraction of all transactions. Which metric should be checked FIRST for this requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Precision: the ratio of transactions predicted as fraud by the model that were actually fraud

choices.label: B
choices.text: Recall: the ratio of actual fraudulent transactions that the model found as fraud

choices.label: C
choices.text: Accuracy: the ratio of correctly classified transactions among all transactions

choices.label: D
choices.text: RMSE: a value obtained by squaring the difference between predicted and actual values, averaging, and taking the square root

exam-aif-c01-64.explanation: The goal is to reduce missed fraud, so recall, the ratio of actual positives that were found, should be the priority. Precision is the ratio of correct predictions among those predicted as fraud, so it is a metric for reducing false positives, and in this situation the cost of false positives is small. Accuracy is inappropriate because with imbalanced data in which fraud is a tiny minority, it comes out high even if everything is predicted as legitimate. RMSE is an error metric for regression models, so it is not used for classification problems.

exam-aif-c01-65.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
exam-aif-c01-65.prompt: At an internal security review meeting, the security manager of a company that plans to launch an Amazon Bedrock-based chatbot asks who is responsible for preventing prompt injection. The chatbot is a web application that receives customer questions and passes them to the model. Under the shared responsibility model, which statement is MOST accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AWS automatically sanitizes all inputs, so customers do not need to implement input validation separately.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The customer must directly inspect and manage the physical security of the data centers and the model hosting hardware.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The model provider is solely responsible for injection defense, so the customer application takes no action.

choices.label: D
choices.text: AWS protects the infrastructure that underlies the service, and the customer is responsible for application-level security such as preventing prompt injection.

exam-aif-c01-65.explanation: AWS documentation explains that AWS is responsible for the security of the physical data centers, the network, and the Amazon Bedrock service itself, while the customer is responsible for preventing application-level vulnerabilities such as prompt injection. The statement that input validation is unnecessary is the opposite of the documentation's recommendation. Physical security and hardware are AWS's area of responsibility. The statement that the model provider is solely responsible for injection defense does not exist in the shared responsibility model.

exam-clf-c02-1.prompt: A startup with five employees operates a photo-sharing app. The startup must create a thumbnail each time a user uploads an image to an Amazon S3 bucket. There are several hundred uploads per day at irregular times, and sometimes there are no uploads for several hours overnight. The team has no infrastructure staff and must currently keep its bill as low as possible. Which processing method is the MOST cost-effective with the LEAST server management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Generate thumbnails with an AWS Lambda function that runs only when an image upload event occurs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use a single Amazon EC2 instance that runs all the time to periodically check for new images and process them.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Continuously deploy dedicated thumbnail-generation pods on an Amazon EKS cluster and manage the nodes directly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run a web server continuously in an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment to convert the uploaded images.

exam-clf-c02-1.explanation: The correct answer is to run a Lambda function triggered by the upload event. The code runs only when there is a request, you are billed only for the time it runs, and there are no servers to manage, which best fits several hundred irregular tasks per day. An EC2 instance that is always on incurs cost even when there is no work and also requires OS management. Always-on pods on Amazon EKS require you to manage the cluster and nodes directly, which creates the greatest operational burden. An Elastic Beanstalk environment also keeps instances running continuously, so it wastes money on small, irregular workloads. Looking at the added conditions in the question, a configuration that is billed only when events occur is advantageous because there are only several hundred uploads per day and long idle periods.

exam-clf-c02-2.prompt: A manufacturing company wants to eliminate the burden of maintaining servers and renewing annual licenses for the internal sales management software that it built and operates itself. Currently 200 employees use it, and it has almost no custom features, so only the data needs to be moved. The company decides to replace it with a vendor's SaaS product that is accessed over the internet and charged by subscription. Which migration strategy does this approach represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rehost, which moves the servers as they are without changes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Repurchase, which replaces the existing product with a different product or SaaS

choices.label: C
choices.text: Replatform, which optimizes only part of the application and runs it on a managed service

choices.label: D
choices.text: Refactor, which redesigns the application into a cloud-native architecture

exam-clf-c02-2.explanation: The correct answer is repurchase, which replaces the existing product with a different product such as SaaS. Replacing the software with a subscription-based SaaS to eliminate server maintenance and license burden is a typical repurchase case. Rehost moves the application without changes, so it does not replace the product. Replatform moves the application while partially optimizing it, for example by using managed services, which is different from replacing the vendor product. Refactor redesigns the architecture and is the most complex and costly approach, so it does not match the requirements. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the product itself is replaced without moving servers or changing code, so this is repurchase.

exam-clf-c02-3.prompt: A company that operates an online payment service decides that the DDoS protection provided by default on AWS is not enough. A recent traffic surge attack delayed payments for several minutes, so the company wants to adopt additional paid DDoS detection, mitigation, and response capabilities for its core application. The company has a small security staff and also wants response support from AWS experts. Which service is the MOST suitable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply AWS WAF alone

choices.label: B
choices.text: AWS Shield Advanced

choices.label: C
choices.text: AWS Artifact

choices.label: D
choices.text: Strengthen the inbound rules of security groups

exam-clf-c02-3.explanation: The correct answer is AWS Shield Advanced. Basic DDoS protection is provided to all customers at no additional cost, and Shield Advanced is a paid service that adds higher levels of DDoS detection, mitigation, and response on top of it. WAF is a rule-based filtering tool for HTTP requests and is not a DDoS-specific response service that you subscribe to separately. Artifact only provides compliance documents and does not stop attacks. Security groups restrict traffic with allow rules and cannot detect or respond to large-scale DDoS attacks. Looking at the added conditions in the question, only Shield Advanced satisfies the requirements for paid extended protection and expert response support.

exam-clf-c02-4.prompt: A manufacturer currently uses Amazon EC2 m5 instances in the Seoul Region. Next year, the manufacturer may move some workloads to AWS Fargate containers and AWS Lambda and may migrate some workloads to the Tokyo Region. The finance team wants a discount in exchange for a 1-year commitment, wants the discount to continue to apply after these changes, and prefers to set the commitment amount as an hourly amount that matches usage. Which option is the MOST suitable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Purchase EC2 Instance Savings Plans for the m5 family and the Seoul Region.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Purchase Standard Reserved Instances for m5 in the Seoul Region and apply them to the same configuration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use Spot Instances for all workloads and get a discount with no commitment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Purchase Compute Savings Plans so that the discount applies even after changes in family, Region, and service.

exam-clf-c02-4.explanation: Compute Savings Plans is the correct answer. It automatically applies to EC2 usage regardless of instance family, size, Region, or operating system, and it also applies to Fargate and Lambda usage, so the discount is retained even when the service and Region change. EC2 Instance Savings Plans are tied to a specific instance family in a specific Region, so they do not apply if you move to Tokyo or switch to Fargate. Standard Reserved Instances are also commitments tied to a specific instance configuration, so they are not flexible for service changes. Spot Instances are used without a commitment, so they do not match the condition of getting a discount through a 1-year commitment. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the discount must apply even when the family, Region, and service change, so Compute Savings Plans, which has the broadest scope, is the answer.

exam-clf-c02-5.prompt: A security officer in a headquarters account wants to let an auditor from an external auditing firm read the configuration of a subsidiary account for only a few days. The auditor is not an employee of the company and belongs to a separate organization. The officer does not want to create and hand over long-term credentials and wants the permissions to disappear automatically when the access period ends. The audit begins next week. Which method is the MOST secure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an IAM user for the auditor and email the access keys.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an IAM role with read-only permissions and have the auditor assume it with temporary credentials.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Share the root user's email address and password only during the audit period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an IAM user with administrator permissions for the auditor and delete it later.

exam-clf-c02-5.explanation: The correct answer is to create an IAM role with read-only permissions and have the auditor assume it with temporary credentials. A role issues temporary credentials with a defined validity period and no long-term keys, so they expire automatically when the period ends, and because the role is read-only, the permissions are also minimal. Access keys for an IAM user are long-term credentials that can leak in transit, and revoking them is manual. Sharing root credentials is the riskiest choice. A user with administrator permissions is far more than needed for a requirement that only involves reading. Looking at the added conditions in the question, temporary credentials expire automatically after the period, so there is no problem of revoking long-term keys.

exam-clf-c02-6.prompt: The marketing team at a large retail company has accumulated several years of sales data at petabyte scale and wants to run complex aggregate analyses by using standard SQL. The analytic queries run mainly at night and at the end of the month for several hours at a time, and the team lacks staff to tune databases. The team wants to use a managed service designed specifically for analytics. Which service is the MOST suitable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amazon Redshift, which sets up a data warehouse that performs SQL analytics on large-scale data

choices.label: B
choices.text: Amazon ElastiCache, which caches frequently read data in memory and runs SQL

choices.label: C
choices.text: Amazon DynamoDB, which looks up large numbers of items by key and performs aggregations

choices.label: D
choices.text: A small Amazon RDS instance, which loads all the data into a transactional database for analysis

exam-clf-c02-6.explanation: Amazon Redshift is the correct answer. It is a managed data warehouse service that analyzes petabyte-scale data by using standard SQL. ElastiCache is for caching and is not a large-scale aggregate analytics store. DynamoDB is a NoSQL database that excels at key-based lookups, so it is not suited to complex SQL aggregations. A small RDS instance is for transaction processing, so it has difficulty handling petabyte-scale analytics. Looking at the added conditions in the question, SQL analytics at petabyte scale is the use case of the data warehouse Redshift.

exam-clf-c02-7.prompt: A startup's finance team wants the responsible person to receive an advance email notification when this month's AWS cost is forecasted to reach 80% of the $5,000 budget. Development environments keep increasing, and twice the team found out about an overrun only at the end of the month. Which tool is the MOST suitable to meet this requirement without having a person check the console every day?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Check the current cumulative cost graph by signing in to AWS Cost Explorer every day.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a cost budget in AWS Budgets and configure an alert at 80% of forecasted cost.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Calculate the estimated monthly amount with AWS Pricing Calculator and record it in a budget document.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Receive the AWS Cost and Usage Report in Amazon S3 and have the responsible person analyze it manually on a regular basis.

exam-clf-c02-7.explanation: AWS Budgets is the correct answer. You can set a cost budget and send an alert by email or an Amazon SNS topic when actual or forecasted cost exceeds a threshold, so no one needs to check every day. Cost Explorer is a tool for analyzing and visualizing costs that a person must sign in to view, and threshold alerts are not its core function. Pricing Calculator is a tool for estimating cost before use and does not monitor actual spending. The Cost and Usage Report provides detailed data but still leaves the effort of analyzing it manually. Looking at the added conditions in the question, alerts based on forecasted cost are a feature of Budgets, and the other options cannot send proactive alerts.

exam-clf-c02-8.prompt: The operations team at an e-commerce company wants to view and set alarms on the memory utilization of 20 Amazon EC2 instances in Amazon CloudWatch, but the default metrics do not include memory. The instances are already running, and the team cannot modify or redeploy the application code. Which solution meets this requirement with the LEAST change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Turn on an AWS CloudTrail trail to record memory usage events for the instances.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Install the CloudWatch agent on the instances to collect memory metrics.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an AWS Config rule to evaluate the memory utilization of the instances.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Check the memory utilization item in the AWS Trusted Advisor check results.

exam-clf-c02-8.explanation: Installing the CloudWatch agent is the correct answer. The agent collects system-level metrics such as CPU, memory, and disk usage, along with logs, from EC2 instances and on-premises servers and sends them to CloudWatch, so you can configure a memory alarm. CloudTrail records API activity and does not collect memory metrics from inside an instance. Config is a service that evaluates resource configuration and compliance. Trusted Advisor is a best-practice check service and has no real-time memory utilization item. Looking at the added conditions in the question, metrics from inside the operating system are collected by the CloudWatch agent, and no code change is required.

exam-clf-c02-9.prompt: A video learning site delivers static course materials to students around the world, and students in South America and Europe complain of long download delays. The origin is in an Amazon S3 bucket in the Seoul Region, and the materials are updated only once or twice a day. The team has three members and cannot manage separate servers in each Region. Which method reduces latency with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create and manually replicate separate web servers in a Region on every continent.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase the number of Availability Zones in the Region that holds the origin to increase processing capacity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the S3 bucket's storage class to a cheaper one.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use Amazon CloudFront to cache and serve the content at edge locations.

exam-clf-c02-9.explanation: The correct answer is to use CloudFront to cache and serve the content at edge locations. Edge locations deliver content from places close to users, which reduces latency, and the origin stays as it is, so the operational burden is small. Creating and replicating web servers on every continent reduces latency but greatly increases the servers to manage and the synchronization work. Adding Availability Zones is about resilience to failures and does not help with latency to distant regions. A cheaper storage class is a cost choice and does not increase delivery speed. Looking at the added conditions in the question, static materials that are rarely updated fit edge caching well, and there is no need to manage servers in each Region.

exam-clf-c02-10.prompt: A security team initially gave a service account broad permissions for development convenience and now wants to reduce them to a least-privilege policy that keeps only the services and actions actually used. The account has several months of access records in AWS CloudTrail, and the team has no time to analyze the permission list manually one item at a time. Which tool automatically generates a policy based on the access activity recorded in CloudTrail?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cost optimization check in AWS Trusted Advisor

choices.label: B
choices.text: The vulnerability scan results of Amazon Inspector

choices.label: C
choices.text: The sensitive data discovery job of Amazon Macie

choices.label: D
choices.text: The policy generation feature of IAM Access Analyzer

exam-clf-c02-10.explanation: The correct answer is the policy generation feature of IAM Access Analyzer. It analyzes the access activity recorded in CloudTrail and creates a fine-grained policy that contains only the services and actions the role actually used, which makes it suitable for reducing permissions to least privilege. Trusted Advisor checks and gives recommendations on cost, performance, security, and more, but it does not generate policies from activity. Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities and network exposure. Macie is a service that finds sensitive data in Amazon S3 and is unrelated to generating IAM policies. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the feature that creates a policy based on CloudTrail activity is in IAM Access Analyzer.

exam-clf-c02-11.prompt: A small company has a database server that runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance. The data must remain even if the instance is stopped or replaced with a new instance, and point-in-time backups must be possible. The server must recognize the disk as an operating-system-level block device, and the company does not want to set up a separate file server. Which storage is the MOST suitable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Store the data on an instance store volume and periodically copy it to another location.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Store the data on an Amazon EBS volume and back it up with EBS snapshots.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mount an Amazon S3 Standard-IA bucket like a disk and store the data files in it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Store the data files in an Amazon Glacier vault and restore them when needed.

exam-clf-c02-11.explanation: An Amazon EBS volume is the correct answer. EBS is block storage that attaches to EC2 and is used like a local disk, it persists independently of the instance, and snapshots create point-in-time backups that you can restore to a new volume. An instance store is tied to the lifetime of the instance, so data retention is not guaranteed when the instance is replaced. S3 is object storage, so it does not fit the use of treating DB data files like a disk. Glacier is for long-term archiving and cannot be used as storage for a running database. Looking at the added conditions in the question, block storage that is separate from the instance lifetime and has snapshots is a characteristic of EBS.

exam-clf-c02-12.prompt: An online education service must comply with a regulation that requires personal information of domestic customers to be stored only within the country. Most users are in Korea, response latency is also important, and transferring data abroad is not possible without approval from the legal team. Which Region choice satisfies all of these constraints MOST appropriately?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Choose the Region with the lowest prices and encrypt all stored data.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Choose the Region where new services launch first and use the new features first.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Do not choose a Region and store the original data at edge locations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Choose the Seoul Region and configure the data to stay within that Region.

exam-clf-c02-12.explanation: The correct answer is to choose the Seoul Region and configure the data to stay within that Region. To satisfy both the data residency regulation and proximity to users, a domestic Region is required. AWS states that it does not move or replicate content outside the Region that the customer selects without the customer's consent (with exceptions for what is necessary to provide the services and for legal requirements). The cheapest Region may be located abroad, which risks violating the regulation, and encryption does not resolve a data location requirement. The Region where new services launch first is a criterion that ignores the regulation and latency. Edge locations are for caching content and are not a store for original data. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the Region that satisfies both the data location regulation and proximity to users is Seoul.

exam-clf-c02-13.prompt: A manufacturing company exchanges large amounts of data between its headquarters data center and AWS every day. The problem is that the speed fluctuates depending on the condition of the internet connection, and the network team says it needs consistent bandwidth and low latency. It is acceptable if setting up the connection takes several weeks. Which service is the MOST suitable for a dedicated connection that does not traverse the internet?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Connect the data center to AWS with a dedicated line by using AWS Direct Connect.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Connect by creating an encrypted tunnel over the public internet with AWS Site-to-Site VPN.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to accelerate transfers with the data center.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a data center hosted zone in Amazon Route 53 to optimize the route.

exam-clf-c02-13.explanation: AWS Direct Connect is the correct answer. It connects your network to a Direct Connect location over fiber-optic cable and reaches AWS without going through an internet service provider, which matches the need for a dedicated path that is not affected by internet conditions. Site-to-Site VPN is encrypted but passes over the public internet, so the problem of fluctuating speed remains. CloudFront is a CDN that delivers content close to users and is not a site-to-site connection. Route 53 is a DNS service and cannot create a transfer path itself. Looking at the added conditions in the question, only Direct Connect satisfies the requirement for a dedicated line that does not traverse the internet.

exam-clf-c02-14.prompt: A security incident is under investigation. Yesterday afternoon someone deleted an important Amazon S3 bucket, and the team must determine which IAM principal called which API, at what time, and from where. The account has never had a separate trail or log collection configured, and there is no time to create new settings right now. Where can the team first look at management events from the last 90 days?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An Amazon CloudWatch metrics dashboard

choices.label: B
choices.text: VPC Flow Logs

choices.label: C
choices.text: AWS CloudTrail event history

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Amazon Inspector findings screen

exam-clf-c02-14.explanation: The correct answer is CloudTrail event history. CloudTrail records actions taken by users, roles, and services as events and tells you who did what, when, and to which resource, and once an account is created, you can view the last 90 days of management events without any additional configuration. CloudWatch metrics show performance figures and do not tell you which principal made an API call. VPC Flow Logs contain network traffic information and do not record API calls such as bucket deletion. Inspector shows vulnerability scan results. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the place that shows 90 days of management events without any setup is CloudTrail event history.

exam-clf-c02-15.prompt: A security team that operates multiple accounts wants to detect compromised credentials and communication with malicious IP addresses by analyzing AWS CloudTrail management events, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs from its accounts, without installing agents or configuring log collection. The security team has few analysts and wants to receive continuous threat detection automatically. Which service is the MOST suitable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amazon Inspector

choices.label: B
choices.text: AWS Config

choices.label: C
choices.text: Amazon GuardDuty

choices.label: D
choices.text: AWS Trusted Advisor

exam-clf-c02-15.explanation: The correct answer is Amazon GuardDuty. When you turn on GuardDuty, it automatically collects CloudTrail management events, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs and uses threat intelligence and machine learning to detect compromised credentials and malicious activity, so no additional configuration is needed. Inspector is a service that scans for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. Config records resource configuration changes and rule compliance. Trusted Advisor provides best-practice checks and recommendations but does not detect threats. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the service that automatically analyzes logs to detect threats is GuardDuty.

exam-clf-c02-16.prompt: An online bookstore runs a web application behind an Application Load Balancer and receives requests that include SQL injection patterns. Security groups control only ports and IP addresses, so they cannot filter the contents of the query string. Because there is only one security staff member, the company wants to apply request-level filtering without the burden of writing all the rules by hand. What is the MOST appropriate method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a rule to the network ACL that denies SQL keywords.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Associate AWS WAF and apply managed rule groups.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turn on Amazon Macie to inspect request bodies.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Automatically block suspicious requests with an AWS Config rule.

exam-clf-c02-16.explanation: The correct answer is to associate AWS WAF and apply managed rule groups. WAF allows or blocks HTTP requests that reach resources such as an ALB based on criteria such as IP addresses and query strings, and using managed rule groups reduces the burden of writing rules yourself. Network ACLs operate at the IP and port level and cannot inspect SQL keywords in a query string. Macie is for classifying data in Amazon S3 and does not inspect web requests. Config only evaluates whether resource configuration is compliant and does not block requests. Looking at the added conditions in the question, inspecting request contents and reducing the burden of writing rules with managed rules is what WAF does.

exam-clf-c02-17.prompt: A log analytics team stores several TB of data in Amazon S3, and it cannot predict which objects will be accessed and when. The team wants rarely accessed objects to move automatically to cheaper tiers, wants no separate retrieval charges when objects are read again, and does not want to manage lifecycle rules itself. Which storage class is the MOST suitable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Store the data in S3 Standard-IA and pay retrieval charges based on object size when needed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Store the data in S3 One Zone-IA to keep the data in a single Availability Zone and reduce cost.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Store the data in S3 Intelligent-Tiering to automatically move objects between tiers based on access patterns.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Store the data in S3 Glacier Deep Archive and request a restore and wait a long time each time the data must be read.

exam-clf-c02-17.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering is the correct answer. It monitors access patterns and automatically moves objects that are not being used to cheaper tiers, and it has only a small monitoring and automation charge with no retrieval charges, which suits data with unknown patterns. Standard-IA charges a per-GB retrieval fee when you read data and does not move objects automatically. One Zone-IA also has retrieval charges and stores data in only a single Availability Zone, so it does not match the requirements. Glacier Deep Archive requires a restore before reading and is for long-term archiving, not for data that is accessed occasionally. Looking at the added conditions in the question, Intelligent-Tiering satisfies the conditions of unpredictable access patterns and no retrieval charges.

exam-clf-c02-18.prompt: A compliance team must encrypt contract documents stored in Amazon S3 on the server side, keep an audit record of which key was used, when, and by whom, and control access to the key through policies. Auditors want to check the key usage history in AWS CloudTrail, and the team wants to perform the encryption without changing application code. What is the MOST appropriate method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use only S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) and do not configure anything else.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Upload over HTTP and configure only bucket-level access control lists.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Apply server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).

choices.label: D
choices.text: Do not encrypt the objects and just keep the bucket private.

exam-clf-c02-18.explanation: The correct answer is server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Access to a KMS key can be controlled through key policies, and key usage is recorded in CloudTrail, so you can audit which key was used, when, and by whom. Using only S3 managed keys encrypts the data, but it is difficult to satisfy the requirement for the customer to set access policies per key and audit the usage records. HTTP uploads are not encrypted in transit, and access control lists cannot control keys. Choosing not to encrypt ignores the requirement itself. Looking at the added conditions in the question, key usage auditing and key policy control are required, so SSE-KMS is the answer.

exam-clf-c02-19.prompt: A single run of a transformation job at a data analytics company takes about 2 hours, and the job is already packaged as a container image. The team does not want to manage Amazon EC2 instances or clusters directly and wants to pay only for what it uses when the job finishes. Which method has the LEAST operational overhead for running this job as a container?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run the job by setting the timeout of an AWS Lambda function to 2 hours.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run an Amazon ECS task with the Fargate launch type to run the container without managing servers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure an EC2 instance directly and run the job while the team operates OS patching and Docker installation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the memory of a Lambda function to the maximum to speed up processing so that it finishes within the timeout.

exam-clf-c02-19.explanation: Running an Amazon ECS task on Fargate is the correct answer. Fargate lets you run containers without provisioning or scaling EC2 instances or clusters, and because it runs container tasks, it is not bound by the Lambda execution time limit, which suits a 2-hour job. A single Lambda invocation is limited to 15 minutes, and asynchronous invocations in Lambda Managed Instances are limited to 90 minutes, so neither can be set to 2 hours. Building a Docker environment on EC2 yourself leaves the burden of operating servers. Increasing memory to speed up processing does not change the time limit itself, and there is no guarantee that the job would finish within it. Looking at the added conditions in the question, serverless container execution that can handle a 2-hour job is Fargate.

exam-clf-c02-20.prompt: A company deployed the same web application in two Regions, Seoul and Oregon. Both Regions operate normally under usual conditions, and users are spread across Asia and North America. The company wants to configure Amazon Route 53 records so that when users connect, they are automatically routed to whichever of the two Regions has the lower network latency. Which routing policy meets the requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A weighted routing policy that splits traffic between the two Regions at ratios that you set directly

choices.label: B
choices.text: A geolocation routing policy that fixes the Region based on the user's country

choices.label: C
choices.text: A latency-based routing policy that responds with the Region that has the lowest latency

choices.label: D
choices.text: A failover routing policy that uses Seoul as the primary and Oregon as the standby

exam-clf-c02-20.explanation: A latency-based routing policy is the correct answer. When you have resources in multiple Regions, this policy routes users to the Region that provides the lowest latency. A weighted policy only splits traffic at set ratios and does not consider latency. A geolocation policy routes based on the user's location, so being geographically close does not guarantee the lowest latency, and this differs from a latency criterion. A failover policy is an active-passive configuration with a primary Region and a standby Region, so it does not match the requirement to use both Regions together. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the policy that automatically connects users to the lower-latency side is latency-based routing.

exam-clf-c02-21.prompt: A security team is creating an internal data retention standard and is reviewing Amazon S3 storage classes. Which TWO classes are the LEAST appropriate for storing the only copy of important data that has no other copy to recover from, that is, classes where the data could be lost if one Availability Zone is lost? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: S3 Standard, the default class that stores data redundantly across multiple Availability Zones

choices.label: B
choices.text: S3 Express One Zone, an ultra-low-latency class that stores data in one Availability Zone that you select

choices.label: C
choices.text: S3 Standard-IA, a class that stores infrequently accessed data across multiple Availability Zones

choices.label: D
choices.text: S3 One Zone-IA, a low-cost class that stores data in only one Availability Zone

choices.label: E
choices.text: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, an archive class that takes minutes to hours to restore

exam-clf-c02-21.explanation: S3 One Zone-IA and S3 Express One Zone are the correct answers. These two classes store data in only one Availability Zone, so data can be lost if the Availability Zone is physically lost. S3 Standard and Standard-IA store data in three or more Availability Zones and withstand the loss of an Availability Zone. Glacier Flexible Retrieval also stores data in three or more Availability Zones, so restores are only slow, and there is no single-copy risk. The official documentation also states that all classes other than these two withstand the loss of an Availability Zone. Looking at the added conditions in the question, One Zone-IA and Express One Zone, which store data in only a single Availability Zone, are the ones that apply.

exam-clf-c02-22.prompt: A financial analyst wants to document in the internal wiki two things that can be done with AWS Cost Explorer. The analyst wants to analyze cost trends by service over more than one past year and also forecast future spending. Which TWO actions can be performed in Cost Explorer? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: View costs and usage for the last 14 months including the current month (the default range, and up to 38 months at monthly granularity if the multi-year option is turned on), filtered and grouped by service.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Record the API calls made by IAM users to investigate who deleted which resource.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Record the history of resource configuration changes in chronological order to evaluate compliance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Forecast the costs that are expected to be incurred going forward based on current usage trends.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Create a budget that automatically sends an alert to an Amazon SNS topic when cost exceeds a set amount.

exam-clf-c02-22.explanation: Viewing past costs and forecasting costs are the correct answers. By default, Cost Explorer shows costs and usage for the current month and the previous 13 months, which is about 14 months, and you can filter and group them by service. If you turn on multi-year data, you can extend this to up to 38 months at monthly granularity, which satisfies the requirement to analyze trends over more than one past year. It can also forecast spending for up to 18 months ahead. Recording the history of configuration changes and evaluating compliance is the role of AWS Config. A budget that sends alerts when a threshold is exceeded is an AWS Budgets feature. Investigating who called which API is the role of CloudTrail, so it is not a Cost Explorer action. Looking at the added conditions in the question, cost analysis and forecasting are Cost Explorer features, and budgets for alerts are a Budgets feature.

exam-clf-c02-23.prompt: Most of the infrastructure team's time is spent on installing server racks, managing power and cooling, and replacing hardware, so development of customer-facing features keeps being delayed. The company serves only domestic customers, has no plans to expand overseas, and has a stable number of servers. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate benefit of migrating to AWS to resolve this problem?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deploy applications to multiple Regions in minutes to provide low latency to overseas users.

choices.label: B
choices.text: As the number of users grows, the cost per server drops because of AWS economies of scale.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Redirect the cost and effort spent on running and maintaining data centers to work that is directly tied to customers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Accurately predict the number of servers needed in the future and make a plan to buy them all at once.

exam-clf-c02-23.explanation: The correct answer is to redirect the cost and effort spent on running and maintaining data centers to work that is directly tied to customers. The constraint in the question is that development is delayed because of heavy infrastructure work such as installing racks, power, and cooling, and AWS takes on that work. Deploying to multiple Regions is a benefit of reduced latency, which does not match this situation. Economies of scale are about unit price and are unrelated to the team's lack of time. Accurately predicting the number of servers and buying them is the capacity-guessing approach that the cloud is meant to eliminate. Looking at the added conditions in the question, there are no overseas expansion plans and the server count is stable, so the key effect is shifting the operational burden to AWS.

exam-clf-c02-24.prompt: A web service serves image and video files stored in Amazon S3 to users in multiple countries. The origin is in a bucket in one Region, and loading is slow for users who are far away. The content does not change often, and the operations team has only two members. Which method has the LEAST operational overhead for delivering the content close to users and reducing latency?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Install AWS Direct Connect connections in every user country.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Build Amazon EC2 web servers directly in each user country and copy the files manually.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution and specify the S3 bucket as the origin.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Place Elastic Load Balancing in front of Amazon S3 to distribute requests across multiple servers.

exam-clf-c02-24.explanation: A CloudFront distribution is the correct answer. It caches content at edge locations around the world and routes user requests to the edge location with the lowest latency, and because an S3 bucket can be used as the origin, the problem is solved with configuration alone. Direct Connect is a service that connects a corporate network to AWS and cannot be applied to general users. Building EC2 servers in each country and copying manually creates a very large operational burden. A load balancer only distributes traffic among servers and does not place content close to users. Looking at the added conditions in the question, CloudFront with S3 as the origin delivers from the edge without separate servers.

exam-clf-c02-25.prompt: A security audit must determine, in chronological order, which ports a particular Amazon EC2 security group had open last month and how its configuration has changed over time. The account under audit turned on configuration recording one month ago, and the auditor is more interested in the change history of the resource settings themselves than in the API callers. Which service is the MOST suitable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amazon GuardDuty

choices.label: B
choices.text: AWS Artifact

choices.label: C
choices.text: AWS Config

choices.label: D
choices.text: AWS Shield

exam-clf-c02-25.explanation: The correct answer is AWS Config. Config records the configuration, relationships, and past configurations of resources such as security groups and shows changes over time, so you can also see which ports were open at a specific point in time. However, you can see only the history from after you turned on recording. GuardDuty only detects threat activity and does not store configuration history. Artifact provides AWS compliance documents. Shield is a DDoS protection service and is unrelated to configuration history. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the time-based history of resource configuration is recorded by AWS Config.

exam-clf-c02-26.prompt: A software company must repeatedly create development, staging, and production environments with identical configurations in two Regions, Seoul and Tokyo. Currently each person creates them manually, so the environments often differ from one another. The company also wants to version-control the history of configuration changes like source code. Which method MOST suitably meets the requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create the resources for each environment directly in the console and follow documented procedures.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Record the configuration history of the existing environment with AWS Config and recreate it manually while referring to the history.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Define the resources in an AWS CloudFormation template and create a stack for each environment and Region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assign a person to each environment and have each person enter CLI commands to create the resources.

exam-clf-c02-26.explanation: CloudFormation templates and stacks are the correct answer. A template describes resources and their properties as text, so you can create the same configuration consistently and repeatedly in multiple Regions, and if you version-control the template, you can track the change history like source code and roll back to a previous state. Manual console work and documentation lead to human error and take time to repeat. Config records history but cannot create environments. Entering CLI commands by individual owners does not guarantee consistency. Looking at the added conditions in the question, defining infrastructure as code, deploying it repeatedly, and version-controlling it is what CloudFormation does.

exam-clf-c02-27.prompt: An online reservation service uses a managed Amazon RDS database and needs to fail over automatically to a standby instance without human intervention if a single Availability Zone fails. There is no on-call staff at night, so the service cannot depend on people for the failure response procedure. Which method meets the requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a read replica in another Availability Zone and have a person manually promote it when a failure occurs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Install the database directly on two EC2 instances and write and operate your own replication and failover scripts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure RDS as a Multi-AZ deployment and keep a standby instance in another Availability Zone.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a snapshot once a day and restore it to a new instance when a failure occurs.

exam-clf-c02-27.explanation: An RDS Multi-AZ deployment is the correct answer. It is a high availability feature that keeps a standby instance in another Availability Zone and fails over automatically when a failure occurs, and because it is managed, the operational burden is small. Note that the standby instance in a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment does not serve read traffic and exists for failure protection. Manually promoting a read replica requires human intervention, so it violates the requirement for automatic failover. Installing the database yourself on EC2 means you must operate replication and failover yourself. Restoring a once-a-day snapshot is slow to recover and also loses a lot of data. Looking at the added conditions in the question, automatic failover is required, so a read replica that needs manual promotion does not fit.

exam-clf-c02-28.prompt: A healthcare startup has been told that to run workloads that handle patient information on AWS, it must enter into a business associate agreement (BAA) with AWS. The legal team wants to check the agreement status directly without asking an AWS sales representative for documents. Which service lets the team review and accept this agreement and track its status in the console?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AWS Config

choices.label: B
choices.text: AWS CloudTrail

choices.label: C
choices.text: AWS Organizations

choices.label: D
choices.text: AWS Artifact

exam-clf-c02-28.explanation: The correct answer is AWS Artifact. Artifact lets you review, accept, and track the status of agreements with AWS at the account level, and it also lets you download compliance reports at no cost. Config is a service that evaluates resource configuration history and rule compliance and has no agreement management feature. CloudTrail records API activity in the account. Organizations is a service that groups and manages multiple accounts and does not provide a feature to accept agreements. Looking at the added conditions in the question, reviewing and accepting agreements is the Agreements feature of AWS Artifact.

exam-clf-c02-29.prompt: A midsize company confirmed that its AWS usage charges are lower than the unit cost it paid when it bought servers directly for its own data center, and that AWS has reduced its prices several times as it has grown. The company's server demand has been almost constant for several years. Which cloud benefit BEST explains this phenomenon?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Economies of scale, in which the usage of many customers is aggregated so that AWS obtains lower unit costs

choices.label: B
choices.text: Agility, in which obtaining resources within minutes when needed reduces the time spent on experimentation and development

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stop guessing capacity, in which you adjust to your needs instead of predicting the required capacity before use

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trading fixed expense for variable expense, in which you pay only for what you use instead of making up-front capital expenditures

exam-clf-c02-29.explanation: The correct answer is economies of scale, in which the usage of many customers is aggregated so that AWS obtains lower unit costs. The key point of the situation is that AWS lowers prices as it grows, which is explained by economies of scale from aggregating customer usage. Agility in obtaining resources within minutes is a benefit of speed and is unrelated to a drop in unit price. The benefit of eliminating capacity guesses is avoiding idle resources and shortages, not the reason prices fall. Converting fixed costs to variable costs is a benefit of the payment model and is not the cause of price reductions. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the lower unit cost and price reductions are explained by economies of scale. Because demand is constant, elasticity is not the key point.

exam-clf-c02-30.prompt: A security officer wants to monitor whether Amazon S3 buckets have been changed to public access and also automatically find whether the documents in the buckets contain personal information and credit card numbers. There are hundreds of buckets, and the officer cannot open the objects directly to check. Which service meets both requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AWS WAF

choices.label: B
choices.text: Amazon Inspector

choices.label: C
choices.text: AWS Key Management Service

choices.label: D
choices.text: Amazon Macie

exam-clf-c02-30.explanation: The correct answer is Amazon Macie. Macie creates an inventory of S3 buckets and monitors security and access control issues such as public access and encryption status, and it uses machine learning and pattern matching to find sensitive data such as personal information inside objects. WAF is a firewall that filters web requests and does not classify S3 data. Inspector is a service that scans Amazon EC2, Amazon ECR, and AWS Lambda for vulnerabilities. KMS creates and manages encryption keys and does not analyze the contents of data. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the service that provides both S3 exposure monitoring and sensitive data discovery is Macie.

exam-clf-c02-31.prompt: A manufacturer starting its cloud transition wants to identify gaps in the required technical skills and manage the training plan and organizational culture change. The biggest concern is the readiness of people and the organization, rather than the technical configuration or cost control. Which perspective of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) MOST directly addresses this activity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The People perspective, which covers culture, organizational structure, and the skills of the workforce

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Governance perspective, which coordinates cloud initiatives and manages benefits, risk, and cost

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Platform perspective, which covers technology such as architecture and workloads

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Operations perspective, which covers how workloads are monitored and supported

exam-clf-c02-31.explanation: The correct answer is the People perspective. This perspective covers culture, organizational structure, leadership, workforce skills, and change management, so it exactly fits skill gap analysis and training planning. The Governance perspective coordinates cloud initiatives and manages benefits, transition risk, and cloud spending, so training and culture change are not its focus. The Platform perspective covers technology itself such as architecture, workloads, and data. The Operations perspective covers how cloud workloads are monitored and supported, which is far from workforce training or organizational change. Looking at the added conditions in the question, skill gaps and culture change are covered by the People perspective.

exam-clf-c02-32.prompt: Twelve Linux Amazon EC2 instances at a media company must read and write content files in the same directory at the same time. The company wants storage capacity to adjust automatically as files grow and shrink without adjusting it manually, and the instances are distributed across multiple Availability Zones. Which storage is the MOST suitable to meet this requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an Amazon EBS volume for each instance and periodically synchronize the files with one another by using rsync.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Copy the files to the instance store of each instance and keep them up to date with a script.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Place the files in Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive and restore them each time they need to be read.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an Amazon EFS file system and mount it on all the instances over NFS.

exam-clf-c02-32.explanation: Amazon EFS is the correct answer. Multiple EC2 instances can mount it at the same time over the NFS protocol, and capacity grows and shrinks automatically as you add or delete files, so there is nothing to manage. Giving each instance its own EBS volume and synchronizing means managing 12 separate copies, and consistency of concurrent writes is not guaranteed. An instance store is temporary storage tied to the instance, so it does not fit the sharing and retention requirements. Glacier Deep Archive is for archiving and cannot be used as a shared directory for reading and writing. Looking at the added conditions in the question, concurrent access from multiple instances and automatic capacity adjustment are characteristics of EFS.

exam-clf-c02-33.prompt: A new development team wants to open the AWS Trusted Advisor console in an account that uses the Basic Support plan. The team lead wants to know first which checks can be viewed without spending extra money. Which of the following is the MOST accurate description of the scope of checks available at no additional cost?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All checks in all categories and automatic refresh

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only all checks in the Cost Optimization category

choices.label: C
choices.text: No checks are provided, and only recommendation emails are received

choices.label: D
choices.text: All checks in the Service Limits category and some checks in the Security and Fault Tolerance categories

exam-clf-c02-33.explanation: The correct answer is all checks in the Service Limits category and some checks in the Security and Fault Tolerance categories. According to the Trusted Advisor check reference, with the Basic or Developer Support plan you can view in the console all checks in the Service Limits category and only a few selected checks in Security (public EBS snapshots, public RDS snapshots, S3 bucket permissions, MFA on the root account, and unrestricted specific ports in security groups) and Fault Tolerance (use of the STS global endpoint). All checks in all categories fall within the scope of the Business Support+ plan or higher. All Cost Optimization checks are also within the scope of a higher plan. Because some checks can be viewed in the console, the statement that no checks are provided is also incorrect. Looking at the added conditions in the question, Basic provides only all Service Limits checks and some Security and Fault Tolerance checks.

exam-clf-c02-34.prompt: Executives have asked to reduce the energy consumed by workloads running on AWS and to increase resource utilization in order to lower the environmental impact. Cost reduction itself is not the goal, and the security and performance requirements are already sufficiently met. Which pillar of the Well-Architected Framework is MOST directly aligned with this requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Sustainability pillar, which addresses reducing environmental impact

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Cost Optimization pillar, which reduces unnecessary monetary spending

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Security pillar, which protects data and systems

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Performance Efficiency pillar, which selects resources to match requirements

exam-clf-c02-34.explanation: The correct answer is the Sustainability pillar. Reducing energy use and environmental impact is the purpose of this pillar, and the situation also explicitly mentions environmental impact. Cost Optimization is the pillar that reduces unnecessary monetary spending, so environmental impact is not its direct subject. Security covers protecting the confidentiality and integrity of data and systems. Performance Efficiency is the area of using resources efficiently to match requirements, but it does not directly address the goal of environmental impact. The framework consists of six pillars, including Sustainability. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the goal is reducing environmental impact, so the answer is the Sustainability pillar.

exam-clf-c02-35.prompt: A headquarters receives separate invoices from 10 AWS accounts and pays them separately. It wants to combine the invoices into a single payment and also view the costs by account. Each account is used by a different team, so merging the accounts or moving resources risks service interruptions. Which method has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Move the resources of nine accounts into one account and close the remaining accounts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Download each account's invoice as a PDF, compile them in a spreadsheet, and pay with a single card.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an AWS Organizations organization, invite the 10 accounts to join it, and use consolidated billing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Share the root user credentials of all accounts so that one person can handle payment in each account.

exam-clf-c02-35.explanation: Consolidated billing in AWS Organizations is the correct answer. It collects the costs of accounts in the organization into a single invoice with one payment method, while usage and cost by account can still be viewed separately in Cost Explorer. Moving resources into one account violates the condition not to merge accounts and also involves a large amount of work. Compiling invoices manually requires human effort every month and invites mistakes. Sharing root credentials is the riskiest approach from a security standpoint, so it cannot be chosen. Looking at the added conditions in the question, consolidated billing while keeping the accounts is a feature of Organizations.

exam-clf-c02-36.prompt: A development team wants to deploy a web application in an environment where it manages only its code and data, and the provider manages the underlying servers and runtime without any operating system installation or runtime patching. The team has an application that it developed itself, so it cannot use a model that subscribes to finished software. Which cloud service model is the closest to this requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: PaaS, a model in which you are given a platform and manage only code and data

choices.label: B
choices.text: IaaS, a model in which you rent virtual servers and networking

choices.label: C
choices.text: SaaS, a model in which you subscribe to and use finished software

choices.label: D
choices.text: On-premises virtualization, a model in which you operate virtual servers on your own hardware

exam-clf-c02-36.explanation: The correct answer is PaaS. The characteristic of PaaS is that the development team deploys its own code and data while the provider manages the platform, such as servers, operating systems, and runtimes. IaaS rents out virtual servers and networking but requires the customer to manage the operating system and runtime, so it does not match the requirement. SaaS is a model for using finished software, and the situation is not one in which a development team is deploying its own code. On-premises virtualization is not a cloud service model and requires you to operate even the hardware. Looking at the added conditions in the question, a model that deploys your own code while delegating the platform is PaaS.

exam-clf-c02-37.prompt: A fintech company must create its own data encryption keys and control access to them through policies as required by regulation, and it wants the keys to be protected in validated hardware security modules. The company must also submit key usage records during audits, and the service must integrate with multiple AWS services such as Amazon S3 and Amazon EBS. Which managed service is the MOST suitable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AWS Certificate Manager

choices.label: B
choices.text: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Amazon Cognito

choices.label: D
choices.text: AWS Artifact

exam-clf-c02-37.explanation: The correct answer is AWS Key Management Service. KMS is a managed service that makes it easy to create and control keys used to encrypt and sign data, and the keys are protected by validated HSMs and never leave KMS unencrypted. You can also use key policies to allow access only to trusted users. Certificate Manager is a service that issues and manages TLS certificates. Cognito handles authentication of application users. Artifact provides compliance documents and does not manage keys. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the managed service that provides key creation, policy control, and service integration is KMS.

exam-clf-c02-38.prompt: A security officer discovered yesterday that a security group rule had been changed. The officer needs to find out two things: who called the change API and when, and what the configuration state of the security group was before and after the change. No new tool needs to be built; the team only needs to turn on the necessary recording features. Which TWO services each meet one of these two requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amazon CloudWatch alarms, which send notifications when a metric exceeds a threshold

choices.label: B
choices.text: AWS Cost Explorer, which visualizes costs and usage by service

choices.label: C
choices.text: AWS CloudTrail, which records API calls made through the console, CLI, and SDKs

choices.label: D
choices.text: AWS Trusted Advisor, which checks cost and security improvement recommendations

choices.label: E
choices.text: AWS Config, which records resource configuration history and compliance status

exam-clf-c02-38.explanation: AWS CloudTrail and AWS Config are the correct answers. CloudTrail records actions taken by users, roles, and services as events and tells you who called which API and when. AWS Config shows the configuration of a resource and its change history over time, so you can check the state before and after the change. CloudWatch alarms are a tool for monitoring metrics and do not tell you the caller or the configuration history. Trusted Advisor provides recommendations based on best practices and does not track individual change history. Cost Explorer is a cost analysis tool and is unrelated to security group changes. Looking at the added conditions in the question, CloudTrail handles who made the call, and Config handles the configuration before and after.

exam-clf-c02-39.prompt: An Amazon EC2 instance in a private subnet of a VPC needs to download OS security updates from the internet. Security policy does not allow connections coming into this instance from the internet, and the network team does not want to operate a separate proxy server itself. Which method meets this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the private subnet route table to point directly to an internet gateway.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assign a public IP address to the instance and open all inbound ports in the security group.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Build a new AWS Direct Connect connection to reach the internet update servers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a NAT gateway in a public subnet and point the private subnet routing to it.

exam-clf-c02-39.explanation: A NAT gateway is the correct answer.
