choices.text: Instead of grouping the two rules into a composite rule, change them to independent rules that each have with threshold > 0.5, and treat a row as having passed with only one of them if each rule passes more than half of the rows, checking the pass ratio per rule.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Move the composite rule to the Analyzers block so that the analyzer calculates per-row statistics, and combine the columns of the result table with OR yourself.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the additionalOptions of EvaluateDataQuality, specify compositeRuleEvaluation.method as ROW so that composite rules are evaluated at the row level.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the OR operator to AND so that only rows that satisfy both conditions pass, and use this result as a substitute for row-level evaluation.

exam-dea-c01-52.explanation: The correct answer is to set compositeRuleEvaluation.method to ROW. By default, composite rules evaluate each rule against the whole data and then apply the operator, but setting this option to ROW makes the composite rule evaluate whole rows as a single rule and also yields row-level results. Attaching a threshold to independent rules only looks at the satisfaction ratio of each and cannot combine them with OR in a single row. Analyzers cannot evaluate conditions. Changing OR to AND changes the required meaning, so a row would have to satisfy both conditions to pass.

exam-dea-c01-53.prompt: A telecom company loads one gzip-compressed CSV file (about 400 GB) created daily by an upstream system into an Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster with 32 slices by using COPY. The file format and compression method are fixed by the upstream system and cannot be changed, and loading has been slow, like a single stream, for several hours, which delays the morning report. The file is already uploaded under one S3 prefix, and a preprocessing step that splits the file before loading can be added. The cluster size must be kept because of cost. The cluster handles BI queries during the day, so the load must finish in the early morning hours, and splitting a compressed file does not change its content. What should the company do to reduce load time?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Instead of COPY, run INSERT INTO ... SELECT statements concurrently from multiple sessions to insert split rows, assuming each session uses a different slice so the whole cluster loads in parallel.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add only the COMPUPDATE OFF option to COPY to skip the compression encoding analysis step and leave the other settings as they are.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Split the compressed file into multiple files of similar size between 1 MB and 1 GB after compression, match the number of files to a multiple of the number of slices, and COPY from the same prefix.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the node type to a larger type to increase the cores and memory that read the single gzip file and raise the load speed for a single file.

exam-dea-c01-53.explanation: The correct answer is to split the file into similar sizes and match the number of files to a multiple of the number of slices. Compressed CSV files such as gzip are not split automatically, so a single file is loaded serially, and the data must be divided into multiple files of 1 MB to 1 GB after compression so that slices read in parallel in the MPP architecture. A single gzip file is not split even if nodes are enlarged, so read parallelism does not increase. INSERT ... SELECT is not a way of reading S3 files and is less efficient than COPY for bulk loading. COMPUPDATE OFF only reduces the analysis time and does not address the root cause, which is serial reading.

exam-dea-c01-54.prompt: A group of data engineers at a company creates and runs AWS Glue jobs directly. The account also has an administrator role and a role for accessing the billing system, in addition to the service role glue-etl-role that AWS Glue assumes. The security team wants engineers to be able to pass only the service role glue-etl-role to AWS Glue, and to prevent privilege escalation by attaching other roles with stronger permissions to a job. Engineers frequently need to create new jobs, so they must be able to create jobs without security team approval. All jobs run in the same account, and engineers already have glue:CreateJob and glue:StartJobRun permissions. What is the MOST appropriate IAM policy design?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allow engineers iam:CreateRole and iam:AttachRolePolicy so that they create and use a dedicated role themselves each time they create a job, and distinguish role names by a prefix convention.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attach AdministratorAccess to glue-etl-role so that no data job fails because of insufficient permissions, and instruct engineers to use only this role.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Allow iam:PassRole only for the glue-etl-role ARN and restrict it with an iam:PassedToService condition of glue.amazonaws.com.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Allow iam:PassRole on all resources in the engineer policy and control access only by restricting the scope of glue:CreateJob to a job name pattern, leaving role selection to the engineers.

exam-dea-c01-54.explanation: The correct answer is to restrict iam:PassRole to a specific role ARN and to use the iam:PassedToService condition so that it can be passed only to AWS Glue. For a user to pass a role to a service, PassRole permission is needed, and restricting the Resource element to the approved role prevents privilege escalation by attaching a role with stronger permissions. If PassRole is opened to all resources, a job name restriction cannot control which role gets attached. Giving the role AdministratorAccess violates the principle of least privilege. Giving permissions to create roles and attach policies lets engineers elevate their own permissions.

exam-dea-c01-55.prompt: A fintech company stores transaction data in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, and the analytics team builds dashboards in Amazon Redshift. Currently, an AWS Glue job that runs every 5 minutes moves the data, but it fails often whenever the schema changes, and reflection delays are long. The company wants to reflect changes in the production database in Amazon Redshift in near real time without creating and operating new pipeline code. Both services are in the same Region in the same account, and the data team has three people and cannot manage replication infrastructure on its own. The analytics team can tolerate a delay of a few minutes but not a delay of a day, and source write performance must not be affected. Which method has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a zero-ETL integration with Aurora PostgreSQL as the source and Amazon Redshift as the target so that changes are replicated automatically after the initial load.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an AWS DMS replication instance yourself, configure a full load and change data capture task, and continuously manage the size and status of the replication instance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a schedule that exports an Aurora snapshot to Amazon S3 every hour, and have AWS Step Functions run COPY when the export finishes. Because the entire snapshot is converted, the delay grows as the data grows.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Modify the application to additionally write an event to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for every transaction, and load it into Amazon Redshift with Amazon Data Firehose.

exam-dea-c01-55.explanation: A zero-ETL integration is the correct answer. When you specify the source and Amazon Redshift, replication happens automatically after the initial load, the integration status is monitored as a managed service, and it recovers by itself where possible when problems occur, so no pipeline code or operations are needed. AWS DMS can also replicate change data, but you must operate the replication instance and tasks yourself, so it loses on the operational overhead constraint. The snapshot export and COPY approach increases the delay to hours and requires building orchestration. Modifying the application to write events twice requires both application changes and operating a new streaming pipeline.

exam-dea-c01-56.prompt: At a data-selling company, partners upload CSV files averaging 150 MB to Amazon S3 irregularly throughout the day (about 300 times a day). Within 5 minutes of upload, each file must be converted to Parquet with cleaned-up column types and stored under a different prefix. A single file can be processed in the memory of a single node, and there are no joins or aggregations between files. The company wants to minimize cost with no always-on infrastructure and keep the code simple. The partners' upload method cannot be changed. The transformation rules consist only of specifying column types and converting the file format, and there are also long periods during the day with no uploads. Which method is MOST suitable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Start a new AWS Glue Spark job on every S3 object creation event to read the file with distributed Spark, transform it, and save the result as Parquet.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run an Amazon EMR cluster continuously, and have a Spark Streaming job that polls the input prefix find new files and convert them to Parquet.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Invoke an AWS Lambda function on S3 object creation events, read the CSV with a pandas-based layer, and save it as Parquet.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Send the file contents to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, and then have Amazon Data Firehose format conversion deliver Parquet files to Amazon S3.

exam-dea-c01-56.explanation: The correct answer is an AWS Lambda function invoked by S3 events with a pandas-based library. It is event-driven, so there is no idle cost, a 150 MB file can be handled in the memory of a single function, and the 5-minute limit is sufficient. Starting an AWS Glue Spark job for every file means startup and DPU charges that are excessive for small files that do not need distributed processing. A continuously running EMR cluster violates the condition of having no always-on infrastructure. A configuration that goes through Kinesis requires splitting file contents into records, making the code complex, and does not match the requirement of file-level conversion.

exam-dea-c01-57.prompt: The finance team at a manufacturing group wants the FinOps team to be notified by email when the total daily scan volume of the Athena workgroup finance-bi exceeds 2 TB. However, during month-end closing hours, queries must not be stopped even if the threshold is exceeded. The notification target is a single shared mailbox address of the FinOps team, and the company does not want to write separate code. The workgroup already has a query result location and Amazon CloudWatch metrics publishing turned on. The response after receiving a notification is decided by the FinOps team using human judgment. The alert threshold is about 1.5 times the usual daily scan average, and the finance team reviews the value every quarter. What is the simplest configuration that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set the per-query data usage control of the workgroup to 2 TB so that queries that reach the limit are canceled and an alert email is also sent. Assume that the per-query limit also monitors the combined daily scan volume.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Subscribe an AWS Lambda function that disables the workgroup to the SNS notification so that scan volume stops growing, and also send an email.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Subscribe the FinOps team by email to the AWS Cost Explorer monthly report so that they review Athena cost on a monthly basis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set a workgroup-level data usage alert with a daily threshold of 2 TB and specify an SNS topic with an email subscription. Queries are not canceled automatically when the threshold is reached.

exam-dea-c01-57.explanation: A workgroup-level data usage alert is the correct answer. This alert sets a threshold on the hourly or daily aggregate scan volume and notifies through a CloudWatch alarm and Amazon SNS, and queries are not canceled automatically when the threshold is reached. The per-query limit cancels a query when its scan volume exceeds the limit, so it would stop queries during closing hours and violate the requirement. An AWS Lambda function that disables the workgroup would also block all subsequent queries. The monthly cost report cannot notify of a daily threshold being exceeded.

exam-dea-c01-58.prompt: An AWS Glue ETL job at a healthcare data company reads data from Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. Security policy requires the database password to be changed every 30 days, and the password must not remain in plain text in scripts or job parameters. The job runs once a day, and connection information is managed with an AWS Glue connection object. The company wants no job code changes when the password changes, and rotation must not cause job failures. The infrastructure team has no staff to write a new rotation script. The RDS instance is in a private subnet, and AWS Glue already accesses it through a connection in the same VPC. What is the MOST appropriate method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Place the password in a plain string parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store and manually update the job parameter each time it is rotated.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Store the credentials in an AWS Secrets Manager secret, set up automatic rotation every 30 days, and have the AWS Glue connection reference that secret.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Put a value encrypted with AWS KMS into the script as a constant, and redeploy the script with a new value every rotation cycle.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a read-only database user, set its password not to expire, and keep using the value set once in the job settings.

exam-dea-c01-58.explanation: The correct answer is an AWS Secrets Manager secret with automatic rotation and an AWS Glue connection that references the secret. If credentials are kept in Secrets Manager, automatic rotation for RDS meets the 30-day cycle, and because the AWS Glue connection references the secret, the script does not need to be changed after rotation, and the password is not exposed in plain text. A plain string in Parameter Store is plain text and needs manual updates. Putting an encrypted constant in the script requires deploying code at every rotation. A password that never expires violates the 30-day rotation policy.

exam-dea-c01-59.prompt: A data engineer specified the job-bookmark-enable option on an AWS Glue Spark ETL job that reads an Amazon S3 path where new JSON files accumulate daily. However, every run rereads files that were already processed, so the output is duplicated on a daily basis and downstream aggregate values are inflated. Looking at the script, the read step has no transformation_ctx argument, and there is no job.commit() call at the end. The input path and job structure must not change, but the script can be modified. The job runs once a day, and previous output accumulates in date partitions, so duplicates are conspicuous when they occur. What is the MOST appropriate action to resolve the problem?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Specify transformation_ctx on the step that reads the data source and call job.commit() at the end of the script so that the bookmark state is saved.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reset the bookmark with reset-job-bookmark before starting every run to keep it clean so that no previous state remains.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the bookmark option to pause so that each run reads only data after the last successful point (do not modify the job script).

choices.label: D
choices.text: Double the number of workers in the job so that processing finishes sooner, which makes bookmark updates happen on time and removes the duplicates.

exam-dea-c01-59.explanation: The correct answer is to specify transformation_ctx and call job.commit(). Bookmark state consists of entries per source, transformation, and sink, identified by the transformation context, and is saved atomically when job.commit() is called, so if either one is missing, the next run does not know the previous state and rereads the files. The pause option reads data after the last successful point but does not update the bookmark state, so it does not fix the problem. A reset erases the state, so each run actually rereads everything. The number of workers affects only processing speed and is unrelated to whether state is saved.

exam-dea-c01-60.prompt: An AWS Glue job at an advertising company reads 2 TB of JSON logs per day and writes the transformed results to Amazon S3. This data is used for BI dashboards and ad hoc analysis queries, and most queries cover short time ranges. Analysts query only 4 of the 80 columns with Athena and mostly filter on the most recent 7 days. The data is currently stored as JSON, and query cost, which is proportional to scan volume, is exceeding the monthly budget. The storage format can be changed in the AWS Glue job, and the company does not want to change the analysts' query statements. The data retention period is 13 months, and even after switching to a new format, historical data does not need to be converted again. How should the output be stored to reduce scan volume and query cost the MOST?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Store it in Parquet format with Snappy compression and partition by event date so that date range queries read only the necessary partitions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Store it in Parquet format but without partitions, piling all dates under a single prefix, and let Athena select and read only the columns.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Store it as gzip-compressed JSON Lines files split by date prefix to reduce storage space so that date filters apply.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Store it in ORC format and partition by user ID, creating millions of partitions to favor per-user lookups.

exam-dea-c01-60.explanation: The correct answer is Snappy Parquet partitioned by date. A columnar format reads only the 4 columns being queried and skips unnecessary blocks using block statistics, and date partitions remove scans of the remaining partitions for the recent 7-day filter. Gzip JSON is row-based, so queries read all columns, and gzip is also disadvantageous for split reads. Parquet without partitions saves on columns but targets the files of every date. Partitioning by user ID does not match the query pattern and degrades performance through small files and an explosion of partitions.

exam-dea-c01-61.prompt: A research company's analytics team runs a Spark job on Amazon EMR for 4 hours once a day. Because some intermediate results remain in HDFS, the job must not restart from the beginning even if nodes are lost, and the company wants to cut cost as much as possible. When the job finishes, the cluster is terminated and restarted as a new cluster the next day. Input and final results are all stored in Amazon S3, and extra processing capacity is needed during peak hours. The team understands the possibility of Spot interruptions and will not modify the code. The HDFS data kept on core nodes during the job consists of temporary shuffle files and intermediate tables. Which TWO configurations meet the requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run core nodes as Spot Instances and lower the HDFS replication factor to 1 to reduce storage cost, assuming node loss is acceptable.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure the primary and core nodes as On-Demand Instances to protect HDFS data and the cluster from being lost to Spot interruptions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure the primary, core, and task nodes all as Spot Instances to get the maximum possible discount, and resubmit the job if interrupted.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure only core nodes as large On-Demand Instances without task nodes so that peak throughput is always secured, and do not use Spot.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Secure the extra processing capacity by configuring task nodes as Spot Instances in an instance fleet that specifies several instance types.

exam-dea-c01-61.explanation: The correct answers are keeping the primary and core nodes On-Demand and configuring the task nodes as a Spot Instance fleet with diverse instance types. Core nodes store data in HDFS, so data can be lost if they are terminated, and the cluster ends if the primary is terminated. Task nodes do not store data, so the impact of Spot interruptions is small, which makes them suitable for capacity expansion. All-Spot would require restarts because of lost intermediate results and violates the requirement. Running core nodes on Spot while lowering the replication factor actually increases the risk of HDFS loss. Using only large On-Demand core nodes increases cost unnecessarily.

exam-dea-c01-62.prompt: A team at a SaaS company wants to enable the UltraWarm tier on an Amazon OpenSearch Service domain. The domain currently uses 3 data nodes with t3.medium.search instances and has no dedicated master nodes. The goal is to reduce log retention cost, and the domain spans 3 Availability Zones. When the team tries to add warm nodes in the console, it reports that the domain does not meet the prerequisites. The team wants to resolve this by changing the existing domain configuration without creating a new domain. Logs accumulate in daily indexes, and the indexes to be moved to the warm tier are old indexes that are no longer written to. Which TWO conditions must be met to enable UltraWarm? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enable dedicated master nodes on the domain.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create the S3 bucket in which warm data will be stored yourself and link the bucket name in the domain settings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turn off encryption at rest on the domain so that warm nodes can read unencrypted objects in S3.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the data nodes to an instance type other than T2 or T3.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduce the number of replicas of all indexes in the domain to 0 so that no replicas remain when moving to the warm tier.

exam-dea-c01-62.explanation: The correct answers are enabling dedicated master nodes and using a data node type other than T2 or T3. The official documentation states that to use warm storage, the domain must have dedicated master nodes, and that warm storage cannot be used if data nodes are T2 or T3 instance types. Reducing the number of replicas to 0 is not a requirement, and replicas of warm indexes are passive replicas that do not use disk. The S3 storage is managed by the service, so you do not create and link a bucket yourself. Turning off encryption is not a condition and is unrelated to the warm tier.

exam-dea-c01-63.prompt: A marketing analytics team uses an Amazon Redshift Serverless workgroup, and inefficient analyst queries once caused month-end cost to exceed the budget. Some reduction in query performance is acceptable, but monthly cost must not exceed a ceiling, and the human intervention needed to manage this must be minimal. The workgroup is shared by 30 analysts and has a base capacity of 128 RPUs. The organization will not accept turning queries themselves into an approval process. Budget approval is made monthly, and an approach of only receiving cost-overrun alerts was already tried before without effect. Which configuration MOST appropriately meets this requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set the Max RPU-hours usage limit and the maximum capacity (Max capacity) on the workgroup so that the service scales and consumes only within these limits.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Raise the base capacity to 512 RPUs so that queries always finish quickly with ample resources and the time consumed is reduced.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Move the price-performance target slider toward performance optimization so that even inefficient queries scale aggressively and finish quickly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set as an operating guideline that an owner manually pauses the workgroup after the 20th of each month and restarts it at the start of the month.

exam-dea-c01-63.explanation: Setting the Max RPU-hours and maximum capacity limits is the correct answer. The documentation explains that Max capacity and Max RPU-hours limit the maximum RPUs that serverless can scale to and the maximum RPU-hours it can consume, and that they are always honored and enforced regardless of the price-performance target. This keeps the monthly ceiling without human intervention, and it matches the stated tolerance for lower performance. Raising the base capacity increases the RPU rate and usage, so cost actually grows. The performance-optimized target scales aggressively even if it costs more. Manual pausing involves a lot of human intervention and blocks month-end work.

exam-dea-c01-64.prompt: A mobility company has an Apache Iceberg table that it queries with Athena. Streaming ingestion creates tens of thousands of small Parquet files per day, and delete files from row-level DELETE operations also accumulate, so queries are getting slower. Old snapshots and orphan files keep increasing Amazon S3 storage and metadata. The table is registered in the AWS Glue Data Catalog, and time travel to snapshots within the last 7 days must be maintained. Most queries read recent partitions, and DELETE operations occur mainly because of personal data deletion requests. Which TWO methods solve these two problems in Athena without operating a new cluster? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run MSCK REPAIR TABLE regularly to re-register partitions, assuming that small files are merged automatically and delete files are applied to data files, and schedule it to run every night.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply a lifecycle rule to the S3 bucket that deletes all objects older than 30 days after creation so that old snapshots and orphan files are removed together, and include the files used by the current table in the same rule.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Run an OPTIMIZE ... REWRITE DATA USING BIN_PACK statement to merge small data files and delete files into files closer to the target size and rewrite them.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run an AWS Glue crawler every hour to reread the table schema, assuming that old snapshots in the Iceberg metadata are cleaned up when the crawler runs, and set the crawler schedule to hourly.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Specify a snapshot retention period in the table properties and then run a VACUUM statement to clean up expired snapshots and remove orphan files that do not belong to the current state.

exam-dea-c01-64.explanation: OPTIMIZE and VACUUM are the correct answers. OPTIMIZE REWRITE DATA rewrites data files into a better layout based on file size and the number of associated delete files, which resolves the small file and delete file problems. VACUUM performs snapshot expiration and orphan file removal, deleting only items older than the retention period (vacuum_max_snapshot_age_seconds), which reduces metadata and storage. A crawler only reads schemas and partitions and neither cleans up snapshots nor merges files. MSCK REPAIR TABLE is a partition registration command and has no file merging effect. An S3 lifecycle deletion can also delete data files that the current table references, which could break the table.

exam-dea-c01-65.prompt: About 30 nightly AWS Glue ETL jobs at a fintech data team occasionally fail or exceed their timeouts. When a failure or timeout occurs, a notification must be sent to an Amazon SNS topic connected to the operations channel without changing the job code. The company wants to avoid the operational burden of adding notification logic to each job. Currently, an owner checks the run history in the console by hand every morning, so automation is needed. Jobs will continue to be added, and the company does not want to create separate notification settings even when new jobs are created. The notification message must include the job name and the failure state, and the operations channel already subscribes to the SNS topic. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a try/except block at the end of each AWS Glue job script and modify the code to call SNS Publish when an exception is caught. All scripts would have to be fixed and redeployed, and SNS publish permission would also have to be added to each job role.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a metric filter that counts the ERROR string in each job's log group, and set up a CloudWatch alarm per job that fires when the value is 1 or greater.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In an Amazon EventBridge rule, match the FAILED and TIMEOUT states among Glue Job State Change events and specify the SNS topic as the target.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure an S3 event notification on the output S3 path so that a notification is sent if no new object is created by a specified time.

exam-dea-c01-65.explanation: An EventBridge rule on Glue Job State Change is the correct answer. AWS Glue sends job state change events to EventBridge for SUCCEEDED, FAILED, TIMEOUT, and STOPPED, so matching the two states and sending them to SNS lets one rule monitor 30-plus jobs without changing job code. Exception handling inside scripts requires fixing all the code and does not run when a job is forcibly terminated due to a timeout. Log metric filters must be configured per job and cannot reliably catch TIMEOUT through log strings. S3 events occur only when an object is created, so they cannot detect that an object was not created.

exam-dop-c02-1.prompt: A fintech company has an Amazon S3 bucket in Account A (the data account) that contains about 300 million settlement report objects. All objects are encrypted with SSE-KMS by using a customer managed AWS KMS key in Account A. A Lambda function in partner settlement Account B, which belongs to a separate organization, must read reports from this bucket every day before dawn. The company recently updated the bucket policy to allow s3:GetObject for the Account B execution role. However, the Lambda invocation fails with AccessDenied because of a KMS permissions error. The two accounts are not in the same AWS Organizations organization, so the issue cannot be resolved with organization-level policies. The data team (3 people) does not have the capacity for a large-scale effort to re-encrypt existing objects or rotate the key. During an external audit, the company must prove that this one role in Account B is the only external principal that can use the key, and the work must be completed this week. The partner manages the Account B Lambda code, so the code cannot be modified. The security team in Account A tracks key policy changes with AWS CloudTrail and reviews access permissions every quarter. The work must be finished before the next settlement deadline, and the only contact on the Account B side is one person on the partner's operations team. Which solution resolves the issue in the SAFEST way while maintaining the principle of least privilege?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Broaden the bucket policy to allow s3:* and change the Principal to the Account B root user so that the encryption error is bypassed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Re-encrypt the objects with the AWS managed key (aws/s3) and add Account B to that key's policy so that both accounts share the same key.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the Principal in the key policy to * so that every AWS account can call kms:Decrypt, with no additional conditions or restrictions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the Account A key policy, allow kms:Decrypt for the specified role in Account B. Also allow kms:Decrypt on that key ARN in the IAM policy of the Account B role.

exam-dop-c02-1.explanation: Allowing the action in both the key policy and the IAM policy is the correct answer. Cross-account use of a KMS key works only when the key policy in the account that owns the key allows the external account or role and the IAM policy in the external account delegates that permission. Either one alone is not enough. Broadening the bucket policy does not resolve the KMS permissions error and only makes the permissions excessive. An AWS managed key has a key policy that cannot be modified, so it cannot be shared with another account. Setting the key policy Principal to * opens decryption permission to every account, which directly violates the principle of least privilege. The constraint that re-encrypting 300 million objects is impractical supports the correct approach, which keeps the existing key, and counts against the option that requires re-encryption. The condition that the partner's code cannot be modified and the audit condition that key usage must be narrowed to a single role are satisfied by only the correct answer.

exam-dop-c02-2.prompt: The platform team at a healthcare information company uses AWS CloudFormation to deploy the same Amazon S3 bucket stack template to 12 accounts. The template does not define the BucketEncryption property at all and leaves default encryption to the service default. One day, an operator used the console to change the default encryption of one bucket to a different KMS key, but the stack drift detection that runs every morning on an Amazon EventBridge schedule reported IN_SYNC. This stack is part of a regulated system, so any arbitrary change in the console that differs from the stack definition becomes an audit finding. The security team wants manual changes like this to be detected as drift too, and wants to keep the stack structure and deployment pipeline as unchanged as possible and minimize changes. There is no dedicated automation staff, and the current detection schedule and notification setup already work correctly. The stack is deployed on its own with no parent stack, the bucket policy and lifecycle rules are defined in the same template, and template changes can follow the existing process that includes code review. The security team receives the drift results in a report every morning and does not want to change this reporting cadence. Which action is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the scheduled job so that drift detection runs at the nested stack level instead of on the parent stack, so that the bucket resource in the nested stack is also included in the scan.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove the bucket from the stack and then import it again with an import operation. The entire actual configuration is then stored as the baseline, and changes to any property are detected as drift afterward.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Explicitly define BucketEncryption with the desired value in the template, update the stack, and then run drift detection. The property is tracked only if it is stated explicitly, even when the value is the same as the default.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Instead of drift detection, create a recurring deployment schedule that runs a stack update with the same template every day so that manually changed properties are overwritten based on the template.

exam-dop-c02-2.explanation: The correct answer is to explicitly define the BucketEncryption property in the template. CloudFormation evaluates drift only for property values that are explicitly specified in the template or parameters, and it does not track properties that are not defined or that rely on defaults. Therefore the property must be stated explicitly, even when the value is the same as the default, for a manual change to be reported as drift. Running detection at the nested stack level only compensates for the fact that a parent stack does not scan its nested stacks. This bucket is not in a nested stack, so that is unrelated to the cause. Importing is also based on the properties defined in the template, so properties that are not defined still go untracked. Redeploying the same template does not change properties that are not in the template, so the manual change is not overwritten. The background that the detection schedule and notifications already work confirms that the cause is not the detection method but the missing property in the template. Because the stack is not nested, the option that changes the detection unit is unrelated to the cause.

exam-dop-c02-3.prompt: An online restaurant reservation service runs on an Amazon ECS service across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. From midnight to 6 AM there is almost no traffic, so alarms based on ALB request metrics often go into INSUFFICIENT_DATA. Recently, after a front-end deployment, an incident occurred in which the seat selection screen returned a blank page with HTTP 200, and the company learned about it only after customer inquiries came in. The three-step screen flow of login, seat selection, and payment confirmation is linked by a session cookie issued after login, and the check must also confirm that a reservation number is displayed on the last screen. When the flow breaks, it must be detected at 1-minute intervals before customers notice, and an alert must reach the on-call engineer within 3 minutes of the failure. The check script must run from outside without modifying production code. A separate test account is used for the checks, so no real payments occur, and notifications are already connected through Amazon SNS to the on-call engineer's paging app. The operations team has 3 people, and a development slot to update the check script is scheduled once per quarter. Which solution BEST meets these requirements without depending on user traffic?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lower the threshold of the ALB HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count alarm to 1 and configure the alarm to treat missing data as breaching.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run a CloudWatch Synthetics canary that executes the three-step browser workflow at 1-minute intervals, and create an alarm on the SuccessPercent metric.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use a Route 53 health check with string matching on the payment confirmation URL's response, and receive the health check failure alarm through Amazon SNS.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a metric filter for ERROR in the application logs, set an alarm to trigger when the 5-minute sum is 1 or greater, and increase log retention.

exam-dop-c02-3.explanation: A Synthetics canary is the correct answer. A canary runs a script on a schedule along the same path as a real customer, supports an interval as short as 1 minute, and emits result metrics even when there is no traffic, so it detects a break at any step of the flow first. A 5xx metric alarm cannot catch cases where the flow breaks with a 200 response, and treating missing data as breaching causes repeated false positives during low-traffic hours. A Route 53 health check is a single-request check, so it cannot verify a multi-step flow from login to payment confirmation. A log-based filter produces no logs when there is no traffic, so there is no detection signal at all. The conditions that the incident was a screen that broke with a 200 response and that the flow has three steps linked by a session cookie eliminate the single-URL check and the options based on error metrics. The condition of a multi-step flow linked by a session cookie eliminates the single-URL check and the error-metric-based alarm.

exam-dop-c02-4.prompt: The infrastructure team at a SaaS company deploys the same AWS CloudFormation template to three environments: development, staging, and production. The AWS::EC2::Volume resource in the template is the data volume, and the operations team plans an update that changes the AvailabilityZone property to move the volume to a different Availability Zone. Changing this property causes the resource to be replaced. This change was initiated because last quarter, data was lost by mistake during a stack update and deletion. The data on the replaced old volume must be recoverable even after the update succeeds, and the volume data must also remain when the stack is deleted later. Keeping the old volume as is not an acceptable cost, and only snapshot storage costs are acceptable. The solution must be achieved with the template alone, without manual procedures by operators. The template also defines an EC2 instance and a security group in addition to the data volume. The audit team verifies that the old data can be restored within 30 days after the replacement, and the operations team already has a process of previewing the impact with change sets. The stack is in the Seoul Region, the volume size is 500 GiB, and the change is scheduled for the early-morning maintenance window next Tuesday. Which template change is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Have an operator manually create a volume snapshot immediately before the update, leave the template unchanged, and run the update. Create a manual snapshot in the same way before deleting the stack.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Specify both UpdateReplacePolicy: Snapshot and DeletionPolicy: Snapshot on the volume resource.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Specify DeletionPolicy: Retain and UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain on the volume resource so that the old volume remains intact after it is replaced or deleted.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Specify only DeletionPolicy: Snapshot on the volume resource so that the deletion policy is applied when a replacement occurs and a snapshot of the old volume is created.

exam-dop-c02-4.explanation: The correct answer is to specify both UpdateReplacePolicy and DeletionPolicy as Snapshot. UpdateReplacePolicy determines what happens to the old resource when a property change causes it to be replaced, while DeletionPolicy applies only when the stack or the resource definition is deleted and does not apply to replacement. EC2 volumes support snapshots, so specifying Snapshot for both leaves only a snapshot in both replacement and deletion. Specifying only the deletion policy causes the old volume to be deleted by default during replacement, which violates the requirement. Retain keeps the entire old volume, which continues to be billed and violates the cost constraint that only snapshots are allowed. A manual snapshot violates the constraint that the solution must be achieved with the template alone. The cost constraint that allows only snapshot storage eliminates Retain, and the constraint that the solution must use the template alone eliminates the manual snapshot.

exam-dop-c02-5.prompt: The real-time battle servers of a mobile game company communicate over UDP and run as Amazon ECS Fargate services behind Network Load Balancers in the Seoul and Tokyo Regions. Peak concurrent users are about 200,000. Some older clients hardcode the server IP in the app or cache DNS responses for a long time, so with Route 53 failover, switching during a Regional failure is delayed by several minutes or more. The solution must keep static IP addresses without changing the clients and must automatically switch to the other Region when one Region has no healthy endpoints. Connection latency to the battle servers is important, so users must be connected to the nearest healthy Region, and app store update review takes 2 weeks, so changing the clients is difficult. The operations staff is also small, and the company does not want to operate its own fleet of proxy servers. The game servers communicate on UDP port 7777, normally 70% of connections go to Seoul and 30% to Tokyo, and the development team has no capacity to change server and client code in this quarter's season update. The backend in both Seoul and Tokyo consists of 40 ECS Fargate tasks, and the configuration in the two Regions is identical. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Assign an Elastic IP address to the Seoul NLB and have clients use this IP address. If a failure occurs, an operator runs a script to reassociate the Elastic IP address with the NLB in the Tokyo Region.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator, register the NLBs in both Regions as endpoint groups, and have clients use the accelerator's static anycast IP addresses.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution, configure the NLBs in both Regions as an origin group, and set up origin failover so that requests are passed to the secondary origin if the primary origin fails.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lower the TTL of the Route 53 failover records to 5 seconds and attach health checks to the NLBs in both Regions so that Route 53 responds with the Tokyo NLB if the Seoul health check fails.

exam-dop-c02-5.explanation: The correct answer is a Global Accelerator standard accelerator. An accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses and automatically routes traffic to healthy endpoints based on endpoint health. It does not depend on DNS caching, so there is no issue with clients that ignore TTL, and it supports both TCP and UDP. Lowering the Route 53 TTL does not solve the problems of clients that do not honor TTL and hardcoded IP addresses. CloudFront is an HTTP-based content delivery service and cannot handle UDP traffic. An Elastic IP address can be used only within a single Region and cannot be moved to and associated with a resource in another Region. The conditions that the clients cannot be changed and that UDP is required eliminate CloudFront and the DNS-based options.

exam-dop-c02-6.prompt: An e-commerce company wants to replace 30 instances in an Auto Scaling group with a new AMI that has security patches applied. On weekday afternoons traffic is high, so service capacity must stay at 90% or more at all times, even during the replacement. The replacement must pause when 20% of the instances have been replaced and again when 50% have been replaced, so that the team can check metrics at each point. If an ALB 5xx alarm fires, the replacement must be stopped and rolled back to the previous configuration without human intervention. Version 2 of the launch template, which uses the new AMI, is ready, and the launch template $Latest version is frequently modified by another team. The on-call responder is not on standby at night, so the rollback decision must be made by the alarm alone, and user requests must continue to be processed during the replacement. All instances to be replaced belong to the same ALB target group and take about 3 minutes to warm up, and the deadline for deploying the security patch is this Friday. In the last manual replacement, some instances remained in service in an unhealthy state and caused an outage. An operations policy has been agreed that for the first 24 hours after deployment, the rollback decision is made by a single alarm only. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Start an instance refresh with a desired configuration that specifies the launch template at the fixed version number 2, and set a minimum healthy percentage of 90%, checkpoints at 20% and 50%, the 5xx alarm, and automatic rollback.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Without using an instance refresh, change the Auto Scaling group termination policy to OldestLaunchTemplate, and increase and then decrease the desired capacity so that instances from the old template are terminated first.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Start an instance refresh with the launch template version set to $Latest, set a minimum healthy percentage of 90% and checkpoints at 20% and 50%, and specify the 5xx alarm with automatic rollback enabled.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Start an instance refresh with a minimum healthy percentage of 90% but without checkpoints, and have a person check metrics; if there is a problem, cancel the refresh and start a new instance refresh again with the previous AMI.

exam-dop-c02-6.explanation: The correct answer is to start an instance refresh with a desired configuration that specifies a fixed launch template version number, and to set up checkpoints and alarm-based automatic rollback. A minimum healthy percentage of 90% satisfies the capacity requirement, checkpoints pause at the 20% and 50% points to give a chance to validate, and when the alarm goes into ALARM, automatic rollback returns to the previous configuration. Rollback is available only when the refresh is started with a desired configuration specified, and it cannot be used with the $Latest or $Default version. A method that cancels manually without checkpoints requires human intervention and violates the requirement. Adjusting the termination policy has no stage-pause or rollback capability. The condition that another team frequently modifies $Latest means a fixed version number must be specified, and the condition that no one is on standby at night eliminates the manual cancellation approach.

exam-dop-c02-7.prompt: The platform team pipeline at a retail group publishes the approved golden AMI ID every week to the AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter /golden/al2023/ami in four Regions: Seoul, Tokyo, N. Virginia, and Ireland. The AWS CloudFormation templates of 12 development teams use hardcoded AMI IDs and per-Region Mappings, so the templates are edited every week. The company wants to make the templates Region-independent and have each stack update use the latest approved AMI. The AMI is published once a week and each team has a different stack update schedule, so there must be no procedure in which the template-owning teams check the AMI ID themselves. The platform team does not want to operate additional Lambda code or a new separate stack. The AMI publishing pipeline is owned by the platform team, and it has been agreed that the parameter name will not change. The CloudFormation execution role of each team already has the ssm:GetParameters permission, and the parameter is published in each Region in the same account. Each team updates its stack on its own schedule, so one team's update must not affect another team's stack. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Build a pipeline that redeploys a template with updated Mappings AMI IDs to each Region every week by using StackSets, automating the template modification and deployment whenever the parameter changes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deploy a separate stack in each Region that exports the AMI ID as a stack output, and modify every team's templates to reference this value with Fn::ImportValue.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add a Lambda-backed custom resource to the template that uses DescribeImages to look up the latest AMI with the approved tag and passes that ID as the ImageId of the launch template.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Declare the template parameter type as AWS::SSM::Parameter::Value<AWS::EC2::Image::Id> and set the default value to /golden/al2023/ami so that the parameter value in that Region is resolved when the stack is created and updated.

exam-dop-c02-7.explanation: The correct answer is to use a template parameter of the SSM parameter type. The AWS::SSM::Parameter::Value<AWS::EC2::Image::Id> type retrieves the latest value from Parameter Store in that Region when the stack is created or updated, so Mappings are not needed and the template is Region-independent. Looking up the AMI with a custom resource requires maintaining Lambda code and implementing the tag rules yourself. Redeploying Mappings with StackSets requires automating template modification and still leaves per-Region values in the template. The export and import stacks require operating a separate stack in each Region and modifying every template, which is a large change. The conditions that there must be no procedure where teams check the AMI ID themselves and that no additional Lambda or stack is operated eliminate the custom resource and the export approach.

exam-dop-c02-8.prompt: The platform team at a game company wants to delegate to a development organization of 200 developers the permission to create IAM roles for CI/CD directly. Roles created by the development teams must not be able to have permissions beyond the scope of Amazon S3, Amazon DynamoDB, and AWS Lambda, and the development teams must not be able to remove or modify the boundary policy. Dozens of roles are created per day, the security team has no staff to review individual roles, and only the security team must be able to change the boundary policy. Previously, roles were created through security team tickets, but this took two days on average and delayed deployments. The security team has already written a boundary policy that allows only common actions of S3, DynamoDB, and Lambda, and development team roles follow a convention of using the cicd- prefix. During audits, the company must be able to prove at once that a boundary is attached to any given role. This delegation applies only to the development account, and the security team keeps the permission to create roles in the production account as it does today. The development teams' CI/CD pipelines use AWS CodeBuild and Lambda deployments. The solution must operate as self-service without central approval. Which solution meets these requirements in the SAFEST way?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Grant the development teams AdministratorAccess, review the IAM Access Analyzer findings once a month, and find and delete roles with excessive permissions after the fact.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Receive all role creation requests as security team tickets, have the security team create the roles directly, and do not grant the development teams iam:* permissions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only set an IAM condition that requires the prefix in development team role names, and allow any managed policy to be attached as long as the prefix matches.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Allow CreateRole and policy attachment only when the specified boundary policy is attached by using the iam:PermissionsBoundary condition, and deny removal and modification of the boundary.

exam-dop-c02-8.explanation: A delegation policy that enforces the permissions boundary condition is the correct answer. If role creation and policy attachment are allowed only when the specified boundary policy is attached through the iam:PermissionsBoundary condition, the effective permissions of a new role are always the intersection with the boundary, and denying the action that removes the boundary and the modification of the boundary policy closes the bypass. Granting administrator permissions and reviewing afterward is unsafe because excessive permissions exist in the meantime. Having the security team create roles directly conflicts with the self-service requirement without central approval. A prefix condition cannot limit the scope of permissions, so permissions beyond the boundary can be granted. Because a prefix cannot limit the scope of permissions, only the approach that enforces the boundary condition satisfies both the audit proof and self-service.

exam-dop-c02-9.prompt: The development team at a media company wants to run unit tests every time a pull request in a GitHub repository is opened or updated and show the result as a status check on the PR. The scope is limited to PRs that target the main branch, and to reduce build costs the tests must run only when files under src/ change. The repository has an average of 30 PRs opened per day, and many PRs modify only documentation, so running a full build on every PR would waste a lot of build time. The company already uses AWS and has no staff to operate its own CI server. The team has 5 people and is considering moving to GitHub Actions next quarter, but this requirement must be handled right away. A Linux container is enough for the build environment, and the tests take 4 minutes on average. The repository is already connected to AWS through AWS CodeConnections, the branch protection rule requires passing status checks as a merge condition, and the company wants to avoid always-on infrastructure that incurs cost even when it is not in use. The development team has already agreed on the rule to skip builds for PRs that change only documentation, and a single src/ path rule is enough given the repository structure. Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Install Jenkins on Amazon EC2 to receive GitHub webhooks, configure a path filter plugin so that only changes under src/ are built, and publish build results to GitHub status checks with a plugin. The platform team manages patching and backups of the Jenkins server.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an AWS CodePipeline that runs on every push, runs the tests in CodeBuild after the source stage, and has an approver manually check the results in an approval stage before allowing the merge.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use an Amazon EventBridge rule to run CodeBuild once a day to test all open PR branches in sequence, and email the results so that a person checks them.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a GitHub webhook on the CodeBuild project and specify a filter group for the PULL_REQUEST_CREATED and PULL_REQUEST_UPDATED events with BASE_REF set to main and FILE_PATH set to src/, and have the build status reported to the PR.

exam-dop-c02-9.explanation: The correct answer is to use a CodeBuild GitHub webhook filter group. When BASE_REF and FILE_PATH filters are applied together to the PR creation and update events, a build starts only for PRs that target main and change src/. There is no server, cost is incurred only for the build time, and the status is reported to the PR. Jenkins violates the condition that the company has no staff to operate a CI server on its own. Running a pipeline on every push without path and branch conditions increases unnecessary builds and also requires manual checks. A once-a-day batch test does not meet the requirement to check every time a PR is opened or updated. The condition of avoiding always-on infrastructure eliminates Jenkins, and the requirement for per-PR status checks eliminates the nightly batch build.

exam-dop-c02-10.prompt: The AWS Organizations organization of a logistics company consists of a management account and 80 member accounts. All member accounts are under the Workloads OU, and a few new accounts are created every month. The company wants the organization to use only the Seoul and N. Virginia Regions. Creating resources in other Regions must be blocked in all member accounts except the management account (including the root user), while calls to global services such as IAM, Route 53, and CloudFront must continue to work. It must also apply automatically to newly created accounts. Account administrators can modify the IAM policies in their own accounts, regulations prohibit data from being stored in unapproved Regions, and only the central security team must make changes. Currently no SCPs are attached other than FullAWSAccess, and the security team has exclusive permission to change SCPs in the management account. A previous audit found that a developer created a test database in an unapproved Region, and it was confirmed that no service is running outside the allowed Regions. Several teams in the organization already use global services such as CloudFront and IAM that are called only in specific Regions. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deploy an IAM policy that denies actions in Regions other than the two Regions to all member accounts by using StackSets, and have it attached to the users and roles in each account.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attach to the Workloads OU an SCP that denies actions when aws:RequestedRegion is not an allowed Region, and use NotAction to exempt global service actions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Attach a Region restriction policy as a permissions boundary to the IAM roles and users in each account, and check that the boundary is attached whenever a new role is created.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Detect resources created outside the allowed Regions with an AWS Config rule and configure an automatic remediation action to delete those resources.

exam-dop-c02-10.explanation: A Region-deny SCP attached to the OU is the correct answer. An SCP is a ceiling that applies to all IAM principals in member accounts, including the root user, and when it is attached to an OU, new accounts inherit it automatically; the NotAction exception allows global services to continue to be used. An IAM policy deployed to accounts can be modified or detached by account administrators and does not apply to the root user. A permissions boundary must be attached to each role and user and has no effect on the root user, so gaps remain possible. Config remediation is a reactive response that deletes the resource after it has already been created, so it does not prevent creation itself. The condition that account administrators can change the IAM policies in their own accounts eliminates the IAM policy deployment approach.

exam-dop-c02-11.prompt: An insurance company operates 40 development accounts under an OU managed by AWS Control Tower. In these accounts, developers repeatedly deploy unencrypted Amazon EBS volumes or Amazon S3 buckets that allow public read through AWS CloudFormation every quarter, which has led to audit findings. The security team wants to evaluate such resources at the stack operation stage before they are provisioned and fail the deployment if there is a violation. Approaches that detect or fix already-created resources after the fact are not acceptable, and the solution must be applied at the OU level without per-account configuration. Developers use the console in addition to CloudFormation, but this requirement is limited to CloudFormation deployments. Each development team has a different CI pipeline, so the security team cannot require each team to add a check stage, and the security team wants to manage rule changes in one place. There are two rules to enforce: required EBS encryption and a ban on S3 public read. The security team wants to check the control enablement history in the Control Tower console. It is enough for the evaluation result to be delivered immediately to developers as a deployment failure message. By regulation, changes to control enablement are approved by the security team, and the development teams do not have permission to disable controls. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a cfn-guard check stage to the CI pipelines of all development teams so that the pipeline fails if the template violates the rules, and have each team pull the rules file from a shared repository on its own.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable a detective control on the OU so that when an AWS Config rule finds a noncompliant resource, the finding is sent through Amazon EventBridge, and have the responsible person check the resource and delete it or encrypt it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turn on an AWS Config automatic remediation rule in each account of the OU so that when an unencrypted volume or a public bucket is found, AWS Systems Manager Automation replaces it with an encrypted volume and a private setting.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable an AWS Control Tower proactive control on the OU. Based on CloudFormation Hooks, it evaluates the resource configuration when a stack is created or updated and blocks the deployment if it is noncompliant.

exam-dop-c02-11.explanation: The correct answer is a proactive control. Control Tower proactive controls are implemented with CloudFormation Hooks, so they evaluate the configuration before resources are created or changed by a stack operation, and when enabled on an OU they apply to all accounts in that OU. Detective controls find already-created resources after the fact through Config rules, which violates the requirement for pre-provisioning evaluation. Automatic remediation rules are also a reactive action that fixes resources after they are created. A cfn-guard check in CI verifies only deployments that go through the pipeline and requires per-team setup, so it does not meet the requirement for OU-wide uniform application. The condition that each team has a different pipeline and a check stage cannot be enforced eliminates the cfn-guard approach.

exam-dop-c02-12.prompt: A manufacturing group wants to view the metrics and log groups of 40 source accounts in its organization from a central monitoring account without switching accounts. The source accounts span 3 OUs, and a few new accounts are added to the OUs every month, and the new accounts should be included automatically. The company will not build a pipeline that replicates the data separately (because of replication cost and latency), and the operations team wants to view metrics, log groups, and AWS X-Ray traces in a single console. Source account administrators must not be given access to the monitoring account, and source accounts may choose which data types to share only within the scope set by the monitoring account. The workloads in both the monitoring account and the source accounts are in the Seoul Region, and source account administrators continue to manage the metrics and log groups of their own accounts directly. The operations team in the monitoring account must not be able to modify resources in the source accounts. The operations team wants additional cost to be minimal and wants the newly created resources to be limited to one in the monitoring account and one per source account. The retention period of the log groups that the operations team views follows the source account's setting as is. Which TWO configurations meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Each source account creates a link within the range of types allowed by the monitoring account, and uses a CloudFormation template for OU-level deployment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create one sink in each source account, and have the monitoring account create a link to each sink to pull the data.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a subscription filter for each log group in each source account that sends logs to a log group in the monitoring account, and replicate metrics by using Metric Streams to collect them.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a sink in the monitoring account and use the sink policy to allow accounts in the organization or in the target OUs to create links.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Even if a source account chooses to share trace types that the monitoring account did not allow, only the allowed types are shared and link creation succeeds.

exam-dop-c02-12.explanation: The correct answers are the sink and sink policy in the monitoring account, and the link that each source account creates within the allowed scope. The sink is the connection point in the monitoring account and the link is managed by the source account; using Organizations and a CloudFormation template means new accounts are onboarded automatically. Subscription filters and Metric Streams are separate pipelines that replicate data, which conflicts with the requirements. If a source account selects more types than the monitoring account allows, link creation fails and nothing is shared. A sink is a resource placed once per Region in the monitoring account and is not created in each source account. The condition that no data replication pipeline is built eliminates the subscription filter approach, and the condition that the source account decides the scope of sharing eliminates E.

exam-dop-c02-13.prompt: A central operations team at an online education company wants to receive AWS Health scheduled events (such as EC2 instance retirement) occurring across all 60 accounts in its organization as a single feed, and respond with Amazon SNS notifications and AWS Systems Manager Automation. The organization has all features enabled and uses a Business or higher Support plan. Currently each account owner receives notifications by email and often misses them, and last month an instance scheduled for retirement was stopped as is. The response staff can access only the operations account, this operations account can be designated as the AWS Health delegated administrator, and when a retirement schedule is announced, the instance must be replaced within 7 days. The target events focus on EC2 instance retirement notifications, and the notifications are delivered through an SNS topic to the operations team's chat channel. The Automation runbook in the operations account already implements the instance replacement procedure, and events must arrive for accounts added to the organization later without separate configuration. The operations team has 5 people and must be able to check the handling records per account in case handling of retirement notifications is delayed. Which TWO configurations meet these requirements without creating rules in each account and without operating custom-built polling code? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Receive AWS Trusted Advisor check results as a weekly report and have the responsible person manually check whether any instances are scheduled for retirement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have a Lambda function in the central account assume a role in each account, query the Health API for new events every minute, and publish the results to Amazon SNS.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enable AWS Health organizational view in the management account and, if needed, designate a delegated administrator account.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use StackSets to deploy to all 60 accounts a rule that matches aws.health events and a cross-account event bus target so that all rules forward to the event bus in the operations account.

choices.label: E
choices.text: In the management account or the delegated administrator account, create a rule that matches aws.health events and set Amazon SNS and Automation as targets.

exam-dop-c02-13.explanation: The correct answers are enabling the Health organizational view and an EventBridge rule in the management account or the delegated administrator account. When the organizational view is turned on, the management account or the delegated administrator account receives the Health events of the entire organization as a single feed, so you only need to place one rule there and connect it to Amazon SNS and SSM Automation. Deploying rules and delivery targets to each account creates configuration in 60 places even though a single feed exists, which conflicts with the requirements. Assuming a role in each account and a 1-minute polling Lambda function involve custom-built code and invocation cost. A weekly Trusted Advisor report requires a person to check it and cannot automatically handle scheduled events immediately. The condition that events must arrive for new accounts without configuration eliminates deploying rules to each account.

exam-dop-c02-14.prompt: An advertising platform needs to receive an alarm when the memory utilization of a JVM application running in an Auto Scaling group (up to 60 instances) exceeds 80%. Instances are replaced dozens of times a day because of scale-in and scale-out, so per-instance alarms are hard to maintain, and the team wants to view the group average as a single metric. The default EC2 metrics do not include memory utilization. A memory threshold breach must be detected within 5 minutes, and the alarm configuration must be managed as code (IaC). The team already deploys the CloudWatch agent configuration through Systems Manager in the launch template, so changing the agent configuration is not a burden. The CloudWatch agent starts automatically at boot through the launch template user data, and metrics are collected at 60-second intervals in the CWAgent namespace. The metric used for the alarm must be aggregated by the group name dimension rather than by instance ID. The alarm should fire when the group's average memory stays above 80% for 5 minutes or more, and individual instance notifications are not needed. Which configuration BEST meets these requirements while minimizing the number of alarms and management tasks?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Collect mem_used_percent with the agent, create a group-level metric by using AutoScalingGroupName dimension aggregation (aggregation_dimensions), and create the alarm on it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an alarm that aggregates the default EC2 metric MemoryUtilization at the Auto Scaling group level, and automatically update the alarm targets when instances are replaced.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have each instance send the result of the free command to PutMetricData with cron, and have a Lambda function create and delete alarms per instance ID.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Turn on Auto Scaling group metrics collection and create an alarm on a group metric such as GroupInServiceInstances as a proxy for memory utilization.

exam-dop-c02-14.explanation: Memory collection by the agent and a group-level aggregation dimension is the correct answer. If the agent collects mem_used_percent and aggregates it with the AutoScalingGroupName dimension, one alarm on a single group metric is enough even when instances change. The default EC2 metrics do not include memory, so an approach that uses a default metric called MemoryUtilization does not work. Adding a Lambda function that creates alarms to a cron and PutMetricData script introduces custom-built code and lifecycle management of per-instance alarms, which is a heavy burden. Group metrics are instance counts and capacity information and are unrelated to memory utilization. The condition that instances are replaced dozens of times a day eliminates the per-instance alarm configuration.

exam-dop-c02-15.prompt: The automated account security remediation at a fintech company works by having an Amazon EventBridge rule deliver events to a Lambda function that fixes violating resources. Sometimes this Lambda function fails to receive events because of temporary throttling and permission errors that occur during deployments. If such an event is lost, remediation is missed, and missed remediation becomes an audit finding, so the company wants to store failed events and reprocess them after the cause is resolved. The existing rule structure and Lambda code must not be changed, and additional development must be minimal. Events occur only in the Region where the rule is located, and there must be no loss during the retention period. The affected Lambda function identifies remediation targets by tags and is written to be idempotent, so reprocessing the same event has no side effects. The default retry settings of the rule target are kept as they are. This rule processes several thousand events per day on average, and one event corresponds to exactly one violating resource. The company wants to confirm that no events were lost by checking the number of messages that accumulate in the queue. Which of the options available in the rule target settings is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Specify an Amazon SQS standard queue in the same Region as the target dead-letter queue (DLQ) and attach a queue policy that allows EventBridge to call SendMessage.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Specify an Amazon SQS FIFO queue as the DLQ of the rule target to guarantee the order of failed events, and reprocess the messages accumulated in the queue with Lambda.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Specify an Amazon SQS standard queue that was already created in a different Region as the DLQ, extending to a multi-Region configuration so that failed events are stored even during a Regional failure.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only set an alarm on the FailedInvocations metric of the rule target and, when the alarm fires, have the responsible person manually recreate and resend the event.

exam-dop-c02-15.explanation: Specifying an SQS standard queue in the same Region as the DLQ is the correct configuration. Errors that cannot be resolved by retrying, such as permission errors, go to the DLQ right away without retries, and later reprocessing the queue messages after fixing the cause means no event is lost; the queue policy must allow EventBridge to call SendMessage. EventBridge DLQs support only standard queues, so a FIFO queue cannot be specified. The DLQ queue must be in the same Region as the rule, so a queue in another Region cannot be used. A metric alarm only tells you about the failure and does not store the event itself, so there is no data to reprocess. The alarm-only approach cannot store the events and therefore does not satisfy the requirement to prevent loss.

exam-dop-c02-16.prompt: A healthcare SaaS company pushes container images to Amazon ECR and runs them on Amazon ECS for months at a time. There were no problems at push time, but a CVE disclosed afterward can introduce new CRITICAL vulnerabilities in already deployed images. The company wants to detect such cases without a separate rescan job and send a notification to the security team's SNS topic whenever an active CRITICAL finding appears. The ECR repository holds hundreds of images, and the deployment pipeline is owned by another team and cannot be modified. When a new CVE is disclosed, the company needs to know which images are affected as soon as possible. The security team has 3 people and does not have the capacity to build and maintain a scan schedule on its own. The ECS services are spread across 5 accounts, but the images are stored in a central registry in the Seoul Region. The security team wants to receive only CRITICAL vulnerabilities as immediate notifications and review the rest on a dashboard. Dozens of new production images are pushed per month on average, and old images also remain in service for long periods. The notification must include the image name, tag, and vulnerability ID so that the responder can act right away. Which solution has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Turn on scan on push with ECR basic scanning, and create a schedule in which a Lambda function calls StartImageScan for all images in the repository every day.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turn on Amazon Inspector continuous scanning for ECR, and send CRITICAL, ACTIVE Inspector2 finding events to Amazon SNS with an EventBridge rule.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turn on Amazon GuardDuty and receive runtime threat detection findings as notifications to stand in for detecting newly introduced vulnerabilities in images.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a vulnerability scanner to the AWS CodeBuild image build stage and, if the build-time result is clean, do not scan again afterward.

exam-dop-c02-16.explanation: Inspector continuous scanning with an event rule is the correct answer. Continuous scanning rescans images not only when a new image is pushed but also when a related CVE is added to the Inspector database, and new findings and status changes are emitted to EventBridge, so you only need to connect the CRITICAL, ACTIVE condition to SNS. Basic scanning runs at push time or as a manual scan, so you would have to build and maintain a daily rescan Lambda function yourself.
