choices.text: Switch to Pipe mode to stream the S3 data through a FIFO pipe, and modify the training code so that only one process reads each pipe.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Move the S3 objects to the Standard-IA storage class to lower storage costs, set a lifecycle rule to transition them automatically, and keep running the training jobs in File mode as they are now.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Specify a larger EBS volume for the training instances and use File mode so that the entire data is downloaded again every time the job starts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mount an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system linked to the S3 bucket on the training job and read the same data with high throughput and low latency.

exam-mla-c01-31.explanation: The correct answer is mounting FSx for Lustre linked to the S3 bucket. FSx for Lustre provides high-throughput, low-latency file access, lazy-loads S3 data so that the same data is read quickly across repeated runs, and mounting finishes quickly regardless of data size. Attaching to a VPC was stated as acceptable. A: Pipe mode must stream from S3 again each time and has the single-process read restriction. B: Standard-IA only reduces storage cost and does not increase throughput. C: Even with a larger volume, the time to download everything again on every run remains.

exam-mla-c01-32.prompt: A recommendation team's model is retrained automatically once a week, and there are only 2 data engineers, so it is hard to operate new infrastructure directly. The feature group in SageMaker Feature Store has both the online store and the offline store enabled. For this retraining, a training dataset must be built in one pass from the last 3 years of history (hundreds of millions of rows), and the past feature values as of the time each training example was created are required. Each training example has an event time recorded, so only feature values from before that time may be used, the query results are stored in Amazon S3 as training input, and records are already accumulating in the offline store. Which method has the LEAST operational overhead and is suitable for large-scale historical queries?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Query the offline store, which accumulates as Parquet in Amazon S3, with Amazon Athena queries to build the training dataset.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Repeatedly call GetRecord against the online store for each record identifier to gather the history, save it as CSV, and use it as training input.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an extraction job that periodically scans the entire online store to reconstruct past values by date and load them into Amazon S3 for use.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Export the ingestion logs of the feature group to Amazon CloudWatch Logs and extract feature values by point in time with Logs Insights queries to build the dataset.

exam-mla-c01-32.explanation: The correct answer is to query the offline store with Amazon Athena. The offline store keeps point-in-time history as Parquet in Amazon S3 and registers it in the catalog, so it suits large-scale historical queries and needs no separate infrastructure. B: The online store reads the latest value per identifier with low latency, so repeated GetRecord calls do not yield past values. C: Scanning the online store also does not reconstruct history and requires operating the extraction job yourself. D: Exporting logs is not meant to store feature values, so it cannot guarantee an accurate history.

exam-mla-c01-33.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
exam-mla-c01-33.prompt: A recommendation service operates 24 hours a day with no maintenance window. The team deploys a new recommendation model v2 to the SageMaker real-time endpoint that is in operation. The team wants to first send only a portion of the traffic to the new fleet and watch it for 30 minutes before shifting the rest, and it must automatically roll back to the previous version if the latency CloudWatch alarm fires. The previous version's instances must be kept until validation is complete, and no one is on standby at night. The new model v2 uses the same input format and instance type as v1, requests must not be dropped even during deployment, and the latency CloudWatch alarm to be used for the rollback decision has already been created. Which method has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the blue/green deployment configuration of UpdateEndpoint, choose the method that shifts all traffic at once, and manually roll back to the previous version if a problem is seen.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the blue/green deployment configuration of UpdateEndpoint, specify canary traffic shifting, a 30-minute baking period, and automatic rollback based on the latency alarm.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add the new model variant to the same endpoint, have a person change the variant weights step by step while watching a dashboard, and roll back if an anomaly is seen.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a separate new endpoint, split traffic with Amazon Route 53 weighted records, and have the person in charge manually edit the record weights if the alarm fires.

exam-mla-c01-33.explanation: The correct answer is blue/green deployment with canary traffic shifting, a baking period, and automatic rollback specified. A canary sends a small amount of traffic to the new fleet first, monitors the specified CloudWatch alarm during the baking period, and automatically returns to the previous fleet if there is a problem, and the previous fleet is kept during baking. A: Shifting all at once affects all traffic if there is a problem and does not meet the automatic rollback requirement. C: A person must change the weights and monitor, which conflicts with the condition that no one is on standby at night. D: The DNS weighting method also requires the person in charge to edit it manually after an alarm, so the operational burden is high.

exam-mla-c01-34.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
exam-mla-c01-34.prompt: Multiple projects run SageMaker training jobs in the same AWS account, and currently all jobs of 5 projects share a single execution role with AdministratorAccess attached. The security team requires least privilege so that each project can access only its own Amazon S3 prefix and the services it needs, and wants the scope of permissions to be easy to explain during audits. Each project keeps data only under its own S3 prefix, and ML engineers create and run jobs directly. Some projects do not need to access other teams' S3 prefixes, the training containers use internal images in Amazon ECR and write logs to CloudWatch Logs, and users sign in with IAM Identity Center. Which method meets this without significantly increasing operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Attach AmazonSageMakerFullAccess to all project roles and allow S3 with wildcards to eliminate permission errors, and separate projects by a resource tagging rule and agreement among team members.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Leave the shared role as it is, and issue a long-term access key to each team member to be included in the training scripts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an execution role for each project that allows only the project's S3 prefix and the required ECR and CloudWatch Logs actions, trusts only SageMaker, and limit users' PassRole to the corresponding role.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pass the credentials of each team member's personal IAM user as environment variables to the training container and run training with personal permissions.

exam-mla-c01-34.explanation: The correct answer is a least-privilege execution role for each project. If each role allows only the required S3 prefix and service actions, the trust policy contains only sagemaker.amazonaws.com, and iam:PassRole is restricted so that users can pass only the corresponding role, access between projects is separated and the scope of permissions can be explained. A: FullAccess and wildcards violate least privilege. B: Putting long-term access keys in code carries a high risk of leakage and creates key management overhead. D: Passing personal credentials as environment variables makes auditing and separation of permissions difficult.

exam-mla-c01-35.prompt: In the training data for a credit card company's fraud detection model, the fraud rate is 0.3%. The current XGBoost model shows 99.7% accuracy but catches almost none of the actual fraudulent transactions, and the cost of missing fraud is much greater than the cost of wrongly blocking legitimate transactions. The data scientist cannot collect more labeled data, and the model algorithm must remain XGBoost. An improvement plan is due within this sprint. Transactions flagged as suspected fraud by the model are reviewed by staff, so some false positives are acceptable, but there is a daily review capacity limit, and the model architecture and data scale will remain unchanged. Which TWO approaches should be applied at the model development stage to improve this problem? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the evaluation metric from accuracy to precision and recall, F1 score, or PR-AUC to directly measure the performance on the minority class.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Correct the class imbalance by giving the minority class a larger weight (such as XGBoost's scale_pos_weight) or by oversampling.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remove all legitimate transactions from the validation data to raise the fraud ratio, and report that result as the final generalization performance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Treat the fraudulent transaction rows as noise, remove them from the training data, and retrain the model with only legitimate transactions.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Keep accuracy as the objective metric as it is and increase the number of epochs, aiming to raise accuracy to 99.9%.

exam-mla-c01-35.explanation: The correct answers are using metrics focused on the minority class and correcting the class imbalance. If fraud is 0.3%, accuracy is 99.7% even when everything is predicted as legitimate, so accuracy does not show the model's ability, and metrics such as precision, recall, F1, and PR-AUC directly reflect the minority class. Weighting the minority class or oversampling lets the model learn fraud patterns. C manipulates the validation data, so the reported performance differs from the real one. D: Removing the fraud rows removes the very thing that must be detected. E: Trying to raise accuracy further only masks the problem and does not improve fraud detection.

exam-mla-c01-36.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
exam-mla-c01-36.prompt: A team wants to validate a new candidate for a payment approval model with real production traffic. The response sent to users must always be the result of the existing model, and the team wants to compare the new model's latency and prediction distribution on the same requests. The model owner has a different schedule from the app team and cannot request an app deployment this quarter, so changing the client app to call twice must be avoided. The existing model is currently served on a SageMaker real-time endpoint. The new model is already registered in SageMaker with the same instance type, the comparison results will be accumulated and reviewed over one week, and the endpoint invocation volume is tens of requests per second, so the additional cost of shadow traffic is acceptable. Which solution is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create two production variants with weights of 90 and 10, and return the responses of the 10% received by the new model directly to users.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a separate endpoint for the new model, and have the client app call both the existing endpoint and the new endpoint and compare the results.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add a shadow variant to the same endpoint configuration so that a copy of the production traffic is sent to the new model and its responses are not returned to users.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run a Batch Transform job with a test set extracted from last month's production logs and compare only the offline prediction distribution of the new model.

exam-mla-c01-36.explanation: The correct answer is a shadow variant. A shadow variant sends a copy of the requests received by the production variant to the candidate model so that latency and predictions can be compared, and the candidate's response does not go to the caller. No app code needs to change. A: A weighted split would let some users receive the new model's response, which violates the condition that only the existing model's result be returned. B is a client modification in which the app calls both endpoints, which conflicts with the condition that an app deployment is not possible. D: Batch Transform on past logs cannot confirm latency under real production traffic.

exam-mla-c01-37.prompt: A quality control team builds a model that classifies 1,200 product photos (6 classes). Labeled data is scarce and the GPU training budget is limited, and training a CNN from scratch resulted in severe overfitting and long training times. The team has no computer vision experts, and the model will be deployed on edge devices on the factory floor, so the model size must not be too large either. There is no time to collect additional labels. The edge devices have ARM CPUs without GPUs and the on-site lighting is inconsistent, so brightness differs greatly from photo to photo; model training is done in SageMaker and reducing cloud training cost is the priority. Which approach improves accuracy with little data while reducing training cost the MOST?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Build a deeper randomly initialized CNN and train it from scratch for a long time with a greatly increased number of epochs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Summarize each image as a single average brightness value to make tabular data, and classify the 6 classes with Linear Learner.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Postpone training until more labels are collected, and in the meantime group the photos into 6 clusters with K-means and use them as classes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Load a model pre-trained on large-scale images and use transfer learning to fine-tune the last layer for the new classes.

exam-mla-c01-37.explanation: The correct answer is transfer learning from a pre-trained model. Reusing the feature extraction layers trained on large-scale data and adjusting only the last layer for the new classes yields high accuracy with little data, greatly reduces training time and GPU cost, and mitigates overfitting. A trains a deeper CNN from scratch, which worsens the overfitting and cost problems and is also disadvantageous for edge deployment. B: Summarizing with a single average brightness removes the information needed for classification. C: There is no time to wait for label collection, and there is no guarantee that the clusters match the actual classes.

exam-mla-c01-38.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
exam-mla-c01-38.prompt: A medical imaging company runs inference on CT files of up to 600 MB each as input. One file is a single input unit that cannot be split, processing takes up to 20 minutes, and the result only needs to be received within 30 minutes of the request. There are an average of a few dozen inference requests per day, and the company does not want to pay for instance costs during hours with no requests. A structure in which the calling application holds a connection open for a long time must also be avoided, and the result may be received as a file in Amazon S3. The calling application may fetch the result from S3 after receiving a notification, waiting in a queue for a few minutes when requests are concentrated is acceptable, and the model runs on a single GPU instance. Which deployment method is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an asynchronous inference endpoint, place the input in Amazon S3 and invoke it, and configure auto scaling to reduce the instance count to 0 when there are no requests.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a real-time inference endpoint with 2 instances, and have the caller keep the connection open and wait for the response until each request finishes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Load the model into an AWS Lambda function and invoke it through Amazon API Gateway so that there is no cost when there are no requests, and run the 20-minute processing in one invocation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Start a new Batch Transform job for each request, send one 600 MB file at a time, terminate the instances when processing ends, and write the results to Amazon S3.

exam-mla-c01-38.explanation: The correct answer is an asynchronous inference endpoint. It supports large payloads (up to 1 GB) and long processing times (up to 1 hour), queues requests and writes results to Amazon S3 so the caller does not hold a connection open, and the instance count can be scaled down to 0, so there is no idle cost. B: A real-time endpoint requires holding the connection and incurs always-on instance cost. C: Lambda has a maximum execution time of 15 minutes, so it cannot perform 20 minutes of processing. D: Batch Transform would have to send the unsplittable file as a single request, but MaxPayloadInMB, which sets the request size, cannot exceed 100 MB, so it cannot process a 600 MB input.

exam-mla-c01-39.prompt: A legal services company wants to improve contract summarization quality by fine-tuning an open-weight large language model with 20,000 of its own contracts. The data must not leave the company, and the fine-tuned model must be operated directly on a SageMaker endpoint inside the company VPC. Prompt engineering alone did not give sufficient summary quality, and the team has almost no staff to manage GPU servers directly. The training data is already organized as JSONL in an internal Amazon S3 bucket, summary quality will be evaluated with human-reviewed samples, and approval has been obtained for the cost of GPU instances to be used for fine-tuning. Which method meets this requirement while writing the LEAST amount of code?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Download the model weights, install PyTorch and a serving server directly on Amazon EC2 GPU instances, build both the training and inference environments yourself, and have the team configure auto scaling, a load balancer, and model version management as well.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Improve quality by requesting summaries with the full text of the contract included in the prompt each time, without changing the model weights.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Upload the contracts to an external SaaS provider's public fine-tuning API, train, and then invoke the issued model ID.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fine-tune a foundation model from SageMaker JumpStart with the training data in Amazon S3, and deploy the resulting model to a SageMaker endpoint inside the VPC.

exam-mla-c01-39.explanation: The correct answer is JumpStart fine-tuning and deployment to a SageMaker endpoint. JumpStart can fine-tune with minimal code using preconfigured training scripts, and it runs training and the endpoint within the customer's VPC settings so the data does not leave. A: Building the environment on EC2 yourself increases the burden of code and GPU server operations. B: Putting the full text in the prompt is not fine-tuning, it is the approach that was already insufficient, and it increases per-call cost and length limits. C: Uploading to an external SaaS API violates the constraint that data must not leave the company.

exam-mla-c01-40.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
exam-mla-c01-40.prompt: A data platform team orchestrates dozens of ETL jobs and SageMaker training jobs as Python DAGs with Apache Airflow that it installed itself on two Amazon EC2 instances. Operating system and Airflow patching cause repeated night-time failures, and jobs back up at month end because of a shortage of workers. The DAG code has accumulated to hundreds of lines each, and the team wants to keep using it as is while reducing the operational burden of patching and scaling the scheduler and workers. The team has 3 people and there is no schedule to rewrite the existing DAGs. The DAGs already use the official Airflow operators that call SageMaker training and AWS Glue jobs, dependent packages are managed with a single requirements file, and the new environment must run inside the existing VPC. Which solution is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rewrite all DAGs as AWS Step Functions state machine definitions and move the job order and retry rules to Amazon States Language.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Move all workflows to SageMaker Pipelines, convert the ETL steps into processing steps, and do not keep the DAG files.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an Amazon MWAA environment, upload the existing DAGs to an Amazon S3 bucket, and run the DAGs, including those with the SageMaker integration operators, as they are.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an Amazon EKS cluster, deploy the Airflow Helm chart, and have the team perform node group upgrades and Airflow version patches itself.

exam-mla-c01-40.explanation: The correct answer is Amazon MWAA. With managed Airflow, the DAGs are uploaded to Amazon S3 and run as they are, and the service takes care of worker auto scaling and version patching, so night-time patch failures and month-end capacity problems are reduced, and operators for SageMaker, AWS Glue, and other services are supported. A requires rewriting in Step Functions, which violates the conditions of using the DAG code as is and the schedule constraint. B: SageMaker Pipelines is tailored to ML steps, so rewriting dozens of general ETL jobs is a heavy burden. D: Deploying directly on EKS actually increases the operations of node upgrades and Airflow patching.

exam-mla-c01-41.prompt: An autonomous driving startup trains a ResNet-family model, which fits comfortably in the memory of a single GPU, on 12 TB of image data. Even with the largest GPU instance currently available, training takes 3 weeks and cannot meet the release schedule. The team uses a framework supported by the distributed training libraries, and the budget has been prioritized for shortening training time. The model structure and the entire training data must be kept. The training code is already a PyTorch version that supports the SageMaker distributed data parallel library, the instance quota has been approved for an increase of up to 8 ml.p4d.24xlarge instances, and the accuracy must be equivalent to single-instance training. Which approach is suitable to reduce training time the MOST?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply model parallelism, which splits the model by layers across multiple GPUs so that each GPU holds only part of the model, and configure micro-batches to flow through each pipeline stage.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Train on only a random 10% sample of the training data and use the remaining 90% only for validation to reduce training time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Apply data parallel distributed training, in which model replicas are placed on multiple GPU instances, the data is split and processed, and gradients are synchronized.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keep the instance type and reduce the batch size to 1 to lower memory usage and shorten the computation time of one step.

exam-mla-c01-41.explanation: The correct answer is data parallel distributed training. Since the model fits on a single GPU, replicating the model on each GPU, processing different batches, and synchronizing weight updates greatly shortens training that takes long because of the large amount of data. A: Model parallelism is used when the model does not fit in single-GPU memory, so it does not address the bottleneck here, which is the amount of data, and the implementation also becomes complex. B uses only 10% of the data, which violates the condition to keep all of the data. D: Reducing the batch size to 1 increases the number of steps and makes training slower.

exam-mla-c01-42.prompt: An AWS Glue ETL job with job bookmarks turned on processes an S3 source every day and writes to an S3 target prefix for the daily aggregate table that the BI team queries every day. A bug in the transformation logic was found yesterday and the fix was deployed today, so the last 7 days must be reprocessed. The reprocessed results must be reflected to the BI team within two days, and duplicate records must not be created in the target. The existing target data must not be deleted because the BI team continues to query it until validation is complete. The source files have not been modified, results older than 7 days were processed correctly, and the BI team's Amazon Athena table points to the target prefix. What is the SAFEST procedure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only rewind the bookmark and write again to the same target prefix as is, expecting AWS Glue to clean up the target files it previously wrote on its own.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delete the job and recreate it with the same name so that it inherits the bookmark state, and rerun the job on the 7 days of source data.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the bookmark option to Pause and append the last 7 days to the same target prefix without updating the state, filtering out duplicates afterward.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rewind the bookmark to 7 days ago, write the results to a new output location, and replace the existing data after validation.

exam-mla-c01-42.explanation: The correct answer is to rewind the bookmark to 7 days ago, write the results to a new output location, and replace the existing data after validation. AWS Glue bookmarks track only source files and not target files, so even if they are rewound or reset, the target is not cleaned up. Therefore, writing to a new location and replacing after validation prevents duplicates and also avoids interrupting the BI team's queries. A: Writing to the same prefix as is duplicates the 7 days of data. B: Deleting the job also deletes its bookmark, so the state is not inherited. C: Appending with Pause creates duplicates in the target and leaves the burden of filtering them out later.

exam-mla-c01-43.prompt: An insurance company wants to build a regression model that predicts annual claim amounts using 300 columns of policyholder information (numerical and categorical features encoded as numbers). The data is 8 GB of CSV in Amazon S3, and the team does not want to write training code itself and wants to get high accuracy on structured data as quickly as possible with a SageMaker built-in algorithm. The team plans to run hyperparameter tuning in the same service, and the model will be used for batch inference after training. Prediction error is evaluated by RMSE, the training data has almost no missing values and most columns are already numerically encoded, and a model interpretability report is not in scope at this stage. Which approach is MOST suitable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use the Random Cut Forest algorithm to classify policies with high claim amounts as outliers, and use the anomaly score as the predicted amount.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Select the Image Classification algorithm and convert each column of the CSV into an image channel to match the input format.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Select the XGBoost built-in algorithm, specify reg:squarederror as the objective function, and train with the CSV data.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cluster the policyholders with the K-means algorithm and use each cluster's average claim amount as the predicted value for individual policyholders.

exam-mla-c01-43.explanation: The correct answer is the XGBoost built-in algorithm. For regression on structured (tabular) data it delivers high accuracy without separate training code, the objective function can be specified as reg:squarederror, and automatic model tuning is supported. A: Random Cut Forest is for unsupervised anomaly detection and cannot directly predict amounts. B: Image Classification is an algorithm for image input and class labels and does not fit structured columns. D: K-means is a clustering algorithm, so using the cluster mean greatly reduces regression accuracy at the level of individual policyholders.

exam-mla-c01-44.prompt: An ML team ingested features into a SageMaker Feature Store feature group (using both the online store and the offline store) with PutRecord, and immediately afterward queried the offline store with Amazon Athena to build a training snapshot, but some of the records that had just been ingested were missing. Retraining runs every day at dawn, and the snapshot job is scheduled to run right after ingestion finishes. The feature group settings and the Athena query are fine, and when the same query is run again much later, the records appear. The retraining snapshot job must read data through the last 24 hours of ingestion with an Athena query, the ingestion pipeline calls PutRecord every few seconds, and the feature group is automatically registered in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. What is the cause and the MOST appropriate action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The online store TTL has expired and the records were deleted, so extend the TTL period and re-ingest the same records from the beginning.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Buffering causes a delay of up to 15 minutes, so run the snapshot job with a delay after ingestion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The offline store rejects all later records when the record identifier is the same, so ingest each record with a newly generated identifier.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Athena has cached the query results, so turn off result reuse in the Athena workgroup and run the query again, saving it under a new name.

exam-mla-c01-44.explanation: The correct answer is to delay the snapshot timing to account for the buffering delay. The offline store collects PutRecord data and writes it to Amazon S3 in batches within 15 minutes, so records may be missing from queries right after ingestion, which matches the symptom of the same query returning them much later. A: The online store TTL has nothing to do with the offline store history. C: Even with the same identifier, records with different event times are all kept as history, so there is no need to create new identifiers. D: Since the records appear when the query is run again, the cause is the delay in writing to S3 rather than caching, so turning off result reuse is not a solution.

exam-mla-c01-45.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
exam-mla-c01-45.prompt: Three ML teams at a company share SageMaker training jobs, endpoints, and notebooks in a single AWS account. At month end, the finance team wants to see SageMaker costs by team separated out in the billing data. It is difficult to split the teams into separate accounts this quarter, and since a single platform owner operates the environment, the burden must also be minimized. The resources currently have a team tag identifying the team, but all other billing settings are at their defaults. The finance team wants to see the amount per team in US dollars in the month-end report, the cost reports can be viewed only by the owner who has Billing console permissions, and the tag key is standardized as team, including capitalization. Which solution is MOST appropriate to determine costs by team?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Attach the team tag to the SageMaker resources, activate it as a cost allocation tag in the Billing console, and view costs by tag in Cost Explorer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Simply attach the team tag to the resources; the amount per team then appears automatically in all cost reports without any activation step, so no additional work is done.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Collect the endpoint instances' CPUUtilization metric by team and calculate the allocation of the total billed amount in proportion to the CPU usage ratio yourself, dividing it among the teams.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Aggregate the number of SageMaker API calls made by team members from CloudTrail logs and divide the monthly billed amount among the teams in proportion to the call count ratio.

exam-mla-c01-45.explanation: The correct answer is to attach the team tag to the SageMaker resources, activate it as a cost allocation tag in the Billing console, and view costs by tag in Cost Explorer. A user-defined tag must be activated before it appears in billing reports and Cost Explorer, and it can take up to 24 hours for the tag key to appear and up to 24 hours for it to be activated. B: If the tag is only attached and not activated, it is not reflected in the reports. C: Allocating by CPU utilization ratio does not match the actual billed amount and creates a heavy calculation burden. D: The number of API calls is unrelated to the instance hours used, so it is not a valid basis for cost allocation.

exam-mla-c01-46.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
exam-mla-c01-46.prompt: A manufacturer runs a defect detection model built with PyTorch on hundreds of ARM-based edge devices (150 per factory). The factory network is unstable, so inference must run offline on the devices, latency must be reduced to match the device hardware, and there is no IT staff on site, so model updates must be deployed remotely. The devices already run an OS on which AWS IoT Greengrass can be installed. The compilation target is ARM64 Linux devices, the model is an image classification model with a fixed input size, and the devices connect for only a few minutes once a day and can receive a new model then. Which combination has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deploy the model to a cloud real-time endpoint and have the devices call the endpoint over the internet for every request to receive the inference results.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Compile the model for the target device with SageMaker Neo and deploy it remotely with AWS IoT Greengrass.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Connect to hundreds of devices over SSH and copy the original, uncompiled model file to them directly, repeating the same work for every update.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deploy the model to a serverless inference endpoint and have the devices reuse the last response from a cache when the network is disconnected.

exam-mla-c01-46.explanation: The correct answer is SageMaker Neo compilation and AWS IoT Greengrass deployment. Neo optimizes models such as PyTorch models for the target processor, including ARM, to reduce latency, and the compiled model can be deployed to Greengrass devices, which enables offline inference on the devices and managed remote updates. A calls a cloud endpoint, so inference is impossible when the network is disconnected. C: Copying directly over SSH imposes a heavy burden for updating hundreds of devices, there is no on-site staff, and there is no hardware optimization. D uses a serverless endpoint and a cache, so it cannot process inference for new inputs offline.

exam-mla-c01-47.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
exam-mla-c01-47.prompt: A team runs a SageMaker training job on data containing PII. The security requirements are that the data must not traverse a public internet path and must be encrypted at rest with a customer managed key. The training data bucket is in the same Region, and the team wants to meet the security regulations with minimal operational changes and without changing the existing training code. There is no reason for the training container to access the external internet. The training container uses a SageMaker-provided image, the S3 bucket is in the same account and the same Region, and the security team must submit confirmation of the VPC and security group settings during audits. Which TWO configurations meet this requirement? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run the training job in a public subnet and configure it to read the data through the internet gateway to the public Amazon S3 endpoint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Copy the training data to the local disk of an unencrypted notebook instance and run the training script from there.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remove all AWS KMS permissions from the execution role and leave encryption to be handled arbitrarily by code inside the training container.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run the training job in a VPC in a private subnet with no internet path, and configure the data access path with an Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoint.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Specify a customer managed AWS KMS key for the output model artifact and the training volume, and grant the execution role permission to use that key.

exam-mla-c01-47.explanation: The correct answers are a private VPC with an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint, and a customer managed KMS key. In a private subnet with no internet access, the training container can reach the S3 data only if there is an S3 VPC endpoint, and the traffic does not traverse the public internet. Specifying a customer managed KMS key for the output and volume and granting key permissions to the execution role satisfies the encryption at rest requirement. A uses a public subnet and an internet gateway path, which allows traversal of the internet. B copies data to an unencrypted local disk, which violates the encryption requirement. C: Removing KMS permissions means the key cannot be used, and arbitrary handling inside the container does not meet the customer managed key requirement.

exam-mla-c01-48.prompt: A data scientist has so far applied a preprocessing flow built with Data Wrangler by manually running notebook cells in order. Because the procedure depends on one individual, retraining once stopped when that person was on vacation. The team wants to operate this preprocessing as a reproducible automated workflow every week, connected with the training, evaluation, and model registration steps, and wants to avoid newly coding the transformation logic that has already been validated. The preprocessing input is raw CSV in Amazon S3 with new files accumulating under the same prefix every week, and the pipeline must register the model in the model registry only when the evaluation metric exceeds a threshold. Which solution is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rewrite the flow's transformation sequence yourself as PySpark code, move it to an Amazon EMR step, and call it from AWS Step Functions. Store the intermediate results of each step in Amazon S3.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Export the Data Wrangler flow to SageMaker Pipelines to create the preprocessing step, and chain the training, evaluation, and registration steps to it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Document the transformation sequence with screenshots, and have the person in charge manually run the flow in Studio whenever retraining is needed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Upload only the transformed result CSV to Amazon S3 and keep no preprocessing logic, reusing only that file for later training.

exam-mla-c01-48.explanation: The correct answer is to export the Data Wrangler flow to SageMaker Pipelines. The export feature turns the flow's transformations into a pipeline processing step, so the validated transformations are not recoded and are connected with the training, evaluation, and registration steps into a single workflow that is operated reproducibly. A requires rewriting in PySpark, which violates the constraint not to newly code. C is manual execution, so it does not meet the automated workflow requirement and the dependence on an individual remains. D: If only the result CSV is kept, the same preprocessing cannot be reproduced on new data.

exam-mla-c01-49.prompt: An analyst with little coding experience must create training data this week. The analyst must join click logs in Amazon S3, an order table queried with Amazon Athena, and a customer master in Amazon Redshift, and data governance policy does not allow deleting or moving the source data. The team wants to avoid building a new pipeline that copies the three sources to one place, and wants to perform transformations and even data quality checks in a visual interface. All three sources are in the same Region, the analyst's Studio execution role has been granted query permissions, and the join result only needs to be saved to an S3 location to be used later as training input. Which solution is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Download each of the three sources as CSV, collect them on the local disk of a notebook instance, join them with pandas, and upload the result to Amazon S3.

choices.label: B
choices.text: First UNLOAD the Redshift and Athena data to Amazon S3, create a new AWS Glue crawler and ETL job, and register the join result in the catalog.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Connect the three sources as the input manifest of a Ground Truth labeling job and configure the job so that workers do the join directly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Import each of the three sources in Data Wrangler, join and transform them inside the flow, and check quality with a data insights report.

exam-mla-c01-49.explanation: The correct answer is a Data Wrangler flow. It can import data from Amazon S3, Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift, and more, join and transform it within a single flow, and even generate data quality and insights reports, so it meets both the visual interface requirement and the requirement to avoid a new copy pipeline. A gathers data on a local disk, which has scale limits and involves a lot of manual work and does not suit an analyst with little coding experience. B creates a new UNLOAD and AWS Glue ETL, which is the copy pipeline the team wants to avoid. C: Ground Truth is a labeling service and is not meant for joins.

exam-mla-c01-50.prompt: A retail company evaluates three regression models that forecast weekly demand per product, using data from the same validation period, and reports the results to the inventory manager. Rare large prediction errors lead to stockout losses and are much more critical than small errors. The average errors of the three models are similar, so the difference is not well revealed by the average error alone. The three candidate models use the same features and the same validation-period data, the comparison result must be reported as a single number at the model selection meeting, and model explainability is not a criterion for this comparison. Which evaluation metric BEST reflects this business characteristic when comparing the candidate models?

choices.label: A
choices.text: RMSE. It squares the errors, averages them, and takes the square root, so it imposes a larger penalty on large errors.

choices.label: B
choices.text: MAE. It averages the absolute values of the errors, so it reflects all errors with equal weight and does not specifically magnify large errors.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Accuracy. It calculates the proportion of predictions that exactly match the actual values and shows how often the model is right.

choices.label: D
choices.text: ROC AUC. It is a classification model metric that summarizes the relationship between sensitivity and specificity as the classification threshold changes.

exam-mla-c01-50.explanation: The correct answer is RMSE. Because the errors are squared before averaging, rare large errors are reflected strongly in the metric, which fits the requirement that large errors are critical. B: MAE averages errors linearly and does not particularly emphasize large errors, so it can easily hide differences between models with similar average errors. C: Accuracy means the proportion of exact matches in continuous-value regression, which is almost useless. D: ROC AUC is a threshold-based performance metric for classification models, so it does not suit evaluating continuous demand forecasts.

exam-mla-c01-51.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
exam-mla-c01-51.prompt: A team operates a SageMaker real-time endpoint on 2 instances, and the response time measured from the client has recently doubled. The number of invocations has barely changed and there are no 5xx errors. To avoid service interruption, the team will not deploy new code and wants to first determine whether the increased latency is caused by the inference time of the model container, by the SageMaker processing segment, or by the network. Default CloudWatch metrics are already being collected. The response time was measured from an Amazon EC2 client in the same Region, the request payload size and the model version have not changed, and the analysis must be finished within a day using a CloudWatch dashboard. Which solution is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Compare the ModelLatency and OverheadLatency metrics over the same period, and treat what remains after subtracting both from the client's total latency as the network.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Compare only the sum of the Invocations metric, and conclude that if the invocation count has not increased, the model container and the SageMaker processing segment are not the cause.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Delete the endpoint, recreate it with a larger instance type, and estimate the cause segment by checking whether the response time decreases.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Judge that if the Invocation5XXErrors metric is 0, the cause of latency is always the client code, and skip investigating the endpoint-side metrics.

exam-mla-c01-51.explanation: The correct answer is to compare ModelLatency and OverheadLatency over the same period. The total response time is the sum of network latency, SageMaker overhead latency, and model latency. Model latency is the time the container spent on inference, and overhead latency is the time from when SageMaker receives the request until it returns the response, excluding model latency, so subtracting both from the client's total latency leaves the network segment. B: The model can slow down even if the invocation count is the same, so Invocations alone cannot separate the causes. C: It causes a service interruption, only costs money, and does not tell the cause. D: Latency can increase even without 5xx errors, so this is no basis for skipping the endpoint-side investigation.

exam-mla-c01-52.prompt: A company manages transaction data accumulating in Amazon S3 as AWS Glue Data Catalog tables and retrains a model with this data every week. Training quality has recently dropped because of a column whose missing values have increased. The team finds it hard to write from scratch which quality rules suit the table and does not want to operate servers. It wants to obtain candidate rules automatically, evaluate them regularly before retraining, and receive a notification when a rule is violated. There is one data engineer, and the team already uses Amazon EventBridge and Amazon SNS. The quality rules must be column-level conditions such as missing ratio, value range, and duplicates, the evaluation results must be checkable before the retraining pipeline starts, and the table has about 500 million rows. Which solution is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use AWS Glue Data Quality to get rule recommendations for the catalog table, create DQDL rules, schedule the evaluation, and receive notifications through Amazon EventBridge.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Install an open-source quality checking tool on an Amazon EC2 instance yourself, run it weekly with cron, and separately write and operate a script that emails the results.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Search the training job logs with Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights, treat the appearance of words related to missing values as a sign of a data problem, and have the person in charge check the columns directly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Turn on S3 object-level logging, treat the point at which the number of PutObject calls in the AWS CloudTrail logs decreases as a sign of increased missing values, and have the person in charge check the data directly.

exam-mla-c01-52.explanation: The correct answer is AWS Glue Data Quality. It is serverless, and for Data Catalog tables it can analyze the data and recommend rules, so the team does not have to write the rules from scratch. Rules can be created in DQDL, evaluation runs can be scheduled, and violations can be notified through integration with Amazon EventBridge or CloudWatch. B requires installing the tool on EC2 and operating the script, which creates server operations overhead. C is a word search in training logs, which cannot systematically measure data quality. D: The number of PutObject calls is just a count of files and has no relation to the missing ratio of a column.

exam-mla-c01-53.prompt: Twelve data scientists on a data science team run dozens of training experiments per day on SageMaker and record hyperparameters and metrics by hand in a spreadsheet. The team already uses open-source MLflow tracking code and must be able to trace which run produced which model during audits. The team members want to record runs the same way in both SageMaker training jobs and notebooks, and there is no staff to operate a tracking server directly. The tracking server must keep parameters, metrics, and artifacts per run, the trained models must be linked to the model registry and managed as versions, and access is controlled with the team members' IAM permissions. Which method has the LEAST operational overhead while minimizing code changes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a managed MLflow tracking server in SageMaker AI and connect the existing MLflow logging code with the AWS MLflow plugin to record runs and models.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Install an MLflow server and an Amazon RDS database yourself on Amazon EC2, store artifacts in an Amazon S3 bucket, and have the team operate patching, backups, and capacity management directly.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have each training script print metrics to CloudWatch Logs and reconstruct the run history by searching the logs for every audit.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Query AWS CloudTrail logs with Amazon Athena to build a weekly report that extracts the API call records for each training job, and record metrics separately by hand.

exam-mla-c01-53.explanation: The correct answer is the managed MLflow tracking server with the AWS MLflow plugin. SageMaker AI integrates with MLflow, so the existing MLflow SDK code can be used almost as is to record and compare the parameters, metrics, and models of runs without operating a server, and training jobs and notebooks connect in the same way through the tracking server ARN. B installs on EC2 and RDS yourself, so the patching and backup burden remains, which conflicts with the constraint of having no operations staff. C: Searching CloudWatch Logs makes structured experiment comparison difficult and the audit evidence is unreliable. D: CloudTrail records API calls and does not contain metric values, so it does not suit comparison between runs and model tracking.

exam-mla-c01-54.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
exam-mla-c01-54.prompt: A marketing team scores a single 400 GB CSV file with SageMaker Batch Transform early every Monday morning. Even when 10 instances are specified, only one instance works and the others sit idle, so the run time does not decrease, and the results are needed before the Tuesday morning meeting. The instance cost budget must stay the same as now, and the scoring model and output format cannot be changed. The scoring results must correspond to the order of the input rows, the output is stored under the same prefix in Amazon S3 regardless of the number of instances, and the input CSV has no header and can be split by row. How can the team process the job in parallel for the same instance cost and reduce the completion time MOST effectively?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Leave the input file as it is and set SplitType to Line, expecting that the single file will be split into mini-batches and distributed across the 10 instances.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase the MaxConcurrentTransforms value to raise the number of concurrent requests that one instance processes for the same file in order to reduce the time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Instead of Batch Transform, create a real-time endpoint, send the entire file as a single request body, and receive the scores in the response.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Split the input CSV into multiple Amazon S3 objects so that Batch Transform distributes the objects across the instances.

exam-mla-c01-54.explanation: The correct answer is to split the input CSV into multiple Amazon S3 objects. Batch Transform maps input objects to instances by key, so if there is only one object, only one instance processes it even when multiple instances are specified. A: SplitType Line only divides a single file into request-sized mini-batches and does not distribute the file across multiple instances. B: Raising the number of concurrent requests only increases parallelism within one instance, so the other instances continue to sit idle. C: Sending 400 GB in one request to a real-time endpoint does not fit the payload limit and also changes how the model is invoked.

exam-mla-c01-55.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
exam-mla-c01-55.prompt: A customer center team operates a sentiment classification model on a SageMaker serverless endpoint, and its monthly budget is fixed. Requests are normally infrequent, but every day from 9 AM, dozens of concurrent requests arrive for 30 minutes, and the first requests are slow at that time because of cold starts. The team wants to avoid switching to a real-time endpoint with instances running 24 hours because of cost. The traffic pattern repeats at the same time every day. The endpoint's memory setting is 4 GB and its maximum concurrency is 20, and during the 9 AM surge the concurrent requests rise to about 15, and the team wants a configuration that incurs extra cost only during the surge window. How should the team solve this while keeping costs down?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Raise the endpoint memory to the maximum so the container uses more vCPUs, which eliminates the need for new compute even when concurrent requests surge.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Schedule a Lambda function that sends a dummy request every minute to keep the container warm and have it absorb the concurrent requests during the surge window.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure provisioned concurrency and raise its value only during the surge window with scheduled scaling.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the serverless endpoint to a real-time endpoint, keep a minimum of 1 instance, and manually increase the instance count during the surge window.

exam-mla-c01-55.explanation: The correct answer is provisioned concurrency with scheduled scaling. Provisioned concurrency pre-initializes the specified amount of compute so that it responds without cold starts, and with Application Auto Scaling scheduled actions the value can be raised only during the surge window, so cost is also kept down for a pattern that repeats at the same time every day. A: Even if memory is raised, cold starts occur again when concurrent requests exceed the concurrency currently in use. B: A dummy request keeps only about one concurrent request warm and does not solve the situation where many requests arrive together. D: Switching to a real-time endpoint is the always-on cost structure the team wants to avoid, and it requires manual adjustment.

exam-mla-c01-56.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
exam-mla-c01-56.prompt: A financial services organization must present deployment history and approvers during audits. The organization wants to register models produced by the training pipeline as versions in the model registry and deploy only the versions approved by the evaluator to the production endpoint. It must be able to roll back quickly to a previously approved version if a production failure occurs, and it must be possible to trace which training result was deployed. The team has a DevOps engineer who operates the CI/CD pipeline. Approval is given by a single evaluator after reviewing the metrics and the bias report, production deployment must proceed automatically only after approval, and the artifacts and evaluation results of previous versions must be retained for more than one year. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Store training results in Amazon S3 folders named by date, and have the deployment owner look at the folder names and manually edit the model location in the endpoint configuration to deploy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Keep overwriting the container image with the latest tag, push it to Amazon ECR, and restart the endpoint so that the latest image is deployed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Evaluate the model in a notebook, and when the owner announces approval via messenger, have a data scientist manually update the endpoint in the console.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Register the model as a version in a model package group, use the approval status change as the deployment trigger, and roll back by deploying the previously approved version.

exam-mla-c01-56.explanation: The correct answer is the configuration that registers the model as a version in a model package group, uses the approval status change as the deployment trigger, and rolls back by deploying the previously approved version. Each version keeps its metadata and lineage, so it is possible to trace which training result was deployed, CI/CD deploys only approved versions, and approver records remain. A: The date-folder method has no approval status or lineage management and depends on manual edits. B: When the image is overwritten with the latest tag, it is hard to identify and roll back to the previous image. C: Approval by messenger and manual updates do not meet the audit trail and automation requirements.

exam-mla-c01-57.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
exam-mla-c01-57.prompt: A company must train on internal customer data with a third-party training container supplied by an outside vendor. Because the container code cannot be verified, data must not be exfiltrated to the internet or other services during training. The training data is in Amazon S3, and the container already includes all the components it needs so that it does not install external packages during training. The security team requires preventive blocking, not after-the-fact log review. The training input and output are in an Amazon S3 bucket in the same account and the execution role has access permissions, the vendor does not disclose the container's internal logic, and training logs are collected in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Which configuration meets this requirement MOST securely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run the training job in a public subnet, restrict the security group's outbound rules to port 443 only, and allow S3 access through the public endpoint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turn on network isolation for the training job to block outbound calls from the container, and have SageMaker handle S3 input and output outside the container with the execution role.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Let the container read the Amazon S3 bucket directly with AWS credentials, and review the logs after training finishes to check afterward whether data was sent externally.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Build the training data into the container image and remove all S3 access permissions from the execution role.

exam-mla-c01-57.explanation: The correct answer is network isolation. When EnableNetworkIsolation is turned on, the container cannot make outbound calls to any service, including Amazon S3, and no AWS credentials are provided, and SageMaker handles S3 downloads and uploads outside the container with the execution role. A allows port 443, so external transmission is possible over HTTPS. C is after-the-fact log review, which cannot prevent exfiltration, and it gives the container direct S3 access permissions. D: Building the data into the image leaves customer data in the image, which could leak through access to the image, and it also increases the management burden.

exam-mla-c01-58.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
exam-mla-c01-58.prompt: An application in a VPC invokes a SageMaker real-time endpoint. The security team wants the invocation traffic not to traverse the public internet, and wants this VPC path to allow only InvokeEndpoint for a single endpoint named myEndpoint. The subnet has no internet gateway or NAT device, and the application authenticates with the IAM role of an EC2 instance profile. The endpoint and the VPC are in the same Region, the calling app calls the default runtime address with the AWS SDK, and the security team wants to deny both invocations of other endpoints and all other SageMaker actions through the VPC path. Which TWO configurations meet this requirement? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an interface VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) for SageMaker Runtime and turn on private DNS.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add a NAT gateway to the subnet so that the app goes out to the public SageMaker Runtime address, and configure the security group to allow only the HTTPS port for outbound traffic.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Attach to the app's IAM role a policy that allows all sagemaker actions on all resources so that no permission error ever occurs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the VPC endpoint policy, allow sagemaker:InvokeEndpoint only for the ARN of myEndpoint.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Include the long-term access key of an IAM user in the app code so that the same key invokes the endpoint from anywhere, inside or outside the VPC.

exam-mla-c01-58.explanation: The correct answers are an interface VPC endpoint for SageMaker Runtime and a VPC endpoint policy restricted to the single myEndpoint ARN. A PrivateLink interface endpoint connects the VPC to SageMaker Runtime without an internet gateway or NAT device, and when private DNS is turned on, the default runtime hostname resolves to this endpoint. Narrowing the allowed actions and resources with the endpoint policy means only invocations of the specified endpoint are possible through this path. B calls the public address through NAT, so it traverses the internet path and also does not match the subnet condition. C allows all actions on all resources, which violates least privilege. E puts a long-term access key in code, which carries a high risk of leakage, and an instance profile already exists.

exam-mla-c01-59.prompt: After a service overhaul, the features for customer churn prediction have grown to more than 60, and the schedule to the model launch is tight. A team is building a Data Wrangler data flow in Studio, and among the features there are values that already reveal the outcome, such as 'refund amount', which is only generated after the cancellation has been processed, so validation accuracy is abnormally high. The team wants to minimize code writing and find such features before training the model. The flow's label column is the binary churn indicator, the training data is 8 million rows of CSV in Amazon S3, and once the team confirms the problematic features, it plans to exclude those columns and continue using the same flow. What should the team do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use Data Wrangler's target leakage analysis to find features that predict the label too well.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add the SageMaker Debugger overfitting rule to the training job to automatically stop the training job when the validation loss starts to diverge.

choices.label: C
choices.text: After deploying the model, attach the Model Monitor data quality monitor to detect whether input distributions different from those at training time are coming in.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Train the model with hyperparameter tuning that raises the regularization strength to the maximum so that the influence of the suspected leakage features becomes small.

exam-mla-c01-59.explanation: The correct answer is Data Wrangler's target leakage analysis. Before training, it lets you visually check how excessively each feature explains the label, so leakage features can be found without code. B: The Debugger overfitting rule monitors the loss curve after training is run, so it does not match the requirement to check before training, and it cannot tell the leakage cause at the feature level. C: Model Monitor looks at input distribution drift after deployment, so the timing is different. D: Raising regularization does not remove leakage features and only lowers model performance.

exam-mla-c01-60.prompt: While training a recommendation model, after epoch 40 the training loss continues to decrease but the validation loss begins to increase. Validation accuracy was highest around epoch 35. More training data cannot be obtained, the team does not want to change the model architecture, and the validation set does not overlap with the training data. The feature that saves model state every epoch is already in use, and training runs on a GPU instance and takes 20 minutes per epoch. Training runs as a SageMaker training job, hyperparameter tuning is not included in this schedule, and the validation metric is already recorded in CloudWatch every epoch. How can the team improve generalization performance with the LEAST amount of change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Double the number of epochs and continue training with the same settings until the training loss converges sufficiently, saving checkpoints every epoch.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply early stopping that monitors the validation loss and stops training when improvement stops, and use the model from the best point.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase the number of hidden layers and nodes to enlarge the model capacity, then retrain with the same data and the same hyperparameters.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lower the regularization strength to 0 so that the model fits the patterns of the training data more precisely, then retrain.

exam-mla-c01-60.explanation: The correct answer is early stopping. A decreasing training loss with an increasing validation loss is a classic sign of overfitting, and stopping training when the validation loss no longer improves and using the model from the best point (around epoch 35) solves the problem without changing the data or the architecture. Since each epoch takes 20 minutes, cutting unnecessary epochs also reduces cost. A: Increasing the epochs makes the overfitting worse. C: Increasing model capacity lets the model memorize the training data more, widening the gap, and it also violates the condition of not changing the architecture. D: Removing regularization eliminates the mechanism that suppresses overfitting, which makes things worse.

exam-mla-c01-61.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
exam-mla-c01-61.prompt: A team deploys a new image classification model to a real-time endpoint. The P95 latency target is 120 ms, traffic is about 300 requests per second and relatively steady. There are 8 candidate instance types, so benchmarking them manually is difficult, the model artifact is already in Amazon S3, and the team plans to use 2 or more instances for availability. The team values cost efficiency, and a single ML engineer must decide within this week. The model size is about 300 MB, the input image is fixed at 224x224, the traffic does not vary much over the day, and there is a monthly cost cap, so the team needs the cheapest configuration among the candidates that meets the target. Which method finds the most cost-efficient instance type and configuration that meets the target with the LEAST effort?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Choose the largest GPU instance to be sure of meeting the latency target, set a high minimum instance count for auto scaling, and take the approach of reducing the cost later while operating.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pick one of the candidate instances at random, deploy it, and replace it with another type if a problem arises.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Register the model with SageMaker Inference Recommender, run load tests on the candidate instances, and compare latency, throughput, and cost metrics.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run one inference manually on each instance type in a notebook, measure the average time, and choose the fastest type.

exam-mla-c01-61.explanation: The correct answer is SageMaker Inference Recommender. After the model is registered or created, it automatically runs load test (benchmark) jobs on the candidate instance types and compares performance and resource usage metrics, so the team can choose a cost-efficient configuration that meets the latency target with little effort. A: The largest GPU instance conflicts with the cost efficiency requirement. B: A random choice has no basis and incurs replacement cost. D: Manually measuring one inference does not reflect the concurrent load of 300 requests per second and the P95 latency.

exam-mla-c01-62.prompt: A payment fraud detection service looks up each user's latest features with low latency at inference time, and uses the same features for automatic weekly retraining. Traffic is hundreds of requests per second and there is only one person who owns the feature definitions. The team wants to reduce the mismatch in which feature values differ between training time and serving time, and to manage feature definitions and ingestion code in only one place. The features are updated from a stream, such as the number of transactions per user in the last hour, the inference latency target is a lookup in single-digit milliseconds, and it must also be possible to reproduce the past feature values as of the time used for training. How should this be configured to minimize operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Load inference features into Redis and separately load training features into CSV files in Amazon S3, maintaining two separate pieces of preprocessing code.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create only an offline store and run an Amazon Athena query each time an inference request arrives to look up that user's latest features.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Copy the feature calculation notebook code used for training into the endpoint container and recompute the features from the source data for every inference request.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use the same features for inference and training from a single feature group with both the online and offline stores turned on.

exam-mla-c01-62.explanation: The correct answer is a single feature group with both the online and offline stores turned on. Because there is one ingestion path, features with the same definition are provided as the latest low-latency values in the online store and as training history in the offline store, which reduces mismatch and keeps definition management in one place. A: Dual preprocessing code is exactly the structure in which logic diverges and causes the mismatch. B: Running Athena for each request makes latency large and violates the low-latency requirement. C: Copying notebook code and recomputing increases latency and leaves two copies of the code.

exam-mla-c01-63.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
exam-mla-c01-63.prompt: A team deployed an inference container built with FastAPI to a SageMaker endpoint, but endpoint creation fails. The container accepts only POST /predict on port 5000, and the team plans to keep the model file in Amazon S3 rather than in the image. The service owner can modify the container code within this week, and the container image is in Amazon ECR. The container has already been pushed to ECR and the execution role has the required permissions, the logs show a message that the container terminated because of a health check failure, and the model file can be compressed and uploaded to Amazon S3. Which TWO changes must be made so that the container satisfies the SageMaker hosting contract? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Specify a non-root user in the Dockerfile and set tini as the ENTRYPOINT so that SIGTERM signals are handled more safely.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Modify the web server to respond on port 8080 to POST /invocations requests and to GET /ping requests for health checks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Upload the model artifact to Amazon S3 as tar.gz, specify it in ModelDataUrl, and read it from /opt/ml/model.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the endpoint configuration, specify the container port as 5000 and register the /predict path as the invocation path so that SageMaker sends requests to that path.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Have the code download the model file directly to the /opt/ml/model path when the container starts and use it there, and lift the read-only permission.

exam-mla-c01-63.explanation: The correct answers are implementing /invocations and /ping on port 8080, and specifying a tar.gz artifact in ModelDataUrl. A SageMaker inference container must accept /invocations and /ping on port 8080, and creation fails if the health check does not return 200 within 8 minutes after startup. If the model is placed in Amazon S3 as tar.gz, it is extracted to /opt/ml/model and provided read-only. A: A non-root user and tini are not requirements of the hosting contract, SageMaker expects to run as root, and tini cannot be used because of the train and serve arguments. D: There is no setting to change the port and path in the configuration. E: Having the container download directly to /opt/ml/model does not work because that path is read-only.

exam-mla-c01-64.prompt: A logistics company loads CSV-format sensor records that arrive through Amazon Kinesis Data Streams into Amazon S3 with Amazon Data Firehose, and wants to run column-oriented queries with Amazon Athena in ML preprocessing. There are thousands of sensors, records arrive at thousands per second, and there are 2 data engineers. The team wants to change the storage format to Parquet but does not want to operate a separate always-running cluster. Firehose buffering is based on a maximum of 5 minutes or 128 MB, queries mainly retrieve only the sensor ID and measurement value columns, and the record schema is fixed enough to be defined in AWS Glue. Which TWO things must be configured to meet this requirement? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add an AWS Lambda function invoked by S3 events that renames the extension of objects written by Firehose to .parquet and saves them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Launch an Amazon EMR cluster every hour and schedule a Spark job that rewrites the CSV objects in Amazon S3 as Parquet.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a table schema in the AWS Glue Data Catalog that matches the record structure and have the Firehose format conversion reference it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Specify CSV as the input format of the format conversion so that the Parquet serializer reads the CSV records as they are.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Add a Lambda transformation to the Firehose delivery stream to convert the CSV records to JSON before passing them to the conversion step.

exam-mla-c01-64.explanation: The correct answers are converting CSV to JSON with Lambda and referencing a Glue Data Catalog schema. Firehose format conversion reads only JSON input, so other formats such as CSV must first be converted to JSON with Lambda, and the converter interprets the data with the schema created in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. A only changes the extension and does not change the file content to Parquet. B rewrites with EMR every hour, which violates the constraint of not operating a separate cluster. D: Specifying that CSV be read directly does not work because there is no supported deserializer (Hive JSON SerDe, OpenX JSON SerDe) for it.

exam-mla-c01-65.prompt: An IoT team wants to convert JSON sensor records arriving through Firehose (thousands per second) to Parquet and store them in Amazon S3. The key naming conventions differ by equipment manufacturer, so conversion failures are frequent. The timestamp is an epoch-millisecond integer, and some JSON keys contain periods, such as sensor.temp. The record format cannot be changed because it is in the equipment firmware. The Firehose delivery stream is already configured to reference an AWS Glue table schema, sensor records arrive as one JSON document per line, and records that fail conversion are accumulating under a separate S3 prefix. How should the team configure the stream to map to columns without conversion errors, with the LEAST amount of change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Select the OpenX JSON SerDe as the deserializer to handle the epoch time format, and use the option that replaces periods with underscores.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Select the Hive JSON SerDe as the deserializer and use keys containing periods as they are as the column names in the AWS Glue schema.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bundle multiple JSON documents into a single JSON array and pass it as one record so that the converter reads all the documents in the array.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the serializer from Parquet to the ORC SerDe, which naturally handles keys containing periods as column names.

exam-mla-c01-65.explanation: The correct answer is the OpenX JSON SerDe. OpenX handles timestamp formats such as epoch seconds and milliseconds and has an option that replaces periods in keys with underscores, so it satisfies both conditions. B: The Hive JSON SerDe does not allow periods in column names, so these keys cause problems. C: A JSON array is not a valid input format, and documents must be concatenated. D: The serializer only determines the output format and has nothing to do with handling periods in input JSON keys, so changing to ORC does not solve the problem.

exam-mls-c01-1.prompt: The data science team (5 people) at a nationwide parcel delivery company uses logistic regression in a SageMaker notebook to predict whether a delivery will be delayed. About 2 million delivery records accumulate in Amazon S3 each day, and the training data is about 300 million records from the most recent 6 months. The postal code column has about 30,000 unique values. One-hot encoding would expand it to 30,000 columns, which slows training and causes severe sparsity. Label encoding, which converts postal codes to integers in sorted order, gives the values a false ordinal meaning in a linear model. New postal codes appear occasionally, the operations team must be able to explain results by looking at the coefficients, and training time must also be reduced. The team keeps a schedule of retraining once a week. The model coefficients are submitted every quarter to the logistics planning team as explanatory material, and the encoding must be reproducible inside the training pipeline. Additional infrastructure cost cannot increase. Given these constraints, which encoding is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
