The infrastructure team has 3 people, so a custom-developed replication tool would be hard to maintain. Eight of the servers are being moved to AWS from on-premises VMware, and the rest are EC2 instances in the Seoul Region. The DNS switch for user access during recovery is already automated separately and is outside the scope of this work. DR drills are currently performed manually once a year over one weekend day, and one goal of this improvement is to repeat the drills every quarter, even during weekday business hours, without burden. The budget must not exceed twice the current DR cost. Which actions must be taken to meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Preconfigure the launch settings for recovery instances and regularly perform nondisruptive recovery drills to validate the RTO.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Shorten the nightly AMI copy interval to 5 minutes and launch instances from the latest AMI during a failure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure an Auto Scaling group that spans two Regions so that it automatically scales out in the other Region during a Regional failure.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run 40 servers identical to production continuously in the DR Region and configure dual writes at the application level.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Install a replication agent on the servers and configure continuous block-level replication to a staging subnet in the DR Region.

exam-sap-c02-9.explanation: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery uses an agent to replicate continuously to a staging area that uses only low-cost storage and minimal compute, so it achieves an RPO of a few seconds without a full always-on environment. Recovery instances are launched only during drills or actual recovery, and the launch settings can be defined in advance and the RTO validated through regular drills. Continuously running identical servers violates the requirement to avoid that cost. AMI copies are snapshot-based even when the interval is shortened, so they cannot guarantee an RPO of a few seconds. An Auto Scaling group is a Regional resource and cannot span Regions. Because the solution must satisfy both an RPO of a few seconds and avoidance of always-on cost, it needs a combination of continuous replication and a recovery-time instance launch structure. Because the solution must satisfy both an RPO of a few seconds and avoidance of always-on cost, a combination of continuous replication and a recovery-instance launch structure is required.

exam-sap-c02-10.prompt: A company runs a nightly settlement batch using cron on an on-premises VM. The job takes about 40 minutes each time, uses 2 GB of memory, and runs a Java program from a shell script. The batch starts at 23:00 every day and must finish by 01:00, and if it fails it must automatically retry once and then notify the operations team. The company wants to reduce VM maintenance cost and patching burden but must keep code changes to the settlement logic to a minimum. The source code is in Git and built on a CI server, and the 3 developers have no capacity to learn Spark or a new language. The current job reads data from an Oracle database, creates a settlement file, and uploads it to an internal SFTP server, and this connection is already linked to AWS by VPN. There are 6 more similar batches besides this job, but the scope of this effort is this one job. The operations team receives early-morning alerts through email and the internal messenger, and it is acceptable for a person to check a failure in the morning, but a situation where the job ends silently without a retry is not acceptable. Which modernization approach MOST appropriately meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Package the batch as a container image and run it as an AWS Fargate task. Have AWS Step Functions invoke it through the synchronous RunTask integration, retry once on failure, and report a final failure through Amazon SNS, with Amazon EventBridge Scheduler starting the state machine at 23:00 every day.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Move the Java program to an AWS Lambda function and invoke it at 23:00 every day with an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule. Increase the function timeout to the maximum configurable value so that the 40-minute job completes in a single invocation, rely on Lambda asynchronous retries on failure, and configure failure notifications with a separate alarm.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create the EC2 instances as an Auto Scaling group and turn them on only at night with scheduled scaling. Copy the existing cron configuration as is and run the batch from the shell script, and have the script rerun once on failure and notify by email.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rewrite the settlement logic as an AWS Glue Spark job, convert it to Python code, and run it every night with a Glue trigger. Configure Glue job retries and notifications on failure, and schedule training for the team to learn Spark.

exam-sap-c02-10.explanation: The correct answer is a scheduled Fargate task. The existing Java program only needs to be wrapped in a container, so code changes are small and server patching disappears, and Fargate tasks do not have a 15-minute execution limit like Lambda, so the 40-minute job can run and you pay only for the time used. EventBridge Scheduler handles the schedule, and the Step Functions synchronous RunTask integration waits for the task to finish, retries only once with Retry, and sends an SNS notification with Catch. Lambda has a maximum execution time of 15 minutes, so it cannot complete a 40-minute job. EC2 Auto Scaling leaves instance patching and operational burden in place. Rewriting in Glue requires developing the logic anew, which conflicts with the requirement to minimize code changes. Because of the combined constraints of a 40-minute run and minimal code changes, the container approach, which has no execution time limit and only needs to wrap the existing program, is the deciding factor. Because the 40-minute run and minimal code changes appear together, the container approach, which has no execution time limit and only needs to wrap the existing program, is the deciding factor.

exam-sap-c02-11.prompt: An OTT streaming company stores subscriber-only HLS video in Amazon S3. Each video is split into thousands of segment files, and the segments and the manifest are under the same path prefix. Only users with a valid subscription must be able to play the video, and the login server already determines subscription status. The bucket must not be directly accessible by any path, and signing a URL for every segment would make the player implementation and signing cost too high. The content must be delivered to viewers worldwide with low latency, and the cache hit ratio must also be kept high. The player team has 4 people across iOS, Android, and web, so they want to minimize client changes. Concurrent viewers number 50,000 on a normal day and grow to hundreds of thousands on days when a popular drama is released. The original videos are in a bucket in the Seoul Region, and it is sufficient to check subscription status once at login. The current player supports both URLs with appended query strings and cookies, but it has no feature to fetch a new segment list URL each time. A video is typically 90 minutes long, with about 2,700 segments. Which access control method has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allow public read on the bucket but set a bucket policy that denies requests without a custom Referer header sent by CloudFront, and give subscribers only the CloudFront domain. Distribute the allowed header value by embedding it in both the mobile app and web player code.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Each time a subscriber opens a video, have the backend generate S3 presigned URLs for thousands of segments at once, pass them to the player, and set a short expiration time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a CloudFront signed URL for each segment and put them all inside the manifest file, and allow both the path through CloudFront and the direct path to the origin S3 bucket.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a CloudFront distribution and apply a bucket policy to the S3 origin that allows only Origin Access Control, and after the subscriber logs in, issue signed cookies that allow access to the entire path pattern.

exam-sap-c02-11.explanation: The correct answer is OAC with CloudFront signed cookies. OAC lets S3 be read only by CloudFront, and signed cookies allow access to multiple files at once without changing URLs, which suits thousands of segments. The Referer header approach is easily forged and, because the bucket is public, does not block direct access. Mass-generating presigned URLs conflicts with the constraint of per-segment signing and also loses the CloudFront caching benefits. Per-segment signed URLs have the same problem, and leaving the direct path open allows bypass access. Because per-segment signing is a burden and the cache hit ratio must be maintained, signed cookies, which allow the whole path pattern at once without changing URLs, are the deciding answer. Because per-segment signing is a burden and the cache hit ratio must be maintained, signed cookies, which allow the whole path without changing URLs, are the deciding answer.

exam-sap-c02-12.prompt: A delivery company's order API (on Amazon ECS) synchronously calls an external label issuing service for each order. When the issuing service slows down, the API times out and orders are lost. Several hundred requests per second arrive during promotion periods. Orders must be processed at least once without loss, failed requests must be reprocessable later, and duplicate processing of an order is acceptable but omission is not. The label issuing service is operated by an external vendor and has a call limit. There are two developers and the next promotion is in 3 weeks, so large structural changes are difficult. Order data is currently stored in Amazon RDS, and the label issuing response is later used to print waybills. The issuing service averages 200 ms response time but rises to tens of seconds during outages. The environment already has other services that use Amazon SQS and the team knows how to use it, while introducing a new service takes a month for security approval. The cost increase must be within 10% per month. Which improvement MOST appropriately increases stability while minimizing changes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase the API timeout to 5 minutes and increase the number of retries so that it waits until the label issuing service recovers, and also increase the load balancer idle timeout.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have the API put orders in an Amazon SQS standard queue and respond immediately, have a consumer call the label issuing service, and send messages that repeatedly fail to a dead-letter queue (DLQ).

choices.label: C
choices.text: Double the number of ECS tasks to increase the number of concurrent calls to the label issuing service.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Accumulate orders in an in-memory queue inside the API container and have a separate thread call the label issuing service asynchronously.

exam-sap-c02-12.explanation: Decoupling the request from the processing with SQS means that even if the issuing service is slow, orders are stored safely in the queue and are not lost, the consumer processes them at its own pace, and a standard queue guarantees at-least-once delivery, while messages that repeatedly fail are isolated in a DLQ so they can be reprocessed later. Increasing timeouts and retries ties up API threads for a long time, spreads the outage, and leaves the risk of order loss unchanged. Adding tasks applies even more concurrent calls to the slow issuing service and can worsen the situation. An in-memory queue loses orders when the container restarts, which violates the requirement to prevent loss. The conditions that omission is not allowed and duplicates are allowed match the at-least-once delivery of a standard queue, and because there is a call limit, a structure in which the consumer controls the rate is needed. The conditions that omission is not allowed and duplicates are allowed match the at-least-once delivery of a standard queue, and because there is a call limit, a structure in which the consumer controls the rate is needed.

exam-sap-c02-13.prompt: A data analytics company exchanges about 40 TB per day with Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB from private subnets in 6 VPCs in the same Region. All of this traffic passes through NAT gateways, and NAT data processing charges amount to tens of thousands of dollars per month, a large share of the monthly cost. All callers are workloads inside VPCs in the same Region, and there is no on-premises access. The security team has agreed to a policy that allows access to S3 and DynamoDB only through paths inside the VPC. The applications were delivered by an outside vendor, so the code cannot be changed, and the infrastructure team has permission to modify the route tables of each VPC directly. All S3 buckets are in the same Region, and only DynamoDB tables in this Region are used. There are 18 NAT gateways in total, one in each of 3 Availability Zones per VPC, and other traffic going out to the internet is about 5% of the total. The applications use the default AWS SDK endpoint names as is, and some subnets within the same VPC use different route tables. The security team wants to attach resource policies to the endpoints to allow only specific buckets. Which method reduces cost the MOST without changing application code?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create interface VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB in every Availability Zone and turn on private DNS so that traffic does not pass through the NAT gateways.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create one more NAT gateway per Availability Zone to spread traffic and lower the throughput burden per gateway.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the private subnets to public subnets and assign public IP addresses to the instances so that they send traffic directly through an internet gateway.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create gateway VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB and associate them with the private subnet route tables.

exam-sap-c02-13.explanation: Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB have no additional charge, and simply adding a route to the route table keeps same-Region traffic from passing through the NAT gateway, so under the condition that there is no on-premises access, they reduce NAT processing charges the most. Interface endpoints have hourly and processing charges, so they are less cost-efficient than gateway endpoints. Adding NAT gateways spreads throughput, but data processing charges and hourly charges actually increase. Changing subnets to public exposes the instances to the internet, which harms the security requirement, and the structural change is too large. The conditions that there is no on-premises access and that route table modification is permitted make gateway endpoints possible, and the absence of additional charges separates them from interface endpoints in cost. The conditions that there is no on-premises access and that route table modification is possible make gateway endpoints possible, and the absence of additional charges separates them from interface endpoints in cost.

exam-sap-c02-14.prompt: A fintech company wants to use Security Hub CSPM across 200 accounts in its organization. The security team wants to view the findings of all accounts from a separate security tooling account, and wants the same security standards and controls to be enabled automatically, without human intervention, when a new account is added to the organization. The management account is accessed only by billing staff, so the company does not want to use it for security work. The security team already uses the same security tooling account as the delegated administrator account for other security services and wants to keep that account structure, and uses only a single Region, Seoul. The 200 accounts are divided into 12 OUs, and the standards and controls to enable differ by OU, for example applying only core standards to the development OU. The security team has 4 people, and about 10 new accounts are created per month through the Control Tower account factory. The findings must be viewable on a single screen in the security tooling account. Currently, each account owner changes Security Hub CSPM settings separately, and the enabled controls differ even within the same OU, which drew an audit finding. The audit is scheduled for the beginning of next quarter, so configuration drift must be eliminated before then. Which method meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Designate the management account as the Security Hub CSPM administrator, and have the security team manually add each new account as a member whenever one is created.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have each account enable Security Hub CSPM independently, and run a script for each new account that connects it to the security tooling account by the invitation method.

choices.label: C
choices.text: From the management account, designate the security tooling account as the Security Hub CSPM delegated administrator, and have the delegated administrator associate central configuration policies with OUs so that standards and controls are applied automatically to new accounts as well.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Export each account's Security Hub CSPM findings to Amazon S3 and query them together with Amazon Athena from the security tooling account, and have each account administrator enable security standards and configure controls themselves.

exam-sap-c02-14.explanation: With AWS Organizations integration, the management account designates the security tooling account as the delegated administrator, and the delegated administrator can enable member accounts and apply service, standard, and control settings to OUs and accounts by using central configuration policies. This meets the requirement for automatic application to new accounts and separates the management account from security work. Using the management account as the administrator is not recommended; even if chosen, Security Hub CSPM would have to be enabled directly in that account, and adding members manually also conflicts with the requirement. A script using the invitation method is manual work that must be run for every new account. S3 export and Athena solve only viewing the findings, not automatic application of standards. The constraint that different standards per OU must be automatically applied to new accounts is satisfied only by associating central configuration policies at the OU level.

exam-sap-c02-15.prompt: A corporate group is building a data lake in Amazon S3 and the AWS Glue Data Catalog in a central data account, and analysts in 10 business accounts query it with Amazon Athena. The customer table has personal information columns, so some departments must not be able to see those columns, and regional subsidiary departments must be able to see only the rows for their own region. Analysts connect to Athena with a different IAM role in each business account, and the security audit must be able to trace through AWS CloudTrail who queried which columns. There are about 300 analysts and 4 regional subsidiaries, the source data is loaded once a day, and column definitions occasionally change. The data team has 3 people and cannot manage policies for each department individually, and a new business account must be able to start analysis within a week. For audit response, column access records must be retained for 1 year, and the Glue Data Catalog currently has 120 tables divided into customer, transaction, and product domains. Only some departments can see personal information columns. Which method meets these requirements while minimizing data copying and policy duplication as business accounts keep increasing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In each business account, create a copy dataset with a Glue ETL job that removes the personal information columns and other regions' rows, store it in that account's S3 bucket, and have analysts query the copy with Athena. Set up a schedule that reruns the transformation job to refresh the copy whenever the source changes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add an access-allow statement for each business account to the central S3 bucket policy, store regional data under different prefixes, and control access at the prefix level.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Separate Athena workgroups per business account and configure the query result location and data usage limits so that the workgroup restricts the data scope analysts can query.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Define permissions in AWS Lake Formation with LF-Tags and column-level and row-level data filters, and grant them cross-account to the IAM roles or groups of the business accounts so that Athena sees only filtered results.

exam-sap-c02-15.explanation: The correct answer is Lake Formation fine-grained permissions. Column exclusion, row filters, and LF-Tag-based access control can be defined centrally and shared cross-account, so filters are enforced in Athena queries, and the setup scales with tags even as accounts increase. Creating per-account copies makes storage and ETL operations grow in proportion to the number of accounts and risks drifting from the source. S3 bucket policies and prefixes cannot control access at the column level and cannot filter rows. Workgroup settings handle only the result location and scan limits and cannot restrict the data a user can view. With a data team of 3 and a growing number of accounts, tag-based central permissions eliminate the copy approach and the duplicated-policy approach.

exam-sap-c02-16.prompt: A healthcare data company backs up Amazon EBS and Amazon RDS data with AWS Backup. Even if a workload account is compromised by ransomware and administrator credentials are stolen, the backups must not be deleted, and copies must also exist in another Region. The company uses AWS Organizations, and regulations require that deletion be impossible before the retention period ends. The backup targets are EBS volumes and RDS instances, and the retention period is at least 365 days under regulations. Access to the backup account must be limited to the security team, and workload account administrators must not have access. The targets are 300 EBS volumes and 40 RDS instances in the Seoul Region, and backups are performed daily by an AWS Backup plan. The security team has 2 people, and the incident response drill assumes a scenario in which an attacker tries to delete the backup vault using administrator permissions in the workload account. Recovery must be done from an uncompromised copy. The current retention policy keeps daily backups for 35 days but will be extended to 365 days to meet regulations. The company accepts the cost increase but wants to leave no path by which a recovery point could be tampered with or deleted. Which two actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode to the target vault, set a minimum retention period, and let the lock be finalized after the grace time passes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Copy backups only to a vault in another Region of the same account, and block deletion by denying backup:DeleteRecoveryPoint in an IAM policy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create the target vault in a dedicated backup account within the organization, and have the workload accounts' backup plans perform cross-account and cross-Region copies to this vault in another Region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Apply Vault Lock in governance mode to the workload account vault and grant the IAM role with delete permission only to the security team. Set the retention period to at least 365 days and minimize the roles that have delete permission.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Export the EBS snapshots to an S3 bucket, turn on cross-Region replication, and deny deletion with a bucket policy to replace the AWS Backup vault.

exam-sap-c02-16.explanation: The correct answer is cross-account, cross-Region copies to a separate backup account together with Vault Lock in compliance mode. Even if an account is compromised, the vault in the separate account cannot be accessed, and in compliance mode, once the grace time ends, no one (including AWS) can release the lock or delete a recovery point before the retention period ends. Governance mode can be released by an authorized user, so it could be bypassed with stolen administrator credentials. Copying within the same account together with an IAM deny policy is neutralized if the compromised administrator changes the policy. Exporting snapshots to S3 bypasses the recovery point management of AWS Backup and can be released by a policy change. Because of the premise that administrator credentials are stolen, same-account settings or locks that can be released do not serve as a line of defense.

exam-sap-c02-17.prompt: An e-commerce company's Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster runs in only one Region, Seoul. To prepare for a Regional failure, the RPO must be a few seconds and the RTO within a few minutes, and the company also wants to lower read latency for users in Tokyo. The current DR is limited to copying a snapshot to another Region once a day. Tokyo users are 30% of all users, most of their activity is reads, and it is acceptable for writes to occur only in Seoul. Management wants to run DR drills twice a year. The current cluster consists of 1 writer and 2 readers, and the data is about 6 TB. Read latency for Tokyo users averages 70 ms and has drawn many complaints, and the application already uses separate read and write endpoints. The additional monthly budget must be within 40% of the current database cost. Last quarter, a partial service outage in the Seoul Region stopped the order system for 2 hours, so management has demanded a Region-level recovery mechanism. Changing the application connection string during failover is already automated. Which method MOST appropriately meets the requirements without changing the database engine?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Shorten the snapshot copy interval to 5 minutes and automate the restore procedure in the Tokyo Region to restore during a failure.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add Multi-AZ readers to the Seoul cluster and send Tokyo users' reads to these readers by using DNS geolocation routing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Convert to an Aurora global database and add a secondary cluster in the Tokyo Region, use it for reads during normal operation, and promote the secondary cluster during a failure.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Install MySQL directly on Amazon EC2 instances in the Tokyo Region and configure manual replication with the binary log (binlog). During a failure, promote this instance and then replace the application connection information.

exam-sap-c02-17.explanation: An Aurora global database replicates to the secondary Region by using dedicated infrastructure, usually with latency of under 1 second, promotes the secondary cluster to the new primary during a Regional failure, and also lowers read latency for users in the nearby Region during normal operation. Snapshots take time to restore even when the copy interval is shortened, so they cannot meet an RPO of a few seconds and an RTO of a few minutes. Multi-AZ readers in the same Region handle only Availability Zone failures and do not protect against a Regional failure. EC2 binlog replication must be operated yourself, and the risks of replication lag and the promotion procedure are large, which is unfavorable for the required RTO and operational burden. The constraint of requiring both an RPO of a few seconds and an RTO of a few minutes without changing the engine is met only by storage-level cross-Region replication.

exam-sap-c02-18.prompt: A core services company protects EBS volumes and RDS databases in 35 production accounts with AWS Backup. To prepare for a breach, it wants to keep backup copies in a separate dedicated backup account so that the copies cannot be deleted even if a production account is taken over, and it wants the same policy to be applied automatically to new accounts. Copies must move only within the same organization. Under regulations, backup copies cannot leave the organization, restore drills are performed every quarter in the backup account, and 2 to 3 new production accounts are created each month. The production accounts are spread across 8 OUs, and each account's team creates its own backup plan, so retention periods vary. The security team limits access to the backup account to a separate team of 3 people, and the audit team verifies that the copies are healthy with restore drills twice a year. In the regulatory audit, auditors directly check whether backup copies can be deleted with administrator permissions of a production account, and access logs of the backup account are forwarded to a separate log archive account. New account onboarding is automated. Which configuration MOST appropriately meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply vault lock to the existing vaults in the production accounts, make no copies to another account, and have each account keep backups in its own vault.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Designate the default backup vault of the dedicated backup account as the copy destination so that the backup plans of all accounts in the organization write copies to this vault.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have a Lambda function in each production account call the snapshot sharing API to share the EBS and RDS snapshots with the backup account, and have the backup account owner create copies manually.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable cross-account backup in the management account, create in the backup account a vault encrypted with a customer managed KMS key together with a resource policy that allows only CopyIntoBackupVault from accounts in the organization, and use an organization backup policy to apply a copy rule to that vault in the backup plans of all accounts.

exam-sap-c02-18.explanation: AWS Backup cross-account copy requires turning on the feature in the management account, a resource policy on the destination account's vault that allows CopyIntoBackupVault, and a shareable customer managed key. If an Organizations backup policy automatically applies a backup plan containing the copy rule to the accounts in an OU, new accounts are included as well. The default vault is encrypted with a key that cannot be shared with other accounts, so it cannot be a copy destination. Vault lock alone in the same account does not satisfy the requirement to keep copies in a separate account. Manual snapshot sharing violates the requirements for automation and automatic application to new accounts and has a large operational burden. Because each account's plan differs and new accounts keep increasing, deploying the rule in bulk with an organization backup policy separates this option from the manual and single-account approaches.

exam-sap-c02-19.prompt: A company is gradually migrating a web service that it ran on premises under a single domain to AWS. To reduce risk in the new AWS environment, it first sends only 5% of requests, then increases to 25% and 100%, and if problems appear it must be able to send most traffic back to on premises within minutes. The domain visible to users must not change. The web servers in both on premises and AWS keep session information in a shared store so that users stay logged in whichever side they reach. Each environment has a health check endpoint. There are two load balancers on premises and an ALB in AWS, and both are accessed over HTTPS. The migration proceeds over 6 weeks, and each stage is observed for at least a day. Some users go through corporate proxies, but most clients respect the DNS TTL. The AWS environment has already completed load testing, and the on-premises data center will maintain its capacity until the contract ends. The operations team wants a way to roll back instantly with a few clicks if user impact is suspected during the cutover, and wants to avoid adding a new proxy server. Which cutover method is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the domain record at once to a CNAME with a one-day TTL pointing to the AWS endpoint, and keep documented operating procedures for reverting the record to the on-premises value if a problem occurs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create Amazon Route 53 weighted routing records for the on-premises and AWS endpoints with a short TTL, change the two weights in sequence to 95:5, 75:25, and 0:100, attach a health check to each record, and roll back by setting the AWS weight to 0 if there is a problem.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use Route 53 geolocation routing to send only users in some countries to AWS, adjust the ratio by adding countries to the list sent to AWS at each stage, respond to problems by removing countries from the list again, and tally the number of users per country in advance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Register on-premises as the primary origin and AWS as the secondary origin in a CloudFront distribution origin group so that requests go to AWS only when the primary origin fails. Set the origin failover criteria to 5xx response status codes and also monitor the secondary origin's response latency.

exam-sap-c02-19.explanation: The correct answer is weighted routing with a low TTL. Requests are split by the weight ratio of the two records, so you can increase gradually starting at 95:5, then 75:25, then 0:100. The same domain is kept, and because the TTL is short, setting the AWS weight to 0 returns most clients that honor the TTL to on premises within minutes. A one-time cutover with a one-day TTL is not a gradual migration, and rollback also takes hours because of caching. Geolocation routing distributes by country, so ratio control is coarse and it cannot send only some of the users in the same country. An origin group is a failover that goes to the secondary only when the primary origin fails and is not a ratio-based distribution. Because sessions are in a shared store and users stay logged in on either side, ratio-based distribution and rollback with a short TTL are the key.

exam-sap-c02-20.prompt: A manufacturer's local apps at 10 factories read and write drawing files over SMB file shares. Recent files are opened frequently and WAN latency is high, so the on-site apps must access files at local speed. The company wants to keep all of the data in Amazon S3 to reduce cost with lifecycle policies and to reduce replacement of on-site storage devices. It does not want to change the on-site apps. Each factory has about 100 Mbps of internet bandwidth, and drawing files average 200 MB. Files worked on in the last 2 weeks account for most access, and old files are rarely opened. The 10 factories are in Korea, and each server room has a hypervisor that can host a virtual appliance. Drawings are rarely modified after the design is finalized and the headquarters design team also views them, so the company wants to consolidate them in one central repository (S3), and the current NAS devices are aging and must be replaced within 3 years. Designers have complained when response latency for opening a drawing exceeds 1 second, and the factory server rooms have no spare power or space for additional equipment. Local storage capacity is sufficient if each factory keeps only the most recent 2 weeks of data. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add AWS Direct Connect for each factory and create Amazon FSx for Windows File Server in AWS so that the on-site apps mount the SMB share directly over the WAN. Configure the FSx file system as Multi-AZ and also add a dedicated circuit for each factory.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deploy an Amazon S3 File Gateway as a virtual appliance at each factory to provide the SMB share, keep recent files in the local cache, and have the gateway store the data in S3.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Copy the data on each factory's NAS to S3 once a day with AWS DataSync, and have the on-site apps continue to use the existing NAS as is, using S3 only as a backup.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an Amazon EFS file system, mount it over NFS from the factory servers through VPN, and change the settings so that the on-site apps use an NFS path instead of SMB.

exam-sap-c02-20.explanation: The correct answer is S3 File Gateway. A gateway deployed on site provides SMB, serves recent files from the local cache with low latency, stores the data as S3 objects so that lifecycle and cost optimization can be used, and requires no app changes. Mounting FSx remotely and directly passes the WAN latency straight to the apps. A daily DataSync copy does not reduce on-site storage replacement and uses S3 only as a backup. EFS supports only NFS, so the SMB apps would have to change and the latency requirement could not be met. The two conditions that a local cache is needed because of WAN latency and that the SMB apps cannot be changed lead to choosing the gateway.

exam-sap-c02-21.prompt: A corporate group manages 4,000 employees and department groups in Okta and gives them access to 90 accounts in AWS Organizations. Employees must access the console and CLI by signing in with Okta, joins, departures, and department transfers must be reflected in AWS permissions through Okta changes alone, and IAM users or SAML providers must not be created in each account. There is a security requirement that a departed employee's access be cut off on the same day, and developers must work from the CLI with temporary credentials and no long-term access keys. Okta has 60 department groups, and the accounts and permissions each department can access differ. The accounts are divided into 6 OUs, the cloud team has 5 people, and a separate IT team manages Okta. For external audits, sign-in records of who accessed which account must be kept. In the past, IAM users of departed employees remained in some accounts and were flagged in a security audit. Developers require a flow in which they sign in with SSO and then receive short-term credentials in the terminal to run the CLI and IaC tools, and MFA is already enforced in Okta. Which configuration meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Register Okta as a SAML identity provider in each account, create IAM roles, and configure Okta app assignments per department as many times as there are accounts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create users manually in AWS IAM Identity Center and have an administrator update group membership directly in the console when a department transfer occurs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have a Lambda function that reads Okta user information every day create and delete IAM users in each account and distribute long-term access keys to the owners.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Connect Okta as the external identity provider of IAM Identity Center, automatically provision users and groups with SCIM, and then assign permission sets to groups and deploy them to the accounts in the OUs.

exam-sap-c02-21.explanation: IAM Identity Center automatically synchronizes users and groups from an external IdP by using SCIM, so Okta joins, departures, and department transfers are reflected on the AWS side, and assigning permission sets to groups deploys them to multiple accounts at once, so no IAM users or SAML providers are needed per account. Registering a SAML provider in each account increases configuration in proportion to the number of accounts and makes change management difficult. Manual user creation violates the requirement that changes in Okta alone be reflected and leaves human intervention. Creating IAM users with Lambda and distributing long-term access keys increases long-term credentials and is the worst from a security standpoint. In an organization where Okta management and the cloud team are separate, the constraint of making changes in only one place requires SCIM automatic provisioning.

exam-sap-c02-22.prompt: A company accumulates hundreds of GB per day of gzip-compressed CSV logs in Amazon S3 and queries them with Amazon Athena. Most queries use only data from the last 7 days and only five or six of the 40 columns, but every query reads all the files, so query time and cost keep increasing. The company does not want to re-ingest the data, so a job that reads the existing logs and writes the transformed results to a new location is allowed. The analytics team requires that query results be the same as before. The monthly Athena cost currently reaches several thousand dollars, and logs are retained for 1 year. The table is registered in the AWS Glue Data Catalog, existing queries already include a date column condition, and the transformation job can be run once a night. The analytics tool uses only Athena SQL. Analysts run queries directly in the Athena console, and a BI tool reads the same table. The data is already stored under date-based prefixes in S3, but the table definition has no partition information and the files are small, so queries take a long time. Which two methods reduce the cost by reducing the amount Athena scans without re-ingesting the data? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Store the transformed results partitioned by date and use the partition key in the query WHERE condition to reduce the range that is read.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Move the log objects in S3 to the Standard-IA storage class to lower the per-object storage cost, which also reduces the query scan cost.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase the number of concurrent queries in the Athena workgroup so that more queries process the same amount of data at once. Set a cost limit on the workgroup to automatically stop queries that exceed it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Convert the logs to a columnar format such as Parquet with an AWS Glue job or Athena CTAS so that only the needed columns are read.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Change the queries to SELECT * to read all columns at once and have the client application pick out the columns it needs.

exam-sap-c02-22.explanation: The correct answer is converting to a columnar format and date partitioning. Athena cost is determined by the amount of data scanned, so Parquet or ORC reads only the needed column blocks and also compresses well, and date partitions prevent reading data other than the last 7 days. The number of concurrent queries is a throughput setting and does not reduce the amount scanned. Standard-IA is a storage cost item and is separate from query scan charges. SELECT * reads all columns and actually increases the amount scanned, so it is the opposite of the requirement. Since Athena cost is proportional to the amount scanned, changing the storage class or concurrency has nothing to do with reducing query cost.

exam-sap-c02-23.prompt: A healthcare company's security account centrally controls its encryption policy with a customer managed AWS KMS key, and ETL roles in 12 application accounts of the organization must use this key to encrypt and decrypt objects in their own accounts' S3 buckets with SSE-KMS. Key management permissions must remain only in the security account, and application accounts must not be able to delete the key or change the key policy. The audit team wants key usage records to also be visible in the security account, and the key permissions granted to the application accounts must follow the principle of least privilege, limited to the needed operations. The ETL roles in the application accounts perform the S3 load every morning, and AWS Glue jobs also use the same key. Key rotation is managed by the security account with automatic rotation once a year. The development teams do not need to read or change the key policy. The security team aggregates key usage events through AWS CloudTrail in the security account and uses an SCP to prevent application accounts from switching to different keys. The key description document already states that application accounts cannot create keys themselves. Which configuration MOST appropriately meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allow kms:* on the security account key ARN only in the IAM policies of the application account roles, leave the key policy in its existing state allowing only the security account root, and review key usage with CloudTrail.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have the security account key policy allow only the encrypt, decrypt, and generate data key operations for the application accounts, and have the IAM policies of the roles in the application accounts allow the same operations on that key ARN.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only add a statement allowing the application accounts to the security account key policy, and add no separate IAM policy on the application account side.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Have the application account S3 buckets use the AWS managed key aws/s3, and have the security account control access by being shared the policy of this key.

exam-sap-c02-23.explanation: Cross-account KMS use requires both that the key policy in the account that owns the key allow the external account (or role) and that the external account's IAM policy delegate that permission. If the key policy opens only cryptographic operations such as encrypt, decrypt, and GenerateDataKey, the permissions to delete the key or change the policy do not go to the external account. A configuration with only an IAM policy has no effect because the key policy does not allow it. A configuration with only a key policy cannot be used because the principals in the external account have no IAM permissions. AWS managed keys have policies that cannot be modified, so they cannot be shared cross-account and cannot meet the central control requirement. To keep key management permissions in the security account, the scope of operations opened to the external account in the key policy must be limited.

exam-sap-c02-24.prompt: A company runs 1,200 Amazon EC2 instances across 25 accounts. A security review recommended allowing only IMDSv2 because of SSRF risk, but it is unknown whether some older applications use IMDSv1, so switching everything at once risks outages. The company wants to switch in stages without outages and also to prevent new instances from being created with v1 afterward. Some instances are frequently replaced by Auto Scaling, and software fixes are handled by each development team. The security team must complete the switch within 6 weeks, and outages during the switch are not allowed. Most instances run Amazon Linux, and some start from in-house AMIs, with new AMIs built weekly by an image builder pipeline. The security team wants to see switch progress across all accounts at a glance and can collect Amazon CloudWatch metrics. Some teams use third-party agents that use IMDSv1, and the vendor has not said which versions are supported. Launch templates differ by team and are hard to change all at once, and an SCP can be applied across the organization from the management account. Which approach is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use the CloudWatch MetadataNoToken metric to find and fix instances that make IMDSv1 calls, then change the existing instances to require IMDSv2, and use an SCP to deny launching instances that are not set to require it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Change all instances to require IMDSv2 immediately, and revert only the instances where outages are reported to the previous setting.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Block outbound traffic to 169.254.169.254 in security groups to prevent access to the instance metadata altogether.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lower the IMDS response hop limit to 1 and keep both IMDSv1 and IMDSv2 allowed to reduce the risk.

exam-sap-c02-24.explanation: The MetadataNoToken metric tracks IMDSv1 calls, so a staged switch without outages is possible by first changing HttpTokens to required on instances with zero usage and fixing applications that use v1 beforehand, and an SCP that uses the ec2:MetadataHttpTokens condition key prevents new instances from allowing v1. Switching everything at once and then rolling back is a way of causing outages without prior knowledge, so it is not the safest approach. Security groups do not control the link-local metadata address, and blocking it would also prevent receiving IAM role credentials. Adjusting the hop limit keeps v1 allowed and does not eliminate the SSRF risk. Because of the no-outage requirement and the 6-week deadline, only a staged approach that first measures current usage satisfies both constraints.

exam-sap-c02-25.prompt: A global mobile game company reads and writes player profiles in three Regions. Players connect to the nearest Region, and single-digit millisecond write latency is required in every Region. If one Region goes down, the remaining Regions must continue to accept writes, and concurrent edits to the same item from different Regions are rare, so conflicts can be handled with a last-writer-wins approach. A profile item averages 4 KB and traffic varies widely by time of day, which makes capacity hard to predict. The team does not want to build its own sharding or replication lag monitoring code. The Regions are Seoul, Frankfurt, and N. Virginia, and peak concurrent players number 2 million. Most profile access is key-based lookups with no complex joins. The data tier team has 3 people and wants to operate without overnight on-call. The last-writer-wins approach has already been approved by game design. Every quarter the team runs a failure drill that intentionally disconnects one Region during maintenance, and even during the drill players must be able to keep playing from another nearby Region. Profile size may double in the future but is nowhere near the 400 KB limit. Which data tier has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use an Amazon Aurora global database to concentrate writes in the primary Region, and have the other Regions use write forwarding to send writes to the primary Region. Have the application in each Region use the same endpoint through the write forwarding feature.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Write only to an Amazon DynamoDB table in one Region and accelerate reads through DAX clusters in the other Regions, restoring the table and switching over during a Regional failure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure an Amazon ElastiCache Global Datastore in which the primary cluster in one Region handles writes and the secondary Regions handle reads, and promote a secondary during a failure.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure a DynamoDB global table in the three Regions, and have the application in each Region perform reads and writes against its local replica.

exam-sap-c02-25.explanation: The correct answer is a DynamoDB global table. It has a multi-active architecture, so every Regional replica accepts writes locally and gets single-digit millisecond write latency, and even if one Region goes down, the other Regions continue to write. Conflicts are reconciled with last writer wins. With Aurora write forwarding, writes go to the primary Region, which adds long-distance latency and requires promotion if the primary Region fails. DAX is only a read cache and does not solve writes in other Regions. A Global Datastore also accepts writes in only one primary cluster. The requirement for local write latency in every Region eliminates all of the single-write-Region architectures.

exam-sap-c02-26.prompt: A media company runs container-based video encoding batches at night. Each job takes 20 to 40 minutes, jobs are delivered as Amazon SQS messages, and if a job is interrupted and the message becomes visible again, reprocessing does not cause any problem with the results. The company does not want to handle server patching or cluster capacity management, and because the jobs only need to finish within a certain time window, it wants to reduce cost as much as possible. The job image is already in Amazon ECR, each job uses 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of memory, and no GPU is needed. The number of nightly jobs varies from 0 to several hundred depending on the queue length. Encoding results are stored in Amazon S3, and result file names are determined from the input key, so reprocessing overwrites the same file. Jobs average 800 per day and only need to finish before 6 AM, and the container image is about 2 GB. The security team does not allow an operating model in which people connect to servers over SSH. The jobs currently run on 40 on-premises render servers, which have reached the end of their life and are being moved to the cloud. Even if some jobs are interrupted during encoding, the overall schedule is not affected as long as they are reprocessed after the SQS visibility timeout. Which configuration is the MOST cost-effective with low operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run ECS tasks on the Fargate Spot capacity provider, have workers pull and process SQS messages, and let messages become visible again on interruption so that other tasks pick them up.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Invoke a Lambda function through an SQS event source, and set the function memory and timeout to the maximum so that each encoding job finishes in a single Lambda invocation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Install the ECS agent on On-Demand EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group and manage capacity yourself, scaling the number of instances up and down at night with scheduled rules. Add a scheduled scaling rule that reduces the number of instances to 0 during the day.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run ECS tasks on Fargate On-Demand capacity and adjust the number of tasks according to the SQS queue depth, using the interruption protection setting so that encoding tasks are not interrupted.

exam-sap-c02-26.explanation: The correct answer is Fargate Spot. Because it is serverless containers, no patching or cluster capacity management is needed, batch jobs that can tolerate interruption reduce cost with Spot, and if a job is interrupted, the message becomes visible again and is reprocessed. Lambda has a maximum execution time of 15 minutes, so it cannot finish a 20-to-40-minute job in a single invocation. On-Demand EC2 Auto Scaling requires you to manage instance patching and capacity yourself and is also more expensive. Fargate On-Demand has the same operational burden but does not take advantage of the interruption-tolerance condition, so it costs more. The two conditions that reprocessing after interruption is safe and that there is slack in the schedule justify using Spot.

exam-sap-c02-27.prompt: A company is moving an ASP.NET application that runs on SQL Server 2016 to AWS and wants to eliminate SQL Server licensing costs. There are hundreds of stored procedures and T-SQL code, and the application connects with a SQL Server driver. The company wants to minimize application code changes and use a managed service for the database. Some stored procedures might use SQL Server-specific features, so the company wants to understand the extent of that in advance. User traffic cannot be reduced during the migration. The database is about 900 GB, writes are concentrated at month-end close, and the application connects with the ADO.NET SQL Server driver. The development team has 6 people, and while changes on the order of recompiling the .NET code are possible, there is no schedule to completely rewrite the queries. Read traffic must continue during the migration, and the license renewal date is 6 months away. SQL Server licensing currently accounts for most of the database operating cost, so this cost must disappear after the migration, and the company can accept a method of using DMS to catch up on changes for the data migration. Which method is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Migrate to Amazon RDS for SQL Server using license-included instances and keep the code as is, treating the license cost as included in the instance price. Configure high availability with Multi-AZ and choose the license-included model.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable Babelfish on Aurora PostgreSQL, assess T-SQL compatibility with Babelfish Compass, and connect the existing application that uses the TDS protocol with minimal changes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Automatically convert all T-SQL procedures to PL/pgSQL with SCT, load them into Aurora PostgreSQL, and rewrite all of the application's queries and drivers the PostgreSQL way.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Move the SQL Server data to Amazon DynamoDB, reimplement the stored procedure logic as Lambda functions, and change the application to call the DynamoDB API.

exam-sap-c02-27.explanation: The correct answer is Babelfish for Aurora PostgreSQL. Babelfish understands the TDS protocol and the T-SQL dialect, so SQL Server drivers and much of the T-SQL code can be used with minimal changes, and Babelfish Compass analyzes source code to report the compatibility scope and the parts that need modification. Because it is Aurora, there is no SQL Server licensing cost and it is managed. RDS for SQL Server leaves the license cost in place. A full conversion and rewrite conflicts with the requirement to minimize application code changes. Moving to DynamoDB requires redesigning both the data model and the code. The two constraints that there is no schedule to completely rewrite queries and that licensing cost must be eliminated eliminate both RDS for SQL Server and the full conversion approach.

exam-sap-c02-28.prompt: A marketing platform ingests thousands of web clickstream JSON events per second, accumulates them in an Amazon S3 data lake, and analyzes them with Amazon Athena. Analysts mostly query by date and a small number of columns and want to reduce scan cost. There are no real-time consumers, and a delay of a few minutes is acceptable. The event schema rarely changes, and a table can be created in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. There are only two data engineers, so they have no capacity to operate stream consumer code or clusters. There are about 400 million events per day, and analysts usually query the last one to two weeks of data by date and three or four columns. Currently the raw JSON is accumulated as is, so Athena queries read entire objects and are slow and expensive, so the team wants to finish format conversion and date-based partitioned storage at the ingestion stage. The team does not want to receive overnight pages. The ingestion endpoint is called directly by the mobile app and the web SDK, and each event averages 1 KB. Monthly cost must not increase significantly compared with a configuration that has no servers at all. How should the ingestion pipeline be designed to meet this with the simplest configuration and no server operations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ingest with Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, have a Lambda consumer gather JSON in batches and compress it, and store it as large JSON files under a single S3 prefix without date prefixes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream, configure it to convert the record format to Parquet by using the AWS Glue Data Catalog table schema, and store the data in S3 with date-based prefixes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Install a log collector on EC2 instances to receive the events, run a cron script every hour that converts them to Parquet files and uploads them to S3, and manage the instances with Auto Scaling.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ingest events with an Amazon MSK cluster, configure the MSK Connect S3 sink connector to store them in S3 in JSON format as is, and query them directly from Athena. Adjust the number of partitions and broker size as traffic grows.

exam-sap-c02-28.explanation: The correct answer is Amazon Data Firehose. Because it is fully managed, no servers are needed, and it converts JSON to Parquet by using the Glue table schema and stores it under date prefixes, so Athena reads only the needed columns and partitions and scan cost decreases. Data Streams with Lambda requires operating consumer code, and storing JSON without prefixes does not reduce the amount scanned. EC2 collectors and cron violate the requirement of no server operations. MSK and connectors carry a heavy cluster operations burden and storing JSON as is gives no columnar benefit. Because two engineers cannot operate servers, a managed delivery stream that handles format conversion and partitioned storage at the ingestion stage is the answer.

exam-sap-c02-29.prompt: A global logistics company operates a transit gateway in each of the Seoul and N. Virginia Regions, each connecting 8 VPCs. Private communication between VPCs in the two Regions is required, and the traffic must not traverse the internet and must be encrypted on the AWS global network. The company wants to avoid managing VPN tunnels and a full mesh of VPC peering. The VPC CIDRs in the two Regions do not overlap, regular data replication traffic is several TB per day so bandwidth must be stable, and there are 2 network staff. The Seoul and N. Virginia transit gateways are owned by different accounts, replication between the two Regions runs 24 hours a day, and latency must be stable at around 100 ms. Communication between the two Regions currently uses a temporary VPN over the public internet, and the security team has demanded that it be eliminated within a month. Static routing changes are acceptable. The routing policies in the two Regions are managed by different teams per account, and the procedure for accepting the connection request needs to be done only once. The company wants availability to be provided on an AWS-managed foundation. Which configuration MOST appropriately meets the requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a Site-to-Site VPN attachment on each Regional transit gateway, connect them to each other with IPsec tunnels over the public internet, and have them learn the other Region's routes with BGP.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a peering attachment between the two transit gateways and accept it, then add the other Region's VPC CIDRs as static routes pointing to the peering attachment in both route tables.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create VPC peering between every pair of VPCs in the two Regions and connect them in a full mesh, and use the transit gateways only for communication within a Region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: After creating the peering attachment, enable route propagation for the peering attachment in the route tables so that the other Region's CIDRs are learned automatically.

exam-sap-c02-29.explanation: Transit gateway peering supports inter-Region connections: when one side requests, the other owner accepts, traffic travels encrypted over the AWS network, and for routing you must add static routes pointing to the peering attachment in both tables. Dynamic route propagation to a peering attachment is not supported, so an approach that relies on propagation to learn routes does not work. A VPN over the internet violates both the requirement to avoid the internet and the requirement to avoid managing tunnels. A VPC peering full mesh causes connections to multiply as the number of VPCs grows, which conflicts with the requirement to avoid a full mesh. Because the company needs to avoid VPN and full-mesh peering and needs encrypted, stable bandwidth on the AWS backbone, TGW peering with static routes on both sides is the answer.

exam-sap-c02-30.prompt: A company in a regulated industry wants, across 150 organization accounts and 3 Regions, to (1) see noncompliant resources (unencrypted EBS volumes and security groups with port 22 open) on a single screen and (2) have the same set of rules deployed automatically to new accounts. Rule management is handled by the security tooling account, and the management account is accessed only by billing staff. The noncompliance criteria are unencrypted EBS volumes and security groups that have port 22 open, and the security team does not want to create rules separately in each account. Results from the three Regions must be viewable in the same place. Currently, Config rules are created by hand in each account, so rule names and thresholds differ, and many of the 150 new accounts are left without rules for several weeks after onboarding. The audit firm requires a status screen of noncompliant resources every quarter, and the security team has 3 people. The team wants to manage the rules as code. The follow-up procedure in which the responsible account team is notified when a noncompliant resource is found is already configured with Amazon EventBridge and is outside the scope of this work. The three target Regions are the same for all accounts. Which actions must be taken to meet the requirements while reducing operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Have each account export AWS Config snapshots to Amazon S3, and directly aggregate noncompliant items with Athena queries from the security tooling account.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From the delegated administrator account, deploy organization Config rules or conformance packs so that common rules are applied automatically to the target accounts and are also deployed when an account is added.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Approve the aggregator authorization in each account individually, and repeat the same approval procedure every time a new account is created.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable the Trusted Advisor organizational view to check noncompliant resources in bulk instead of using Config rules.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Create an AWS Config organization aggregator in the security tooling account to aggregate configuration and compliance data from all accounts and Regions in one place.

exam-sap-c02-30.explanation: An organization aggregator collects configuration and compliance data from all accounts and Regions in the organization into the delegated administrator account without individual approvals, enabling a single-screen view. When the delegated administrator deploys organization Config rules or conformance packs, the same rules are applied in bulk to the target accounts, and they are deployed together when a new account joins. Approving aggregator authorization account by account is the older approach that increases manual work without organization integration. Athena aggregation must be built yourself and does not solve automatic rule deployment. Trusted Advisor cannot replace custom compliance checks based on Config rules or the deployment of rule sets. The two requirements, deploying rules in bulk as code and viewing the results in one place, call for organization rule deployment and an aggregator, respectively.

exam-sap-c02-31.prompt: A bank connects its on-premises data center to AWS with AWS Direct Connect and operates a hybrid environment during the migration period. Audit requirements say that all traffic on every segment must be encrypted with IPsec and must not pass over the internet. A Direct Connect connection is not encrypted by default. The bank uses a transit gateway because there are multiple VPCs. The on-premises network and three AWS VPCs are already connected through the transit gateway, and Direct Connect is a 10 Gbps dedicated connection. The security team wants to exchange routes dynamically with BGP. On premises there are two routers that support BGP, and VPN equipment is also available. Under the bank's regulations, encryption must be configured with AWS service features, and the path must switch automatically during a failure. The migration period is 18 months and the transfer volume averages about 4 Gbps. An internet VPN is currently being used temporarily for development, and an audit flagged this path for retirement. The network team has 3 people and wants to keep using BGP rather than introduce a new routing protocol. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use a transit virtual interface attached to a Direct Connect gateway, and create a private IP Site-to-Site VPN connection on the transit gateway that uses Direct Connect as the transport, encrypting the traffic with IPsec.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure only a Direct Connect private virtual interface and connect with private IP addresses, and document that, because it is a dedicated circuit, the audit requirement is met without any separate encryption.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure a Site-to-Site VPN over the internet separately from Direct Connect, send all traffic through the VPN, and keep the dedicated circuit only as an inactive backup for failures.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an AWS Client VPN endpoint for each VPC and have on-premises servers connect as individual clients to encrypt server-to-server communication over Direct Connect. Collect connection logs with Amazon CloudWatch and issue certificates per user.

exam-sap-c02-31.explanation: The correct answer is a private IP VPN. If you create a Site-to-Site VPN connection on the transit gateway that uses Direct Connect as the transport, the tunnels are built with private IP addresses, IPsec encryption is applied, and the traffic does not pass over the internet. This requires a Direct Connect gateway and a transit virtual interface. Using only a private virtual interface has no default encryption even on a dedicated circuit, so it does not meet the requirement. An internet VPN violates the ban on internet paths. Client VPN is an access service for individual users. Because Direct Connect is not encrypted by default and internet paths are prohibited, an IPsec configuration over the dedicated connection is required.

exam-sap-c02-32.prompt: At an e-commerce company, three teams (payments, shipping, and analytics) subscribe to a single order-created event. The payments team must receive only orders of 1 million KRW or more, the shipping team only domestic shipping orders, and the analytics team all orders. A failure in one team's consumer must not affect the other teams' processing, and each team must be able to retry independently. The company wants to minimize code changes to the publishing service. Messages carry the order amount and shipping country as message attributes, and each team's consumer processes at a different speed and may stop temporarily. The company does not want to deploy the publishing service every time a team is added. Orders arrive at 1,000 per second at peak, and the payments team's consumer stops for several hours a day for maintenance, during which messages must not be lost. The analytics team may add more consumers in the long term. The publishing service currently runs on Amazon ECS and is operated by a team experienced with AWS SDK calls such as Amazon SNS, and the cost should be on the order of tens of dollars per month. Each team changes its filter conditions often and does not want the order service code or a deployment to be required when conditions change. Even if a consumer fails, messages must be reprocessed within the retention period. Which design is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Have the order service publish to a single Amazon SNS topic only, subscribe a separate Amazon SQS queue for each team, and use subscription filter policies based on the amount and shipping country attributes to deliver only the needed messages to each queue.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Change the order service to send messages directly to each of the three teams' SQS queues, and select the destinations inside the publishing code according to the amount and shipping country conditions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Put all orders in one SQS queue and have the three teams' consumers poll the same queue, with each consumer skipping messages that do not match its team's conditions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Have the order service invoke one Lambda function, which checks the conditions and synchronously calls each team's API in sequence, retrying inside the function on failure. Store the processing results in each team's DynamoDB table to check for duplicate processing.

exam-sap-c02-32.explanation: The correct answer is a design that uses SNS fan-out to per-team SQS queues with subscription filter policies. The publisher needs to send to only one topic, the filter policies screen the targets for each team with numeric comparison and string matching, and the per-team queues act as buffers so that one team's failure does not propagate to the others and retries are independent. If the publisher sends directly to multiple queues, the routing logic goes into the publishing code and the change becomes large. With a shared queue, only one consumer receives each message, so per-team delivery does not work. Synchronous Lambda invocation spreads one team's failure into overall latency and failure. Because condition changes must not require changes to the publishing code and one team's failure must not affect the others, one topic with per-team queues and subscription filter policies is the right choice.

exam-sap-c02-33.prompt: An e-commerce company wants to read messages from an order intake Amazon SQS standard queue, look up the customer tier, and process only paid orders with an AWS Step Functions state machine. The customer tier can be obtained only through an external REST API that requires an authentication header. Today the company runs polling and API call code itself on Lambda, which is a heavy maintenance burden. Order messages arrive at several hundred per second, about half of which are paid orders, there is no requirement to process them one at a time in order, and messages for unpaid orders can be discarded in this flow because a separate path already handles them. With a small development staff, the company does not want to write new integration code. The external REST API requires an API key to be sent in a header on every call, and the response contains the customer tier. There is a call limit, so the company wants to control the number of calls per minute, and unnecessary API calls for unpaid messages would increase cost. The state machine has already been built and expects the order and the customer tier as input. The development team has 3 people, and the person who built this flow has left, so nobody understands the hand-written polling code. Reducing the code maintenance burden takes priority over monthly operating cost. Which configuration MOST appropriately minimizes code writing and incurs no cost for messages that are not to be processed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Register the SQS queue directly as an event source on an Amazon EventBridge event bus, match the paid-order condition in a rule, specify the Step Functions state machine as the target, and perform the tier lookup inside the state machine.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Place an Amazon SNS topic in front of the SQS queue and deliver only paid-order messages with a subscription filter policy, and have a subscriber Lambda function call the external API and start the Step Functions execution. Configure the subscriber Lambda function to retry on failure and log the processing results.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deploy a polling application on two EC2 instances to read the queue and perform the filtering, API call, and state machine start, and ensure availability with an Auto Scaling group.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Connect the SQS queue as the source of an Amazon EventBridge Pipe, configure a filter for the paid-order condition, use an API destination as the enrichment, and specify the Step Functions state machine as the target.

exam-sap-c02-33.explanation: The correct answer is EventBridge Pipes. A pipe connects an SQS source, an optional filter, an enrichment step (an API destination can call an external REST API that requires authentication), and a Step Functions target in a single configuration without code, only events that match the filter are billed, and messages from an SQS source that do not match are automatically removed from the queue. An event bus cannot read an SQS queue directly as an event source. Placing SNS in front and using Lambda still means continuing to operate invocation code, and the structure is also not suited to targeting messages already accumulated in SQS. An EC2 polling application only increases the existing burden of direct operations. The conditions of minimizing code writing and avoiding cost for non-target messages point to Pipes, which has source filtering and API destination integration.

exam-sap-c02-34.prompt: A company that runs an online shopping mall with an Auto Scaling group (40 instances in normal times) and Amazon Aurora in the Seoul Region wants to build a DR environment in the Osaka Region. The goals are an RPO within 1 minute and an RTO within 10 minutes, and the current backup-and-restore approach takes 4 hours to recover. The monthly cost of the DR environment must be 30% or less of the production environment, and during a failure the DR Region must be able to immediately handle some traffic and then increase capacity without any separate infrastructure deployment work. Traffic does not stop even late at night, and the VPC, subnets, and security groups are already deployed in the Osaka Region with AWS CloudFormation. The team wants to regularly check the DR environment's operation with a small amount of synthetic traffic. Aurora write traffic averages several hundred requests per second, and the team runs a drill every quarter that assumes a complete outage of the Seoul Region. The team plans for Osaka's minimum running capacity to be about 10 to 20% of the normal 40 instances, and the DNS switch is automated with Amazon Route 53. Management does not want people to manually add servers during each drill. Read latency in the DR Region and the player experience are not important, and the recovery targets are the web tier and the data tier. The synthetic traffic check is entirely feasible with low-capacity servers. Which is the MOST cost-effective DR strategy that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Replicate the data with an Aurora global database, keep a scaled-down web server fleet always running in Osaka, increase Auto Scaling capacity during a failure, and switch traffic with Route 53.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continuously run a web server fleet of the same 40-instance size as Seoul and a writable Aurora configuration in Osaka as well, and use weighted routing so that both Regions handle user requests. Replicate Aurora across the two Regions with a global database to meet the RPO requirement as well.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Maintain only cross-Region AWS Backup copies and AMI copies, and during a failure deploy the entire stack newly in Osaka by using CloudFormation templates and then restore the data from the latest backup.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Replicate the data with an Aurora global database but deploy no web servers, preparing only AMIs and templates, and during a failure launch the instances for the first time and configure the application.
