choices.text: Turn on DMS data validation to compare row-level consistency between the source and the target, and resolve the cause for tables where mismatches are reported before cutover.

exam-sap-c02-60.explanation: The correct answers are data validation and confirming that CDC lag has cleared after stopping writes. Validation finds data mismatches between the source and the target, and if you confirm that CDC lag has disappeared after stopping writes, you can switch over with the last change reflected on the target. CDC has no real-time guarantee and lag can grow to several minutes or more, so confirmation is necessary. reload-target reloads from scratch, which increases downtime and risk and does not automatically guarantee consistency. Stopping the task right away on a source that is still being written to loses changes. Reducing log retention may prevent DMS from reading the logs it needs. Because loss and inconsistency at the switch must be prevented and LOB columns make row counts alone insufficient, both confirming lag clearance after stopping writes and data validation are needed.

exam-sap-c02-61.prompt: A fintech company runs its payment ledger on an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster in us-east-1. Regulations require that, in the event of a complete Regional failure, writes be resumed in another Region within a few minutes and that data loss be within a few seconds. In addition, the analytics team in ap-northeast-2 must be able to query the same data read-only from a nearby Region during normal operation. The current DR copies snapshots to another Region and takes tens of minutes to recover. The application already uses an Aurora MySQL 8.0-compatible version, so replacing the engine or large-scale code changes is difficult, and management requires Region failover drills every quarter. The ledger data is currently about 3 TB and is expected to triple over the next 2 years. Analytics queries run several times a day and must not affect the write cluster. Region failover drills are held quarterly, pausing writes briefly during a drill is acceptable, and the infrastructure is managed with AWS CloudFormation. Management required recovery to a state where writes are possible during a Regional failure, not a read-only state, and the snapshot restore method took 40 minutes in a drill, exceeding the criterion. The application connections are specified only by the cluster endpoint name. Which configuration meets the above requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Schedule cross-Region copies with AWS Backup every 5 minutes, and during a failure restore a new Aurora cluster in ap-northeast-2 from the most recent recovery point and change the connection information. In every drill, create a new cluster with the same procedure and verify normal operation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a separate Aurora MySQL cluster in ap-northeast-2 and synchronize it with an AWS DMS ongoing replication (CDC) task, and during a failure stop the replication task and switch the application over.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add a secondary cluster in ap-northeast-2 with an Aurora global database to handle analytics reads during normal operation, and during a Regional failure promote (fail over) the secondary cluster to the new primary cluster.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Distribute the Aurora replicas of the us-east-1 cluster across three Availability Zones to prepare for Availability Zone failures, and keep the existing snapshot copy procedure for Regional failures.

exam-sap-c02-61.explanation: The correct answer is an Aurora global database. It replicates to the secondary Region with dedicated storage-layer infrastructure, usually with latency of under 1 second, so the RPO is a few seconds, promoting the secondary cluster resumes writes within a few minutes, and during normal operation readers in the secondary Region also handle read queries. Restoring a new cluster from a recovery point has a long restore time like the snapshot approach, so it cannot meet an RTO of a few minutes. DMS CDC has no SLA on replication lag, which can grow to several minutes or more, and the replication task and the switchover procedure must be operated by you. A configuration that only spreads Availability Zones within the same Region does not protect against a complete Regional failure. The requirements of an RTO of a few minutes, an RPO of a few seconds, and nearby reads during normal operation are met by a single global database secondary cluster.

exam-sap-c02-62.prompt: A financial affiliate is building a dedicated network connecting two on-premises data centers to AWS. The target availability SLA for the critical workloads is 99.99%, and connectivity must be maintained even if an entire single AWS Direct Connect location goes down. The company wants to meet this requirement, which goes beyond the development and test level, without ordering more connections than necessary. The two data centers are near Seoul and each requires 10 Gbps or more of bandwidth. The network team wants to order with the connection wizard of the Resiliency Toolkit and to spend on monthly port costs only at the necessary level. The two data centers each have separate ISP circuits and are currently connected only through an internet VPN. The budget owner wants to use only as many locations and ports as needed, but the 99.99% SLA requirement is an audit item and cannot be compromised. Port speed is standardized at 10 Gbps. Traffic from each data center to AWS averages 3 Gbps per day, and an incident in which an entire location went down occurred once in the past. The network team has 4 people and will configure the Direct Connect gateway and virtual interfaces themselves after the wizard. Which configuration is MOST appropriate based on the Direct Connect Resiliency Toolkit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Order two dedicated connections that terminate on different devices at a single Direct Connect location, create a virtual interface on each of the two connections, and make them redundant with BGP.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A Maximum resiliency model in which you order two dedicated connections at each of two or more different Direct Connect locations, with each connection terminating on a different Direct Connect device.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A High resiliency model that orders only one dedicated connection at each of two different locations, terminating on one device per location, and uses both connections as active. Order one 10 Gbps connection per location to lower port cost.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Place one dedicated connection at a single location and configure an internet-based Site-to-Site VPN as a backup path that reroutes BGP routes through the VPN when the dedicated connection fails.

exam-sap-c02-62.explanation: The correct answer is the Maximum resiliency model. Placing connections at two or more locations and terminating each on separate devices tolerates device, connection, and entire location failures and targets the 99.99% SLA. A configuration that only splits devices within one location is the development and test model and is vulnerable to a location failure. The High resiliency model with one connection per location has a target SLA of 99.9%, which falls short of the requirement. A single connection with a VPN backup can survive a location failure but does not satisfy the 99.99% dedicated connection SLA requirement. The requirements of an entire single location failure and a 99.99% SLA point to the Maximum resiliency model with dual connections at different locations.

exam-sap-c02-63.prompt: A securities firm's Java Lambda API receives a rush of requests just before market open between 08:50 and 09:30 on weekdays, and traffic is low at other times. During this period, cold starts cause p99 latency to exceed the SLA. Keeping provisioned concurrency all day would be too costly, and the traffic pattern is the same every day. The function uses Java 17 and takes 3 seconds to initialize, 20 times the usual requests arrive during the 30 minutes just before market open, and latency during the rest of the day is within the SLA. The function is already deployed with published versions and an alias, and the alias is connected to API Gateway. It is enough for capacity to be ready 30 minutes before market open, and there is no market open on weekday holidays. SnapStart is not considered in this scope, and the team has 3 people. The operations team wants to make configuration changes without a code deployment. During the 30 minutes before market open, responses must be within target even when 20 times the usual requests arrive, and after market open, traffic quickly returns to the usual level. The company wants to leave the function memory and code as they are and adjust only the settings. Which method meets the SLA MOST cost-effectively?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set provisioned concurrency on the function's $LATEST version at the market-open peak level and keep it all day.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an alias for a published version of the function and set provisioned concurrency on it, and use Application Auto Scaling scheduled actions to increase it just before market open and decrease it afterward.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Set the function's reserved concurrency to the peak level so that execution environments are initialized in advance before market open.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Raise the function memory to the maximum and warm up the execution environments with an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes the function at 5-minute intervals before market open, starting the invocations 30 minutes before open and continuing after open.

exam-sap-c02-63.explanation: Provisioned concurrency secures pre-initialized execution environments and eliminates cold starts, and it can be configured only on a version or an alias. If the pattern is predictable, Application Auto Scaling scheduled scaling can raise it only during peak hours to reduce cost. Provisioned concurrency cannot be set on $LATEST, and keeping it all day also violates the cost constraint. Reserved concurrency only secures capacity and does not pre-initialize environments, so it does not solve cold starts. Warming with periodic invocations does not guarantee as many concurrent environments as are needed at the same time, and increasing memory only raises cost. Because capacity is needed only for the 30 minutes just before market open and the pattern is the same every day, increase and decrease the provisioned concurrency of the published version with scheduled scaling.

exam-sap-c02-64.prompt: A payments platform team wants consuming accounts' VPCs (40 accounts in the organization) to call an authentication API that runs in a private subnet in account A. The CIDRs of the consumer VPCs overlap with each other, and some are the same 10.0.0.0/16 as the provider VPC, and CIDR reassignment is not possible. The entire provider network must not be exposed to the consumer side, and only one-way access, in which the consumer accounts initiate calls to the provider, is needed. The consumer account teams have different schedules and cannot negotiate CIDRs with the provider, and the provider team does not want to change its own network configuration, such as routing, peering, and CIDRs, as consumer accounts are added (registering allowed principals on the endpoint service is fine). There are 40 consumer accounts in total, and 1 to 2 are added every week. The authentication API is served over TLS behind an NLB, and the call volume is thousands of requests per second. Some consumer VPCs have the same CIDR as the provider VPC, so peering or a TGW connection cannot be established at all. The security team wants only consumer accounts allowed by the provider to have access. The API terminates TLS at the NLB, and requests arrive only on TCP 443. Each account team manages the consumer VPC's routing configuration directly, and the central network team is not involved. Which configuration MOST appropriately meets the requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Connect account A and all 40 consumer VPCs to a transit gateway, and configure the TGW route tables so that only the API subnet route is propagated.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Connect the VPC in account A to each consumer VPC with VPC peering, and allow only traffic to the API port in the consumer-side security groups.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Connect each consumer VPC to a virtual private gateway in account A with a Site-to-Site VPN, restrict the exposed subnets to the API subnet with a routing policy, and narrow the access scope once more with consumer-side security groups.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Put an NLB in front of the API in account A and publish it as a VPC endpoint service, register the root ARNs of the 40 consumer accounts as allowed principals, and have each consumer VPC access it through an interface VPC endpoint.

exam-sap-c02-64.explanation: With PrivateLink, an endpoint network interface is created in a subnet of the consumer VPC, the service is accessed through a consumer-side private IP, the connection is initiated by the consumer, and only the endpoint service (behind the NLB) is exposed rather than the entire provider network, so it works even when CIDRs overlap. If you register only consumer account ARNs as allowed principals, only the allowed accounts can create endpoints. VPC peering cannot be created between VPCs with overlapping CIDRs and does not support transitive routing. A transit gateway cannot route VPC attachments with overlapping CIDRs together in one route table, so it has the same problem. A VPN causes route conflicts when the CIDRs on both sides overlap, requires operating a tunnel for each VPC, and limiting exposure at the subnet level is also incomplete. Because the CIDRs overlap, only one-way access is needed, and no network changes are allowed on the provider side, PrivateLink is the only one that works.

exam-sap-c02-65.prompt: A company is replicating 30 order system servers with AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) and has a cutover window of 2 hours starting at 2 AM at the end of the month. All replication is healthy, and the application team wants to minimize cutover risk. A cutover instance does not receive changes from the source server after it is launched. It must be possible to return to the source server if a problem occurs. The 30 servers are divided into web, application, and database tiers, and write transactions keep arriving at the database. If service normalization is not confirmed by 4 AM, when the window ends, the company must fall back to the source servers. The 30 servers consist of 12 web, 12 application, and 6 database servers. A post-launch configuration script must run on each replicated server, and test instances can be launched several times outside the cutover window. The criterion for the rollback decision is whether the core business flows are normal by 4 AM. After cutover, the database tier receives writes on the new instances, so changes after cutover are not reflected on the source. Considering this, the scope of data loss at the time of rollback must be explained to management in advance, and DNS must also be switched back when returning. Which cutover plan is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Without any separate testing, launch the cutover instances as soon as the window opens, and keep the source servers accepting writes during cutover with replication maintained so that changes automatically follow to AWS. Before cutover, match the target instance security groups to the source's and keep the source running.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immediately after launching the cutover instances, click finalize cutover right away to clean up the replication resources, and if a problem occurs, recover by re-creating new instances instead of using the source servers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Launch the cutover instances one hour before the cutover window opens, keep the source servers in service until the window closes, and then switch over by changing only DNS.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Verify functionality with test instances before cutover; when the window opens, stop application writes, confirm that replication has caught up, launch the cutover instances and validate them, and finalize the cutover only after stability is confirmed.

exam-sap-c02-65.explanation: The correct answer is pre-testing, stopping writes and confirming replication sync, launching and validating the cutover instances, and finalizing after stability is confirmed. A cutover instance reflects the latest state at launch time and does not receive later source changes, so writes must be stopped first to prevent data loss. Finalizing the cutover stops replication, cleans up replicated data and resources, and removes the agent, which eliminates any room for rollback, so it must be done after validation. If you let the source keep receiving writes, the changes are not reflected on the cutover instances and the data diverges. An instance launched in advance also does not receive changes after that point. Because changes are not reflected on the source after cutover and because of the rollback deadline, pre-testing and stopping writes are needed, and finalization must come after stability is confirmed.

exam-sap-c02-66.prompt: An insurance company operates 25 VPCs (in 12 accounts) connected with a transit gateway in the Seoul Region and connected to an on-premises data center with AWS Direct Connect. On-premises servers need to resolve the name (app.internal.example) in an AWS private hosted zone, and all AWS VPCs need to resolve the on-premises domain corp.example.com. The network team decided not to add staff for DNS server patching and incident response, and name resolution must not be interrupted by the failure of a single Availability Zone. The on-premises DNS servers can forward queries over Direct Connect to private IP addresses in AWS, and conversely, queries for the on-premises domain are answered by two on-premises DNS servers. The VPC private hosted zone is associated with the shared services VPC and with each VPC. Query volume is thousands per second. Long latency in on-premises domain resolution leads to login failures, so the forwarding path must be redundant across Availability Zones. The network team wants to configure the endpoints only once and handle growth in accounts just by sharing rules. Which configuration is the MOST cost-effective, without operating EC2 for DNS forwarders yourself and without creating duplicate endpoints per account?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create Amazon Route 53 Resolver inbound and outbound endpoints in the shared services VPC that use IP addresses in two or more Availability Zones, share the corp.example.com forwarding rule with the organization through AWS RAM and associate it with each VPC, and associate the private hosted zone with the shared services VPC as well.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure two DNS forwarder EC2 instances in the shared services VPC with two-way conditional forwarding, point the DHCP option sets of all VPCs at these servers, and have the network team handle server OS patching and incident response.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create outbound endpoints and forwarding rules separately for every VPC in each account, register all the VPC inbound endpoint IPs in the on-premises DNS, and update this registration every time a VPC is added.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Replicate the on-premises domain into a Route 53 public hosted zone so that VPCs resolve it over the internet path, publish the private zone records publicly so that on premises can query them, and rely on internet DNS for internal name resolution.

exam-sap-c02-66.explanation: If you place an inbound endpoint in the shared services VPC, on premises can query the private hosted zone associated with that VPC, and if you share the outbound endpoint and forwarding rule through RAM and associate them with each VPC, all VPCs forward corp.example.com to on premises without creating duplicate endpoints in each account. Forwarder EC2 instances conflict with the constraint that you would have to operate them yourself. Creating endpoints per VPC violates the prohibition on duplicate creation and is less cost-efficient because hourly endpoint charges increase. Replicating into a public hosted zone exposes internal names externally, which is a security problem, and it is also not a private name resolution architecture. Because the company must avoid operating EC2 forwarders and avoid creating duplicate endpoints in each account, the shared services VPC Resolver endpoints with RAM rule sharing are right.

exam-sap-c02-67.prompt: A manufacturing company charges back the costs of 60 accounts in AWS Organizations to departments based on the CostCenter tag. Teams use the tag keys costcenter, CostCenter, and cost-center inconsistently and with different value formats, so Cost Explorer aggregation is off. The finance team wants to standardize key spelling and allowed values at the organization level, prevent noncompliant tagging, and view costs classified by a single standard key. The chargeback report closes at the beginning of each month, so the standard must be applied within this month, and the manual work of the report author converting tag values separately must be eliminated. The tags are currently used across Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon S3 buckets, and both are resource types supported by enforced_for in tag policies. The standard key is decided as CostCenter alone, and the allowed values are a list created by the finance team (40 department codes). The company wants new resources with incorrect tags to be blocked at creation time, and cleanup of already created resources will be a separate later task. The chargeback report is created by grouping by the CostCenter tag in Cost Explorer, and the finance team updates the department code list quarterly. The policy must be applied within this month, so approaches that require code changes or development deployments are difficult. Which combination MOST appropriately meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the billing console of each member account, activate all three tag keys as cost allocation tags, create a report per key in Cost Explorer, and add up the numbers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use an AWS Config required-tags rule to detect resources without tags and send a weekly report, delegate key spelling cleanup to each team lead to do manually every quarter, and have the finance team check compliance through the report.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use AWS Cost Categories rules to map the values of the three keys to departments for reporting, and let teams keep using the tag keys they use now.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Define the CostCenter key spelling and allowed values in an Organizations tag policy, specify enforced_for for ec2:instance and s3:bucket to block noncompliant tagging at creation time, and activate CostCenter as a cost allocation tag in the billing console of the management account.

exam-sap-c02-67.explanation: A tag policy defines the capitalization of tag keys and allowed values at the organization level, and for resource types specified with enforced_for (ec2:instance and s3:bucket support enforcement, whereas for example RDS DB instances support report-only mode and not enforcement), noncompliant tagging can be blocked at creation time. The standardized CostCenter key must be activated as a cost allocation tag in the management account for it to appear in Cost Explorer and reports. Activating it in member accounts does not work because the management account is the only place in an organization that can access the cost allocation tags manager. A Config rule only reports missing tags after the fact and cannot standardize spelling or block. Cost Categories are for classification in reports, do not block noncompliant tagging, and leave the sprawl of tag keys in place. Because the standard must be applied within this month and the report author's manual work must be eliminated, tag policies together with activating the cost allocation tag are right.

exam-sap-c02-68.prompt: An advertising analytics team loads hundreds of GB of CSV logs per day into Amazon S3 and queries them with Amazon Athena. Most queries look up only specific campaign IDs from the last 3 days, but every query scans the entire table, so the monthly Athena bill is large and queries are slow. The analysts' SQL must be preserved, and the team does not want to operate a new cluster. Analysts use standard SQL, and a BI tool connects through the Athena JDBC driver. The goal is to cut query cost by half or more within this quarter. The CSV files are already stored in S3 under date-based prefixes, there are about 60 columns, and queries reference fewer than ten of them. One nightly transformation run is sufficient, and new data is transformed and accumulated the same way. The team has 2 people and wants to avoid services that must be operated around the clock. The original CSV files are kept for archival purposes. Query results refresh the BI dashboard every morning, and analysts must be able to query by the same table name without changing their SQL. Data older than the last 3 days is rarely queried but must be retained for 1 year for auditing. Which improvement is the MOST cost-effective?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the S3 bucket storage class to Intelligent-Tiering to lower the storage unit price of the data that queries scan, and adjust lifecycle rules together.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Convert the data to Parquet with AWS Glue ETL or Athena CTAS and partition it by date so that queries read only the needed partitions and columns.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster, load the CSV files, and have analysts query with Redshift.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Turn off Athena query result reuse and increase the number of concurrent queries to shorten processing time.

exam-sap-c02-68.explanation: Athena is billed by the amount of data scanned, so converting to a columnar format (Parquet) reads only the needed columns, and adding date partitions scans only the partitions of the last 3 days, which reduces both cost and time, while the same SQL keeps working and the serverless model is maintained. The storage class concerns the storage unit price and does not change Athena's scan-based billing. A Redshift cluster brings new operational burden and violates the constraint. Turning off result reuse and increasing concurrency does not reduce the amount scanned, so cost does not go down and may even go up. Because the SQL must be preserved and no new cluster is to be operated, reducing the amount scanned with Parquet conversion and partitioning is right.

exam-sap-c02-69.prompt: A real-time multiplayer game company deploys game servers that communicate over UDP behind NLBs in Seoul and Frankfurt. Some customer firewalls need to manage fixed IPs in an allow list, and when one Region is unhealthy, players must be directed immediately to the healthy Region without a delay caused by DNS caching. It is good for players to enter the AWS backbone from the nearest edge. Game clients often connect with IP addresses registered in the allow list instead of domain names, and players are spread across Asia and Europe. When an entire Region stops responding, traffic must move to the healthy Region quickly, not in minutes. The server process uses a single UDP port, and the NLB supports UDP listeners. Some customers take a month to update an allow list, so the IPs must not change, and the company wants to reduce connection latency for players worldwide through the AWS backbone path. The client app is hard to modify for two months because of marketplace review. The Seoul and Frankfurt Regions use the same server image and the same UDP port. Waiting for the DNS record TTL to expire when one Region's NLB is unhealthy caused players to leave in the last outage. The operations team has 2 people. Which configuration MOST appropriately meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator, register the NLBs in both Regions as endpoint groups, and send traffic to the healthy Region with static anycast IPs and endpoint health checks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure Amazon Route 53 latency routing records with health checks and lower the TTL to 60 seconds so that the record of an unhealthy Region is excluded from responses.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution, register the NLBs in both Regions as an origin group, and enable origin failover so that game UDP traffic also receives caching and acceleration at the edge.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assign an Elastic IP address to the NLB in each Region and have customers allow both IPs, and change the client code so that the application retries with the other Region's IP on a connection failure. Keep a fixed IP in front of each Regional NLB so that the allow list does not change.

exam-sap-c02-69.explanation: The correct answer is Global Accelerator. Two static anycast IPs satisfy the allow list requirement, endpoint health checks remove unhealthy endpoints immediately so that failover occurs without DNS cache delay, and traffic enters the AWS backbone at the nearest edge. It supports both TCP and UDP. Route 53 delays failover because of TTL and resolver caching and does not provide fixed IPs. CloudFront focuses on HTTP/HTTPS and WebSocket, so it does not suit UDP game traffic. The client retry approach requires client code changes and customer allow list management, which is a heavy operational burden. The requirements for fixed IPs, failover independent of DNS caching, and edge entry point to Global Accelerator, which provides anycast IPs.

exam-sap-c02-70.prompt: A company set up an Amazon S3 bucket in ap-northeast-2 encrypted with SSE-KMS to be replicated cross-Region to a bucket in us-west-2 in a different AWS account. Versioning and a replication rule exist, but objects encrypted with AWS KMS are not replicated. Objects in the destination bucket must also be encrypted with a customer managed key in the destination account. The bucket already contains billions of objects, and newly written objects from now on are the replication targets. The destination account's security team wants to manage the key policy of the replica key directly. The replication targets are only new objects written from now on, and existing objects will be handled in a separate task. The source account's replication role has already been created, and ownership override is not needed. The destination account belongs to a separate organizational unit, and the destination key is a customer managed key created by that account. The replication latency target is within 15 minutes. The current replication rule applies to the whole bucket with no prefix filter, and the destination account already has a bucket policy that allows the replication role to write to the destination bucket. Replication status shows FAILED in the object metadata. Which two actions solve this problem and meet the requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Specify an AWS managed key (aws/s3) as the replica encryption key of the destination bucket so that the destination account does not need to manage a key policy separately. AWS manages key rotation automatically, which reduces the security team's operational burden.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Replace the source key with a multi-Region key; S3 shares the key automatically through the multi-Region feature, so the replica key is not specified separately in the replication rule.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Grant the replication IAM role kms:Decrypt permission on the source key and kms:Encrypt permission on the destination key, and have the destination account's key policy allow use by the account that owns the source bucket (the replication role).

choices.label: D
choices.text: Grant the replication IAM role only s3:GetObjectVersion permission on the source object versions, which is enough to replicate even KMS-encrypted objects.

choices.label: E
choices.text: In the replication rule, explicitly enable replication of KMS-encrypted objects (SseKmsEncryptedObjects) and specify a customer managed key in the same Region as the destination bucket (us-west-2) as the replica encryption key.

exam-sap-c02-70.explanation: The correct answers are enabling KMS object replication in the replication rule and specifying the destination key, together with granting permissions in the role and key policy. By default S3 does not replicate SSE-KMS objects, so you must turn on SseKmsEncryptedObjects and specify a key in the destination Region, the replication role needs permission to decrypt with the source key and encrypt with the destination key, and for cross-account, the key policy must allow it. AWS managed keys cannot be used cross-account, so they cannot be used. Even with a multi-Region key, S3 treats it like a single-Region key, so specifying the replica key is still required. GetObjectVersion alone cannot replicate KMS objects. The conditions that the destination account manages the key policy and a key in the destination Region must be used require both the KMS settings in the replication rule and the role permissions.

exam-sap-c02-71.prompt: A game company's Amazon DynamoDB table receives concentrated reads on a few popular item keys during events, and the company has significantly overprovisioned read capacity. Most reads are fine with eventual consistency, responses at the microsecond level would be ideal, and the application calls the DynamoDB API with the Java SDK. Read requests are concentrated on a few keys, writes are relatively rare, and the development team must finish the improvement within 2 weeks before the next event. The table has about 200 million items with an average item size of 2 KB. Popular item keys are read tens of thousands of times per second during events but modified only dozens of times per day. Currently, read capacity is provisioned large to match the peak, and the application already uses only DynamoDB Query and GetItem calls. The team evaluated the number of cluster nodes and the maintenance cost, and DynamoDB read capacity cost accounts for half of the monthly cost. After an event ends, access frequency drops sharply, and eventual consistency is sufficient for read consistency. There are 2 operations staff. Which method MOST appropriately reduces both read cost and latency while minimizing code changes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an Amazon ElastiCache cluster and implement cache lookup, update, and invalidation logic in the application code yourself so that reads are served from the cache.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Convert the table to a global table to spread reads across replicas in multiple Regions and have clients read from the replica in the nearest Region.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Place a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster in front of the table, replace the DynamoDB client with the DAX client by changing only the endpoint, and cache the reads.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the table to on-demand mode and use strongly consistent reads by default so that the most recent data is read.

exam-sap-c02-71.explanation: DAX is a managed in-memory cache compatible with the DynamoDB API; it reduces eventually consistent reads to microseconds, absorbs repeated reads of frequently read keys to reduce the overprovisioning of read capacity, and requires only a code change at the level of replacing the client. ElastiCache requires you to write cache consistency and invalidation code yourself, which violates the requirement to minimize code changes. Global tables are for cross-Region replication and do not resolve read cost for hot keys or microsecond latency. Strongly consistent reads consume double the capacity and have no caching benefit, and are also the opposite direction from the requested latency reduction. Minimal code changes, microsecond responses, and tolerance of eventual consistency point to DAX, and global tables do not solve the read latency problem.

exam-sap-c02-72.prompt: A company is migrating a 6 TB Windows file server to AWS. It wants to keep the on-premises Active Directory users and NTFS ACLs as they are and not change the existing share paths. File service must continue even if one Availability Zone fails, and the company wants to reduce operational burden such as server patching and storage management. The on-premises AD domain continues to operate on premises and is connected to AWS with AWS Direct Connect. 120 users use files all day, so the cutover is allowed only over a weekend. The file server has 40 shared folders, and NTFS permissions are set differently for each folder. Users connect from multiple branches, and a write freeze of a few hours over the weekend is acceptable for synchronizing the last changes before the cutover. The file server name can be pointed at the new server with a DNS alias. User accounts are in the on-premises AD domain, and the AWS file service must also be accessible with the same domain accounts. Users should not have to change their drive mappings after the migration, and one backup per day using a service feature is sufficient. Two Availability Zones in the Seoul Region are used. Which migration configuration is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure the file server yourself on two EC2 Windows instances with attached EBS volumes, make it redundant with DFS replication, and operate instance patching and backups yourself. Point the existing file server name at the new server with DNS to reduce path changes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an Amazon EFS file system, copy the files with AWS DataSync, have Windows clients mount it with the NFS client feature, and map NTFS ACLs to POSIX permissions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Move the files to Amazon S3, have users access them with an S3 browser tool, control folder-level access with IAM policies, and replace the existing share names with bucket names.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create Amazon FSx for Windows File Server in a Multi-AZ configuration, integrate it with Active Directory, copy the SMB files and NTFS permissions with AWS DataSync, and keep the existing share names with a DNS alias.

exam-sap-c02-72.explanation: The correct answer is Multi-AZ FSx for Windows File Server. It is a fully managed Windows share that provides SMB, NTFS ACLs, and AD integration, withstands Availability Zone failures with Multi-AZ, keeps existing paths through a DNS alias, and DataSync copies ACLs and metadata while preserving them. An EC2 file server requires you to operate patching and DFS replication yourself, which conflicts with the operational burden requirement. EFS supports only NFS, so it cannot preserve NTFS ACLs and SMB paths. The S3 and IAM approach discards the existing AD permissions and share names. The conditions of NTFS ACLs, AD integration, Availability Zone failure tolerance, and reduced operational burden converge on Multi-AZ FSx for Windows.

exam-sap-c02-73.prompt: A manufacturer needs to move 180 virtual servers on VMware and 20 non-virtualized physical servers to AWS. The data center contract ends in 4 months and application code cannot be modified. Services must keep operating during the migration, and cutover downtime per server must be within tens of minutes. The servers are a mix of Windows Server 2012 R2 (an OS that is out of Microsoft support but is on the MGN supported list, with .NET Framework 4.5 or later installed) and RHEL 7, and some are database servers with many changes, so replication lag must be monitored. The migration team prefers bulk work by wave because there are many servers. The migration must be completed before the data center contract ends, and waves are divided by application, taking dependencies between servers into account. A 1 Gbps Direct Connect already exists, and a bandwidth limit is needed so that replication traffic does not disrupt business. After the migration, the servers keep the same OS on Amazon EC2. Before each server's cutover, the team must be able to confirm the final sync and roll back to the source if there is a problem, and wants to run test cutovers repeatedly without interrupting operations. Administrator privileges to install agents have been obtained on all servers. Which method is MOST appropriate when grouping servers by application and migrating them in sequence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Export the VMware virtual servers as OVA files, upload them to Amazon S3, and create AMIs with VM Import/Export, and for physical servers take images and import them the same way. Run the image import jobs in parallel per server and validate the resulting AMIs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: First carry out a refactoring project that redesigns the applications with containers and serverless, and then switch services to the new architecture within 4 months.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Install the AWS Replication Agent on each server and perform continuous block-level replication with AWS Transform MGN (formerly AWS Application Migration Service); for each application and wave, validate with test instances and then launch the cutover instances.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Shut down all servers, take snapshots, move them to EC2 using an AWS Snow family device, and leave the service stopped during the migration period.

exam-sap-c02-73.explanation: The correct answer is rehosting with continuous block-level replication in AWS Transform MGN (formerly Application Migration Service). The agent continuously replicates changed blocks regardless of whether servers are physical, virtual, or on another cloud, so migration proceeds while keeping the service running, validation is done with test instances before cutover, and bulk work by wave fits the 4-month schedule. Both OSs are on the MGN supported OS list (Windows Server 2012 R2 is an out-of-support OS, so an upgrade is recommended, and .NET Framework 4.5 or later is required). No code changes are needed, which also matches the constraints. Image export is a one-time copy that cannot sync changes, so downtime grows long, and it cannot be used for physical servers. Refactoring conflicts with the no-code-modification constraint and the 4-month schedule. Moving with a device while stopping the service violates the requirement to keep operating during the migration. The conditions of no code changes, cutover within tens of minutes, and wave-based work point to continuous block replication.

exam-sap-c02-74.prompt: An insurance company's 40 AWS Lambda and Amazon ECS services keep the RDS MySQL password in plaintext in environment variables and change it manually once a year. A security audit required automatic rotation within 90 days and an access audit trail. Rotation must not interrupt the services and must not require redeploying applications. All the services use the AWS SDK, and there is no plan to upgrade the database engine. The audit team requires a record of who retrieved the credentials and when. The database and the secret must not get out of sync during password rotation, and existing connections must not be dropped during rotation. There are 40 services and a development team of 5, so code changes are limited to one or two lines of SDK calls. The audit team wants to check retrieval history in AWS CloudTrail. The service and time at which credentials were retrieved must remain in the audit log, and the company wants existing connections not to drop while connections switch to the new credentials after rotation. All services are in the Seoul Region and there is only one password per database. Which method meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Store the password in an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store standard parameter, have an owner edit the value manually every quarter and then update the application settings, and record the time of the change in a change management ticket.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager, configure automatic rotation for RDS with the alternating users strategy on a 90-day schedule, and change the applications to retrieve the secret at runtime (including caching).

choices.label: C
choices.text: Put a KMS-encrypted password value in the environment variables, and have the deployment pipeline redeploy the services with the new value every 90 days.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the number of database users per service to reduce account sharing, and set an expiration date with the database password policy.

exam-sap-c02-74.explanation: Secrets Manager supports automatic rotation for RDS, lets you set the rotation schedule, and allows access to be tracked with CloudTrail. The alternating users strategy rotates between two users, so the previous credentials remain valid until the next rotation, which matches the requirement of no service interruption during rotation, and if the application retrieves the secret at runtime instead of through an environment variable, it receives the rotated value without redeployment. Manual edits in Parameter Store violate the automatic rotation requirement. Keeping an encrypted value in an environment variable and redeploying periodically conflicts with the requirement to rotate without redeployment and without service interruption. Adding users and setting an expiration date would block services when passwords expire and also does not provide automatic rotation or an audit trail. Because the company must rotate automatically every 90 days without redeployment and keep retrieval history, the Secrets Manager alternating users strategy is right.

exam-sap-c02-75.prompt: A media company serves video segments worldwide through Amazon CloudFront, and the origin is an on-premises packager in Seoul with limited bandwidth. Viewers are spread across several continents, and because each Regional edge cache requests the same object from the origin separately, the origin bandwidth saturates right after popular content is released. Requests for popular content concentrate in the 10 minutes after release, after which the cache hit ratio becomes high, and there is no budget this quarter for migrating the origin or adding bandwidth. The origin packager sits in a single data center in Seoul with a 1 Gbps uplink. The current cache hit ratio itself is not bad, but right after release, many edge caches request the same segment almost simultaneously, causing origin requests to surge. The application on the origin side cannot be modified, and only CloudFront settings can be changed. For popular content, origin requests rise to as much as 30 times normal in the 10 minutes after release, and afterward most are served from the cache. The cache TTL is already set appropriately per segment, so the TTL policy is not part of this improvement. Which method MOST effectively reduces the number of requests to the origin without expanding the origin?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the cache policy TTL to 0 so that every request fetches the latest object from the origin, align cache consistency with origin response headers, and also adjust origin-side cache control headers separately.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable Origin Shield for that origin and choose the Origin Shield Region with the lowest latency to the origin (Seoul) so that requests from all cache layers pass through it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add an NLB in front of the origin to distribute origin connections and have the load balancer absorb the number of connections coming from the edge.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Split the distribution by continent so that each distribution calls the origin directly, and use a separate cache key for each continent.

exam-sap-c02-75.explanation: Origin Shield adds an additional caching layer between the Regional edge caches and the origin, collapsing requests for the same object into one so that they reach the origin almost only once; an on-premises origin with limited bandwidth is a typical use case, and you choose the Region with the lowest latency to the origin. Setting the TTL to 0 removes caching and actually causes origin requests to surge. An NLB only distributes connections and does not reduce duplicate requests for the same object nor solve the bandwidth limit. Splitting the distribution by continent separates the cache layers and increases duplicate requests. Because the company must reduce the number of origin requests without expanding the origin, Origin Shield, which places a single intermediate cache in front of the cache layers, is right.

exam-scs-c03-1.prompt: A fintech startup has 50 developers who deploy more than 40 microservices every week. Each service needs a dedicated IAM role, so role requests occur several times a day. Currently, the security team creates the roles on behalf of the developers, and deployments are frequently blocked while waiting for approval. The platform team wants to delegate to developers the ability to create IAM roles for their services on their own. However, the platform team must prevent developers from escalating their privileges by creating roles that have administrator permissions. Developers must be able to create roles immediately without waiting for approval. The security team has only 3 members and cannot rely on after-the-fact reviews or manual attachment. The developer accounts are consolidated in a single organization, and most service roles need access only to Amazon S3, Amazon SQS, and Amazon DynamoDB. The last audit flagged a large number of exception approvals. Which configuration will meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Grant developers the iam:* permission. Use an SCP to deny only the action of attaching the AdministratorAccess managed policy to a role, to block the escalation path.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When a developer creates a role, use an AWS Config rule to detect roles that have no boundary policy. Have the security team manually attach a boundary policy the next day.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the developer policy, allow iam:CreateRole and iam:AttachRolePolicy only if a specified permissions boundary policy is attached. Deny modification and deletion of the boundary policy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Accept role creation requests as tickets. Have the security team create the roles on behalf of developers, and grant developers only the iam:PassRole permission.

exam-scs-c03-1.explanation: By using the iam:PermissionsBoundary condition key to allow role creation and policy attachment only when the specified boundary policy is attached, every role that is created is restricted within the boundary. Modification and deletion of the boundary policy must also be denied so that it cannot be bypassed. This approach allows immediate creation and requires no human involvement. An SCP that denies only iam:* and attachment of the administrator policy can be bypassed with other broad policies or inline policies. Manual attachment after the fact leaves the roles exposed without a boundary in the meantime. The ticket-based approach violates the requirement for immediate creation.

exam-scs-c03-2.prompt: A retail company's AWS organization consists of 120 accounts across 3 Regions, and each account administrator changes security groups frequently. Last quarter, there was an incident in which a development account left port 22 open to 0.0.0.0/0 for two weeks. The security team has only 4 members and cannot inspect every account. From now on, the company must detect the creation of such a rule within minutes and automatically revert it with no human involvement. The history of rule changes must be retained for auditing, and maintaining separate scripts for each account is not allowed. Different teams operate each Region, so once a rule is defined, it must be applied in the same way to new accounts and new Regions. The evaluation results for noncompliant resources must be viewable aggregated at the organization level. Which configuration will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deploy the restricted-ssh AWS Config managed rule as an organization conformance pack, and attach an AWS Systems Manager Automation automatic remediation action for violations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Export the AWS Trusted Advisor security group check results every week for the security team to review, and open a ticket for the responsible account administrator to fix each violation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Receive Amazon Inspector network reachability findings through Amazon EventBridge, and implement an AWS Lambda function that deletes the violating security group rules one account at a time.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a custom AWS Config rule that runs every 24 hours in every account, review the results on a dashboard, and have the responsible person fix the rules directly in the console.

exam-scs-c03-2.explanation: restricted-ssh is a managed rule whose evaluation is triggered when a security group configuration changes, so it finds violations within minutes. Attaching a Systems Manager Automation runbook as an automatic remediation action reverts the change with no human involvement. An organization conformance pack deploys the rule and the remediation action to all accounts with the same configuration from a single template, and the evaluation history is also retained in AWS Config. A weekly Trusted Advisor review violates both the within-minutes requirement and the automatic reversion requirement. Inspector reachability applies to EC2 targets and requires you to implement Lambda directly. A 24-hour evaluation cycle with manual fixes leaves delay and human involvement.

exam-scs-c03-3.prompt: A banking-affiliated fintech company protects customer data with SSE-KMS in Amazon S3. The financial regulator requires that key material exist only in HSMs in the company's data center and that all encryption and decryption operations also be performed in those HSMs. The company already has redundant on-premises HSMs and a team that operates them. If the company revokes access, ciphertext remaining in AWS must be impossible to decrypt. Importing key material and using HSMs inside AWS are not allowed, and storing key material in any other way is considered a regulatory violation. The ciphertext is stored in Amazon S3. The regulator conducts an inspection every six months to verify proof of key ownership, and all S3 buckets used by the application are in the Seoul Region. Which AWS KMS configuration will meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Connect an external key store (XKS) to the on-premises external key manager through an XKS proxy that the company operates, and create the KMS key inside that external key store.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure an AWS CloudHSM cluster in a VPC, create a CloudHSM key store, and have the key material and operations for the KMS key performed in dedicated HSMs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a customer managed KMS key, and use the key policy to allow only the Amazon S3 service principal to use it, keeping key usage under the company's control.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an external-origin (EXTERNAL) KMS key by importing key material generated in the on-premises HSM, and set a short expiration time for the key material.

exam-scs-c03-3.explanation: The correct answer is an external key store. With XKS, an external key manager owned by the company stores the key material and performs encryption and decryption. If access is revoked, AWS cannot access the key and therefore cannot decrypt the ciphertext. In exchange, responsibility for availability, latency, and durability shifts to the customer. Importing key material copies the key material to AWS HSMs and the operations also occur in AWS, and this approach is prohibited. A CloudHSM key store has its HSMs inside AWS and so does not satisfy the on-premises storage requirement. Restricting the key policy does not change the fact that the key material is in an AWS HSM.

exam-scs-c03-4.prompt: A financial company manages 28 AWS Config rules that implement its internal security standards, together with AWS Systems Manager Automation remediation actions to run on noncompliance, as a single bundle. Some of these are custom rules written directly by the company's security team. Currently, every time a new account is created, an administrator creates the rules by hand, so the settings differ slightly from account to account. The company wants to deploy this bundle consistently to the 90 member accounts of the organization and to make changes in only one place. The target Regions are Seoul and Tokyo, and the security team has 5 members. Changes occur about once per quarter, and every change must be completed in a single approved deployment. The audit team wants to see at a glance which accounts are using which version of the bundle. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enable the AWS Control Tower mandatory controls on all OUs so that the organization applies, in bulk, the rules that correspond to the internal standards.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard in AWS Security Hub across the organization to check accounts against the same standard and automatically remediate violations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Log in to each member account, create the 28 Config rules one by one in the console, attach a remediation action to each rule, and distribute the procedure as a document.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the management account or a delegated administrator account, define the rules and remediation actions in a YAML template and deploy them to all member accounts as an organization conformance pack.

exam-scs-c03-4.explanation: The correct answer is an organization conformance pack. A conformance pack bundles AWS Config managed or custom rules and remediation actions in a single YAML template, deploys them as a single unit to a single account and Region or to an entire organization, and lets you modify them in one place. Creating rules manually per account requires repeating 28 rules across 90 accounts and breaks consistency. The FSBP standard is a set of controls defined by AWS and cannot contain the company's own rules and specified remediation actions. Control Tower mandatory controls are also protective controls defined by AWS and cannot be used as a bundle of custom company rules.

exam-scs-c03-5.prompt: A VPC that runs 300 Amazon EC2 instances for a payment workload was recently assessed as having a high likelihood of a security incident. The company must block the instances in the VPC from resolving known malicious domains. In addition, a path has been identified in which some instances bypass the VPC resolver and query public DNS servers on the internet directly (port 53), and this path must also be blocked. Amazon Route 53 Resolver query logging and Amazon GuardDuty are already enabled, but an approach that only detects does not meet the requirements. All instances are in private subnets, and the security groups already restrict destination ports, but outbound port 53 is open. Resolution of internal names for normal services must continue to be handled by the VPC resolver. Which TWO actions will meet these two requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Send Route 53 Resolver query logs to Amazon S3, periodically query for malicious domain lookups with Amazon Athena, and deliver a report to the responsible person.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add a stateful rule to AWS Network Firewall that drops TCP and UDP port 53 traffic leaving the VPC, and make the outbound path go through the firewall.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Receive GuardDuty DNS-related findings through Amazon EventBridge, and automate an AWS Lambda function to isolate, after the fact, the instances that queried a malicious domain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a rule that blocks the AWS managed malicious domain list to a Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall rule group, and associate the rule group with the VPC.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Apply AWS Shield Advanced to the VPC and configure it to automatically mitigate abnormal query traffic destined for public DNS servers.

exam-scs-c03-5.explanation: DNS Firewall blocks queries that pass through the VPC resolver based on domain lists, but it cannot see queries that bypass the resolver and go directly to an external DNS server. Network Firewall blocks that path by dropping external port 53 traffic, so both actions must be used together to meet the requirements. Automatic isolation based on GuardDuty is a response after the fact, after the query has already gone out. Query logging and Athena lookups provide visibility only and cannot block. Shield Advanced is a DDoS protection service and is unrelated to domain blocking.

exam-scs-c03-6.prompt: CloudTrail confirms signs that temporary credentials for the IAM role PaymentProcessorRole, used by an e-commerce company's payment service, were leaked through malware on a developer's laptop. The role has a maximum session duration of 12 hours and hundreds of active sessions, and because it is the middle of a Black Friday event, payment processing cannot be stopped for long. Normal workloads must resume immediately by obtaining new credentials with the same role ARN, and deleting the role or modifying the content of the existing permissions policies is not allowed. It is not possible to identify individually which session the leaked credentials belong to, and although the laptop has been isolated, an attacker can access payment data for as long as the already-issued credentials remain valid. Which action will immediately invalidate the already-issued credentials?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Temporarily attach an SCP that denies all actions to the organization root so that all principals in the account are prevented from sending new requests.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delete the role, re-create it with the same name, and replicate the trust policy and permissions policy so that the existing credentials are no longer valid.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reduce the maximum session duration of the role from 12 hours to 1 hour so that credentials issued from now on expire within a short time.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run revoke active sessions for the role in the IAM console so that requests made with credentials issued before this moment are all denied.

exam-scs-c03-6.explanation: The correct answer is revoking the role's active sessions. This feature adds an AWSRevokeOlderSessions deny inline policy to the role, which denies all credentials issued up to the revocation time (about 30 seconds later, allowing for propagation delay). It does not apply to sessions assumed afterward, so normal workloads resume by obtaining new credentials with the same role ARN. The content of the existing permissions policies is not changed. Deleting and re-creating the role violates the constraint that prohibits deletion, and the role's unique ID changes, which can break references. Reducing the maximum session duration changes only the lifetime of sessions issued in the future and does not invalidate already-leaked credentials. Denying all actions with a root SCP also blocks workloads unrelated to this role and the resumption of normal operations, so it does not fit the requirements.

exam-scs-c03-7.prompt: A healthcare data company has an Amazon S3 bucket containing approximately 10 TB of patient consultation records, and it must check for personal information every quarter. The bucket is encrypted with a customer managed KMS key (SSE-KMS), and the key and the bucket are owned by the same account. When an Amazon Macie sensitive data discovery job was run, many objects were reported with metadata only and without content analysis, and almost no sensitive data findings were produced. There is no problem with the bucket policy, the sampling depth is 100%, and the security team has one week left before this quarter's inspection deadline. The discovery job must not affect other teams' buckets in the account, and the security administrator can modify the key policy directly. Because the same bucket is scanned again every quarter, the fix must continue to work afterward once it is applied. Which action will allow Macie to analyze the object content?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a statement to the bucket policy that allows the Macie service-linked role to perform s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket, to open up object read permissions first.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower the object sampling depth of the discovery job, and instead adjust the job scope to be split by object prefix and run in multiple separate runs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the bucket default encryption to SSE-C, and modify the application to pass a customer-provided key in the request header for every newly uploaded object.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a statement to the KMS key policy that allows the Macie service-linked role AWSServiceRoleForAmazonMacie to perform kms:Decrypt.

exam-scs-c03-7.explanation: Macie decrypts and analyzes objects encrypted with a customer managed key only when the key policy allows the service-linked role to perform kms:Decrypt. If it is not allowed, Macie stores and reports only metadata. When the same account owns the key and the bucket, adding a statement to the key policy is sufficient. Adjusting the bucket policy is unrelated to the cause because the problem statement says there is no problem with it. The sampling depth is already 100%, so there is nothing more to change. Objects encrypted with SSE-C cannot be decrypted by Macie, so this would make analysis impossible instead.

exam-scs-c03-8.prompt: A logistics company must apply customer managed KMS key encryption to its unencrypted production Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database (Multi-AZ, 1.5 TB). The service runs 24 hours a day, and orders are lost if write traffic is interrupted, so the write downtime during the transition must be kept as short as possible. Data loss is not allowed, and changes to the application's endpoint settings must be minimal. The transition will be performed during the nighttime maintenance window, and a plan to return to the previous state if a problem occurs must also be in place. Five reporting tools connected to the same database have hardcoded the endpoint and are difficult to change. The storage is gp3, and order processing stops if write latency exceeds a certain level. Before the switchover, the company must verify that all storage data in the new environment has been loaded and that latency has stabilized. Which method is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a read replica from the unencrypted instance that is encrypted with a customer managed key, and promote the replica when the replication lag disappears.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When creating a blue/green deployment, specify a customer managed key as the target KMS key for the green DB instance to create an encrypted green environment, and switch over after synchronization and storage loading are complete.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Modify the running DB instance to turn on the storage encryption option, specify a customer managed key, and apply immediately with an instance reboot.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a manual snapshot, copy it while encrypting it with a customer managed key, restore a new instance from the copy, and move the application to the new endpoint.

exam-scs-c03-8.explanation: The correct answer is encrypting the green environment of a blue/green deployment with a customer managed key. When you create a blue/green deployment, you can encrypt the green instance with a different KMS key by using TargetKmsKeyId in the target resource configuration, and this is documented as a way to encrypt an unencrypted instance. At switchover, RDS renames the green instance to the same name and endpoint as blue, so the hardcoded endpoints do not need to be changed. Because the switchover happens after synchronization catches up, the write downtime is short. If the switchover fails, the changes are rolled back and the previous blue instance also remains. The green instance is restored from a snapshot and then lazily loaded, so completing storage initialization before the switchover stabilizes latency. An instance can be encrypted only at creation, so you cannot turn on encryption by modifying an existing instance. An encrypted read replica of an unencrypted instance cannot be created. Copying and restoring a snapshot is possible, but writes made after the snapshot must be applied separately and the endpoint must be changed, so the downtime is longer.

exam-scs-c03-9.prompt: A company that operates a global service runs an Amazon Aurora global database in Seoul (primary) and Tokyo (secondary), and applications in both Regions read the same database credentials from AWS Secrets Manager. Security policy requires that the password be rotated automatically every 30 days and that the values in both Regions always match. Applications in Tokyo must be able to read the secret even during a Seoul Region outage. The operations team has 3 members and wants to avoid the burden of configuring and checking a rotation function separately for each Region. The Tokyo application normally reads the secret through the local Region endpoint to reduce latency, and redeploying the applications in both Regions when the database password changes is not allowed. At rotation, the applications in both Regions must see the same value. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule and an AWS Lambda function to copy the value to AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store in the Tokyo Region whenever the Seoul secret changes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have the Tokyo application call the Secrets Manager endpoint in the Seoul Region directly, and do not create a separate secret in Tokyo.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create independent secrets in Seoul and Tokyo, and configure a rotation Lambda function for each secret so that the database password is rotated every 30 days.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure automatic rotation only on the primary secret in Seoul and replicate it to the Tokyo Region, so that the Tokyo replica is encrypted with a KMS key in the Tokyo Region.

exam-scs-c03-9.explanation: The correct answer is to configure rotation on the primary secret and replicate it to Tokyo. When the primary secret is rotated, the new value is propagated to all replicas, so there is no need to manage rotation for each replica, and the replica can be encrypted with a key in the Tokyo Region, so it can be read from Tokyo even during a Seoul outage. Rotating two independent secrets separately would change the same database password twice independently and cause the values to diverge. Copying to Parameter Store would require a heavy burden of direct implementation. Calling the Seoul endpoint cannot read the secret during a Seoul outage.

exam-scs-c03-10.prompt: A media service with users around the world operates an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses an internet-facing ALB as its origin, and AWS WAF is associated with CloudFront. The ALB security group currently allows port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. However, an attacker has discovered the ALB's DNS name and is connecting to it directly, bypassing CloudFront, where WAF is associated. The solution must not increase the maintenance burden of people continually updating security group rules, and the user response path must remain the same as it is now. Traffic averages tens of millions of requests per day, and origin response time must not increase. The security team wants to block the path by which requests that do not go through CloudFront reach the origin, at both L3/L4 and L7. Which TWO actions will ensure that the ALB accepts only requests that come through CloudFront? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Download the public IP ranges of the CloudFront edge servers directly, register them as ALB security group rules, and update them manually whenever the ranges change.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Change the ALB security group inbound rules to allow only port 443 traffic from the AWS managed prefix list for CloudFront origin-facing servers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Replace the ALB listener certificate with an ACM public certificate and upgrade the TLS security policy to the latest version to block clients that connect directly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Have CloudFront add a custom header with a secret value to origin requests, and configure the ALB listener rule to forward only requests that have that header and return 403 for all others.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Use Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to steer users toward CloudFront, and do not publicly disclose the ALB's DNS name.

exam-scs-c03-10.explanation: The managed prefix list is updated by AWS even if the CloudFront origin-facing IPs change, so it blocks direct access at L3/L4 without any security group maintenance burden. The secret custom header lets the ALB listener rule forward only requests that came through CloudFront at L7. Managing the edge IP ranges directly keeps adding update work. Changing the certificate and TLS policy does not restrict the access path. Steering with DNS routing cannot stop an attacker who already knows the ALB DNS name from connecting directly.

exam-scs-c03-11.prompt: The AWS Security Hub CSPM findings that analysts on a large enterprise's security operations team review each day average 600, and most are low-risk items from development environments. Informational-level findings are piling up from 30 accounts in the organization's development OU, and analysts are missing findings from production accounts. Findings for the same controls in production accounts must continue to be displayed as they are now, and the company wants to avoid disabling controls or writing and operating code. The security team has 4 members, and the administrator account is already delegated. Findings from development accounts must not be deleted entirely and must be retrievable when needed, and suppressed findings must not appear on the analysts' default dashboard. Which solution has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disable the relevant controls in all accounts across the organization and re-enable them only in production accounts, to stop findings from being generated in development accounts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the administrator account, create an automation rule that uses the development account IDs and informational severity as conditions and changes the workflow status to SUPPRESSED.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Write and deploy a function so that an Amazon EventBridge rule and AWS Lambda call BatchUpdateFindings to change the status whenever a development account finding is received.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a custom insight filtered by the development account IDs, and change the work procedure so that analysts view only the insight instead of the default findings screen.

exam-scs-c03-11.explanation: An automation rule is defined in the administrator account with conditions such as account ID and severity, automatically changes attributes such as the workflow status when findings are ingested, and requires no code. Disabling controls stops the generation of findings, so there is a risk of affecting production accounts as well, and it is not the method requested. Lambda and BatchUpdateFindings create the burden of writing and operating code. An insight only filters the view and cannot change the status of findings, so development findings keep piling up. Also note that a rule applies to findings ingested after it is created.

exam-scs-c03-12.prompt: A data processing platform uses KMS CreateGrant just before a job starts to give the batch worker role in the same account the Decrypt permission on a specific key, and revokes the grant when the job finishes. This approach comes from a security design that grants only temporary permissions per job, and thousands of jobs run every day. The key policy cannot be modified each time because of the change approval process. However, the first Decrypt call immediately after a grant is created intermittently fails with AccessDenied, and the job is retried. The grant applies to only one specific key, and the permission must disappear as soon as the job ends. Lengthening the retry logic was not accepted because of job delays. Which method guarantees use immediately after the grant is created while minimizing code changes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a kms:Decrypt allow for the worker role to the key policy as a permanent statement so that access is possible without a grant.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add kms:* permissions on the key to the worker role's IAM policy so that all KMS operations are allowed regardless of the grant propagation delay.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pass the grant token returned by CreateGrant in the GrantTokens parameter of the first Decrypt request so that the grant can be used before it propagates.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use ListGrants to look up the ID of the grant that was just created, and call Decrypt passing that grant ID as the GrantTokens value.

exam-scs-c03-12.explanation: The correct answer is to pass the grant token. KMS uses an eventual consistency model, so AccessDenied can occur immediately after a grant is created and before propagation completes. If you include the grant token returned by CreateGrant in the request, you can use the grant's permissions immediately, even before propagation. Adding a permanent allow to the key policy violates the change process constraint and also defeats the purpose of temporary permissions. Giving kms:* in the IAM policy grants excessive permissions and does not solve the problem if the key policy does not allow it. ListGrants returns only the grant ID and not the token, and the token can be obtained only from CreateGrant.

exam-scs-c03-13.prompt: A cloud security team has an internal standard that EBS snapshots must not be shareable publicly from any account. Until now, the team has used an SCP that denies ec2:ModifySnapshotAttribute, but the team needs a guarantee that the standard will continue to hold even when the service adds new APIs or features. Account administrators already hold many IAM policies that include snapshot sharing permissions, so it is difficult to revoke the policies in bulk. The scope is 150 accounts, and the security team wants to enforce this standard without depending on the cooperation of account administrators. In the past, the security team had to modify the SCP every time a new API was added, and as a result the standard was left unenforced for two weeks on one occasion. Which method will apply the standard consistently across the 150 accounts?

choices.label: A
