choices.text: Deploy to the organization a configuration that uses an AWS Config rule to detect snapshots that can be publicly restored and uses AWS Lambda automatic remediation to remove the sharing setting.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In AWS Organizations, specify block public access for snapshots as blocked in an EC2 declarative policy, and attach it to the organization root.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add more EC2 API names related to snapshot sharing to the SCP to expand the deny list, and update the policy every time a new API is released.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Distribute guidance for account administrators to turn on EBS snapshot block public access on their own, and verify whether it is set by using CloudTrail logs.

exam-scs-c03-13.explanation: The correct answer is an EC2 declarative policy. A declarative policy enforces the desired configuration directly at the service control plane, so the standard persists even when the service adds new features or APIs, and it supports the Snapshot Block Public Access attribute. SCPs control permissions at the API level, so the deny list must be updated whenever a new API appears, which does not meet the requirement for a lasting guarantee. Detection and automatic remediation with AWS Config are a reactive response that fixes the problem after the snapshot becomes public, leaving a window of exposure. Manual per-account settings cannot guarantee consistency or enforcement.

exam-scs-c03-14.prompt: The legal team requires both disk evidence and memory evidence from an EBS-backed Amazon EC2 instance suspected of being compromised. Traffic has already been drained from this instance in the production service, volatile data must not be lost, and the evidence collection process must be recorded. The collected evidence is stored in encrypted buckets and snapshots in a dedicated incident response account. The suspect instance is a single m5.2xlarge with 3 EBS volumes attached. The incident response account is in a separate security OU of the organization, and there are two forensic analysts. Every evidence collection step must be traceable to who did what and when, and the analysts can access the instance through SSM Agent. Which TWO actions are MOST appropriate to secure both kinds of evidence without stopping or terminating the instance? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run a read-only memory acquisition tool on the running instance, save the memory image to the evidence bucket, and record its hash.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Install an antivirus agent on the instance to clean up malicious files, then create a snapshot to keep evidence of the clean state, and return the instance to service.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stop the instance first, then create snapshots of the attached EBS volumes to freeze the disk state, and perform later analysis from the snapshots.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Without stopping the instance, create snapshots of all attached EBS volumes, share them with the incident response account, and keep encrypted copies there.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Terminate the instance with the delete-on-termination option turned off so that the EBS volumes remain, and attach them to another instance later for investigation.

exam-scs-c03-14.explanation: Volatile data such as memory and processes is lost when an instance is stopped, terminated, or rebooted, and EBS snapshots contain only the data written to the volume, so memory must be acquired separately. Therefore, two actions together preserve both kinds of evidence: first acquiring a memory image with a read-only tool while the instance remains running and recording its hash, and then creating snapshots of all volumes without stopping the instance and moving them to the incident response account. Stopping first and then taking snapshots preserves the disk but loses the memory evidence. Terminating and preserving only the volumes also loses the memory. Cleaning files with antivirus alters files and timestamps, which destroys evidence and also breaks the chain of custody.

exam-scs-c03-15.prompt: A video streaming company protects its Amazon CloudFront distributions and ALB with AWS Shield Advanced and subscribes to Business Support. After an outage caused by a surge of web requests last quarter, the company wants to set up a system in which the AWS Shield Response Team (SRT) contacts the company first when an event occurs. The company has registered the protected resources and two SRT contacts, has enabled the proactive engagement feature, and has created the web ACLs with AWS WAF v2. However, the SRT did not contact the company first even in a recent web request surge incident. The operations team has 3 members, and the company does not want to upgrade the support plan because of cost. The SRT contacts have both an email address and a phone number registered, and the Shield Advanced subscription is under consolidated billing for the entire organization. Which action will make proactive engagement work?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the subscription tier by upgrading the support plan from Business to Enterprise, because that is the only way to meet the SRT proactive engagement requirement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable the Shield Advanced cost protection feature to meet the conditions for being reimbursed for usage charges that increased because of a DDoS attack, and then start the SRT contact procedure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Associate Route 53 health checks with each protected resource and configure the health checks to reflect the actual application health.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Re-create the web ACLs with AWS WAF Classic and change the configuration to pre-delegate permissions that let the SRT modify rules directly.

exam-scs-c03-15.explanation: SRT proactive engagement determines whether an event qualifies for proactive engagement by looking at the status of the Route 53 health check associated with the protected resource. Without a health check, the SRT does not contact you first even if it detects the event. A Business or Enterprise Support plan satisfies the requirement, so no tier change is needed. Cost protection addresses charge increases caused by DDoS and is separate from proactive engagement. The web ACL must be AWS WAF v2, so reverting to Classic would actually violate the requirement.

exam-scs-c03-16.prompt: A global fintech company stores customer documents encrypted with the AWS Encryption SDK in Amazon S3 in the Seoul Region, and it must also decrypt the same documents in the Tokyo Region, its disaster recovery Region. Decryption must be possible even during a Seoul Region outage, and the data must not be re-encrypted and the KMS in the Seoul Region must not be called. The company wants to control key policies separately for each Region. Even during normal operation, the company wants decryption to complete within each Region without cross-Region calls, and the ciphertext has already been copied to both Regions. Security policy requires that documents be encrypted on the client side, and the audit team checks key usage records for the Seoul and Tokyo keys separately in each Region's CloudTrail. Encryption is handled using the envelope method by generating a data key for each object. There are not yet any resources in Tokyo created with this key. Which key configuration is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a multi-Region primary key in Seoul, create a replica key in Tokyo, and set the key policy and grants separately on the key in each Region.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use AWS managed keys in both Seoul and Tokyo, and modify the policy of the Tokyo Region key to match the contents of the Seoul Region policy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Continue to use the single-Region KMS key in Seoul, and have the Tokyo application make cross-Region Decrypt calls to the KMS endpoint in the Seoul Region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a new single-Region KMS key in Tokyo, re-encrypt all ciphertext in Seoul with the Tokyo key, and copy it to a bucket in the Tokyo Region.

exam-scs-c03-16.explanation: The correct answer is a multi-Region key. Related multi-Region keys share the same key ID and key material, so data encrypted in one Region can be decrypted with the replica key in another Region without re-encryption or cross-Region calls, and key policies and grants are managed independently for each Region. Calling the Seoul key cross-Region makes decryption impossible during a Seoul outage and also conflicts with the prohibition on calling KMS. Creating a new key in Tokyo would require re-encrypting all data, which violates the constraints. AWS managed keys are always single-Region keys, so they cannot share key material across Regions, and their policies cannot be modified.

exam-scs-c03-17.prompt: A company must record management events from all accounts in the organization in a single Amazon S3 bucket in a central log archive account. Newly created accounts must also be included automatically, and administrators of member accounts must not be able to stop or modify the trail. The company has a separate log archive account, and the audit team must also be able to verify the integrity of the log files. Dozens of accounts are added every month. Some existing accounts have trails that teams created themselves, but the company intends to consolidate to a single central bucket going forward. Logs must be retained for 7 years, and only the security team can modify the bucket policy in the log archive account. The security team has 3 members and has no capacity to handle per-account exceptions, and it verifies whether log files have been tampered with by using digests. Which method has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to create individual trails with the same settings in all accounts, and add stack instances when a new account is created.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have the trail in each account write to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, and configure log group subscription filters to replicate the logs to the central account.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Forward the AWS CloudTrail events in each account to an event bus in the central account with Amazon EventBridge rules, and configure it to store them in Amazon S3 from there.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the management account or a CloudTrail delegated administrator account, create an organization trail that delivers the events of all member accounts to the central bucket.

exam-scs-c03-17.explanation: The correct answer is an organization trail. When an organization trail is created once in the management account or a delegated administrator account, it records the events of all member accounts in the organization and of accounts added later, and member accounts can view it but cannot modify or stop it. Individual trails created with StackSets can be stopped or modified by member account administrators. Event bus forwarding is not a trail, so it cannot prevent member accounts from deleting rules, and it adds configuration for cleaning up the delivery targets. Log group replication is also a per-account setting that members can modify.

exam-scs-c03-18.prompt: A threat intelligence report warned of possible malware infection on the company's EC2 instance i-0abc, but there are no related findings at all in Amazon GuardDuty. The instance is in production, and installing an agent or performance degradation is not allowed. The instance has two attached volumes, and rebooting or stopping it is not allowed under the change approval process. This instance uses two EBS volumes, and GuardDuty is already enabled across the organization. The inspection results must be reported within one day, and only one person has permission to access the instance. The investigation results must be attached to the incident report, and the indicators in the threat intelligence report point to only this one instance. Which method confirms whether the attached EBS volumes contain malware with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Scan the instance with Amazon Inspector, review the software vulnerability findings, and compare them against known malware signatures to determine whether it is infected.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Wait and watch the status for a GuardDuty-initiated scan, which starts automatically when GuardDuty generates a malware-related finding.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Start an on-demand scan of GuardDuty Malware Protection for EC2 by using the instance ARN.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use Systems Manager to install an antivirus agent on all instances, schedule a full file system scan, and check for infection.

exam-scs-c03-18.explanation: The correct answer is an on-demand malware scan. You can start it by providing only the instance ARN even when there are no related GuardDuty findings, it scans the attached EBS volumes without an agent, and it is designed not to affect resource performance. A GuardDuty-initiated scan starts only when a finding that indicates possible malware is generated, so it does not run now when there are no findings. Inspector is a service that finds software vulnerabilities and does not determine malware infection. Installing an antivirus agent violates the constraints that do not allow an agent or performance degradation.

exam-scs-c03-19.prompt: Under the company's ransomware response policy, no one, including administrator accounts and the root user, may be able to delete the recovery points in an AWS Backup vault during the retention period. However, because mistakes can be made in the retention period settings, it must be possible to cancel or change the configuration for a few days after the lock is applied. The backup targets are Amazon EBS and Amazon RDS, the retention period is 1 year, and no team other than the security team has permission to change vault settings. Backups run every day at dawn, and the recovery points are gathered in one vault in the same Region. The security team considers it sufficient to be able to correct configuration mistakes only within the first few days. The backup resources are 200 EBS volumes and 40 RDS instances, and the recovery points created after the time the vault lock is applied are the ones to be protected. Which configuration is MOST appropriate to meet the requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set the vault access policy to deny the backup:DeleteRecoveryPoint action for all principals, and limit the permission to change the policy to the security team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure the backup plan to copy recovery points to a vault in another account, and operate without applying a separate lock to the source vault.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a vault lock in governance mode, specify the minimum and maximum retention periods, and allow only users with sufficient permissions to remove the lock.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a compliance mode vault lock and specify a changeable period (grace time) of at least 3 days.

exam-scs-c03-19.explanation: The correct answer is a compliance mode vault lock with a grace period. In compliance mode, after the grace period (minimum 3 days) ends, no one, including the customer, the account owner, or AWS, can change or delete the lock, and during the grace period the lock can be removed or the configuration changed, so configuration mistakes can be corrected. In governance mode, users with sufficient IAM permissions can remove the lock, which does not satisfy the requirement that no one can delete. A vault access policy can be removed by an administrator who can change the policy. Copying without locking leaves the original recovery points vulnerable to deletion.

exam-scs-c03-20.prompt: 120 developers at a SaaS company start and stop EC2 instances for 40 projects. A project tagging scheme is already applied to all instances, and each developer must be able to work only with instances that have the same Project tag as the project the developer belongs to. A few new projects are created each quarter, and the company wants to operate with a single policy without creating or modifying IAM policies each time. Employee accounts and per-project groups are managed in an external IdP, and users sign in to AWS with IAM Identity Center. The security team has 3 members. A developer belongs to only one project and not to multiple projects at the same time, and when a project ends, removing the developer from the group must be enough to complete the revocation of permissions. Which method is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create one permission set and IAM policy for each project that lists the ARNs of that project's instances, and assign it to the developer group.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pass the IdP's project value as an attribute for access control in IAM Identity Center, and in the permission set policy, allow EC2 actions only when the Project tag on the resource matches the tag on the principal.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure an organization SCP to deny EC2 actions whose project tags do not match, and grant the PowerUserAccess permission commonly to developers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Attach a resource-based policy to each instance that allows the account IDs of that project's developers, and update the policy when a project is added.

exam-scs-c03-20.explanation: Attribute-based access control passes IdP attributes as session tags, and a single policy compares whether the aws:PrincipalTag and aws:ResourceTag values are equal, so no policy changes are needed even as projects increase. Per-project policies leave the burden of continually adding to 40 policies. An SCP cannot grant permissions, and even when combined with PowerUserAccess it cannot map the tag comparison to a person's tag. EC2 instances do not have resource-based policies.

exam-scs-c03-21.prompt: A security analysis SaaS vendor uses a single account ID to call AssumeRole on read-only IAM roles in dozens of customer accounts to inspect their configurations. Customers enter the role ARN for each customer directly in the vendor's service screen. Currently, the trust policy is restricted to only the vendor's AWS account. However, there is a concern about the confused deputy problem: if one customer finds out another customer's role ARN and registers it with the vendor service, the vendor could assume that role on the customer's behalf and display the information. The number of customers keeps growing, so the vendor cannot make major changes to its code, and customers can modify only the trust policies in their own accounts. The vendor can issue and manage a unique identifier for each customer, and customers can copy the value that the vendor provides into the trust policy as is. Which method MOST appropriately reduces this risk?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Narrow the principal in the trust policy from the entire vendor account to one specific IAM role ARN used by the vendor, to restrict other principals from assuming it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reduce the role maximum session duration from one hour to 15 minutes to change the setting so that the period in which issued temporary credentials can be abused is shortened.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Put a sts:ExternalId condition that is unique to each customer in the trust policy, and have the vendor pass the per-customer value in the AssumeRole call.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a read-only IAM user in the customer account and hand the access keys to the vendor so that the vendor calls directly without assuming a role.

exam-scs-c03-21.explanation: The external ID condition makes the role assumable only by a caller that knows the unique value that the vendor issued per customer. Therefore, even if another customer registers someone else's role ARN, the vendor's call that uses that customer's external ID is denied, which prevents the confused deputy problem. The value must be generated and controlled by the vendor for each customer, not by the customer. Narrowing to one specific vendor role still leaves confusion among customers because the vendor calls all customers with the same role. Reducing the session duration only shortens the period of abuse after issuance and does not block the cause. Long-term access keys increase the risk further.

exam-scs-c03-22.prompt: The security team used Amazon GuardDuty to confirm signs that an attacker has already opened an SSH session on an EC2 instance in a public subnet and is communicating with an external C2 server. The instance security group allows inbound port 22 only from a specific administrator IP range and allows only some ports outbound. There is only this one instance in the subnet, and the instance must remain running because of the memory evidence. The credentials the attacker used on the instance have already been disabled, but the forensics team must acquire memory from the running instance within one hour. The instance role is not used by other services. This instance is directly accessible through its public IP, and there are currently no other instances using the same subnet. The subnet's network ACL uses the default settings (allow all traffic). Which isolation method is MOST appropriate to immediately cut off connections that are already established while preserving evidence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add deny rules for all inbound and outbound traffic to the subnet network ACL at the highest priority, and also apply an isolation security group.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Replace the instance's security group with a dedicated isolation security group that has empty inbound and outbound rules, and wait for the existing connections to be dropped.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stop the instance, then create snapshots of the attached EBS volumes and share them with the analysis account to make sure that the attacker's access is cut off.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Terminate the instance, launch a new instance from a clean golden AMI, and detach only the compromised instance's EBS volumes to keep as evidence.

exam-scs-c03-22.explanation: The correct answer is to add deny rules to the subnet network ACL. Security groups use connection tracking, so even if you change or remove the rules, connections that are already tracked remain allowed until they time out, but block rules in a stateless network ACL also cut existing connections. There is only one instance in the subnet, so other workloads are not affected. Replacing the group with an empty security group alone may leave the SSH and C2 sessions in place, so it does not satisfy the requirement for immediate blocking. Stopping the instance causes the memory evidence to be lost, which violates the constraint to keep it running. Terminating and relaunching destroys both the volatile evidence and the running state.

exam-scs-c03-23.prompt: A company that manages employee accounts and department groups in its on-premises identity provider wants employees to sign in to the AWS Management Console through its on-premises SAML 2.0 IdP. Employees must be able to choose different AWS roles depending on their department when they sign in, and the company has decided not to create separate IAM users on the AWS side. There are about 800 employees, and the IdP can already include department information in the SAML assertion. Two members of the infrastructure team will handle the federation work. The federation configuration on the AWS side is managed as IaC, and when the temporary credentials expire after an employee signs in, the employee signs in again through the IdP. The company plans to create 8 roles in total, one per department. Which TWO items must be configured for this federation to work? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure the IdP to include the Role and RoleSessionName attributes in the SAML response to pass the role ARN to assume and the provider ARN.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an IAM SAML identity provider from the IdP's SAML metadata, and create IAM roles with a trust policy that allows sts:AssumeRoleWithSAML.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create roles with a trust policy that allows sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, and have the IdP submit OIDC ID tokens directly to AWS.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an IAM user for each employee, name it the same as the IdP account name, and pass the console password in the SAML response.

choices.label: E
choices.text: In the IAM role trust policy, add the public IP address of the IdP server as an aws:SourceIp condition so that only requests from that IP can assume the role.

exam-scs-c03-23.explanation: SAML federation requires an IAM SAML provider created from the IdP metadata and roles that trust that provider and allow AssumeRoleWithSAML, and the IdP must include the Role and RoleSessionName attributes in the SAML response to indicate which role to assume. There is no need to create IAM users for each employee, and passwords are not placed in the SAML response. AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity is used for OIDC-based federation, so it does not fit SAML. An IdP server IP condition does not match the request path of the user's browser and is not a required setting.

exam-scs-c03-24.prompt: An online bookstore's login page receives millions of requests per day, and many enterprise customers connect from behind their corporate NAT. An AWS WAF web ACL is associated with the ALB. Recently, password brute-force attacks against the /login path have continued, and the company wants to block a client IP when it exceeds 100 requests in 5 minutes. However, enterprise customers behind the same NAT legitimately call paths other than /login thousands of times every 5 minutes, so they must not be blocked. The rule must be managed in the web ACL without a code deployment. The rule will be applied directly as Block without first being tested in Count, and the evaluation window will use 5 minutes from the values that WAF supports. Which rule will meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a rate-based rule that aggregates by IP with a 5-minute evaluation window and a limit of 100, and use a scope-down statement so that only requests whose URI path is /login are counted.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an IP-aggregated rate-based rule with a limit of 100 requests per 5 minutes without a scope-down, so that requests on all paths of the web ACL are counted against the same limit.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add the AWS WAF Bot Control targeted-protection-level managed rule group to the web ACL to automatically distinguish and block brute-force attacks on login requests.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set a request rate limit value in the ALB security group inbound rules to deny connection attempts of 100 or more per 5 minutes per client IP.

exam-scs-c03-24.explanation: A rate-based rule counts the requests within the evaluation window for each aggregation key such as IP, and by using a scope-down statement it can track only requests to the /login path and apply the limit, so normal calls to other paths are not affected. Without a scope-down, all calls from users behind the NAT are counted against the same IP limit and are blocked. Bot Control incurs additional charges and is excessive compared with the simple limit rule that was requested. Security groups do not have a request rate limiting feature.

exam-scs-c03-25.prompt: A company introduced a security requirement to turn on EBS encryption by default. The administrator enabled default encryption only in the Seoul Region, and a subsequent audit found that new unencrypted volumes had been created in the Virginia Region and that some existing volumes in Seoul are also not encrypted. There are hundreds of target volumes in each Region, and all changes are made through a planned procedure. The short downtime needed to replace volumes is allowed during the scheduled maintenance window, but data loss is not allowed. The volumes to be replaced include a mix of databases and file servers, so the mount points differ by volume, and each new volume must be created in the same Availability Zone as the existing volume. The tags and snapshot metadata before and after the replacement must be retained for cost tracking. Which TWO actions are MOST appropriate to resolve both problems? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use ModifyVolume to turn on the encryption attribute of the volume and encrypt the existing volume in place.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable EBS encryption by default in every other Region where workloads run.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a snapshot of each unencrypted volume, copy it with the encryption option, create a new volume from that snapshot, and replace the existing volume.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the default key setting in the Seoul Region by switching the default encryption KMS key to a customer managed key, so that existing volumes are re-encrypted with the new key.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Only recheck the setting status in the Regions that were flagged, because the Seoul default encryption setting is automatically propagated to all Regions in the account.

exam-scs-c03-25.explanation: The correct answers are to turn on default encryption in the other Regions and to replace existing volumes with encrypted snapshot copies. Default encryption is a per-Region setting, so it must be turned on in each Region, and it does not affect existing volumes and snapshots, so existing volumes are converted by encrypting the snapshot while copying it and creating a new volume. The statement that the Seoul setting propagates to other Regions is wrong. ModifyVolume has no capability to turn on encryption for an existing volume. Changing the default key affects only volumes created in the future and does not re-encrypt existing volumes.

exam-scs-c03-26.prompt: An external auditor requires SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certification reports for the physical security of AWS data centers and for AWS infrastructure. What is requested is AWS's own compliance documentation, not evidence of the configuration of the company's workloads, and the responsible person wants to download it directly from the account and submit it. The audit deadline is tight, so the company wants to obtain the documents directly from the account without going through a separate request process. The company has already collected configuration evidence for its own accounts with AWS Config and AWS Security Hub CSPM, and the auditor received that as separate evidence. The responsible person must obtain the documents by the day before the audit starts. The requested items are the SOC 2 Type II report and the ISO 27001 certificate, and the responsible person already has permission to sign in to the account. Which service will meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Evaluate the compliance status of the company's resources with an AWS Config conformance pack, and submit the score and the list of noncompliant resources as a report.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an assessment in AWS Audit Manager to automatically collect evidence about the company's AWS usage, generate a report, and submit it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Download the AWS infrastructure compliance reports and certificates on demand from AWS Artifact and submit them to the auditor.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Export the security standard check results from AWS Security Hub and submit the per-account control pass rates to the auditor as evidence.

exam-scs-c03-26.explanation: The correct answer is AWS Artifact. Artifact is a self-service portal where you can download directly from your account the certificates and reports that show that AWS infrastructure meets compliance requirements. Audit Manager is a service that collects evidence showing whether the company's AWS usage complies with regulations, so it is not AWS's own certification documentation. An AWS Config conformance pack evaluates the configuration compliance of the company's resources. Security Hub only shows the results of security standard checks for the account and does not provide AWS's own certification reports.

exam-scs-c03-27.prompt: A manufacturing company that manages the accounts of its 800 employees in Microsoft Entra ID wants to consolidate access to its 60 AWS accounts with AWS IAM Identity Center. Hires, departures, and department transfers occur every week, and the HR team enters changes only in Entra ID. The security team wants a departing employee's AWS access to be removed within one day. Permission sets are assigned to accounts at the department group level. The company does not want a procedure for creating and deleting users manually on the AWS side, and the cloud team has 2 members and cannot build and operate a separate synchronization program. The Entra ID group names are the same as the department names, and the AWS accounts belong to a single organization. Currently, IAM users exist in each account, and the company is phasing them out. Which configuration meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Connect Entra ID only as a SAML provider and bulk import users into Identity Center from a CSV file, with the responsible person re-importing whenever there are changes such as hires or departures.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Connect Entra ID as the external identity provider for IAM Identity Center, synchronize users and groups with SCIM automatic provisioning, and assign permission sets to the groups.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Register an IAM SAML provider in each of the 60 accounts, create an IAM role for each department, and have the Entra ID app pass the per-account role attributes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create users directly in the Identity Center directory, and operate a procedure in which the responsible person receives an HR team request email and deletes the user when someone leaves.

exam-scs-c03-27.explanation: Identity Center automatically synchronizes users and groups with an external identity provider through SCIM, so hires, departures, and transfers are reflected on the AWS side without manual work, and assigning permission sets to the synchronized groups consolidates per-account access. Connecting only SAML and importing a CSV requires periodic manual handling of the user lifecycle. Per-account SAML providers and roles increase the configuration across 60 accounts and run counter to the goal of centralization. Creating and deleting users directly is in direct conflict with the requirement.

exam-scs-c03-28.prompt: A security lead in an organization attached an SCP that denies all ec2:* actions to the organization root, and the default FullAWSAccess policy remains in place. The organization has a management account, a member account that acts as the delegated administrator for security services, and dozens of general workload member accounts. This SCP is attached to the organization root, so it applies normally to all member accounts. Afterward, the team found cases in which EC2-related calls still succeed in accounts that should not be using EC2, and is investigating the cause. The principle is that the management account is used only for organization management tasks, but some administrators sometimes sign in directly and use it when in a hurry. A few accounts still have workloads that use load balancers. Considering the scope of SCP application, which TWO cases are the most accurate in which EC2-related calls still succeed? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: A call by an administrator role in the member account designated as the delegated administrator to launch an instance

choices.label: B
choices.text: A call by the Elastic Load Balancing service-linked role in a member account to create a network interface for a load balancer

choices.label: C
choices.text: A call by an IAM role with the AdministratorAccess policy attached in a member account to launch an instance

choices.label: D
choices.text: A call by the root user of a member account to launch an instance with ec2:RunInstances

choices.label: E
choices.text: A call by an administrator role that has ec2:RunInstances permission in the management account to launch an instance

exam-scs-c03-28.explanation: The correct answers are a call from the management account and a call by a service-linked role. SCPs do not affect the users and roles of the management account, and they cannot restrict actions performed by service-linked roles. The root user of a member account is subject to SCPs, so the call is denied. A member account role with AdministratorAccess also fails because the SCP deny takes precedence. A member account designated as a delegated administrator is also subject to the SCP as is, so the call is blocked. Therefore, only the management account and the service-linked role cases succeed.

exam-scs-c03-29.prompt: A healthcare data company has received an audit requirement that, under regulations, data must be accessed only over private paths and that requests that pass through a NAT gateway are not allowed. The data bucket must be accessed only from workloads in the VPC vpc-0a1, and traffic must come only through an S3 gateway endpoint. The team allowed the VPC CIDR 10.0.0.0/16 with aws:SourceIp in the bucket policy, but all requests were denied. The workload instances are in private subnets, and the gateway endpoint is already associated with the route table. There is one bucket, and the changes must stay within the scope of the policy and the endpoint. The audit team prefers using a deny condition in the policy rather than an allow condition, and administrator console access has already been separated to a different path for this bucket. Which fix will meet the requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add the VPC's NAT gateway Elastic IP address to the aws:SourceIp condition of the bucket policy, so that requests leaving through the internet path are also included in the same allowed range.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove the aws:SourceIp condition from the bucket policy and change it to deny requests where aws:SourceVpce does not match the ID of that gateway endpoint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Attach an endpoint policy to the gateway endpoint that allows only that bucket, and keep only the block public access setting in the bucket policy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Associate a security group with the gateway endpoint that allows only port 443 from the VPC CIDR, and leave the IP condition in the bucket policy as it is.

exam-scs-c03-29.explanation: The aws:SourceIp key is not included in the request context for requests that go through a gateway endpoint, so allowing the VPC CIDR with this condition results in everything being denied. To allow only endpoint-based access, use an aws:SourceVpce condition in the bucket policy to deny requests that do not come from the specific endpoint. Allowing the NAT Elastic IP would open an internet path that is not the endpoint and violates the requirement. An endpoint policy only restricts requests leaving the VPC and is not a means for the bucket to block external access. A security group cannot be associated with a gateway endpoint.

exam-scs-c03-30.prompt: A financial company has only 3 incident response staff, and the time available for an investigation is within 1 hour per case. Today, GuardDuty produced a finding that the credentials of an EC2 instance role in a production account were used from an external IP. The analyst must check, in a single-screen workflow, without building a separate log pipeline or query tables, how much the role's API call volume and the connecting IPs and geolocations differ from the usual pattern, and what the related instances and IPs are. Time is short to determine the scope of the investigation and include it in the incident report. CloudTrail and VPC flow logs are already enabled in all accounts, but no query environment for analysis has been configured. The responsible analyst is using the relevant service for the first time. What should be used to perform this scoping investigation with the LEAST effort?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Collect the CloudTrail logs and VPC flow logs in Amazon S3, create Amazon Athena tables, and directly aggregate call statistics per role ARN and IP with SQL.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an AWS Security Hub CSPM insight to gather the findings associated with the role, and compare the historical call volume trend on the insight screen.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Scan the buckets the role accessed with Amazon Macie, and trace back records to determine what sensitive data was sent to which IP.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pivot from the GuardDuty finding to Amazon Detective, and compare against the normal pattern by using the entity profiles and behavior graph visualizations for the role and the IP.

exam-scs-c03-30.explanation: Detective automatically ingests CloudTrail, VPC flow logs, GuardDuty findings, and more to build a behavior graph. From a GuardDuty finding, you can go directly to an entity profile such as a role or IP, compare call volume and connecting geolocation against the usual pattern, and follow related entities. Athena aggregation requires you to build the log tables and queries yourself, which takes a lot of effort. Security Hub CSPM insights only group and display findings and do not provide behavioral baseline comparison. Macie is for detecting sensitive data in S3 and is not a tool for investigating the scope of credential misuse.

exam-scs-c03-31.prompt: A medical records archive system must ensure that all objects in an Amazon S3 bucket cannot be deleted or overwritten by anyone, including the root user, for 7 years. In addition, because of litigation, some objects must not be deleted even after 7 years, for a period whose end point is unknown, and only the legal team must be able to release them. Versioning is already turned on for the bucket, and there are tens of millions of objects. Some patient records may receive deletion requests before the retention period ends, but under regulations the retention period takes precedence. The security team wants to avoid the work of managing a retention period separately for each object. The legal team organizes the list of objects subject to litigation by case number and delivers it, and the targets change frequently. The auditor wants a history of changes to retention settings to remain. Which configuration will meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set the Object Lock default retention to governance mode for 7 years, and give only the legal team role the s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permission so that it manages retention during litigation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set the Object Lock default retention to compliance mode for 30 years, locking all objects for a long period so that retention is never released before the litigation ends.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turn on MFA delete for the bucket and deny s3:DeleteObjectVersion to all principals in the bucket policy to prevent deletion during the retention period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set the Object Lock default retention to compliance mode for 7 years, apply legal holds to the objects subject to litigation, and grant the legal hold permission only to the legal team.

exam-scs-c03-31.explanation: The correct answer is the combination of compliance mode default retention and legal holds. Compliance mode prevents anyone, including the root user, from deleting or overwriting an object version within the retention period, and a legal hold has no expiration date and remains until it is explicitly released, and only users with the s3:PutObjectLegalHold permission can set or release it. Governance mode lets users with the bypass permission change retention or delete, which violates the requirement that not even root can do so. A 30-year compliance retention cannot be shortened and is excessive for all objects. MFA delete and a bucket policy can be removed by an administrator who can modify them, so they are not immutable.

exam-scs-c03-32.prompt: In a company that uses two accounts in the same organization, the CI pipeline in account A tries to assume the deploy role in account B at every deployment but gets AccessDenied (no sts:AssumeRole permission). The trust policy of the deploy role in account B lists the account A root as the principal, and the CI role in account A has only an S3 access policy attached. Today's deployment is blocked and the release is delayed, and there is no time to touch organization-wide policies or the configuration of other accounts. The CI role is used only for the pipeline in account A, and account B has already reviewed and approved the permissions policy of the deploy role. The two accounts are in the same OU in Organizations, and only the default FullAWSAccess SCP is applied. Which method is MOST appropriate to resolve this with minimal changes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the principal in the trust policy of the deploy role in account B from the account A root to the ARN of the account A CI role, to narrow the trust scope.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attach a permissions boundary to the deploy role in account B and include a statement that allows sts:AssumeRole in the boundary policy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add an allow for sts:AssumeRole on the ARN of the deploy role in account B to the identity-based policy of the CI role in account A.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add an sts:AssumeRole allow statement to the SCP of the OU that account A belongs to so that all accounts can assume each other's roles.

exam-scs-c03-32.explanation: Cross-account role assumption must be allowed both in the trust policy of the target account and in the identity-based policy of the calling principal in the caller's account. The trust policy already allows account A, so what is missing is the sts:AssumeRole permission on the CI role. Narrowing the trust principal to the CI role is a more restrictive change and does not resolve the missing permission on the calling side. A permissions boundary does not grant permissions and only restricts them. An SCP also cannot grant permissions with an allow statement.

exam-scs-c03-33.prompt: An organization operates 80 accounts with AWS Organizations, and dozens of new accounts are created each month. The security team wants GuardDuty to be turned on in both the Seoul and Tokyo Regions for both existing accounts and accounts that will be created in the future. The team does not want to use management account credentials for day-to-day security operations, and wants to avoid having a responsible person enable it account by account or building and operating separate automation each time an account is created. Accounts are created directly with the Organizations API without using Control Tower, and new accounts must be protected by GuardDuty within the same day after creation. The security team has 3 members. The team wants to eliminate the procedure of making a request to a responsible person each time an account is created. Which method has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Designate a dedicated security member account as the GuardDuty delegated administrator, and from that account set organization auto-enable to all accounts (ALL) in each of the Seoul and Tokyo Regions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Designate a dedicated security member account as the GuardDuty delegated administrator, and from that account set organization auto-enable to new accounts only (NEW) in each of the Seoul and Tokyo Regions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Receive the account creation event of the management account with an Amazon EventBridge rule, and implement an AWS Lambda function that enables GuardDuty in both Regions of the new account.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Document a procedure for signing in to each member account and enabling GuardDuty in both Regions in the console, and have the responsible person repeat it each time an account is created.

exam-scs-c03-33.explanation: The correct answer is a delegated administrator with organization auto-enable (ALL). When the management account designates the security account as the delegated administrator, that account manages the organization's member accounts, and setting auto-enable to ALL turns on GuardDuty for both existing accounts and newly joining accounts. GuardDuty is a Regional service, so it must be configured separately in Seoul and Tokyo. NEW applies only to new accounts, so the 80 existing accounts would be missed. An event plus Lambda implementation carries the burden of building and maintaining code. Manual per-account enablement results in omissions and repetition as accounts grow.

exam-scs-c03-34.prompt: Application code calls AWS Secrets Manager by using the default name secretsmanager.ap-northeast-2.amazonaws.com, and the code cannot be changed. The company is creating an interface endpoint so that dozens of servers in private subnets can use this service without an internet path, but when the option to enable the private DNS name is selected, enabling fails because of the VPC settings. DNS resolution is turned on and DNS hostnames is turned off for this VPC. The endpoint security group already allows port 443 from the entire VPC. The VPC spans multiple subnets and Availability Zones, and the servers that use the same endpoint are replaced with new ones at every deployment. The application settings are fixed in the server image, so a deployment that changes the call address is not allowed. What should be done to resolve this with the fewest settings and without code changes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the call URL in the application settings to the endpoint-specific DNS name, and apply it to all servers through the deployment pipeline.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint and a forwarding rule to send queries for the default name to an internet DNS server to be resolved.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Allow the entire VPC CIDR on port 443 in the inbound rules of the endpoint security group so that connections succeed even if the default name resolves to a public IP.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable the DNS hostnames attribute of the VPC, and then turn on enabling the private DNS name for the endpoint.

exam-scs-c03-34.explanation: To use a private DNS name, both DNS resolution and the DNS hostnames attribute of the VPC must be turned on. Once hostnames is turned on, the endpoint resolves the default service name to the endpoint's private IP inside the VPC, so no code changes are needed. Changing to the endpoint-specific DNS name violates the constraint against code changes. An outbound endpoint and internet DNS forwarding would instead cause the name to resolve to a public IP. Allowing the security group does not change the name resolution problem.

exam-scs-c03-35.prompt: An OU managed by AWS Control Tower already has 300 running Amazon RDS instances, and some of them have storage encryption turned off. The security team wants to view the list and status of the currently noncompliant databases on a dashboard without interrupting applications, and does not want to block existing operations or new deployments. Control Tower is already managing the accounts registered in the landing zone, and the security team wants to see the control status for each OU on a single screen. The RDS instances to be investigated number 300, spread across 40 accounts. The security team will carry out the encryption conversion separately after a schedule is set, so for now it needs only to understand the current state. The team wants to view noncompliance by OU on the Control Tower dashboard, and the development team is concerned that schedules will slip if new database deployments are interrupted. Which control type will meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A preventive control, which uses an SCP to deny at the organizational unit level the action of creating an unencrypted RDS instance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A mandatory control, which applies to the OU the default controls that protect the resources deployed by Control Tower, to check RDS encryption.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A detective control, in which an AWS Config rule evaluates the resources in the accounts and shows the noncompliant state as a violation on the dashboard.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A proactive control, in which an AWS CloudFormation hook inspects the template before provisioning and stops the creation of noncompliant resources.

exam-scs-c03-35.explanation: The correct answer is a detective control. A detective control is implemented with an AWS Config rule, evaluates existing resources in the accounts, shows states such as clear or in violation on the dashboard, and does not block operations. A preventive control denies actions with a policy such as an SCP, so it cannot report the state of existing resources and blocks later operations, which conflicts with the requirements. A proactive control only inspects resources provisioned through CloudFormation before they are created and does not evaluate databases that are already running. Mandatory controls protect the resources that Control Tower deployed and are unrelated to checking RDS encryption.

exam-scs-c03-36.prompt: The key of an IAM user with administrator permissions in one member account of AWS Organizations has been leaked, and an attacker is creating resources. No one is responsible for the root user credentials of this account, so they cannot be used. The team wants to stop the attacker's activity immediately while preserving evidence without deleting resources, and to allow only one designated response role, IR-Forensics, to be used for the investigation. The attacker may have already created additional IAM users and roles, so the entire account must be controlled at once. The attacker has already created dozens of EC2 instances and S3 buckets, and the billing amount for the affected account continues to grow. The legal team requires that the state of the resources be preserved as is. Access must be blocked before checking the IAM users or roles the attacker created, and the organization's management account continues to be responsible for the billing information of this account. Which action is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: From the management account, attach to the account an SCP that denies all actions except for the response role.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run a script that sets permissions boundaries on all IAM users and roles to reduce the scope of permissions the attacker can use.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remove the account from the organization to make it a standalone account, register billing information separately, and completely isolate it from the other accounts in the organization.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Close the account to put it in a suspended state, and then investigate the resources of the closed account within the suspension period to secure evidence.

exam-scs-c03-36.explanation: The correct answer is to attach to the account an SCP that denies everything except the response role. An SCP restricts the requests of all IAM users and roles in the member account, including the root user, so an attacker with administrator permissions is blocked, the resources remain as they are, and only the role allowed by the condition can investigate. Removing the account from the organization loses the SCP control from above and leaves no means of stopping the attacker. Closing the account puts it in a suspended state, which makes investigative access difficult, and the content is deleted after the suspension period. A permissions boundary can be removed or bypassed by an attacker with administrator permissions.

exam-scs-c03-37.prompt: A security audit has requested a list of software vulnerabilities for all instances. The account has 300 EC2 Linux instances, 40 of which do not have the SSM Agent, and security policy does not allow installing an agent. The 40 instances are EBS-backed with an ext4 file system and 2 volumes totaling 500 GB. The remaining 260 instances are already managed with the SSM Agent, Amazon Inspector is not enabled, and the audit deadline is 2 weeks away. The 40 instances are in production, so they must be assessed without restarting or installing software, and the results must be delivered as a CVE list for each instance. The account uses Inspector only in the Seoul Region. Which method requires the fewest changes to obtain OS package vulnerability results for these instances without installing an agent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Keep the Amazon Inspector scan mode agent-based, and deploy the SSM Agent and an instance profile in bulk to the 40 instances to convert them into managed instances.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set the Amazon Inspector EC2 scan mode to hybrid scanning so that instances not managed by SSM receive agentless scanning based on EBS snapshots.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turn on GuardDuty Malware Protection for EC2 to periodically scan the volumes of the 40 instances and receive the OS package vulnerability list as the result.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Turn on Amazon Inspector ECR container image scanning and judge host vulnerabilities instead from the vulnerabilities of the images deployed on the instances.

exam-scs-c03-37.explanation: Inspector's hybrid scan mode applies agent-based scanning to instances managed by SSM and agentless scanning that reads EBS snapshots to unmanaged instances, and these instances meet the conditions of being EBS-backed, using ext4, having fewer than 8 volumes, and totaling 1,200 GB or less. Keeping agent-based scanning conflicts with the constraint that an agent cannot be installed. Malware Protection for EC2 is malware detection and not package vulnerability scanning. ECR image scanning cannot substitute for the host OS packages.

exam-scs-c03-38.prompt: About 50,000 files are uploaded per day, with varied extensions and sizes. There is one Amazon S3 bucket (ap-northeast-2) to which customers upload documents, and this account does not use GuardDuty. The security team wants to scan only the uploaded files for malware without turning on all of GuardDuty, and it needs to receive the scan results as object tags or events and automatically decide whether to quarantine. Most uploaded objects are a few MB in size, and some PDF and Office documents reach hundreds of MB. The quarantine handling has already been built with AWS Lambda, and it is acceptable for the scan charges to be proportional to the upload volume. The bucket policy uses presigned URLs for uploads from outside, and the upload path cannot be changed. Objects determined to be quarantine targets must be blocked from access immediately. Which configuration meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Turn on GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 as a standalone feature for the bucket, and build the quarantine flow with scan result tagging or Amazon EventBridge events.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turn on GuardDuty and S3 Protection in the account, treat anomaly detection findings based on AWS CloudTrail S3 data events as a malicious file verdict, and integrate a Lambda function that moves the object to a quarantine bucket when a finding appears.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Run an Amazon Macie sensitive data discovery job every day to find malware signatures in the uploaded objects, and send the results to Amazon EventBridge.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable Amazon Inspector and configure it to perform a vulnerability scan on every object uploaded to the bucket to determine whether the file is malicious.

exam-scs-c03-38.explanation: Malware Protection for S3 can be turned on for a bucket as a standalone feature without enabling the GuardDuty service. It automatically scans newly uploaded objects and new versions, then publishes the results to EventBridge and a CloudWatch namespace, and tagging is also optional. The combination of all of GuardDuty and S3 Protection only detects anomalous behavior in S3 data events, does not scan file contents for malware, and is broader than the requested scope. Macie is a service for finding sensitive data and not a malware scanner. Inspector scans software vulnerabilities in EC2, ECR, and Lambda, so it does not fit determining whether an S3 object is malware.

exam-scs-c03-39.prompt: A deployment pipeline runs on GitHub-hosted runners, and security policy prohibits storing long-term AWS keys in repository secrets. The company wants a GitHub Actions workflow to deploy to an AWS account without long-term access keys. Only workflows on the main branch of a specific repository, acme/web, must be able to assume the deployment role. The workflow runs in a single repository, acme/web, and the deployment target is a single account, and the security team wants to prevent workflows from other repositories or workflows on development branches from assuming this role. The deployment tool is the AWS CDK, and only one role will exist in the deployment account. The default value for the temporary credential lifetime is sufficient. Which TWO configurations are MOST appropriate to meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Register the GitHub OIDC issuer token.actions.githubusercontent.com as an IAM OIDC identity provider.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the deployment role trust policy, allow sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity and set conditions with aud as sts.amazonaws.com and sub as repo:acme/web:ref:refs/heads/main.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Specify the root of the AWS account owned by GitHub as the principal in the deployment role trust policy and allow sts:AssumeRole, to allow all GitHub workflows to assume the role.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Store the access key of a deployment IAM user in the GitHub repository secrets, and operate a procedure in which a responsible person rotates the key every 90 days.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Put the entire IP range of GitHub-hosted runners in an aws:SourceIp condition on the deployment role and allow all requests coming from those IPs.

exam-scs-c03-39.explanation: GitHub Actions authenticates to AWS with an OIDC token, so you register the issuer as an IAM OIDC provider, allow AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity in the role trust policy, and restrict the repository and branch with the aud and sub conditions. This way no long-term keys are needed. Access keys in repository secrets violate the requirement against long-term credentials, and rotation is manual. Trusting the GitHub account root would make any workflow or repository a possible caller. Allowing the runner IP ranges also allows the runners of other repositories.

exam-scs-c03-40.prompt: A data protection team wants to centrally enforce that the S3 buckets and KMS keys in all member accounts of the organization do not allow access to principals from AWS accounts outside the organization. The control must block mistakes even if a development team adds a statement allowing an external account to a bucket policy, and because there are 150 accounts, modifying bucket policies one by one would be too heavy an operational burden. The team determined that, because the teams that own buckets differ from account to account, owner education alone cannot fully prevent such mistakes. There are no buckets legitimately shared with accounts outside the organization, and when external auditors need access, a separate account is invited into the organization for their use. Requests in which AWS services access buckets and keys on behalf of users must continue to work. The compliance team wants to apply this control to the entire organization at once and to manage change history with a single policy. Which method is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Turn on the S3 account-level Block Public Access setting in all member accounts to block the path by which principals from external accounts access buckets and objects.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attach to the organization root an RCP that uses the aws:PrincipalOrgID condition to deny S3 and KMS access by principals outside the organization, excluding requests from AWS service principals where aws:PrincipalIsAWSService is true.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Attach to the organization root a service control policy (SCP) that contains the same deny condition and the AWS service principal exception, to block S3 and KMS access by external principals all at once.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deploy, with AWS CloudFormation StackSets, bucket policies that contain a statement denying principals outside the organization to each bucket, and handle new buckets in the deployment pipeline.

exam-scs-c03-40.explanation: The correct answer is to attach an RCP to the organization root. Placing an aws:PrincipalIsAWSService exception in the deny condition keeps requests that AWS service principals make on behalf of users allowed. An RCP sets the maximum permissions on resources in member accounts, and even if a resource-based policy allows an external account, it can block requests from principals outside the organization, and it supports S3 and KMS. An SCP restricts only IAM users and roles inside the organization and does not apply to requests from principals in external accounts. Block Public Access blocks public access but does not block access that is allowed to a specific external account principal. Deploying bucket policies with StackSets can be overwritten by bucket owners who can modify the policies, and KMS keys would need to be handled separately.

exam-scs-c03-41.prompt: A financial company wants to continuously understand where personal information is located across thousands of S3 buckets in its organization's 120 accounts while minimizing cost, and to run a precise full-object scan on only a few buckets that appear to be high risk. The personal information to be identified includes common types such as credit card numbers and bank account numbers, and the 4 members of the security team will review the results every month. Some buckets have been reported in the past as having public read status. New buckets are continually created, the total data volume is several PB, and there are no staff to build and operate separate analysis code. Most buckets are archives with few changes, and a precise scan is needed only for the buckets that the security team designates. The results must be viewable for the entire organization in one place. The number of accounts and buckets keeps growing, so new buckets must also automatically become evaluation targets. Which approach is MOST cost-effective?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an AWS Lambda function for each bucket to read objects and analyze personal information with Amazon Comprehend, and store the results in a central bucket.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turn on GuardDuty S3 Protection across the organization and configure it to detect the personal information types contained in objects along with anomalous access.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turn on automated sensitive data discovery across the organization, and run discovery jobs only on the buckets with high sensitivity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a sensitive data discovery job that targets all buckets and repeats daily, so that all objects are analyzed without omission every day.

exam-scs-c03-41.explanation: The correct answer is the combination of automated sensitive data discovery and targeted discovery jobs. Automated discovery continuously evaluates the bucket inventory, selects representative objects as samples to analyze, and provides broad visibility through sensitivity scores and heatmaps at a low cost, while jobs analyze risky buckets in greater depth. Running a daily job on all buckets repeatedly analyzes all objects, which makes the cost large. A per-bucket Lambda function with Comprehend requires direct implementation and management. GuardDuty S3 Protection detects anomalous access and does not identify personal information inside objects.

exam-scs-c03-42.prompt: An e-commerce company's security team is strengthening its data loss prevention policy and wants to apply the same rule to both development and production accounts. Under the organization's policy, instances in a VPC must not be able to copy data through an S3 gateway endpoint to buckets in external AWS accounts that are not owned by the organization. Recently, a developer uploaded test data to a bucket in a personal account. The organization has many accounts, the company's own policies cannot be applied to external buckets, and access to buckets inside the organization must remain as it is now. Endpoints have already been created for each VPC, and there is no case in which data needs to be exchanged with external partners. The policy must be applied in the same way to new VPCs as well. Which method is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deploy bucket policies that deny external account principals to all S3 buckets in the organization, to block copy requests to other accounts from the bucket side.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove the S3 prefix list from the outbound rules of the instance security groups, and allow access to organization buckets only through the NAT gateway path.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the S3 gateway endpoint policy, allow S3 actions only on resources where aws:ResourceOrgID equals the organization ID.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a rule to the VPC subnet NACL that denies the domain name of buckets in external accounts, to block data copy requests before they leave.

exam-scs-c03-42.explanation: The endpoint policy applies to requests going from the VPC to S3, and allowing only when the target resource is owned by the organization, by using the aws:ResourceOrgID condition, blocks copying to buckets in external accounts while keeping access to organization buckets. A bucket policy applies only to the organization's own buckets, so it cannot control requests that write to external buckets. Removing the prefix list and using a NAT path instead leaves an internet path for reaching external buckets. A NACL works on IP and port and cannot deny bucket domain names.

exam-scs-c03-43.prompt: A broker service in a multi-tenant SaaS creates a new session for each request, calls AssumeRole on the per-tenant role tenant-role, and passes a session policy along with it. The role's identity-based policy allows only s3:GetObject on the entire bucket. The session policy passed with each call allows s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject on the tenantA/ prefix. The development team is verifying whether this configuration isolates tenants from each other and whether writes also work. The bucket policy has no separate denies or allows, and the session was created for tenantA. The broker runs in one of the organization's accounts, and the team wants to check only the policy configuration without code changes. Which is the MOST accurate description of the results of the actions that the tenantA session attempts?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both reading and writing objects under tenantA/ succeed, and only reading objects under tenantB/ is denied because it is outside the scope of the session policy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only reading objects under tenantA/ succeeds, and both writing objects under tenantA/ and reading objects under tenantB/ are denied.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reading and writing objects under tenantA/ succeed, and reading objects under tenantB/ also succeeds because the role policy allows it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because the session policy takes precedence over the role policy, all actions succeed, including writes to the tenantA/ prefix that the session policy allows.

exam-scs-c03-43.explanation: A session policy does not grant permissions and only reduces the permissions allowed by the role's identity-based policy, and the effective permissions of the session are the intersection of the two policies. Reading is allowed by both policies, so reading tenantA/ objects succeeds. Writing is not allowed by the role policy, so it is denied even though the session policy allows it. Reading tenantB/ is allowed by the role policy but is not in the session policy, so it is denied. Any explanation that the session policy increases permissions beyond the role policy is wrong.

exam-scs-c03-44.prompt: The security team of a company that creates 5 to 10 new accounts per month aims for consistent policy application without manual checks. The team created an AWS Firewall Manager AWS WAF policy so that an AWS WAF web ACL is automatically associated with all ALBs, including those in new accounts, across the 40 accounts of an AWS Organizations organization. However, in some accounts the resources within the policy scope are not evaluated and the noncompliant state persists. The policy itself and the organization configuration have been confirmed to be correct, and the Firewall Manager administrator account is also designated. Most of the problem accounts recently joined the organization. The administrator checked the status of those accounts in the Firewall Manager console, and they are not accounts excluded from the policy scope. Several weeks have passed since the policy was created. What should be checked and fixed first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add an inbound allow rule to the ALB security group of those accounts so that the Firewall Manager service can access it, to allow the policy association.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Change the policy scope to the management account alone, move the ALBs to the management account, and have the same policy evaluated within a single account.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Issue an IAM user access key in each account, and configure the Firewall Manager administrator account to associate web ACLs with those keys.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Verify that AWS Config is enabled and recording resource configurations in the accounts and Regions included in the policy scope, and turn it on where it is off.

exam-scs-c03-44.explanation: Firewall Manager can evaluate resources and apply rules only when AWS Config is enabled in the accounts and Regions within the policy scope, and accounts in which Config is off remain noncompliant or unevaluated. The service works through service-linked roles and the Organizations integration rather than security group rules, so allowing it in a security group is irrelevant. Moving ALBs to the management account gives up the goal of automatic protection across the whole organization. Issuing access keys increases long-term credentials and is not how Firewall Manager works.

exam-scs-c03-45.prompt: A role in account B must read S3 objects that are encrypted with a customer managed KMS key in account A. The two accounts are in different OUs of the same organization, and the objects are encrypted with SSE-KMS. The IAM policy of the account B role has an allow for kms:Decrypt on the key ARN, and the access allow on the S3 bucket side is also in place, but decryption fails with AccessDenied. The key policy in account A has only the default statement for the account A root. The key is also used by other workloads in account A, so account A's existing access method must not be changed. Account B is operated by another team, the security administrator of account A can modify the key policy directly, and the deployment deadline is within this week. Which resolution is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because the account B IAM policy allow already exists, have the account A root user delete the default statement of the key policy so that only account B uses the key.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In account A, convert the key to a multi-Region key to create a replica, and change the key ID so that account B decrypts with the replica.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Specify the account A key ARN explicitly with a Condition in the kms:Decrypt allow of the account B role policy, to make the cross-account allow scope more specific.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add to the account A key policy a statement that allows kms:Decrypt with the account B account or that role as the principal.

exam-scs-c03-45.explanation: KMS key access is based on the key policy. For a principal in another account to use the key, the key policy must allow that account or principal, and the calling account's IAM policy must also allow it. The key policy has only account A, so account B's request is denied. Deleting the default statement also removes the delegation to IAM policies in account A itself, which actually makes access management harder. Multi-Region keys are for replication across Regions and cannot replace a cross-account access allow. Adding a condition to the IAM policy does not resolve the absence of an allow in the key policy.

exam-scs-c03-46.prompt: A public subnet that hosts a public web service accepts connections from the internet on TCP 443. Currently, the NACL for this subnet has, besides the default deny rule, only one rule, numbered 100, that allows inbound TCP 443 from all IPs. This morning, attack traffic was confirmed to be coming from 198.51.100.0/24. Normal user access to the service must continue to be allowed, and without touching the security groups, only this range must be blocked at the subnet boundary within minutes. The subnet has 12 web servers, and the service spans multiple Availability Zones. NACLs are managed per subnet, and the current change history is retained in AWS CloudTrail. The blocking rule must be easy to remove after the attack stops. Which method is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add an inbound deny rule for 198.51.100.0/24 TCP 443 to the NACL as rule number 200, so that the range is blocked after the existing allow rule.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add an inbound deny rule for 198.51.100.0/24 TCP 443 to the NACL with a number lower than 100, so that it is evaluated before the allow rule.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add a deny entry for 198.51.100.0/24 to the inbound rules of the web server security group to block HTTPS requests from that range in front of the servers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a route for the destination 198.51.100.0/24 to the subnet route table so that response traffic is directed to a blackhole target, cutting off the connections.

exam-scs-c03-46.explanation: NACL rules are evaluated starting from the lowest number, and the first matching rule is applied, so the deny rule must be given a number lower than the allow rule 100 so that the range is blocked before it reaches the allow rule. A deny rule numbered 200 is never evaluated because rule 100 matches first. Security groups have only allow rules and cannot have deny rules. Changing the response route cannot prevent the TCP connection from being established, so it is unreliable, and it also fails to meet the requirement to block at the subnet boundary.

exam-scs-c03-47.prompt: A company wants users of its mobile app to sign up with email and, after signing in, have the app upload directly only to their own S3 prefix, uploads/{unique user ID}/.
