There are an average of 200,000 users per day, and uploads are made directly from the app, so they must be handled without server involvement. The development team has 3 members and has no capacity to create per-user policies separately or to operate an upload server. The app must obtain temporary AWS credentials without going through a server, and the company wants to handle per-user prefix isolation with a single policy. User information is stored in an Amazon Cognito user pool at email sign-up, and uploaded objects need to be read and written only by the user. The mobile app already uses the AWS SDK. Latency only needs to be at a level that does not affect the start of an upload. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Have the app present the ID token issued by the Cognito user pool directly to Amazon S3 for authentication, restrict the prefix in the bucket policy by the sub claim of the token, and when the token expires, have the app obtain a new token from the user pool with a refresh token and present it again.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Build an Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda upload proxy so that the app sends the file to Lambda, and Lambda adds the prefix by user ID and stores it in Amazon S3.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sign in with the Cognito user pool, obtain temporary credentials for the authenticated role through an identity pool, and restrict the prefix in the role policy by using the cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub policy variable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Issue an IAM user and access key for each user and store it in the app, and attach an individual IAM policy that uses the user name as the prefix.

exam-scs-c03-47.explanation: The user pool handles authentication and token issuance, and the identity pool issues temporary credentials for an IAM role to authenticated users. Using the cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub policy variable in the role policy isolates per-user prefixes with a single policy. S3 does not directly authenticate user pool JWTs. A Lambda proxy creates problems with the requirement not to go through a server and with the cost of relaying upload data. Per-user IAM users and long-term keys are inappropriate for both security and management.

exam-scs-c03-48.prompt: After a breach, an auditor requires proof that the CloudTrail log files accumulated in the central S3 bucket over the last 90 days were not modified or deleted after delivery. The trail had log file integrity validation turned on from the beginning, and there are records of an attacker with administrator permissions attempting to access this bucket. The bucket is in the security account, and the logs contain management events from all Regions, with a retention period of 1 year. While the attacker was attempting access, objects in the log delivery bucket may have been deleted, so the auditor wants signature-based evidence. The validation will be performed in the security account, and the logs are stored in the bucket with SSE-S3. The security team wants to provide the proof using the method that CloudTrail provides by default, without building new tools or a separate server. Which method is MOST appropriate to meet this requirement with no additional infrastructure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use the CLI validate-logs command to verify the digest file signatures and the log file hashes for that period.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply S3 Object Lock in compliance mode to the bucket now, and explain to the auditor that the logs from the past 90 days could not have been modified.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Query the bucket configuration change history in the AWS Config timeline, and present it as evidence that the contents of the log objects did not change.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Import the CloudTrail event history into a new event data store, and report by comparing whether the event count equals the count in the original logs.

exam-scs-c03-48.explanation: The correct answer is to verify the digest files with validate-logs. When integrity validation is turned on, CloudTrail creates a hash for each log file and delivers a signed digest file to the same bucket every hour, so you can use SHA-256 and RSA signatures to check whether a file was modified or deleted after delivery. Because the feature was already turned on, there is no retroactivity problem. Object Lock only prevents future deletions and cannot prove that past data was not tampered with. The configuration history in AWS Config cannot show changes to object contents. Comparing counts cannot cryptographically prove that the contents were not tampered with.

exam-scs-c03-49.prompt: Amazon GuardDuty reported a finding about an unusual API call pattern from an IAM role in a development account. The analyst does not want to use SQL and wants to follow the IP addresses, other accounts, and resources associated with this role and compare them with normal activity to judge the scope of the damage. The period under investigation is the last 3 months, and the analyst is not given separate access to the raw log storage. The analyst must report the investigation results within one day, and the account is linked to other accounts in the organization through IAM role chaining, so the analyst must also check whether the damage spread to other accounts. The role under investigation is used jointly by the CI pipeline and developers in the development account and has high activity volume. Which service meets this requirement while minimizing the work of collecting and parsing logs directly?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a CloudTrail log table with Amazon Athena and directly query the call history per role ARN to narrow down the anomaly times and counterpart resources.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use Amazon Detective to move from the finding to the role's entity profile and review the activity of the connected IPs and resources through the behavior graph.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Scan the software vulnerabilities of the instances that use the role with Amazon Inspector, and trace back the breach path and affected resources.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Aggregate the findings across accounts and Regions with AWS Security Hub, then create a custom insight to examine the role's call trend and connected targets.

exam-scs-c03-49.explanation: The correct answer is Amazon Detective. Detective builds a behavior graph from logs such as CloudTrail and VPC flow logs and lets you move directly from a GuardDuty finding to an entity profile and visualize the relationships among IPs, accounts, and resources, which suits the scoping stage. Security Hub aggregates and organizes findings but does not provide a log-based behavior graph or entity activity comparison. Athena requires you to write SQL and prepare tables yourself, which conflicts with the no-SQL condition and with minimizing operational burden. Inspector is a vulnerability scanner, so its purpose differs from investigating the scope of damage from API call patterns.

exam-scs-c03-50.prompt: It has been confirmed that a developer committed the access key of the IAM user deploy-bot to a public GitHub repository. This key may also be used in one nightly deployment pipeline, so the company must be able to check whether a usage site is interrupted and, if necessary, roll back. At the same time, use by an attacker must be blocked right now. Key usage history can be queried through CloudTrail, but the developer who created the key has left for the day and cannot be reached. The commit history of the public repository includes the secret value of the key, and this user has broad write permissions. The pipeline is scheduled to run once within 2 hours after the leak notice. The IAM user has no other access keys and does not use console access, and the security team plans to schedule the key rotation after the investigation. Which first action is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Detach all policies attached to the user, delete the user, and create a new user with the same name to clean up the impact of the key leak.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Change the access key to the inactive state and check the call records for the key ID in CloudTrail.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Delete the access key immediately, issue a new key and deploy it to the pipeline configuration, and check the usage history of the old key in CloudTrail.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reset the IAM user's console password and register a new MFA device so that the attacker can no longer use the user account.

exam-scs-c03-50.explanation: The correct answer is to change the key to the inactive state. Deactivation blocks authentication immediately while allowing the key to be reactivated, so it fits the requirement to check whether the pipeline actually uses this key and then restore it, and searching CloudTrail by key ID also lets you trace the attacker's activity. Deleting the key cannot be undone, so there is no way to roll back if the pipeline stops. The console password and MFA affect only console sign-in and have no effect on access key authentication. Deleting and re-creating the user is excessive, cannot be undone, and loses the linkage information needed for the investigation.

exam-scs-c03-51.prompt: A company has AWS Network Firewall in an inspection VPC (10.100.0.0/16) and centrally inspects the outbound traffic of spoke VPCs (10.1.0.0/16, 10.2.0.0/16) through AWS Transit Gateway. The company put only .example.com in the domain list allow rule group, but HTTPS leaving the spoke VPCs passes even for domains that are not on the list. The firewall policy is already associated with the Transit Gateway attachment path, and the domain list in the stateful rule group is evaluated based on the HTTP host header and the TLS SNI. No variables were set separately for the domain list rule group, so it remains at the default values. The operations team has 2 members and wants to avoid additional configuration such as certificate deployment. Traffic is several TB per day, and increases in latency must be minimized. Firewall endpoints are already deployed in each Availability Zone. What should be done to apply domain filtering with the fewest changes and without TLS decryption?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Modify the HOME_NET variable of the rule group to include the CIDR ranges of the inspection VPC and both spoke VPCs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add a TLS inspection configuration to the firewall policy and decrypt all HTTPS sessions with an ACM certificate to filter based on the body instead of the SNI.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Switch the firewall policy rule evaluation order to strict order, and change the stateless default action so that traffic is not forwarded to the stateful engine.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deploy a separate Network Firewall and domain rule group for each spoke VPC so that each VPC uses its own CIDR as the home network.

exam-scs-c03-51.explanation: Domain list inspection by default filters only traffic within the range of HOME_NET, which is the CIDR of the VPC where the firewall is deployed, so to inspect traffic from other VPCs coming through Transit Gateway, you must manually add those CIDRs to HOME_NET. HTTPS domains are determined by SNI, so TLS decryption is not needed. Changing the evaluation order or the stateless default action does not change the reason that traffic outside HOME_NET does not match the domain rules. Deploying a firewall per VPC abandons the centralized inspection architecture, and the changes and cost are large.

exam-scs-c03-52.prompt: A company issued a *.example.com public certificate with ACM in the Seoul Region and completed DNS validation. However, this certificate does not appear in the custom SSL certificate list of the CloudFront distribution. The domain's DNS is managed in Route 53, and no person should have to track the certificate renewal schedule separately. The domain is also used by an ALB in the Seoul Region, so the Seoul certificate is still needed for the ALB. The CloudFront distribution already exists, and the domain name is registered as an alternate domain name (CNAME). The CNAME record for DNS validation has already been created in Route 53, and certificate issuance takes only a few minutes. The company wants to make changes only in the distribution settings on the CloudFront side. How can the problem be resolved with the fewest changes while keeping the certificate in an automatically renewing state?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Re-create the distribution in the Seoul Region so that the CloudFront distribution can use the Seoul Region certificate, and also move the origin server settings to be Seoul-based.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turn on cross-Region replication of the Seoul certificate in the ACM settings so that a copy of the same certificate is automatically created in the Region that CloudFront uses.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Manually upload the Seoul Region certificate to the IAM certificate store as if it were an external CA certificate, attach it to the CloudFront distribution, and renew it yourself before it expires.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Newly issue an ACM public certificate for the same domain with DNS validation in the US East (N. Virginia) Region, and attach it to the CloudFront distribution.

exam-scs-c03-52.explanation: The correct answer is to newly issue an ACM certificate in US East (N. Virginia) (us-east-1). ACM certificates are Regional resources and CloudFront uses only ACM certificates in us-east-1, so if you issue one in that Region and keep DNS validation, ACM renews it automatically. Uploading to the IAM certificate store is manual management and violates the automatic renewal requirement. CloudFront is a global service, so a distribution cannot be moved to the Seoul Region. ACM has no feature to automatically replicate a certificate between Regions.

exam-scs-c03-53.prompt: The security team received a report that abnormally long domain queries are going out from 200 servers in the Seoul Region and suspects DNS tunneling. The instances run in a VPC that uses the default Amazon DNS, and the security team had turned on VPC flow logs, but no queried domain names were found, and even the traffic going to the Amazon DNS server did not appear in the records. The servers are in production, so restarting them or installing an agent is difficult, and the security team has 3 members and has no capacity to operate a new separate analysis system. All the servers are in private subnets of the same VPC, and the team wants to retain query records for 90 days for use in forensics. The only DNS currently used is the VPC default resolver, and there are no custom DNS servers. What should be done with the fewest changes to obtain the queried domain names?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Customize the VPC flow log record format to add a query domain field, and reduce the maximum aggregation interval to 1 minute to collect again.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a Traffic Mirroring session on every instance network interface and configure a fleet of separate analysis appliances to interpret the DNS packets.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Modify the trail to enable the Route 53 item of CloudTrail data events so that DNS queries sent by instances are recorded as API calls.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure Route 53 Resolver query logging for that VPC, associate the VPC, and deliver the query logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs or Amazon S3.

exam-scs-c03-53.explanation: Traffic to and from the default Amazon DNS server is not recorded in VPC flow logs, and flow logs have no domain name field either, so the queried names are obtained by associating Route 53 Resolver query logging with the VPC. Customizing the format cannot add a domain field that does not exist and does not change what is collected. Traffic Mirroring and analysis appliances impose a very large configuration and operational burden compared with the requirement. DNS queries from instances are not recorded as CloudTrail events.

exam-scs-c03-54.prompt: The 40 accounts in a sandbox OU must be able to use only four services: Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon CloudWatch, and any new services that AWS releases in the future must be automatically blocked until the SCP is explicitly modified. Currently, the default FullAWSAccess SCP is attached to this OU, and other OUs must be left unchanged. When a new account moves into this OU, the same restriction must be applied automatically without extra work. The sandbox OU is for developer experimentation and uses only the Seoul Region. The security team wants SCP changes to be made only through an approval process, and the core goal is to prevent new services from being used unnoticed. Which configuration is MOST appropriate to meet the requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Detach FullAWSAccess from the organization root and attach an SCP that allows only the four services to the root, to restrict the allowed scope for the entire organization.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Detach FullAWSAccess from the sandbox OU and attach an SCP that allows only the four services. Leave the root as it is.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Keep FullAWSAccess and additionally attach to the sandbox OU an SCP that allows the four services, to restrict the allowed scope to the four services.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keep FullAWSAccess and attach to the sandbox OU an SCP that denies all currently known services except the four, to restrict them.

exam-scs-c03-54.explanation: The correct answer is to replace FullAWSAccess on the sandbox OU. For a permission to be allowed, there must be an explicit Allow at every level from the root to the account, so keeping a full allow at the root and having only an SCP that allows the four services on the sandbox OU turns that OU into an allow list alone, and new services are denied by default. If FullAWSAccess remains at the same level, the allows are merged and effectively everything is allowed. A method that denies known services automatically allows services released later. Replacing it at the root would restrict other OUs as well, which violates the requirement.

exam-scs-c03-55.prompt: Five teams, including the analytics, marketing, and finance teams, share a single data lake bucket. Each team has different prefixes it can access, and the analytics team's access must be allowed only from within a specific VPC. The bucket policy has grown to hundreds of lines, and incidents in which changing one place affects other teams keep recurring. The data is separated by prefix, and multiple pipelines depend on this bucket, so splitting or migrating the bucket itself is difficult given the schedule. Per-team access history is reported separately in audits, and the work of migrating each team's application to use a new access path can be scheduled team by team. Which method separates per-team permission management with the LEAST risk without splitting the bucket?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Keep adding only per-team IAM policies, and put an allow for all prefixes in a single statement in the bucket policy so that no policy edits are needed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a separate bucket for each team and use S3 replication to copy the data lake prefixes to each team's bucket, to completely separate access permissions by team.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an S3 access point and a per-prefix policy for each team, and make the analytics team's access point accept only requests from the designated VPC.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Put all the aws:SourceVpce conditions and per-prefix conditions in a single bucket policy, to manage allow rules by team and network path in one policy.

exam-scs-c03-55.explanation: The correct answer is a per-team S3 access point. Each access point applies its own policy and network controls and can be configured to accept only requests coming from a VPC, and access point policies are evaluated together with the bucket policy, so team rules are separated and a change in one place does not spread to other teams. Only adding IAM policies and allowing all prefixes in the bucket policy loses per-prefix separation and the VPC restriction. Creating a bucket for each team and replicating violates the constraint of not splitting the bucket. Putting all conditions in a single policy leaves the current problem as it is.

exam-scs-c03-56.prompt: A company that operates dozens of payment-related microservices runs an Amazon EKS cluster built with EC2 node groups (not Fargate). The security team wants to use Amazon GuardDuty to detect both runtime behavior, such as malicious processes and file access running inside containers, and anonymous access and privilege escalation attempts against the Kubernetes API server. GuardDuty is already enabled in the account, and the team does not want to manage EKS control plane logging itself. The nodes are based on Amazon Linux, and the team wants to avoid introducing a new separate security product. The cluster is a single cluster in the Seoul Region, and the namespace to be monitored is a single production environment. The security team wants to merge the results directly into the existing GuardDuty findings flow. Which TWO actions are MOST appropriate to meet these two requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Turn on Amazon Inspector ECR scanning to detect malicious processes in running containers in real time and deliver the results to the security team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable GuardDuty EKS Runtime Monitoring and deploy the GuardDuty security agent to the cluster to collect OS-level events from containers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure the cluster VPC to publish flow logs to Amazon S3 so that GuardDuty can analyze the network activity of containers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable GuardDuty EKS Audit Log Monitoring to analyze suspicious activity targeting the API server from the Kubernetes audit logs.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Enable GuardDuty Lambda Protection to analyze process execution and file access events of containers in the cluster nodes.

exam-scs-c03-56.explanation: Audit Log Monitoring analyzes activity targeting the API server, such as anonymous access and privilege escalation, from Kubernetes audit logs, and Runtime Monitoring detects malicious behavior by having a security agent collect process, file, and network events from containers. Each of the two features handles one requirement. Lambda Protection targets the network activity of Lambda functions, so it is unrelated to EKS nodes. Inspector ECR scanning is image vulnerability scanning and not detection of running processes. GuardDuty analyzes flow logs through its own independent stream, so the user does not need to publish flow logs.

exam-scs-c03-57.prompt: A company connects a central inspection VPC, with firewall endpoints in two Availability Zones, to a transit gateway to inspect traffic between spoke VPCs. The firewall endpoints are healthy in both zones and there are no errors in the route tables. However, TCP communication between spoke VPCs in different Availability Zones is intermittently dropped, and logs show that the stateful firewall's session state does not match. Communication within the same Availability Zone is normal. The service is in production, and for availability reasons the workloads cannot be consolidated into one zone, and the change must be completed on the inspection VPC side. The failure appears only for some flows at the moment a new connection is created, and monitoring has not shown a shortage of throughput. What should be done to resolve this problem with the fewest changes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enable appliance mode on the inspection VPC's transit gateway VPC attachment so that the round trip of a flow passes through the appliance in the same Availability Zone.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add two firewall endpoints in each Availability Zone and adjust the transit gateway route table to an evenly distributed path to increase throughput.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the firewall policy's stateless default action to drop so that all packets whose state does not match are discarded and the client retransmits them.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Merge the spoke VPC subnets by Availability Zone and move all workloads to one Availability Zone to eliminate cross-Availability Zone traffic altogether.

exam-scs-c03-57.explanation: When appliance mode is turned on, the transit gateway selects one network interface in the inspection VPC by hashing for each flow and uses the same interface for the round-trip traffic until the flow ends. Symmetric routing to the same Availability Zone is therefore guaranteed, and stateful inspection keeps session state consistently. Adding endpoints does not resolve the asymmetry in which the round trip splits across different Availability Zones. Changing the stateless default action to drop can discard normal traffic as well. Consolidating workloads into one Availability Zone undermines the availability requirement.

exam-scs-c03-58.prompt: A company collects GuardDuty findings from 60 accounts in AWS Organizations into a delegated administrator account. When a finding of the InstanceCredentialExfiltration type occurs, indicating that EC2 instance role credentials were used from an external IP, the sessions of that role must be automatically invalidated within 5 minutes. The company wants to avoid the operational burden of building separate detection infrastructure for each account. From detection to remediation, the process must complete automatically with no human judgment, and a dedicated response IAM role is already deployed in the target accounts. The audit team must be able to look up the response records later. The role subject to session revocation is used as an instance profile, and deleting or re-creating the role is not allowed. In case of a false positive, the affected workload must recover immediately with a new session. Which automated response configuration has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Evaluate IAM role configurations with an AWS Config organization rule, and attach a remediation action so that Systems Manager Automation revokes sessions when a noncompliant role is found.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create CloudTrail metric filters and Amazon CloudWatch alarms in every account, notify the responsible person through Amazon SNS, and have the responsible person revoke the role sessions directly in the console.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have an Amazon EventBridge rule in the delegated administrator account match the finding and invoke AWS Lambda, and have Lambda attach the session revocation policy through the response role in the target account.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Export GuardDuty findings to Amazon S3 in each account, run an Amazon Athena query every hour, and have AWS Lambda revoke sessions when that type is found.

exam-scs-c03-58.explanation: The correct answer is the combination of an EventBridge rule and Lambda in the delegated administrator account. GuardDuty sends findings to EventBridge in near real time, and a rule in the delegated administrator account also reacts to findings from member accounts, so a single rule automatically handles 60 accounts and meets the 5-minute requirement. Per-account metric filters and alarms must be configured in each account and involve humans, which fits neither the speed nor the operational burden requirements. A Config rule only evaluates configuration state and does not take GuardDuty findings or anomalous credential usage as input. Exporting to S3 and hourly Athena queries cannot meet the 5-minute target.

exam-scs-c03-59.prompt: A media company's KMS request costs have surged because of billions of GET requests per month on an S3 bucket encrypted with SSE-KMS using a customer managed key. The client code cannot be changed, and the use of the customer managed key and the CloudTrail audit requirement must be maintained. Even after S3 Bucket Keys were turned on for the bucket, KMS calls did not decrease when existing objects were read. The data consists of about 800 million objects, and most objects are read several times a day. Objects are mostly small and are not modified, and bulk copy jobs can be run during the weekend maintenance window. There are 800 million objects, mostly small files, and read service must continue while the existing objects are copied. Cost analysis shows that the number of KMS requests is the main cause of the charges. Which additional action reduces the cost MOST efficiently?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use an S3 Batch Operations copy objects job to copy the existing objects in place so that they are re-encrypted with the Bucket Key applied.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Switch the bucket default encryption to dual-layer server-side encryption (DSSE-KMS) so that the number of KMS requests is reduced together with Bucket Keys.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Switch the bucket default encryption to SSE-S3 so that no KMS requests occur, and substitute S3 server access logs for object access auditing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Turn on automatic rotation of the KMS customer managed key so that the key material changes periodically and the KMS request cost on object reads decreases.

exam-scs-c03-59.explanation: The correct answer is to copy the existing objects so that Bucket Keys are applied. A Bucket Key applies only to objects written after it is configured, and existing objects do not use a Bucket Key. Rewriting them with CopyObject applies it, so the objects can be copied in bulk with a Batch Operations job. Switching to SSE-S3 violates the customer managed key and KMS-based audit requirements. DSSE-KMS does not support Bucket Keys. Automatic key rotation only changes the key material and has nothing to do with the number or cost of KMS requests generated by reading objects.

exam-scs-c03-60.prompt: An SCP allow list approach has been applied to all member accounts in the development OU. In this OU, the default FullAWSAccess SCP was detached, and the SCP attached to the OU allows only ec2:* and s3:*. FullAWSAccess remains at the organization root. In one member account in this OU, a developer's IAM user has the AdministratorAccess managed policy attached directly, and the developer has asked since yesterday why they cannot create RDS instances. The security team wants to explain the cause with the policy evaluation logic. The user has no permissions boundary and no session policy is used. The SCP at the organization root is not being changed, and the account in question was recently moved to that OU. Which is the MOST accurate description of this user's effective permissions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The user can perform EC2 and S3 actions, but creating RDS instances, which the SCP does not allow, is denied even with the administrator policy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because the administrator policy allows all actions, all service actions, including creating RDS instances, are possible even though the SCP is an allow list.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because an SCP is a policy that grants permissions, the user can perform EC2 and S3 actions even without the administrator policy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All actions are denied, and only the root user of the user's account is unaffected by the SCP and can perform EC2 and S3 actions.

exam-scs-c03-60.explanation: An SCP does not grant permissions but sets the boundary of the maximum permissions that principals in a member account can have, and the effective permissions are the intersection of the SCP allow and the allow in the user's identity-based policy. Therefore, a user with the administrator policy can perform only the EC2 and S3 actions that the SCP allows, and creating RDS is denied. The administrator policy cannot exceed the SCP. The explanation that an SCP grants permissions directly is wrong, and without a policy there is no allow. The root user of a member account is also affected by SCPs.

exam-scs-c03-61.prompt: A security team that operates 60 accounts in an organization currently reviews permissions by team every quarter, but cleanup based on usage history is not taking place, so unused roles have accumulated. The team wants to find and clean up IAM roles that have not been used in the last 90 days, as well as service and action permissions that were granted but not used. The team does not want to run scripts in each account and needs to see organization-wide results in one place, and the results must be continuously updated. The delegated administrator account is already designated, and the security team has 4 members. The cleanup targets are thousands of roles, and the results must show the last used service and action information so that the responsible team can check before deletion. Which method is MOST appropriate to meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an IAM Access Analyzer for external access with the organization as the zone of trust, and judge unused roles from the results about resources shared with external principals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the delegated administrator account, create an IAM Access Analyzer for unused access at the organization level, set the tracking period to 90 days, and review the unused findings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Download the IAM credential report from each account every week, merge the last-used date columns, and organize into a table the items that have not been used for more than 90 days.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deploy the AWS Config managed rule iam-user-unused-credentials-check as an organization rule to check items with unused credentials.

exam-scs-c03-61.explanation: An Access Analyzer for unused access can be created at the organization level, continuously updates findings for unused roles, unused credentials, and unused service and action permissions, and lets you specify the unused-access tracking period. An external access analyzer finds access opened to external principals, so it cannot find unused permissions. Credential reports are collected manually per account and cover only user credentials. The Config rule checks only IAM user credentials and does not cover whether roles and permissions are used.

exam-scs-c03-62.prompt: A company is migrating a MySQL database that it installed and operated directly on EC2 to Amazon RDS for MySQL. The company has only two DBAs, so reducing operational burden is the main reason for the migration, and all settings are subject to audit. The company intends to write a new security checklist after the migration. In the next security audit, the company must provide evidence that distinguishes which controls AWS is responsible for and which controls the company is responsible for. The database contains customer personal information, so both data at rest and data in transit must be protected, and the company wants to write the checklist separating the areas AWS handles from the areas the company handles. Under the shared responsibility model, which TWO responsibilities MOST appropriately remain with the customer after the migration to RDS? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Applying security patches to the host operating system on which the DB instance runs

choices.label: B
choices.text: Designing database user accounts and permissions, and deciding whether to use encryption of data at rest and which KMS key to use

choices.label: C
choices.text: Designing the security groups and subnets that allow access to the DB instance, and setting whether public access is enabled

choices.label: D
choices.text: Managing the security of the hypervisor and physical servers of the hosts on which the DB instance runs

choices.label: E
choices.text: Power and cooling equipment in the data center, and physical destruction of decommissioned storage devices

exam-scs-c03-62.explanation: The correct answers are the network access configuration and the database account permissions and encryption decisions. Even with a managed service, who can connect through security groups and subnets, the database users and permissions, and whether to use encryption at rest and which key to select are the customer's security responsibilities. The security of the hypervisor and physical servers is security of the cloud itself, which AWS manages. Patching the host operating system is also handled by AWS in RDS, which is different from running it directly on EC2. Data center equipment and the destruction of storage devices are also AWS's physical security responsibilities.

exam-scs-c03-63.prompt: The HTTPS listener of an ALB for a public web service that general users access with browsers uses 20 ACM public certificates, all issued with email validation. The domains are managed in a single hosted zone in Route 53. A certificate expired because the responsible person missed the renewal confirmation email for one certificate, which caused a service outage. The company wants certificates trusted by public browsers to be maintained and renewed automatically in the future with no human action, with minimal changes. The 20 certificates are for different subdomains and are all attached to ALBs in the same Region. The domain registrar is already in Route 53, so the company has permission to add DNS records directly. Which method is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Request the certificates again with DNS validation and keep the validation CNAME records in Route 53 so that ACM automatically renews the certificates in use.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Register commercial CA certificates by importing them instead of using ACM, create a scheduled job in each account to re-import the renewed certificate 30 days before expiration, and operate a procedure to manually replace the ALB listener certificate when the renewed certificate is ready.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Issue private certificates from ACM Private CA and attach them to the ALB, and distribute the private root certificate to client devices so that they trust it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Receive certificate-expiring-soon events through EventBridge and send notifications to the responsible person so that the person does not miss approving the renewal confirmation email.

exam-scs-c03-63.explanation: An ACM public certificate issued with DNS validation is renewed automatically by ACM as long as the validation CNAME record is maintained, so no human action is needed and browser trust is maintained. Importing commercial CA certificates requires you to automate renewal yourself, which increases the operational burden. Private CA certificates are not trusted by public browsers, which violates the requirements. Expiration notifications leave the manual action of email approval in place, so the same mistake can be repeated.

exam-scs-c03-64.prompt: A company runs workloads in three Regions, ap-northeast-2, us-east-1, and eu-west-1, and AWS Security Hub CSPM is already enabled in all three Regions. Twelve security analysts work in shifts and want to handle everything in one place without switching consoles. The analysts want to view the findings of all Regions from the console in the single Seoul Region and want the workflow status they change there to be reflected in each original Region as well. The security team has no capacity to operate code directly, and the existing settings in each Region must be kept. All three Regions are in the same AWS account, and Regions may be added in the future. The analysts also want to see insights and control statuses together in the home Region console, and only the security team has permission to modify findings. Which method is MOST appropriate to meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Build a pipeline directly that uses Amazon EventBridge rules and AWS Lambda functions to bring each Region's Security Hub CSPM findings back into the Seoul Region.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use Security Hub CSPM only in the Seoul Region, and disable the service in the other two Regions to gather the findings in one place.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Export each Region's findings to an Amazon S3 bucket, build a dashboard that combines them with Amazon Athena queries, and have analysts manage status there.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Designate the Seoul Region as the home Region, turn on cross-Region aggregation, and select us-east-1 and eu-west-1 as linked Regions.

exam-scs-c03-64.explanation: With cross-Region aggregation, once you set the home Region and choose linked Regions, findings, insights, and control statuses are replicated to the home Region, and updates made in the home Region are also replicated back to the linked Regions. An EventBridge and Lambda pipeline requires operating code you build yourself and requires separate implementation of reverse reflection of status, which violates the requirements. Enabling only the home Region means findings for resources in the other Regions are not generated at all, so visibility is lost. The combination of S3 and Athena is read-only analysis and cannot reflect workflow status in the original findings.

exam-scs-c03-65.prompt: In an organization that uses 180 accounts and 4 Regions, the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices (FSBP) standard in AWS Security Hub must be enabled in all accounts and Regions, and member account administrators must not be able to turn it off arbitrarily. New accounts must also automatically receive the same settings. The standard enablement status is checked in regular audits, and a situation in which settings differ between accounts is considered a security incident. Some existing accounts have already turned on Security Hub with local settings. The security team wants to make configuration changes only from a single delegated administrator account. Once central configuration is applied, account administrators must be prevented from turning off the standard directly in the console, and the audit team wants to see on a single screen which policy is applied to which account. Which method prevents configuration drift with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the delegated administrator account, turn on central configuration, and attach a configuration policy with FSBP enabled to the organization root to designate the accounts as centrally managed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy a stack that enables the FSBP standard to all accounts and Regions, and add stack instances for new accounts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have each member account administrator turn on the standard directly, check whether the standard is disabled with an AWS Config rule, and send a notification to accounts that violate it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keep local configuration, and specify in the delegated administrator account's settings that Security Hub and the default standards be turned on automatically for new organization accounts.

exam-scs-c03-65.explanation: The correct answer is a central configuration configuration policy. The delegated administrator applies Security Hub, the FSBP standard, and the controls in one step to the home Region and linked Regions with a configuration policy. For centrally managed accounts, only the delegated administrator can change the settings, so drift is prevented, and attaching it to the root makes new accounts inherit it. Auto-enable under local configuration applies only to new accounts and the current Region, so drift arises in existing accounts or other Regions. StackSets cannot prevent member administrators from turning off the standard in the console. Manual enablement with after-the-fact checks requires human involvement and is not preventive.

exam-soa-c02-1.prompt: The operations team (4 people) of an online payment processing company collects application logs from its payment API servers in a single Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group, and three weeks of logs have accumulated so far. After an incident yesterday in which errors spiked, management asked for the number of ERROR entries over the past 7 days right now, and going forward the team must be notified through an existing Amazon SNS topic when there are more than 20 ERROR entries within 5 minutes. The historical count is a one-time request, and the company does not want to build a separate pipeline to move the logs to another system. The operations team has no dedicated developers. The log group's retention period is already 30 days, so all three weeks of logs are still available, and the report to management is needed this afternoon. Which combination of steps meets both requirements with the LEAST development effort? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase the log group's retention period so that a metric filter re-evaluates the historical logs, and generate the metric for the past 7 days.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because a metric filter is applied retroactively to existing logs, query the same filter metric to check the number of ERROR entries over the past 7 days.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a new metric filter for the ERROR pattern, and create an alarm that goes to the ALARM state when the 5-minute sum of that metric exceeds 20, with an SNS notification attached.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use a CloudWatch Logs Insights query to filter the ERROR events from the past 7 days and count them.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Create a subscription filter to resend the existing logs to Amazon Data Firehose, and count the entries from the past 7 days by using Amazon S3 and Amazon Athena.

exam-soa-c02-1.explanation: The correct answer is the combination that handles the historical count with a Logs Insights query and handles future notifications with a metric filter and an alarm. Logs Insights queries logs that are already stored on demand, so it fits the past-7-days count. According to the documentation, a metric filter publishes metrics only for events that occur after the filter is created, so it takes care of the forward-looking threshold alarm. The claim that a filter is applied retroactively to existing logs is not true. Increasing the retention period does not cause a filter to re-evaluate past logs. A subscription filter delivers log events in real time as they are ingested, so it is not a means of retroactively sending logs that have already accumulated, and setting up Athena as well increases the development effort.

exam-soa-c02-2.prompt: An internal order-processing web server (one EC2 instance with the SSM Agent and the CloudWatch agent installed) at a logistics company went down twice in the early morning last month because temporary files piled up and filled the disk. The company now wants an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to run without human intervention to clean up old temporary files when the disk usage alarm goes to the ALARM state. The alarm has already been created from CloudWatch agent metrics, and a standard runbook that runs without a reboot is ready for the cleanup. No one is on call overnight, and the burden of writing new code must be kept to a minimum. The cleanup path is already set as a runbook parameter, and this server's IAM instance profile has Systems Manager permissions attached. Which configuration is MOST suitable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Specify running the SSM Automation runbook directly as an EC2 action in the existing alarm's alarm actions, connecting it in one step without a separate rule.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Wrap the alarm in a composite alarm, and specify running the cleanup runbook as the composite alarm's Systems Manager action.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Receive the alarm notification by SNS email, have an engineer review it and run the SSM Automation runbook manually from the console, and record the execution result in a ticket. Document the details in a wiki for post-incident review.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Receive the alarm state change event with an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches when the state is ALARM, and specify the SSM Automation runbook as the target.

exam-soa-c02-2.explanation: The correct answer is the configuration that receives the alarm state change event with an EventBridge rule and specifies SSM Automation as the target. CloudWatch sends an event to EventBridge every time an alarm changes state, and a rule that matches only the ALARM state can run the runbook without any code. The direct actions of a standard metric alarm are SNS notifications, EC2 actions, and Auto Scaling actions, and none of them lets you specify running a runbook directly. The Systems Manager action of a composite alarm is for creating OpsItems or incidents and does not run runbooks. Receiving an email and then running the runbook manually violates the requirement for no human intervention.

exam-soa-c02-3.prompt: The security team at a fintech startup was cited in an external audit last quarter for leaving one Amazon S3 bucket accidentally open to public read access for three weeks. The team now wants any bucket policy change that would allow public read access to be blocked automatically, without human intervention. The scope is several hundred buckets in a single account, and auditors must be able to query the configuration change history and compliance status later. Checks and remediation must run continuously, including outside business hours, and the security team does not have enough staff to maintain code themselves. No bucket needs an exception to be public, and the on-duty security engineer works under the condition of not being called at night. Which method meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Receive AWS CloudTrail events with Amazon EventBridge, and implement a custom-written AWS Lambda function that parses the bucket policy, determines whether it is public, and blocks it. Record the compliance history in a separate Amazon DynamoDB table that you build yourself for querying.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable the AWS Config managed rule (s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited) and attach automatic remediation that uses an SSM Automation document.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty to send an alert email when a public bucket is found, and have an engineer block public access on that bucket from the console.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Check the AWS Trusted Advisor results every day, and have an engineer manually find the buckets flagged as public and block public access.

exam-soa-c02-3.explanation: AWS Config evaluates bucket configurations with a managed rule and retains the compliance status and change history, and attaching an SSM Automation document as a remediation action lets it fix noncompliant resources automatically. A custom Lambda function requires you to implement and maintain the policy-parsing logic and exception handling, and you would also have to build the compliance history yourself. Having an engineer block the bucket after a GuardDuty alert, and checking Trusted Advisor every day, both require human intervention, so they fail the requirement to block automatically and the requirement to query compliance history.

exam-soa-c02-4.prompt: At 10:12 AM, a developer accidentally dropped the orders table in a production Amazon RDS for MySQL database (Multi-AZ deployment) at an online shopping company. Automated backups are turned on with a 7-day retention period, and the data as of 10:10 AM, just before the deletion, must be recovered. The shopping site is otherwise operating normally, and new data keeps accumulating in the payments and inventory tables even after the deletion, so that data must not be lost. The recovery must be performed with minimal service interruption. Only one table needs to be recovered, its size is a few GB, and the developer reported the deletion immediately. What is the MOST appropriate recovery method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run a point-in-time restore on the production instance to roll the same instance back in place to its 10:10 AM state.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run a point-in-time restore to 10:10 AM to create a new DB instance, export the orders table from the restored copy, and load it back into the production database.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Run a failover to the Multi-AZ standby and promote the standby, which still holds the data from before the deletion, to be the new primary instance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Restore the latest daily snapshot to create a new instance, switch the service to that instance's endpoint, and then change all application connection strings. Have an engineer review the changes before the switchover.

exam-soa-c02-4.explanation: The correct answer is to create a new instance with a point-in-time restore and reload only the needed table. According to the documentation, a point-in-time restore does not modify the source and always creates a new DB instance, and because transaction logs are uploaded every 5 minutes, you can restore to a point in time such as 10:10 AM. Rolling the same instance back in place is not offered and would also lose the latest data in the other tables. The standby is replicated synchronously, so the drop command has already been applied to it. A daily snapshot would lose all table changes made after the snapshot, which violates the requirements.

exam-soa-c02-5.prompt: A logistics software company wants to enable communication among 12 VPCs used by different accounts and teams in the same Region, and 2 to 3 VPCs will be added each quarter. The CIDR blocks of all the VPCs do not overlap. There are only two network administrators, so the company wants to reduce the number of connections and the routing configuration to manage, and the effort required to attach a new VPC must also be small. Most inter-VPC communication consists of small API calls, and there is no requirement for internet-bound traffic or on-premises connectivity. Each VPC is owned by a different team, so every routing change request requires an approval process, and the total traffic volume is modest at a few hundred GB per month. Which configuration has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a VPC peering connection for every pair of VPCs to configure 66 peering connections, and add a route to the peer CIDR in each VPC's route table.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Peer one hub VPC with each of the other VPCs, and configure an EC2 proxy in the hub to forward traffic, working around the transitive routing limitation of peering.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a transit gateway and attach each VPC to it, and centrally manage the routes between VPCs by using the transit gateway route table.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Attach a virtual private gateway to each VPC and connect the VPCs to one another with site-to-site VPN tunnels to create encrypted paths between VPCs, managing BGP routing for each tunnel yourself.

exam-soa-c02-5.explanation: The correct answer is a transit gateway hub configuration. A transit gateway is a hub that connects VPCs and on-premises networks, each VPC needs to create only one attachment, and routes are managed centrally in the route tables, so the workload grows only linearly as VPCs are added. Peering all 12 VPCs would require 12×11÷2 = 66 connections plus route table changes on both sides, and this would grow sharply as VPCs are added. VPC peering does not support transitive routing, so a configuration that goes through a hub VPC requires you to operate EC2 proxies yourself, which become a bottleneck and a point of failure. VPN between VPCs is the most complex because you must manage both the tunnels and the devices.

exam-soa-c02-6.prompt: The platform team at a SaaS company deploys the network layer by using a nested stack template that is shared by multiple product teams. During a routine check, the team ran drift detection on the parent stack and the result was IN_SYNC. However, it was later discovered that someone had directly changed the inbound rules of a security group created by a child stack from the console. There are too many stacks for people to inspect the console one by one, and the team must find such changes without exception going forward. The security group change in question has already occurred once, and the audit team has requested a per-stack report if the same type of change occurs in the future. What is the MOST appropriate method for this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because drift detection on the parent stack does not cover the nested stacks, run drift detection directly on each nested stack as well.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If you run drift detection on the parent stack repeatedly, the results of the child stacks are merged into the parent result over time, so run detection frequently.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because drift detection supports only EC2 instance resources, security group changes can be monitored only with AWS Config rules.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If you use a stack policy to deny updates to security group resources, console changes are also blocked, so drift cannot occur.

exam-soa-c02-6.explanation: When you detect drift on a parent stack, CloudFormation does not detect drift on the nested stacks that belong to it, and you must initiate the detection operation directly on each nested stack. Therefore, running detection on each child stack is the correct answer. Running it repeatedly does not merge the child results into the parent result. Drift detection works across supported resource types, including security groups, not just EC2, so the claim that the support is limited to EC2 is not true. A stack policy controls only stack update operations and cannot prevent directly changing resources through the console or the API.

exam-soa-c02-7.prompt: The site of an e-commerce company has a core revenue path that runs from logging in to adding an item to the cart. Last month, because of a misconfiguration on the login server, users could not add items to their carts for 3 hours in the early morning, but the health checks on the target servers were all normal, so no one noticed. The company must verify every minute, even in the early morning when there is almost no traffic, that this flow works from a real user's perspective, and an alarm must fire if it fails. The check results must be kept as CloudWatch metrics, and the company must not operate servers for the checks itself. It would be good for the canary results to leave evidence such as screenshots, but this is not required, and the incident response owner receives notifications by SNS email, not SMS. Which method has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use an Amazon Route 53 health check to check the HTTP response code of the login page URL, and send an alarm when the health check fails.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an alarm on the HealthyHostCount metric of the ALB target group, and treat a decrease in the number of healthy targets as an outage.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a CloudWatch Synthetics canary as a multistep script with a 1-minute schedule, and set an alarm on the canary's success rate metric.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Place a cron-based curl script on a separate EC2 instance, upload the results as a CloudWatch custom metric, and set an alarm on it.

exam-soa-c02-7.explanation: The correct answer is a CloudWatch Synthetics canary. A canary is a script that runs on a schedule and follows the same paths and actions as a customer, it can run as often as every minute, it works even when there is no traffic, and you can set an alarm on its success rate metric. A Route 53 health check looks at the result of a single URL request, so it cannot verify a multistep flow from login to the cart. The number of healthy targets on an ALB only shows whether servers respond and does not tell you whether the user flow succeeds. The EC2 with cron approach violates the requirement because you would have to operate a server for the checks yourself.

exam-soa-c02-8.prompt: A media company processes image conversion jobs that accumulate in an Amazon SQS queue by using 40 worker instances in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. The jobs are idempotent, a job that is interrupted during processing is processed again from the queue, and it is acceptable for results to be several hours late. The workers do not store state locally, and the units of work are split into short pieces. Compute costs exceeded the budget last quarter and the finance team demanded savings, and the team wants to solve this with purchasing options and configuration alone, without changing the workload code. A single job finishes in 2 minutes on average, and the workers currently all use one single instance type and run On-Demand. Which method reduces cost the MOST while securing capacity reliably?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Purchase 3-year All Upfront Standard Reserved Instances for 40 instances' worth of capacity and run all workers as Reserved Instances.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lease a Dedicated Host, consolidate the 40 workers onto it, and reduce instance costs with host-level pricing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Consolidate the workers into 10 larger On-Demand instances to reduce the number of instances and the number of servers to manage.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use a Spot Instance configuration with multiple instance types and Availability Zones specified in the Auto Scaling group, and let interrupted jobs be processed again after the SQS visibility timeout.

exam-soa-c02-8.explanation: Spot Instances let you use spare EC2 capacity at a large discount, but the capacity can be reclaimed when it is needed again. This workload is idempotent, stateless, and delay-tolerant, and it is reprocessed through SQS, so it can tolerate interruptions. Mixing multiple instance types and Availability Zones makes the workload less sensitive to a capacity shortage in any single pool, which makes it easier to secure capacity. A 3-year All Upfront Reserved Instance commits to a long term for a batch workload that varies greatly and tolerates delay, and its discount is smaller than Spot. Dedicated Hosts are used when licensing or regulatory requirements demand them and are not a way to reduce cost. Consolidating into larger On-Demand instances gives no unit-price discount, so the cost savings are limited.

exam-soa-c02-9.prompt: The on-call team at an online gaming company wants to receive an SNS paging notification only when the web server CPU utilization alarm and the ALB 5xx error count alarm are both in the ALARM state at the same time. Both alarms have already been created, but a page goes out when only one of them fires, and over the past month there have been more than 20 unnecessary early-morning pages, which has greatly increased team fatigue. Pages for cases where only one alarm fires must be reduced. The team must not write new code or operate separate servers, and it must keep using the existing SNS topic for notifications. The evaluation periods of the two alarms are the same at 5 minutes each, and the PagerDuty integration for paging is already subscribed to the SNS topic. What is the MOST appropriate method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a composite alarm that references the two alarms, set the rule expression to an AND of the ALARM conditions of the two alarms, and attach the SNS action only to the composite alarm.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attach the same SNS topic to each of the two alarms, and have the engineer who receives the notification check whether the other alarm has also fired and then manually page the on-call engineer only when necessary.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an EventBridge rule for each of the two alarms that matches events whose state is ALARM among the alarm state change events, and specify the same SNS topic as the target.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lower the threshold of the CPU alarm and lengthen the evaluation period of the 5xx alarm so that the times at which the two alarms change state overlap and the SNS notifications go out together.

exam-soa-c02-9.explanation: The correct answer is a composite alarm. A composite alarm does not evaluate metrics directly but evaluates a rule expression that references the states of other alarms, and the expression can use the AND, OR, and NOT operators and state functions such as ALARM, so the composite alarm goes to ALARM only when both alarms are in ALARM, and the SNS action can run at that time. Attaching SNS to each alarm sends a notification even when only one fires and leaves a manual checking step for a person. An EventBridge rule matches one event at a time, so the target runs as soon as either alarm goes to ALARM, and the rule cannot express a simultaneous condition. Adjusting thresholds and evaluation periods only changes alarm sensitivity and does not logically combine the notification conditions.

exam-soa-c02-10.prompt: An Amazon S3 bucket at a healthcare data company contains about 40 million objects that were stored without encryption. A new regulation requires that all objects be encrypted with SSE-KMS and that key usage be auditable through AWS CloudTrail, and the audit is next month. New objects continue to be uploaded to this bucket, and the upload application is difficult to modify. Because of the large number of objects, processing them manually one by one is not realistic, and the operations team has 3 people. Versioning is turned off on the bucket, and the external partners who upload do not include an encryption option in the request headers. Which method meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set the bucket default encryption to SSE-KMS, since existing objects are automatically re-encrypted, and wait without any additional work after changing the setting. Periodically check that newly uploaded objects are handled the same way.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set the bucket default encryption to SSE-KMS to handle new objects, and use an S3 Batch Operations copy job to create encrypted copies of the existing objects.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use a lifecycle rule to transition the existing objects to the S3 Standard-IA storage class, because they are encrypted with KMS during the transition.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a bucket policy that denies unencrypted upload requests, so that existing objects are automatically encrypted the next time they are accessed.

exam-soa-c02-10.explanation: The default encryption setting applies only to new objects uploaded afterward, and objects that are already stored are not encrypted, so existing objects must be processed by creating encrypted copies with S3 Batch Operations. Simply changing the default encryption to SSE-KMS does not re-encrypt the 40 million existing objects. A storage class transition does not change an object's encryption method. A bucket policy only inspects upload requests and does not apply encryption when stored objects are read. When you create copies with a batch job, they are encrypted with the key that you specify.

exam-soa-c02-11.prompt: The infrastructure team at a company received a report that connections on port 443 to an EC2 web server in a newly created subnet are failing. This subnet has a custom network ACL applied to meet security requirements. The security group allows inbound 443 and allows all outbound traffic. The network ACL has only an inbound allow rule for 443 and an outbound allow rule for 443. The VPC flow logs record the 443 traffic from the client to the server as ACCEPT and the response from the server to the client's ephemeral port as REJECT. The team has checked the server's OS firewall and the application settings and found no problems, and other servers in the same subnet show the same symptom. What is the MOST appropriate action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a rule to the security group outbound rules that explicitly allows TCP traffic to the ephemeral port range.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add a rule to the network ACL outbound rules that allows TCP traffic to the ephemeral port range (1024-65535).

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the number of the network ACL inbound 443 rule to a lower number to raise its rule evaluation priority.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add an explicit route for the client CIDR range to the subnet route table so that the response traffic can return.

exam-soa-c02-11.explanation: The correct answer is to allow the ephemeral port range in the network ACL outbound rules. Network ACLs are stateless, so the response to an allowed inbound request must be allowed separately by an outbound rule, and the combination of request ACCEPT and response REJECT in the flow logs points to exactly this situation. Security groups are stateful, so responses are allowed automatically, and because all outbound traffic is already open, adding a rule would have no effect. The request is already ACCEPT, so the inbound rule number is not the problem. For responses within the same VPC the local route already exists, so adding a route is not the solution.

exam-soa-c02-12.prompt: A manufacturing company wants to automatically install security patches every Sunday on EC2 instances spread across 25 accounts and 4 Regions in AWS Organizations, and on several hundred on-premises servers registered through Systems Manager hybrid activation, and to view compliance status in one place. The company wants to avoid repeating the same configuration in every account and Region. The patch schedule is managed by the central security team, not by the owners of each account, and it would be good if the same policy applied when a new account is added to the organization. Patching starts at 2:00 AM on Sunday and requires one reboot per server, and the on-premises servers are already registered as Systems Manager managed nodes. Which method meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In Systems Manager Quick Setup, configure a patch policy targeting the organization, and specify the installation schedule and the patch baseline.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create maintenance windows in each account and Region, and run the AWS-RunPatchBaseline document as a Run Command task on the schedule.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure the Quick Setup Host Management option for the entire organization, and set the weekly patch installation schedule with this configuration.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Have the owner of each account and Region manually run a Patch now operation with Scan and install every Sunday.

exam-soa-c02-12.explanation: A Quick Setup patch policy integrates with Organizations, so a single policy can define the schedule and patch baseline and target multiple accounts and Regions across the organization, or even only some OUs, and it can run scanning and installation on different schedules. A task in Maintenance Windows targets only a single account and Region combination, so the configuration has to be repeated for each account and Region. The Host Management option is limited to scanning for missing patches and creating reports and cannot install patches. Patch now also targets only one account and Region at a time and is run manually without a schedule, so it does not meet the requirements.

exam-soa-c02-13.prompt: A company runs its web service in the Seoul Region with an Application Load Balancer and an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. Currently the subnets are in only one Availability Zone, so during a recent AZ failure the service was down for about 2 hours. Going forward, the service must stay available even if one AZ fails completely, and the capacity of the failed AZ must be restored automatically in the remaining AZs. The company wants to solve this mainly by changing settings of the existing configuration without redesigning the architecture, and no one is on call overnight. The service does not store state on local disks, sessions are stored in Amazon ElastiCache, and the database is already configured as Multi-AZ. Which TWO actions meet these requirements with the LEAST change? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Upgrade the instance type to one twice as large as the current type and place more instances within a single AZ to reduce the chance of a single-instance failure.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure the ALB across subnets in the same three AZs and associate the Auto Scaling group with the target group so that requests go to targets in the healthy AZs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reduce the minimum capacity of the Auto Scaling group to 0, and when an AZ failure is detected, have an operator add a subnet in a new AZ from the console to restore capacity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Associate an Elastic IP address with the EC2 instances, and prepare a procedure and checklist in which an engineer manually moves the address to a standby instance in another AZ during a failure. Also run switchover drills regularly.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Specify subnets in three different AZs for the Auto Scaling group to distribute instances across the AZs, so that capacity is replenished in the remaining AZs when an AZ fails.

exam-soa-c02-13.explanation: The correct answer is the combination that configures both the Auto Scaling group and the ALB across multiple AZs. When the group uses subnets in multiple AZs, it launches new instances in the unaffected AZs when an AZ becomes unhealthy and rebalances evenly after recovery, and the load balancer must also enable the same AZs so that traffic goes to targets in the healthy AZs. According to the documentation, an ALB must enable at least two AZs. Scaling up or adding instances within the same AZ does not protect against an AZ failure. A minimum capacity of 0 with manually adding subnets, and manually moving an Elastic IP address, depend on human response rather than automatic recovery.

exam-soa-c02-14.prompt: The platform team at a SaaS company is looking for a way to prevent a recurrence after an incident in which a production CloudFormation stack was accidentally deleted. The stack contains about 40 resources, including an Amazon RDS database, an ALB, and an Auto Scaling group, and a CI/CD pipeline updates the stack several times a day. Going forward, attempts to delete the stack must fail, but stack updates resulting from template changes must remain allowed through the pipeline without being blocked, as they are now. The template is shared across several parts of the team, so the team wants to avoid any method that significantly changes the template structure. The stack deletions were mostly caused by developers clicking by mistake in the console, and the pipeline uses its IAM permissions only for stack updates. What is the MOST appropriate method that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set DeletionPolicy: Retain on all resources in the stack so that the resources remain even if the stack is deleted.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use a stack policy to deny Update actions on all resources.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enable termination protection on the stack.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Turn on the disable rollback option when creating the stack so that the stack cannot be deleted.

exam-soa-c02-14.explanation: When termination protection is enabled, deletion attempts fail and the stack and its state are kept as they are, and it does not affect updates, so it meets both requirements together. DeletionPolicy: Retain only leaves the resources behind when the stack is deleted and does not prevent deletion of the stack itself. Denying all updates with a stack policy would block the CI/CD updates that happen several times a day, which violates the requirement. Disable rollback is an option about automatic rollback when creation fails, which is a different feature from termination protection, and it does not prevent deletion.

exam-soa-c02-15.prompt: A total of 200 EC2 instances in private subnets at a video analytics company download about 5 TB per day from an Amazon S3 bucket in the same Region. They currently connect through a NAT gateway, so data processing charges account for a large share of the monthly cost, and the finance team asked to reduce this item. All the clients are inside the VPC, and access from on premises is not needed. S3 access permissions are already granted through IAM roles, and all the objects are in a bucket in the same Region. The application code must not be changed. All S3 access is based on IAM roles, and the bucket policy does not yet have a condition that allows only a specific VPC. Which method is the MOST cost-effective and the simplest to configure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an S3 interface endpoint in each subnet and turn on private DNS so that S3 requests go to the endpoint ENIs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add one NAT gateway per AZ to distribute data processing throughput and reduce inter-AZ data transfer charges.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the application settings to use the S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint to optimize the transfer path.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an S3 gateway endpoint and associate it with the route tables used by the private subnets.

exam-soa-c02-15.explanation: The correct answer is to associate an S3 gateway endpoint with the route tables. According to the documentation, a gateway endpoint lets you reach S3 without an internet gateway or NAT device and has no additional charge, so it eliminates the NAT data processing charges while satisfying the requirement that access come from within the VPC. An interface endpoint carries hourly charges and data processing charges, which is an unnecessary cost in this situation. Adding NAT gateways increases hourly charges and leaves the data processing charges unchanged. Transfer Acceleration is for improving upload speed over long distances and does not reduce NAT costs.

exam-soa-c02-16.prompt: The operations team at a financial services company wants to keep the CloudWatch agent installed and running on EC2 instances tagged Env=prod (about 150 instances that grow and shrink frequently with Auto Scaling). Even if someone stops the agent or a new instance with the same tag is added, the instances must return to the desired state within a set interval, and compliance must also be verifiable. The agent configuration uses a standard document defined by the security team, and all instances are managed by Systems Manager. The installation document is already registered as a Systems Manager document, and the agent configuration is set up to read values from Parameter Store. Which method has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run the install command once with Run Command, and then have an engineer periodically check for later changes and rerun it if needed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a State Manager association on a set schedule that runs the agent installation and configuration documents against the target tag.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Register a task that runs once a month in a maintenance window so that the agent is reinstalled on a set day.

choices.label: D
