choices.text: Put a script that checks the agent status via cron on each instance, collect the results directly through Lambda, and build a report.

exam-soa-c02-16.explanation: A State Manager association keeps applying a document to target nodes on a set schedule to maintain the desired state, and when you target by tag, instances added later are included as well and compliance status is reported. State Manager is the right tool for automating system compliance, and Maintenance Windows is the right tool for time-sensitive tasks in a set time window. Running Run Command once does not restore later changes or cover new instances, and it requires people to check. A once-a-month task could leave a stopped agent unattended for up to a month, which does not meet the requirement to recover within a set interval. Self-built cron and Lambda increase the operational burden even though a managed feature exists.

exam-soa-c02-17.prompt: The web service of an online education company runs on multiple instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an ALB. Last night the web process died on one instance and it returned only HTTP 503. The EC2 status checks all passed, so the group marked the instance as healthy, and the ALB reported the target as unhealthy, but the group did not replace the instance. The company does not want to repeat this situation, in which the on-call engineer had to terminate the instance manually in the early morning. The target group health check is already configured to expect a 200 response on the /health path, and the instance warmup time after launch is appropriately set to 300 seconds. What is the MOST appropriate action to have failed instances replaced automatically without changing application code?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reduce the health check interval of the ALB target group to 5 seconds and lower the unhealthy threshold count so that an instance is judged unhealthy more quickly.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase the health check grace period so that the group waits longer after an instance launches before it starts health checks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Run a Lambda function on an EventBridge schedule that analyzes the ALB access logs and terminates the instance when 5xx errors increase, and let the group refill the terminated instance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Additionally turn on the Elastic Load Balancing health check type for the Auto Scaling group so that instances the ALB considers unhealthy are replaced.

exam-soa-c02-17.explanation: The correct answer is to turn on the Elastic Load Balancing health check type for the group. By default, Auto Scaling uses only EC2 status checks and ignores the load balancer health check results, so if the EC2 checks pass it does not replace an instance even when the process has died. When the ELB checks are turned on, an instance that the load balancer reports as unhealthy is marked unhealthy at the next check and replaced. Shortening the target group health check interval is useless if the group does not use that result. The grace period only delays when checks begin right after launch and has no effect on a failed instance that is already running. The access log and Lambda approach must be built and operated yourself.

exam-soa-c02-18.prompt: The operations team at a retail company applies patches to 12 EC2 web servers behind an ALB only between 02:00 and 04:00 every Saturday. Before patching, each instance must be deregistered from the load balancer, and the order of re-registering it after patching must be guaranteed, and no work may start outside that time window. This is a time-sensitive task that runs in a set time window, and the team does not want to build an orchestration server that it operates itself. All the instances are managed by Systems Manager, and the team has 3 members. The load balancer deregistration step proceeds in batches of 3 instances at a time, and even if a patch fails, the remaining batches must continue. What is the MOST appropriate method that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a maintenance window with a Saturday 02:00 schedule and a 2-hour duration, and register as a task an AWS Step Functions Standard state machine that defines the order of deregistration, patching, and re-registration.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run the AWS-RunPatchBaseline document periodically with a State Manager association to patch all 12 instances at the same time all at once. Check the execution results per instance in the State Manager compliance report.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use Patch now to run Scan and install on all 12 instances at once, and after it completes, have a person check the load balancer registration status.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure the patch installation schedule for the entire organization with the Quick Setup Host Management option, and have the installation run on early Saturday morning.

exam-soa-c02-18.explanation: Maintenance Windows is a tool that runs potentially risky tasks at set times by specifying a schedule and a maximum duration, and a Step Functions task can orchestrate the sequence of removing a node from the load balancer, patching it, and adding it back (only Standard state machines are supported). A State Manager association is intended for maintaining state and compliance, so it does not fit this task that requires control of the time window and ordering, and patching the instances at the same time could interrupt the service. Patch now is a manual immediate run that ignores schedules and does not guarantee the deregistration and re-registration order. The Host Management option is limited to scanning for and reporting missing patches and cannot install patches.

exam-soa-c02-19.prompt: Forty CloudWatch Logs log groups used by multiple Lambda functions and Amazon ECS services at a media streaming company have never had their settings changed since creation, and they are driving up monthly costs. Under the audit policy, logs only need to be retained for 90 days and can be deleted after that. All the log group names start with /app/, and it would be good if the same policy also applied to log groups created with this prefix in the future. The operations team has no capacity to write code. Some of the log group names keep increasing as new services are added, and the company has confirmed that deleting logs older than 90 days causes no regulatory problem. What is the MOST efficient way to reduce cost without writing code?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure an EventBridge scheduled rule and a Lambda function to delete the 40 log groups every month and recreate them with the same names.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run an export task to Amazon S3 every day for each log group, and leave the logs on the CloudWatch Logs side as they are with no further action after exporting.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an account-level retention policy that specifies a 90-day retention period for the /app/ prefix, and set it to a mode that also applies retroactively to existing log groups.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because the default retention period of log groups is already 90 days, leave the log group settings as they are and add only an S3 lifecycle rule.

exam-soa-c02-19.explanation: The correct answer is to create an account-level retention policy for the /app/ prefix with 90-day retention in retroactive mode. CloudWatch Logs stores logs indefinitely by default, so you must specify a retention period to reduce costs, and a prefix-based account-level policy applies to all 40 groups at once without code, and retroactive mode (RETROACTIVE) also applies to existing groups (the policy takes effect about 24 hours after it is created, and expired events are not deleted immediately but can take up to about 72 hours). Deleting and recreating log groups every month would also erase logs within the 90 days needed for the audit. An S3 export only copies the logs and does not reduce the cost of retaining the originals. The premise that the default retention period is 90 days is wrong, because the default is never expire, so an S3 lifecycle rule has nothing to do with CloudWatch Logs costs.

exam-soa-c02-20.prompt: A global retail company has 70 accounts in AWS Organizations, and the audit team wants to collect management events from all enabled Regions in all accounts into a single Amazon S3 bucket. Newly created accounts must be included automatically, and administrators of member accounts must not be able to turn off or change the trail. Under company policy, logs are kept centrally in only one place, and the audit team has no staff to check the settings in each account. The organization's management account is operated separately by the security team, and CloudTrail trusted access is already enabled. Which method meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deploy a trail with the same settings to each account by using StackSets, and have all the trails deliver logs to the central S3 bucket.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have the audit team export each account's CloudTrail Event history by hand every 90 days and collect it in the central bucket.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a single-Region trail in the management account, and bring in and retain events from other Regions by using S3 Cross-Region Replication.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a multi-Region organization trail in the management account or a delegated administrator account, and deliver the logs to the central S3 bucket.

exam-soa-c02-20.explanation: An organization trail is created in the management account or a delegated administrator account and logs events from all member accounts of the organization to a single bucket, and it is applied automatically when a new account is added to the organization. Users in member accounts can only view the organization trail and cannot delete it, turn off logging, or change it. An organization trail created in the console is a multi-Region trail that covers all enabled Regions. Trails deployed to each account with StackSets can be modified or turned off by member account administrators. Exporting Event history is manual and limited to a 90-day range. A single-Region trail does not record activity in other Regions, so it cannot be supplemented with replication.

exam-soa-c02-21.prompt: A mobile gaming company runs 60 Linux EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The operations team must be notified when memory utilization exceeds 85%, but it cannot find a memory item in the default EC2 metrics in the console. Instances are replaced frequently as traffic changes, so configuring each instance by hand must be avoided, and security policy does not allow SSH access to the instances to be left open. An SNS topic for notifications already exists. All the instances run Amazon Linux, and the instance profile already has CloudWatch agent permissions attached. Which configuration has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Turn on EC2 detailed monitoring so that the 1-minute default metrics include memory utilization, and set an alarm on that metric to notify through SNS.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a metric filter on the application log group to calculate system memory utilization, and set an alarm on the metric that the filter creates.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Include the installation and configuration of the CloudWatch agent in the launch template so that it publishes a memory utilization metric, and set an alarm on that metric to notify through SNS.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run a Lambda function every 5 minutes that connects to each instance over SSH, reads the output of the free command, and sends an SNS notification when the threshold is exceeded.

exam-soa-c02-21.explanation: The correct answer is the configuration that deploys the CloudWatch agent through the launch template to publish a memory metric and sets an alarm on that metric. The default AWS/EC2 metrics include CPU, network, and disk throughput, but not memory utilization inside the guest OS, so an agent is required, and putting it in the launch template applies it automatically to replacement instances with no manual work. Detailed monitoring only shortens the collection interval from 5 minutes to 1 minute and does not add a memory metric. A metric filter extracts values from log strings and does not calculate OS memory utilization. The Lambda and SSH approach has the largest burden because you must also operate key management and handling of connection failures yourself.

exam-soa-c02-22.prompt: A company that operates an internal HR system wants to use an internal Application Load Balancer in the Seoul Region as the primary endpoint and an internal Application Load Balancer in the Tokyo Region as the secondary, and to switch the access of corporate VPN users with failover routing in an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone. The ALBs have no public IP addresses and the security groups allow only the VPC-internal CIDR range, and the security team does not allow exposing the ALBs to the internet for health checks. Switchover during a failure must happen automatically without human intervention. The ALBs in both Regions serve an application with the same configuration, and user traffic must normally go only to Seoul. What is the MOST appropriate way to have Route 53 determine the state of the primary endpoint?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an endpoint health check that targets the private IP address of the primary ALB and associate it with the failover record.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a CloudWatch alarm on a metric such as the ALB's HealthyHostCount, and associate a Route 53 health check that monitors that alarm with the failover record.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Specify the ALB DNS name as the target of an endpoint health check, shorten the check interval to a fast 10 seconds, lower the failure threshold count, and associate it with the record. Also publish the check results to a separate dashboard.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Switch to weighted routing instead of failover, and prepare a runbook for manually changing the weight of the primary record to 0.

exam-soa-c02-22.explanation: The correct answer is to create a Route 53 health check that monitors a CloudWatch alarm. According to the documentation, endpoint health checks send requests from Route 53 over the internet, so they cannot reach an internal ALB that has no public IP address, and such private resources are evaluated with a health check based on a CloudWatch alarm. An endpoint check that targets a private IP address or the ALB DNS name will always fail for the same reason, even if you shorten the check interval. Weighted routing and a manual runbook are not automatic failover, so the switchover is tied to the speed of human response.

exam-soa-c02-23.prompt: A healthcare information company must encrypt all of its EBS volumes to meet a compliance requirement. The Seoul Region currently has 20 production instances with unencrypted volumes attached, and volumes that team members create in the future must be created encrypted without mistakes. Developers create new volumes themselves with the console and the CLI. Existing volumes can be replaced during a monthly maintenance window, but service interruption at any other time is not allowed. For the AWS CloudTrail audit evidence to pass, the Encrypted attribute of every EBS volume must be true, and using AWS managed keys is allowed. Which TWO actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the KMS key attached to the existing volumes to a customer managed key so that the unencrypted volumes become encrypted.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable EBS encryption by default in the Seoul Region.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because enabling encryption by default automatically encrypts existing volumes that are already attached, wait without any additional work.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a snapshot of each existing volume, create a new encrypted volume from that snapshot, and replace the existing volume with it during the maintenance window.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Turn on the encryption attribute for the existing volumes with ModifyVolume to encrypt the volumes in place without stopping the instances.

exam-soa-c02-23.explanation: The correct answers are turning on encryption by default and creating new encrypted volumes from snapshots and swapping them in. Encryption by default makes newly created volumes, and volumes created from unencrypted snapshots, encrypted, but it does not change volumes that already exist. An existing unencrypted volume cannot be encrypted directly, and you must create a snapshot and create a new encrypted volume from it. ModifyVolume changes the type, size, and performance, so it cannot turn on the encryption attribute. An unencrypted volume has no KMS key to change, and the key of an existing volume cannot be changed. The claim that encryption by default applies retroactively to existing volumes is not true.

exam-soa-c02-24.prompt: An accounting software company has a group of EC2 instances whose CPU utilization is high only in the last week of each month because of quarter-end close processing. When the company turned on AWS Compute Optimizer in the middle of this month, it produced an over-provisioned finding and a recommendation for an instance type one size smaller, but the team is concerned that the month-end load may not have been reflected. If month-end processing slows down, it directly affects customers' closing schedules, so performance risk must be reduced, and simply keeping the instances large is not consistent with the cost goal. All of these instances are of recent-generation types, memory metrics are not yet being collected, and changes can be made only after month-end processing. What is the MOST appropriate action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Opt out of Compute Optimizer and opt in again at month-end so that it newly collects only the metrics from the month-end load period.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If you add memory metrics with the CloudWatch agent, the analysis period of Compute Optimizer is automatically extended to more than one month.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Activate enhanced infrastructure metrics so that it looks at 93 days, which is longer than the default recommendation analysis period of 14 days.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ignore the recommendation and move all instances up to a type one size larger to match the month-end load, preventing performance problems.

exam-soa-c02-24.explanation: After you opt in, Compute Optimizer analyzes CloudWatch metrics over a default period of 14 days, and turning on enhanced infrastructure metrics (a paid feature) extends the analysis period for the selected resources to 93 days so that it can reflect the monthly cycle. Opting out and opting in again does not make use of analysis history and would actually hinder the accumulation of metrics. Memory metrics can improve the accuracy of recommendations but do not change the analysis period. Ignoring the recommendation and running larger instances goes in the opposite direction of the goal of reducing costs.

exam-soa-c02-25.prompt: Account A at an insurance company has an Amazon EBS snapshot encrypted with a customer managed AWS KMS key, and for a disaster recovery drill the snapshot must be restored to a volume in account B. The snapshot has already been shared with account B, but when an administrator in account B tried to restore it, a KMS permissions error occurred. The security team does not allow making the snapshot public or removing its encryption, and both accounts belong to the same AWS Organizations organization. The restore is performed by a specific IAM role in account B. The snapshot in account A is already shared with account B, and the account B role already has the EC2 and EBS related permissions. Which TWO actions are required to meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reapply the snapshot sharing setting, because granting the snapshot sharing permission again also delegates access to the KMS key.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attach an IAM policy that delegates kms permissions on the account A key ARN to the IAM role in account B that performs the restore.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the snapshot sharing setting to public, because it can then be restored from any account, and do not deal with KMS permissions separately.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a statement to the key policy of the account A KMS key that allows account B (or a specific role in account B) to use the key.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Change the KMS key associated with the snapshot in place to a key owned by account B to remove the dependency on the existing key.

exam-soa-c02-25.explanation: The correct answers are allowing account B in the key policy and delegating that permission with an IAM policy in account B. Cross-account KMS use requires both the key policy in the account that owns the key and an IAM policy in the external account, and one of the two alone is not enough. An encrypted snapshot cannot be made public and can be shared only with specific accounts, and the security team also prohibits making it public. The KMS key of an existing snapshot or volume cannot be changed, and it can be switched to a different key only during a copy. Sharing a snapshot is only a permission on the snapshot and does not automatically grant KMS key permissions.

exam-soa-c02-26.prompt: The security team at an e-commerce company newly enabled AWS Security Hub CSPM and turned on the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard. The findings from Amazon GuardDuty and Amazon Inspector appeared immediately, but even after several days almost no security control check results have been generated for Amazon S3 and IAM. The account uses only a single Region, Seoul, and the team uses only AWS services without any separate third-party security tools. The status of the account's AWS Config recorder has not been checked yet, and there is talk that the company ran without turning on AWS Config because of cost. What is the MOST likely cause of this problem and its solution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: CloudTrail data events are turned off, so enable S3 data event logging and connect the logs to Security Hub CSPM.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The 30-day free trial of Security Hub CSPM must end before control checks begin, so wait for the trial period to pass.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cross-Region aggregation is turned off, so specify an aggregation Region and configure it to receive control results from all Regions in one place.

choices.label: D
choices.text: AWS Config is not turned on or is not recording resources, so enable Config recording in that account and Region.

exam-soa-c02-26.explanation: For most controls, Security Hub CSPM runs its checks by using AWS Config service-linked rules, so control results are generated only when Config is turned on and recording resources. The findings from GuardDuty and Inspector are sent by other services, so they appear regardless of Config. CloudTrail data events are not a prerequisite for control checks. The free trial period concerns billing, and checks run even during the trial. Cross-Region aggregation is a feature that shows results from multiple Regions in one place and does not itself produce control checks.

exam-soa-c02-27.prompt: During a disaster recovery drill at a financial company, a database was brought up on a gp3 volume created from a 4 TB encrypted EBS snapshot, and during the first few days the latency was high each time a block was read for the first time, so the recovery time objective (RTO) was not met. A single snapshot is used for recovery, and recovery is set to be performed in only one AZ in the Seoul Region. A new snapshot is created once a day, and the database instance type cannot be changed. The snapshot lifecycle is managed with Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM), and the recovery drill runs once per quarter. Which method provides full volume performance right after restore while minimizing additional cost?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Restore with the volume type changed to io2 and specify the maximum provisioned IOPS so that the latency of first-time block reads disappears.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable fast snapshot restore in all AZs in the Seoul Region and apply the same setting to all the snapshots you hold.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Move up to an instance type with greater EBS-optimized bandwidth so that the first-read speed of the restored volume increases.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable fast snapshot restore for that snapshot only in the one AZ where recovery will be performed.

exam-soa-c02-27.explanation: The correct answer is to turn on fast snapshot restore only for the needed snapshot and a single AZ. This feature fully initializes volumes created from the snapshot at creation time, which eliminates the latency on first reads of blocks and matches the symptom exactly, and because an hourly charge applies for each snapshot and AZ combination, limiting it to the one snapshot and one AZ used for recovery gives the lowest cost. The volume type and provisioned IOPS are performance factors separate from the latency of fetching snapshot blocks for the first time. Enabling it for all AZs and all snapshots only adds cost and goes beyond the requirement. Increasing instance bandwidth still leaves the first-access latency.

exam-soa-c02-28.prompt: The operations team at a SaaS company wants to know in advance about hardware retirement and maintenance events that AWS has scheduled for the EC2 instances in its account, and wants to send automatic notifications to an Amazon SNS topic connected to the company's internal messenger. Last quarter instances restarted without warning and customer inquiries increased. The company must avoid installing an agent on every instance for the notifications, and the scope is a single account. The notification channel is already consolidated into an SNS topic, and the target instances include standalone instances outside Auto Scaling groups. Retirement notices usually arrive several weeks in advance, and when the team receives one, it responds by stopping and starting the instance itself during a maintenance window. Which configuration has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an alarm on each instance's StatusCheckFailed metric to notify the SNS topic when a status check fails.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use an EventBridge rule to match AWS Health scheduled change events for EC2, and specify the SNS topic as the target.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Query the CloudTrail event history every day to see whether there were retirement-related API calls, and have an engineer share them manually in the messenger.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Check the Trusted Advisor results screen once a week, download the list of instances scheduled for retirement, and forward it to the messenger by hand.

exam-soa-c02-28.explanation: The correct answer is the configuration that receives AWS Health events with an EventBridge rule and delivers them to SNS. Health emits scheduled changes to account resources as events, and the documentation also describes using SNS and other targets from an EventBridge rule, so this gives advance notification without an agent. A status check failure alarm fires after a problem has already occurred, so it cannot give advance notice of the schedule. CloudTrail is a record of API calls by users and services, not a maintenance notice that AWS has scheduled. Periodically checking the Trusted Advisor screen requires continuing manual work.

exam-soa-c02-29.prompt: A log analysis pipeline at a telecommunications company performs large sequential reads from a dedicated data volume (12 TiB) on EC2 and must continuously sustain a throughput of about 400 MiB/s. There is almost no random I/O, and this volume is not a boot volume. Most read operations happen in large blocks of 1 MiB or more. The company currently uses an SSD volume, so storage cost has become a burden, and latency is not important. The volume is attached to only a single instance, the instance type is a large type with sufficient EBS throughput, and the read block size is consistently 1 MiB or more. Which EBS volume type meets the required throughput at the LOWEST cost?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An st1 Throughput Optimized HDD volume

choices.label: B
choices.text: An sc1 Cold HDD volume, to get the lowest cost per GiB

choices.label: C
choices.text: A gp3 volume with throughput provisioned at 400 MiB/s or higher

choices.label: D
choices.text: An io2 Block Express volume with IOPS provisioned to match the required throughput

exam-soa-c02-29.explanation: st1 is an HDD designed for large sequential workloads such as big data and log processing. Its baseline throughput is 40 MiB/s per TiB, so a 12 TiB volume sustains 480 MiB/s even without burst credits, and the per-volume maximum is 500 MiB/s, so it meets the requirement to sustain 400 MiB/s while costing less than SSD. The condition that it is not a boot volume allows HDD to be used. sc1 has a baseline throughput of 12 MiB/s per TiB and a maximum of 250 MiB/s per volume even with burst, so even at 12 TiB it reaches only 144 MiB/s and falls short. gp3 can reach up to 2,000 MiB/s, but as an SSD its unit price is higher, so it does not fit the condition of lowest cost. io2 Block Express is for workloads that need sub-millisecond latency and high IOPS, so it is excessive for sequential processing.

exam-soa-c02-30.prompt: The ALB RequestCount metric at an online ticket sales company runs to tens of thousands per minute during weekday daytime and drops to a few hundred in the early morning and on weekends. If a fixed threshold is set based on daytime, anomalies in the early morning are missed, and if it is set based on early morning, false positives are frequent during the day. This daily and weekly pattern has repeated in the same shape for several weeks. The operations team does not want to adjust thresholds by time of day by hand. The metric has already accumulated more than 5 weeks in CloudWatch, notifications can go to the existing SNS topic, and the team is interested in deviations in both directions from the normal range. Which method, among those that learn the day-of-week and time-of-day pattern and notify only when the metric leaves the normal range, has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fix a high threshold to match the daytime peak, and handle early-morning false positives by changing the alarm action to only log records instead of SNS.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run a Lambda function every hour that calculates the average for the same day of week and time of day last month and publishes it as a custom metric, and set a fixed-threshold alarm on that metric.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a composite alarm that combines the request count alarm and the CPU alarm with OR so that it notifies when either one fires, reducing missed detections.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable an anomaly detection model on the RequestCount metric, and create an anomaly detection alarm that goes to ALARM when the metric leaves the expected range band.

exam-soa-c02-30.explanation: The correct answer is an anomaly detection alarm. CloudWatch anomaly detection learns the time-of-day and day-of-week seasonality and trends from the metric's historical data to build a band of expected values, and the alarm fires when the metric goes above or below the band, so it meets the requirement without a fixed threshold. A fixed threshold based on daytime will never catch early-morning anomalies. Calculating and publishing averages with Lambda can work, but you must maintain the code, schedule, and seasonality adjustments yourself, so the operational burden is large. A composite alarm only combines existing alarm states and does not learn patterns, so it keeps the fixed-threshold problem.

exam-soa-c02-31.prompt: An operations team at a company failed while updating a CloudFormation stack (with EC2, RDS, and S3 resources), and during the rollback, the attempt to restore the previous version of the RDS instance failed again, leaving the stack in the UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED state. Investigation showed that the cause was that, before the update, an operator had directly deleted that RDS instance from the console. This instance cannot be recovered, and the remaining EC2 and S3 resources are in production, so the stack cannot be deleted. The operations team has not manually touched any resources since the rollback failure, and the latest snapshot of the deleted instance is kept separately. What is the MOST appropriate action to return the stack to a state in which it can be updated again?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run UpdateStack again with the same template to create the deleted RDS instance anew, thereby bypassing the UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED state. Review the impact in advance with a change set before running it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Call ContinueUpdateRollback and specify the logical ID of the RDS resource that failed to roll back in ResourcesToSkip, and then bring the template and the actual resources into agreement afterward.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Delete the entire stack, create a new stack with the same template, and manually migrate the running EC2 and S3 resources to the new stack.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run drift detection on the stack so that the deleted RDS instance is automatically recovered based on the template and the rollback continues.

exam-soa-c02-31.explanation: The correct answer is to specify the failed resource in ResourcesToSkip with ContinueUpdateRollback. When the cause of the rollback failure (the RDS instance deleted outside CloudFormation) cannot be fixed, you can skip that resource and return the stack to UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE, and because the skipped resource will be out of sync with the template, you must reconcile it before the next update. A stack in the UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED state cannot be updated, so running UpdateStack again with the same template is rejected. Deleting and recreating the stack requires moving running resources, which affects the service, and violates the constraint that the problem states the stack cannot be deleted. Drift detection only reports differences and does not recover resources or advance a rollback.

exam-soa-c02-32.prompt: A StackSet at a company that has multiple business units deploys a logging bucket stack to 30 accounts in AWS Organizations. One business unit is being spun off, so the stacks in its 3 accounts must be removed from StackSet management, but the resources in those accounts, including the buckets that contain the logs accumulated so far, must continue to run as they are. After the transition, the business unit's own staff will operate those accounts directly, and the remaining 27 accounts will continue to be managed with the StackSet as they are now. The logging buckets contain logs under a retention policy, and if the buckets disappear because the stacks are deleted, it would be a compliance violation. What is the MOST appropriate method that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delete the stack instances without any options, and then manually create the same stack anew in those accounts from the same template.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deploy an update that removes the logging bucket resource from the StackSet template to all accounts to exclude it from management. Make sure it is reflected identically in all 30 accounts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Run an operation to delete the stack instances in those 3 accounts while selecting the Retain stacks option.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Delete the entire StackSet, then create a new StackSet for the remaining 27 accounts and redeploy.

exam-soa-c02-32.explanation: When you delete stack instances and select the Retain stacks option, the stacks in those accounts and Regions are detached from the StackSet but the stacks and resources are left in place, so they can then be managed independently in the target accounts. Deleting without the option deletes resources such as the buckets along with the stacks and could lose the accumulated logs, and a newly created stack would not take over the existing resources. An update that removes the resource from the template applies to all stack instances, so the buckets in all 30 accounts would become targets for deletion. Deleting the entire StackSet and redeploying creates unnecessary change risk for the remaining accounts too.

exam-soa-c02-33.prompt: An application server (10.0.5.20) in a newly created subnet times out when connecting to port 3306 on a database server in another subnet of the same VPC. The company wants to determine with evidence, not guesswork, whether the cause is a security group, a network ACL, or routing. Changing server settings requires a change approval process that takes several days, and work that touches traffic on the production database server must be avoided. The two subnets have network ACLs associated with them that were created by different teams, and flow logs are not yet turned on. Which TWO actions narrow down the cause the fastest without touching server settings or traffic? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Turn on VPC flow logs on the database server's ENI to check whether 3306 traffic from the app server's address is ACCEPT or REJECT, along with the records by direction.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reboot the app server and the database server so that open connection states are reset, and then try the connection again.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Analyze the path between the two ENIs with Reachability Analyzer to identify the security group, network ACL, or routing component that blocks the path.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Turn on Route 53 Resolver query logs to first check whether the app server resolves the database hostname to the correct IP address.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Use Traffic Mirroring to replicate all packets from the database server to a security appliance and analyze the packet captures in detail with a separate analysis tool. Review the results together with the security team.

exam-soa-c02-33.explanation: The correct answers are Reachability Analyzer and VPC flow logs. Reachability Analyzer is a configuration analysis tool that does not send packets; if the destination is reachable it shows the hop-by-hop path, and if not it identifies the blocking component such as a security group, network ACL, or route table. However, it analyzes only the network configuration, so it cannot show whether the server OS firewall or the application is listening on the port, and if the configuration all comes back as allowed, that layer must be checked separately. This problem is about determining which of the security group, network ACL, or routing is the cause, so configuration analysis is sufficient. Flow logs record allowed and denied traffic as ACCEPT and REJECT, so they provide evidence of where the actual request is being denied. Traffic Mirroring is for packet-level analysis, is excessive here, and requires configuration changes. Resolver query logs are a tool for name resolution problems and differ from diagnosing a timeout when connecting by IP. A reboot provides no evidence.

exam-soa-c02-34.prompt: A global gaming company has identical ALB-based stacks in the Seoul and N. Virginia Regions. Regardless of a user's country, each user must be connected to the Region with the faster network response, and if the ALB in one Region is unhealthy, that Region must be excluded from DNS responses. The Seoul and N. Virginia stacks already have synchronized data so that either side can handle requests, and there are no country-specific data residency regulations. The domain is already in a Route 53 hosted zone. The ALB in each Region has a /ping path for health checks, and latency-based routing must be applied at the DNS response stage. What is the MOST appropriate Route 53 configuration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use geolocation records to map Asian users to Seoul and North American users to N. Virginia, with the default location set to Seoul.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a latency-based record for each Region and associate that ALB's health check with each record.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create weighted records at 50 to 50 so that both Regions receive traffic at the same ratio, and associate health checks.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create failover records with Seoul as primary and N. Virginia as secondary, so that traffic goes to N. Virginia only when Seoul is unhealthy.

exam-soa-c02-34.explanation: The correct answer is latency-based records per Region with health checks associated. Latency routing responds with the Region that has the lowest latency to the user when resources are in multiple Regions, and a record with an associated health check is excluded from responses when it is unhealthy, so both requirements are met. Geolocation routing sends users to a predefined place based on user location and does not guarantee the Region with the faster response. Weighted routing only splits by ratio and does not consider per-user latency. Failover routing is an active-passive configuration that uses only the primary Region, so even users in N. Virginia would go to Seoul.

exam-soa-c02-35.prompt: An order management company runs MySQL that it installed directly on EC2 with a 500 GiB data volume, and it consistently requires an average of 12,000 IOPS. Single-digit millisecond latency is sufficient, and sub-millisecond latency or more than 60,000 IOPS is not needed. The database runs on a single instance and does not use read replicas. The company currently uses a gp2 volume, but costs are rising because it has inflated the capacity to get the IOPS. Snapshots are taken once a day, and the instance type's EBS bandwidth fully supports the required IOPS and throughput. Which EBS volume configuration meets the performance requirements at the LOWEST cost?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 500 GiB io2 Block Express volume with 12,000 IOPS provisioned to secure consistent sub-millisecond latency

choices.label: B
choices.text: A 500 GiB gp2 volume, covering 12,000 IOPS with burst performance

choices.label: C
choices.text: A 500 GiB gp3 volume with 12,000 IOPS provisioned

choices.label: D
choices.text: A 500 GiB st1 Throughput Optimized HDD volume, using steady throughput as a substitute for the IOPS requirement

exam-soa-c02-35.explanation: gp3 provides 3,000 IOPS as a baseline and lets you provision additional IOPS at a ratio of 500 IOPS per GiB up to 80,000 IOPS, so you can set 12,000 IOPS on a 500 GiB volume. Single-digit millisecond latency is sufficient, and its price per GiB is 20% lower than gp2, so it meets the requirements at the lowest cost. io2 Block Express is for workloads that need sub-millisecond latency or performance beyond 80,000 IOPS, so it incurs unnecessary cost in this problem. gp2 has IOPS proportional to capacity, a baseline of 1,500 IOPS at 500 GiB and bursting only to 3,000 IOPS, so it cannot sustain 12,000 IOPS. st1 is an HDD with a maximum of about 500 IOPS, so it does not suit an IOPS-driven database.

exam-soa-c02-36.prompt: A software company creates a golden AMI with OS patches and the company's security agent applied every month and deploys it to 8 accounts in the Seoul and Tokyo Regions. Currently, an engineer connects to an EC2 instance and creates and copies the AMI manually, and last month an image with missing patches was deployed. Only images that pass testing must be deployed, and the company wants to minimize the servers and scripts it must manage itself. The infrastructure team has 2 members. The test stage is already defined as running a CIS benchmark check script, and all 8 target accounts belong to the same organization. What is the MOST appropriate method that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Place a cron script on a build EC2 instance to create the AMI and use the AWS CLI to copy and share it to each Region and account.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Back up a reference instance every month with AWS Backup and copy the recovery points to other Regions and accounts to use as AMIs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Define an EC2 Image Builder pipeline with a monthly schedule, build and test components, and a distribution configuration that specifies the target Regions and accounts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Have an engineer manually enter the latest AMI ID into the ImageId parameter of the CloudFormation template every month to update the stack.

exam-soa-c02-36.explanation: In an EC2 Image Builder pipeline that creates images on a schedule, the build components of the recipe apply the patches and the agent, the image is distributed only when all test components succeed, and the distribution configuration specifies the Regions and account sharing. A self-built cron script requires you to operate the server and script yourself and to implement guarantees such as distributing only after tests pass. An AWS Backup recovery point is a feature for copying backups and has no patch application or testing stages. Entering the ImageId manually does not solve the problem of creating the AMI and leaves only manual work.

exam-soa-c02-37.prompt: Under security policy, the operations team of a public agency system must let administrators connect with a shell to 50 EC2 instances in private subnets that have no public IP addresses and no internet route. Inbound port 22 must not be opened, and bastion hosts and SSH keys must not be operated. Access permissions must be controlled with IAM, and connection records must be kept. The latest SSM Agent is installed on the instances. Administrators sign in with AWS IAM Identity Center, and the team wants to keep session logs in Amazon S3 or Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Which TWO actions are required to meet these requirements by using Session Manager? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a new key pair for each instance, distribute it to the administrators, and operate a procedure to rotate the keys every 90 days.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create interface VPC endpoints for Systems Manager (ssm, ssmmessages, ec2messages) so that the instances can connect to the service without the internet.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Attach to the instance profile an IAM role that includes the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy so that the instances become Systems Manager managed nodes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Place a bastion host in a public subnet, allow only port 22 connections from the administrators' IP range in the security group, and connect again from the bastion to each instance by using SSH keys.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Assign public IP addresses to the instances, open port 22 for the administrators' IP addresses in the security group, and connect by using EC2 Instance Connect.

exam-soa-c02-37.explanation: The correct answers are attaching a role that includes AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore to the instance profile and creating interface VPC endpoints for Systems Manager. The former is needed so that the instances register as managed nodes and access can be controlled with IAM, and the latter lets the SSM Agent connect privately to the service from private subnets that have no internet route. Depending on the agent version, ec2messages is also used, so create all three endpoints together. A bastion host requires port 22 and host operations, which violates the constraints. Distributing and rotating key pairs works against the goal of eliminating SSH key management. Assigning public IP addresses and opening port 22 violates both the condition that there be no internet route and the condition that inbound ports not be opened.

exam-soa-c02-38.prompt: A legacy application running on a single EC2 instance at an internal business systems company occasionally stops responding because of an OS kernel problem. When this happens, only the instance status check fails and the system status check passes. The instance must be rebooted without human intervention while keeping its public IP address, instance ID, and disk data, and a configuration that replaces the instance with a new one is not allowed. The application is already configured to start automatically after a reboot. An Elastic IP address is attached to the instance, a reboot finishes in about 1 minute, and the company wants the alarm to act only after 3 consecutive failed evaluations. What is the MOST suitable method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an alarm on the StatusCheckFailed_Instance metric and specify rebooting the EC2 instance as the alarm action.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an alarm on the StatusCheckFailed_System metric and specify recovering the EC2 instance as the alarm action.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Put the instance in an Auto Scaling group with minimum and maximum capacity of 1, and have the group replace it with a new instance when a health check fails.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an EventBridge rule that runs an SSM Automation to stop and start the instance when CPUUtilization stays below 1% for 5 minutes.

exam-soa-c02-38.explanation: The correct answer is attaching a reboot alarm action to the instance status check failure metric. The problem scenario is an OS-level problem in which only the instance status check fails, the metric that watches for that signal is StatusCheckFailed_Instance, and the reboot action keeps the instance ID and EBS data as they are. The system status check metric and the recover action are for host hardware problems, and the documentation also explains that automatic recovery does not work when only the instance status check fails. Auto Scaling replacement creates a new instance, which violates the condition to keep the instance. A low CPU signal often produces false positives unrelated to a kernel problem, and stop and start can change the host so that the public IP address may change.

exam-soa-c02-39.prompt: The development account of a startup repeatedly exceeds its monthly budget of $5,000. The team wants to notify the owner when forecasted cost reaches 80% of the budget, and to automatically restrict the creation of new resources when it reaches 100%. There are 15 developers and no dedicated FinOps staff, so custom-built automation must be minimized. Notifications must be delivered both to the owner's email and to an SNS topic. The development account is a separate AWS Organizations member, the budget owner is comfortable with the Budgets console, and the restriction on creating resources must not block read operations. What is the MOST appropriate method that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Save a daily cost report in Cost Explorer, and have the owner check it every day and manually revoke IAM permissions if the budget is exceeded. When costs exceed the threshold, the owner directly checks and adjusts the resource creation permissions in the account.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Receive Trusted Advisor cost optimization check results with EventBridge and have a custom-written Lambda function stop resources in the development account.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a CloudWatch billing alarm to send a notification through SNS when the threshold is reached, and have the owner restrict permissions manually afterward.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set up an 80% forecasted cost alert through SNS on an AWS Budgets cost budget, and configure a budget action that applies an IAM policy denying resource creation at the 100% threshold.

exam-soa-c02-39.explanation: AWS Budgets can send alerts on actual and forecasted cost through SNS or email, and a budget action can automatically apply an IAM policy that blocks resource creation when a threshold is reached, so it meets both requirements without custom development. Cost Explorer is a tool for analyzing and viewing costs and has no alert thresholds or automatic actions. Connecting Trusted Advisor to Lambda does not match a budget-versus-cost criterion and requires custom development. A CloudWatch billing alarm provides only notifications and does not automatically restrict permissions, so it does not meet the automatic restriction requirement.

exam-soa-c02-40.prompt: The operations team at a food delivery app company receives the web tier CPUUtilization alarm and the ALB 5xx error alarm separately through SNS, so a brief alarm on just one of them often causes a night-time page. Over the past month, most of the early-morning pages were cases in which only one metric briefly crossed its threshold. The team wants to page the on-call engineer only when both alarms are in ALARM at the same time, while keeping the existing individual alarms themselves for dashboard display. The team cannot build new code or separate servers. The evaluation periods of both alarms are 5 minutes, and the individual alarm widgets on the dashboard must remain after switching to a composite alarm. Which method is MOST suitable while minimizing changes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Double the thresholds of both metrics so that exceeding only one of them does not trigger a notification, and keep using the existing SNS topic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a composite alarm and connect actions such as rebooting an instance or running an Auto Scaling policy directly as the composite alarm's alarm actions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Receive each alarm's state change event with two EventBridge rules, and have Step Functions determine whether they occurred at the same time before paging.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a composite alarm that references the two alarms with an AND condition, attach the on-call SNS notification only to the composite alarm, and remove the notification targets from the individual alarms.

exam-soa-c02-40.explanation: The correct answer is to attach the on-call notification only to a composite alarm that combines the two alarms with AND. A composite alarm evaluates only the states of other alarms, so it can reduce alert noise while leaving the existing individual alarms as they are, and the documentation also describes composite alarms as a way to reduce alarm noise. Doubling the thresholds lowers the sensitivity for detecting a single-metric failure, which differs from the requirement. A composite alarm can perform SNS notifications and create OpsItems, but it cannot perform EC2 actions or Auto Scaling actions, so connecting those actions does not work. The EventBridge and Step Functions combination has many new components to build and operate, which does not fit the goal of minimizing changes.

exam-soa-c02-41.prompt: An online bookstore company runs its web service on m5 instances in the Seoul Region, but next year it plans to move some of it to AWS Fargate and relocate some workloads to m6i and c6i in the Tokyo Region. The company wants to lower costs with a 1-year commitment, and the discount must continue to apply even with these changes. Current average monthly usage is relatively steady, and the finance team requires the freedom to change configurations even after committing. Usage fluctuates within 10% per month, and the company prefers to pay a fixed monthly amount with no upfront payment. Which purchasing option meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Purchase a 1-year EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the m5 family in the Seoul Region to secure the highest discount rate on current usage.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create On-Demand Capacity Reservations for the current m5 usage so that the needed capacity is always secured.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Purchase a 1-year Compute Savings Plan so that the discount applies to EC2 even when the instance family and Region change, and also to Fargate usage.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Convert all workloads to Spot Instances to use the lowest unit price with no commitment, and have them restart to prepare for interruptions.

exam-soa-c02-41.explanation: Compute Savings Plans apply automatically to EC2 usage regardless of instance family, size, Region, or operating system, and also apply to Fargate and Lambda usage, so the discount is retained when you move from c5 to m5, change Regions, or migrate from EC2 to Fargate. EC2 Instance Savings Plans are tied to a specific instance family in a specific Region, so they do not apply when the Region or family changes or when you move to Fargate. A capacity reservation secures capacity but does not provide a price discount. Spot Instances can be interrupted, so they are not suitable for an entire web service, and they differ in nature from a commitment discount.

exam-soa-c02-42.prompt: The operations team at a travel booking company runs Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL as a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Month-end report queries slow down the primary DB, so the team tried to send the report queries to the standby instance, but there is no way to connect to the standby. The service requires 24-hour write availability, and the failover configuration must be kept. It is acceptable for the reports to use data that is a few minutes old. The report queries are read-only SELECT statements, and write throughput must not decrease just because the read load increases. What is the MOST appropriate way to separate the report read load from the primary instance while keeping the write availability configuration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disable the Multi-AZ configuration and separate the endpoint so that the existing standby instance is used as a standalone read instance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Find the secondary endpoint address of the standby instance in the console and specify it as-is as the connection address of the reporting tool.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a read replica and have the reporting tool connect to the replica endpoint, leaving the Multi-AZ configuration as it is.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Raise the DB instance class of the primary instance by two sizes so that report queries and service queries are processed together on the same instance.

exam-soa-c02-42.explanation: The correct answer is to add a read replica and send the report queries to the replica endpoint. The standby of a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment is a synchronous replica for failover, and the documentation explicitly states that it cannot serve read traffic, so separating reads requires a read replica or a Multi-AZ DB cluster. Disabling Multi-AZ would violate the availability requirement, and the standby would not become a read instance. The standby has no separate secondary endpoint that you can connect to. Increasing the instance class does not separate the load, and contention on the same instance continues.

exam-soa-c02-43.prompt: A retail company purchased a 3-year Compute Savings Plan. Because it is reducing some workloads, it is worried that the committed amount may not be fully used, and it wants to be notified right away if the commitment goes underused and is wasted. The alert criterion is when daily utilization falls below 80%. A trend of declining usage is already visible a few months after the purchase. Notifications should go to the finance team's SNS topic, and the company does not want to build a separate analysis tool. The Savings Plan was purchased in the organization's management account, and the budget can be created in the same management account. What is the MOST appropriate configuration that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a daily Savings Plans coverage budget and configure it to send a notification when coverage is below 80%.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a monthly cost budget with the same value as the committed amount and configure it to send a notification when forecasted cost exceeds 100%.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a daily Savings Plans utilization budget and configure it to send a notification when utilization is below 80%.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an hourly EC2 usage budget and configure it to send a notification when usage falls below the committed hours.

exam-soa-c02-43.explanation: A utilization budget tracks how much of the purchased Savings Plans commitment is being used and notifies you when it falls below a threshold, so it fits detecting wasted commitment on a daily basis. A coverage budget tracks the percentage of eligible usage that is covered by Savings Plans, so it drops when usage grows and more of it is uncovered, and it cannot tell you about a situation in which commitment is left over. The forecast alert of a cost budget looks at cases where spending grows, which is the opposite direction from an underused commitment. A usage budget tracks service usage itself rather than whether the commitment is used, so it cannot directly reflect wasted commitment.

exam-soa-c02-44.prompt: An application at a payment services company publishes the value 1 to a PaymentErrors custom metric only when a payment error occurs. The company created an alarm on this metric with a 5-minute period, 1 data point, and a threshold of greater than or equal to 1, but during normal times with no errors the alarm remains in the INSUFFICIENT_DATA state and appears gray on the operations dashboard. This has led to complaints that it is hard to tell whether the alarm is working correctly. It is hard to add code that makes the application publish the metric when there are no errors, and the only alarm action needed is an SNS email notification. What is the MOST appropriate setting so that the alarm shows OK during normal times and goes to ALARM only when errors come in?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set the alarm's missing data treatment to notBreaching so that periods in which the error metric is not published are treated as normal values within the threshold.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set the alarm's missing data treatment to breaching so that periods in which the metric does not arrive are also treated as threshold violations, so the alarm always shows a checked state.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Set the alarm's missing data treatment to ignore so that the previous alarm state is maintained during periods with no data.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lengthen the alarm evaluation period to as much as one day so that the alarm keeps showing OK if data arrives even once during the day.

exam-soa-c02-44.explanation: The correct answer is to treat missing data as notBreaching. For a metric that is published only when an error occurs, the absence of data means everything is normal, and the documentation also recommends notBreaching for such metrics. Setting breaching would put the alarm in ALARM during normal times with no errors, which is the opposite of the requirement. ignore maintains the current state, so the initial INSUFFICIENT_DATA state would remain, and once the alarm goes to ALARM there would be no new data to move it out of ALARM. Lengthening the evaluation period still treats periods with no data at all as missing, so the state does not change and only the detection of errors is delayed.

exam-soa-c02-45.prompt: A backup server in the on-premises data center of a manufacturing company connects to a VPC through an AWS Direct Connect connection and must upload backups to an Amazon S3 bucket in the same Region without going over the internet. The VPC already has an S3 gateway endpoint, but access from on premises does not work. Under security policy, backup traffic is not allowed to use a public internet path, and the network team does not want to change the Direct Connect connection itself. The backup data is about 2 TB per day, and on premises already uses a Direct Connect private virtual interface. What is the MOST appropriate change that satisfies the requirement of not using a public internet path?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an S3 interface endpoint in the VPC and configure DNS so that S3 requests from on premises are sent to the endpoint's private IP addresses.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add the Direct Connect virtual interface to the route table associations of the gateway endpoint so that the on-premises path uses the endpoint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a NAT gateway in the VPC and route on-premises traffic through the NAT to the S3 public endpoint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a condition that allows the on-premises CIDR to the gateway endpoint policy so that the endpoint accepts requests from that range.

exam-soa-c02-45.explanation: The correct answer is to create an S3 interface endpoint and have on premises access it through its private IP addresses. According to the documentation, gateway endpoints cannot be used by resources over VPN, VPC peering, a transit gateway, or Direct Connect, and in such scenarios you must use an interface endpoint, which has additional cost. A gateway endpoint is only a route table target, and there is no concept of attaching it to a virtual interface. Going through a NAT gateway would use the S3 public endpoint and the internet gateway path, which violates the requirement. An endpoint policy only defines the scope of permitted access and does not add reachable paths.

exam-soa-c02-46.prompt: The operations team at a manufacturer wants to view application log files and memory and disk utilization from 40 on-premises Linux servers and 110 EC2 instances together in a single CloudWatch. The definition of what to collect must be changeable in bulk in one place, without being managed separately for each server. With as many as 150 servers, per-server manual configuration is unacceptable, and the operations team has 4 members. Assume that the on-premises servers are not covered by Systems Manager hybrid activation. The log files are under /var/log/app, memory and disk metrics are collected at 1-minute intervals, and configuration changes must be applied without redeploying servers. Which TWO actions meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Attach an IAM role with the CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy to the EC2 instances as an instance profile, and configure credentials with the same permissions on the on-premises servers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turn on detailed monitoring for the EC2 instances to collect memory and disk utilization, and install and operate the agent only on the on-premises servers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enable VPC flow logs and send them to a log group, which also collects the application log files and memory utilization inside the instances.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Install the unified CloudWatch agent on all servers, and place a configuration file that defines the log files and metrics to collect in SSM Parameter Store so that each server retrieves it.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Upload logs to Amazon S3 from each server with cron, run a Lambda function from S3 events to convert them into memory and disk metrics and publish them, and have an engineer check failures weekly. Also operate a separate reprocessing queue for conversion failures.

exam-soa-c02-46.explanation: The correct answer is the combination of deploying the unified agent to all servers with the same configuration file and granting the agent permission to write to CloudWatch according to the server type. The unified agent collects logs and system-level metrics on both EC2 and on-premises servers, placing the configuration file in a single location in Parameter Store lets you change what is collected in bulk, and permissions come from an instance profile on EC2 and from credentials on premises. Detailed monitoring only shortens the collection interval and does not add memory or disk metrics. The S3 and Lambda conversion requires custom development and operation. Flow logs are network traffic metadata and have nothing to do with in-instance logs or memory.

exam-soa-c02-47.prompt: A news media company serves the JS and CSS files of its static website through Amazon CloudFront with a default TTL of 24 hours. The company deploys 20 times a week, but even after deployments some users still see old files. The company must maintain the cache hit ratio and must also avoid the cost of invalidation requests and the problem of old files remaining in browser and corporate proxy caches. The origin is Amazon S3, and the team can modify the build pipeline itself. The HTML files have a short cache time configured, and the team uses a build tool that can rename only the JS and CSS files with hashed names. What is the MOST appropriate deployment approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an invalidation request for the /* path immediately after every deployment to clear the cache at all edge locations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower the default TTL to 0 so that CloudFront checks the origin for changes to the file on every request.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a new CloudFront distribution for each deployment and switch the Route 53 record to the new distribution to separate the caches.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Include a hash or version in the file name at build time and upload under the new name, and have the HTML reference the new file names.

exam-soa-c02-47.explanation: The correct answer is to deploy with the version in the file name. The documentation recommends versioned file names over invalidation when you update files frequently, because versioned names give you control over which file users receive even when old files are cached in user browsers or corporate proxies, and they incur no invalidation charges. Invalidation only clears the CloudFront edge cache, so old files that remain in browser and proxy caches can continue to appear until they expire, and it incurs costs depending on the number of requests. Setting the TTL to 0 eliminates the cache hit ratio. Creating a new distribution for each deployment adds the burden of managing DNS switchover and warming a new cache.

exam-soa-c02-48.prompt: A SaaS company has a recovery time objective (RTO) of around 5 minutes and a recovery point objective (RPO) of a few seconds for the case where its three-tier application in the Seoul Region suffers a Region failure. The company wants a structure in which scaled-down web and app servers are always running in the Tokyo Region so that they can handle requests immediately during a failure, and only capacity needs to be increased. The cost of always running full capacity is a burden, and management has limited the DR budget to a fraction of normal infrastructure costs. The database can already use cross-Region replication. The data replication lag between Seoul and Tokyo is normally within a few seconds, and the Auto Scaling group in Tokyo is already running with a minimum capacity of 2 instances. Which cost-effective strategy meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure a warm standby in which a scaled-down version of the whole environment is always running in Tokyo, data is replicated across Regions, and the Auto Scaling target capacity is increased during a failure.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure a pilot light in which only the data replica and AMIs are kept in Tokyo and the app servers are kept off, and the infrastructure is started and scaled out during a failure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure a multi-site active/active in which a full environment with the same capacity as Seoul is always running in Tokyo, both Regions handle traffic, and data is replicated in both directions. Also place health check based routing between the two Regions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure backup and restore in which Seoul backups are periodically copied to the Tokyo Region and, during a failure, the environment is created anew with CloudFormation and restored.

exam-soa-c02-48.explanation: The correct answer is warm standby. According to the AWS whitepaper, in warm standby a scaled-down but fully functional environment is always running, so it can handle requests immediately at reduced capacity and then only needs to scale up, which provides a short RTO while reducing normal costs. In pilot light, the app servers are off, so startup and additional infrastructure deployment are required and requests cannot be handled immediately. Multi-site active/active always runs full capacity, which violates the cost constraint. Backup and restore creates and restores the environment from scratch, so it is hard to meet an RTO of 5 minutes and an RPO of a few seconds.

exam-soa-c02-49.prompt: Under the financial regulations that apply to an insurance company, database backups must be retained for at least 7 years, and during that period no one, including the root user and security administrators, may delete a recovery point or shorten the retention period. Backups are already managed with AWS Backup, and the auditors require a control that can prove immutability. The company wants to use its existing AWS Backup vault without introducing a new backup tool. The vault is already encrypted, the recovery points exist only in the Seoul Region, and the security team keeps vault change history in AWS CloudTrail. What is the MOST appropriate configuration that meets the requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply a governance mode vault lock to the backup vault with a minimum retention period of 7 years, so that only authorized IAM users can remove the lock.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply a compliance mode vault lock to the backup vault with a minimum retention period of 7 years (about 2,557 days), so that the lock becomes immutable after the grace period ends.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deny the delete recovery point action for all principals with a vault access policy, grant the permission to change the policy only to a small number of security team administrators, and audit the change history with CloudTrail.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Copy the recovery points to an S3 Glacier vault and apply an S3 Glacier Vault Lock policy to prevent deletion for 7 years.

exam-soa-c02-49.explanation: The correct answer is a compliance mode vault lock with a 7-year minimum retention period. In compliance mode, after the grace period (at least 3 days) passes, the lock becomes immutable, so no user, including root, and not even AWS can delete the lock or the recovery points, and the minimum retention period enforces the retention lifetime. In governance mode, a user with sufficient IAM permissions can remove the lock, which violates the requirement that no one, root included, can do so. A vault access policy can be changed by a principal that has permission to change policies, so it cannot prove immutability. S3 Glacier Vault Lock is a different feature from AWS Backup Vault Lock and applies only to Glacier vaults.

exam-soa-c02-50.prompt: A company with group affiliates must deploy the same security baseline IAM role to 60 accounts in a single organizational unit (OU) in AWS Organizations, and the same role must also be created automatically in any account added to this OU in the future, without any additional work. The security team does not want to create execution roles for StackSets in every target account by hand, and trusted access for CloudFormation StackSets is enabled in the organization. The role to be deployed is a simple configuration with a few security baseline IAM policies attached, and it is enough for the role to be created within a few minutes after a new account is created. Which method meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a StackSet with self-managed permissions, and each time a new account is created, create an administration role and an execution role and then add stack instances. The same work must be repeated every time accounts are added.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a separate CloudFormation stack in each account, and when a new account is added, have an engineer manually create a stack from the same template.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a StackSet with service-managed permissions, specify the target OU, and turn on automatic deployment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Declare cross-account resources in a single stack template in the management account so that it creates the IAM roles in all 60 accounts at once.

exam-soa-c02-50.explanation: Service-managed permissions create the required IAM roles on StackSets' behalf and integrate with Organizations, and they support automatic deployment, which automatically deploys stack instances to accounts newly added to an OU. This meets both the constraint of not creating execution roles by hand and the requirement that new accounts be covered automatically. Self-managed permissions require you to create roles in each target account yourself, and the work is repeated for every new account, so the operational burden is high. Creating a separate stack per account makes consistent deployment and updating difficult and increases manual work. A single stack can create resources only in the account and Region it belongs to, so declaring resources across multiple accounts is not possible.

exam-soa-c02-51.prompt: A company attached an SCP to a workloads OU that denies ec2:RunInstances in Regions other than ap-northeast-2. Users with AdministratorAccess in member accounts cannot create instances in us-east-1. However, during an audit it was discovered that administrators working in the management account can still create instances in us-east-1. Some workloads are currently run directly in the management account, and the company wants to apply its Region restriction governance consistently across the entire organization. The schedule allows moving the workloads that run in the management account to member accounts, and the organization already has a trusted SCP structure in place. What should the company do to meet this requirement most appropriately?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because the management account is not affected by SCPs, move the workloads to member accounts where SCPs apply, and use the management account only for managing the organization.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attach the same SCP once more to the organization root that contains the management account so that the deny statement also applies to users and roles in the management account.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Grant the management account administrators a service-linked role so that those users are subject to the SCP restrictions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Specify the management account ID in the Principal element of the SCP's Deny statement so that the deny also applies to users in the management account.

exam-soa-c02-51.explanation: SCPs affect only member accounts in the organization and do not affect users and roles in the management account, so workloads that need the restriction should run in member accounts where SCPs apply, and the management account should be used only for managing the organization. Attaching an SCP to the root still leaves the management account excluded.
