Service-linked roles are among the things that are not affected by SCPs, and granting one to a user does not make that user subject to SCP restrictions. SCP syntax has no way to target the management account by using a Principal element that specifies a particular principal.

exam-soa-c02-52.prompt: A financial services company wants to detect when any of the 40 accounts managed with AWS Organizations communicates with malicious IP addresses or makes anomalous API calls. The security team does not want to enable VPC flow logs and DNS query logs by itself or to build a collection pipeline. The security team is small, so it is also hard to operate separate collection servers, and new accounts must automatically become targets. No account has ever enabled threat detection, and the team wants to view the findings in one place. Which method meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Turn on flow logs in all VPCs and collect them in a central S3 bucket, and then periodically compare them against a list of known malicious IP addresses with Amazon Athena queries.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty for the whole organization from a delegated administrator account, and configure it to be turned on automatically for newly created accounts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enable Amazon Inspector for the whole organization to detect malicious IP communication and anomalous API calls that occur on EC2 instances.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Collect security group and network setting changes with an AWS Config organization aggregator and evaluate them with custom rules.

exam-soa-c02-52.explanation: When enabled, GuardDuty automatically analyzes CloudTrail management events, VPC flow logs, and Route 53 Resolver DNS query logs as independent streams, so users do not need to configure flow logs or DNS logs separately. A delegated administrator account can manage the organization's accounts all at once. Collecting flow logs and comparing them with Athena requires you to build and operate the collection and analysis yourself. Inspector is a service that finds software vulnerabilities and network reachability, so its purpose differs from detecting malicious communication and anomalous API calls. Config only evaluates configuration changes and does not detect threat activity.

exam-soa-c02-53.prompt: The web tier of an online shopping mall runs in an Auto Scaling group behind an ALB. During a large sale event, when the request count triples, response latency grows even though CPU utilization stays around 40%. This is because each request waits a long time for an external payment API, so CPU is not the bottleneck. The company wants to automatically add and remove instances in proportion to the number of requests processed per instance. The warmup time after instance launch is already defined, and the minimum and maximum capacity are also set. Load testing has already confirmed that a single instance can handle about 800 requests. Which method is the simplest to configure and tune?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In a target tracking scaling policy, choose the ALBRequestCountPerTarget metric and specify the target number of requests per instance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Specify the total ALB RequestCount metric as the metric of a target tracking policy so that instances are added as requests increase.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a target tracking policy with an average CPUUtilization target of 50% so that instances are added when CPU rises.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Estimate the event time windows and create scheduled scaling actions that raise the desired capacity at the same time every day, one for each expected request volume.

exam-soa-c02-53.explanation: The correct answer is a target tracking policy that uses ALBRequestCountPerTarget as the metric. This metric is the average number of requests received per target, so the number of instances is determined in proportion to the load, and you only need to specify the target value because AWS manages the alarms. According to the documentation, the RequestCount of the entire load balancer does not change in value when the number of instances in the group changes, so it is not a metric that can be used for target tracking. If CPU is 40% while latency is long, as it is now, a CPU-based policy does not trigger scaling. Scheduled scaling requires guessing the time pattern, and wrong predictions lead to shortages or waste, so tuning continues.

exam-soa-c02-54.prompt: A healthcare SaaS company wants to back up the EC2 instances, EBS volumes, and RDS instances tagged Backup=daily every day and retain the backups for 35 days, and also copy the same backups to another Region for disaster recovery. Newly tagged resources must be included automatically without extra work, and the company does not want to operate separate backup scripts for each service. The operations team wants to view the backup status on a single screen. Some RDS instances use encrypted snapshots, and a KMS key must be available for restores in the other Region. Which configuration has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Put a 35-day retention rule and a copy action to the destination Region in an AWS Backup plan, and specify the resource assignment with the tag condition Backup=daily.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run a Lambda function for each service daily on an EventBridge schedule that creates EBS snapshots and RDS snapshots and copies them to another Region with the copy API.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Automate only EBS snapshots with an Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policy, and set the RDS automated backup retention period to 35 days.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create the backup plan in only the Seoul Region, and set up S3 Cross-Region Replication to replicate the backup data to the other Region.

exam-soa-c02-54.explanation: The correct answer is an AWS Backup plan with tag-based resource assignment and a cross-Region copy rule. AWS Backup manages EC2, EBS, and RDS in a single plan with a schedule and retention period and provides the ability to copy backups to another Region, and when you assign resources by a tag condition, newly tagged resources are included automatically. Lambda scripts violate the condition of not operating per-service code yourself. Data Lifecycle Manager focuses on EBS, and setting the RDS automated backup retention alone does not meet the requirements for cross-Region copy and unified management. S3 Cross-Region Replication replicates S3 objects, not AWS Backup recovery points.

exam-soa-c02-55.prompt: An infrastructure engineer at a startup received a report that an EC2 instance in a newly created private subnet cannot reach the OS patch repository (on the internet). The public subnet in the same VPC already has a NAT gateway, and an internet gateway is attached. The route table of the private subnet has only the VPC local route, and the security group outbound rules allow all traffic. Under security policy, the instance must not be directly exposed to the internet. There is only one NAT gateway, in a single public subnet rather than one per Availability Zone, and the company is keeping this configuration for now for cost reasons. What is the MOST appropriate action to solve the problem without directly exposing the instance to the internet?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a route to the private subnet's route table that sends 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT gateway.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add a route to the private subnet's route table that sends 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway and assign a public IP address to the instance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Move the NAT gateway into the private subnet so that address translation happens in the same subnet as the instance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a rule allowing all traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 to the outbound rules of the instance's security group to open external connectivity.

exam-soa-c02-55.explanation: The correct answer is to add a route to the private subnet's route table that sends 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT gateway. A NAT gateway goes out through the internet gateway from the public subnet, and a private subnet has no way to reach external addresses without a default route, so the missing route is the cause. Adding an internet gateway route and assigning a public IP address directly exposes the instance to the internet, which violates the condition. If you move the NAT gateway into the private subnet, there is no route to the internet gateway, so it does not work. Security group outbound rules do not solve the problem of a missing route.

exam-soa-c02-56.prompt: A manufacturing company must resolve a private hosted zone in a VPC (app.internal.example) from on premises, which is connected through AWS Direct Connect, and must also resolve corp.example.local, which is managed by on-premises DNS servers, from EC2 instances in the VPC. The company does not want to operate its own DNS server instances on either side. The network team has 2 members, and redundancy is needed because a DNS failure affects the entire business. The connection between on premises and the VPC already works reliably over Direct Connect, and endpoint ENIs can be placed across two AZs. Which TWO actions have the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint in the VPC, and have the on-premises DNS forward queries for app.internal.example to the endpoint IP addresses.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Install BIND on EC2 instances in the VPC to configure conditional forwarding in both directions, point the on-premises DNS to these instances, and place one instance in each AZ for redundancy. Also manage the synchronization settings between the two servers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint in the VPC, and associate with the VPC a rule that forwards corp.example.local to the on-premises DNS.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Specify only the on-premises DNS server addresses in the VPC's DHCP option set so that the DNS queries from all EC2 instances go to the on-premises servers.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Copy the records of the private hosted zone into a public hosted zone and publish them, and have on premises resolve them through internet DNS.

exam-soa-c02-56.explanation: The correct answer is the configuration that uses an inbound endpoint together with an outbound endpoint and a forwarding rule. Route 53 Resolver cannot be used directly from outside the VPC, so an inbound endpoint is needed to resolve VPC names from on premises, and an outbound endpoint and a per-domain forwarding rule are needed to resolve on-premises domains from the VPC, and the IP addresses of both endpoints must be reachable over Direct Connect or VPN. If you specify only the on-premises DNS in the DHCP options, Route 53 Resolver is bypassed and the private hosted zone cannot be resolved. Publishing private records in a public zone exposes internal names. BIND instances are servers that you must operate yourself.

exam-soa-c02-57.prompt: A global retail company deploys template updates with StackSets to 120 accounts and 3 Regions (ap-northeast-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1). The company wants to detect problems quickly and have the operation stop automatically before a faulty template spreads to all Regions and accounts. If failures in the first Region exceed the limit, the operation must not proceed to the remaining Regions. The responsible team cannot watch continuously during the deployment. Each stack instance contains only one or two resources per account, so the deployment itself finishes in a few minutes, and safety takes priority over deployment time. What is the MOST appropriate configuration that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set Region concurrency to Parallel and raise the maximum concurrent accounts to the full count to reduce deployment time, and investigate failures after the operation finishes. If needed, select only the failed accounts and redeploy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set Region concurrency to Sequential and specify the Region deployment order, and set the failure tolerance low, such as 2 stacks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Set the failure tolerance to 100% to deploy to all accounts for now, and collect only the failed stack instances to retry later.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a separate StackSet for each Region, and have an engineer check each Region's results and then manually start the operation for the next Region.

exam-soa-c02-57.explanation: The correct answer is to deploy Regions sequentially with a low failure tolerance. When the number of failed stacks in a Region exceeds the tolerance, that Region's operation becomes FAILED, the overall operation also becomes FAILED, and the operations for the remaining Regions are canceled. Parallel deployment spreads to all Regions at once, which does not match the requirement to stop quickly, and raising concurrent accounts only enlarges the blast radius. With a tolerance of 100%, the operation never stops no matter how many failures occur. Chaining separate per-Region StackSets manually replaces the requirement to stop automatically with human work and only adds operational overhead.

exam-soa-c02-58.prompt: A logistics company wants to continuously scan 200 EC2 instances for software package vulnerabilities. Most are SSM managed nodes, but 15 legacy instances on which regulations prohibit installing an agent (EBS-backed, xfs file system, 3 volumes totaling 600 GB) must also be included in the scan, and the company does not want to make any changes to those instances. The security team wants to see the scan results in one place and cannot operate a separate scanner server. It would be good if the results could be sent to Security Hub CSPM, and all the instances to be scanned are in the same Region. What is the MOST appropriate setting that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fix the Amazon Inspector EC2 scan mode to agent-based and exclude the legacy instances on which an agent cannot be installed from scanning. Compile the scan results into a separate report by hand and share it with the security team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set the Amazon Inspector EC2 scan mode to hybrid so that SSM managed nodes are scanned agent-based and the other instances are scanned agentless based on EBS snapshots.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Install the SSM Agent as an exception only on the legacy instances to register them as managed nodes, and then scan them agent-based.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty EC2 Runtime Monitoring so that package vulnerabilities on the legacy instances are also detected.

exam-soa-c02-58.explanation: The hybrid scan mode uses both agent-based and agentless scanning: SSM managed nodes are scanned with the agent, and unmanaged EBS-backed instances are scanned by collecting the software inventory from snapshots. The legacy instances are EBS-backed, use ext4 or xfs, and meet the agentless conditions of fewer than 8 volumes and a total of 1,200 GB or less. The agent-based-only mode scans only SSM managed nodes, so it would miss the 15 legacy instances. Installing an agent violates the regulation that an agent cannot be installed. GuardDuty is a threat detection service and is not intended for package vulnerability scanning.

exam-soa-c02-59.prompt: In an Auto Scaling group behind an ALB at a video education company, every time a scale-in event occurs, some users are disconnected during report downloads that take up to 90 seconds and receive 5xx responses. The deregistration delay of the target group is currently 30 seconds. Downloads are synchronous requests handled inside the instance, scale-in is performed by a CPU target tracking policy, and scale-in itself cannot be prevented because of cost. Instances must not receive new requests before they are terminated, and the company wants to remove instances as quickly as possible during scale-in to save cost. What is the MOST appropriate adjustment to protect in-flight requests?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reduce the deregistration delay to 0 seconds so that new requests go to other instances as soon as a target is removed, reducing request disconnections.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turn off cross-zone load balancing so that only the instances in each AZ handle requests for that AZ, limiting the scope of impact during scale-in.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase the target group health check interval to delay the point at which an instance that is scaling in is judged unhealthy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the deregistration delay to 120 seconds, which is longer than the maximum request processing time, so that in-flight requests finish before the instance is terminated.

exam-soa-c02-59.explanation: The correct answer is to increase the deregistration delay beyond the longest request time. When a target is deregistered, the load balancer stops sending it new requests and, in the draining state, waits for in-flight requests to finish for the length of the delay, and according to the documentation, Auto Scaling also waits for that time or for requests to complete before it terminates the instance. The current 30 seconds is shorter than the 90-second download, which causes the disconnections. Setting the delay to 0 seconds does not protect in-flight requests. The cross-zone setting changes only the scope of request distribution and has nothing to do with protection at termination time. The health check interval does not increase the draining wait time.

exam-soa-c02-60.prompt: An application at an online insurance company stores the credentials of an application account for Amazon RDS for MySQL in AWS Secrets Manager. Under security policy, the database password must be changed every 30 days, and the application code must not need to be redeployed when the password changes. The application retrieves the secret at startup and when a connection fails. The development team has 5 members and has no capacity to build and maintain a rotation script. The secret contains the user name and password as JSON, and the database is in a private subnet in the same VPC. Which method meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Store the password in a Parameter Store SecureString and run a custom-written rotation script every 30 days on an EventBridge schedule.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure automatic rotation on the secret with a 30-day schedule, and have the application read the latest value with GetSecretValue when needed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turn on automatic key rotation for a KMS customer managed key so that the database password also changes every 30 days.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Store the password in a Lambda environment variable and redeploy with a new value through the CI/CD pipeline every 30 days.

exam-soa-c02-60.explanation: Secrets Manager provides automatic rotation on a schedule you specify and updates the credentials in both the secret and the database, and if the application retrieves the secret at run time, it uses the new value without redeploying code. Parameter Store with a custom script requires you to implement and operate the rotation procedure and the database update yourself, so the burden is large. KMS key rotation changes the encryption key material and does not change the database password. Storing the password in an environment variable and redeploying violates the constraint that code must not be redeployed and exposes the password in configuration.

exam-soa-c02-61.prompt: The operations team at a telecommunications company patches 300 Amazon Linux servers. The policy is to auto-approve, 7 days after release, only patches whose classification is Security and whose severity is Critical. One specific patch that caused an outage in the past must not be installed on any server. The predefined baselines provided by AWS cannot be modified and have approval conditions that differ from this policy. All the servers are managed by Systems Manager, and patching must run automatically on a schedule. Baselines can be created separately for each operating system, and new patches must not be installed right after release but only after 7 days have passed. What is the MOST appropriate method that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set classification and severity conditions and a 7-day auto-approval delay in a custom patch baseline, and add the problem patch to the rejected patches list.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use the predefined patch baseline as is, and exclude the problem patch manually in the package manager by connecting to the servers. After installation, compare the package list of each server to check that the exclusion was honored.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an Install Override list that enumerates every patch ID to approve by hand, and install based on this list instead of conditional rules.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run only Scan operations periodically to get a missing-patch report, and have an engineer manually install patches on each server after looking at the report.

exam-soa-c02-61.explanation: A custom patch baseline lets you define the approval targets by classification and severity, supports auto-approval rules that wait a number of days after release, and lets you exclude a specific patch with the rejected list, so it meets all three requirements. The predefined baselines cannot be modified and also approve Important severity and Bugfix patches, so they do not fit this policy, and excluding manually on each server creates consistency and operational overhead problems at 300 servers. An Install Override list uses a fixed list in place of rules, so it cannot express the auto-approval rules and requires you to maintain the list every time a patch is released. Running Scan only reports and installs no patches.

exam-soa-c02-62.prompt: A financial holding company wants to prevent anyone from stopping or deleting CloudTrail trails in the 40 accounts in a workloads OU in AWS Organizations. The restriction must also apply to each account's administrator roles and root user, and account administrators must not be able to lift the policy themselves. Account administrators already have broad IAM permissions, and the security team has no staff to check settings in each account. The actions to block are StopLogging, DeleteTrail, and UpdateTrail, and the security team's account does not need an exception to this restriction. What is the MOST appropriate method that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add the same deny statement as an inline policy to all IAM roles and users in each account to block CloudTrail changes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set a permissions boundary on all IAM users and roles that excludes the permissions to change CloudTrail.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Detect that a trail has been turned off with an AWS Config rule and send a notification, and operate so that an engineer turns the trail back on immediately.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Attach to the workloads OU an SCP that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, and similar actions.

exam-soa-c02-62.explanation: An SCP sets the maximum permissions available to IAM users and roles in member accounts, including the root user, and it can be changed only from the organization management side, so account administrators cannot lift it. Inline policies added to each account can be modified or deleted by account administrators and do not apply to the root user. A permissions boundary applies only to IAM users and roles, so it cannot block the root user, and administrators can also change the boundary. A Config rule only detects after the fact and cannot prevent the stop itself, so it does not meet the requirement to prevent it.

exam-soa-c02-63.prompt: A database on a 200 GiB gp2 volume at a data analytics company uses little I/O during normal times, but when the daily batch starts, it requires about 3,000 IOPS for more than an hour. When the batch runs long, response times become sharply slower and recover only after a long while. The company wants to confirm the cause and fix it with the least operational burden, without detaching the volume or interrupting the service. The database is OLTP in nature with a lot of random I/O. The current instance is an EBS-optimized type, and increasing the volume size is not preferred from a cost perspective. Which TWO actions are required? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Check the CloudWatch BurstBalance metric to see whether the gp2 I/O credits are being exhausted.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stop the instance, create a new io2 volume from a snapshot and replace the volume, and then start the instance again. Switch the service to maintenance mode while it is being replaced.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reduce the volume size so that I/O credits accumulate faster and the burst time during the batch period increases.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the volume type to gp3 with Elastic Volumes and provision the IOPS needed for the batch.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Change the volume to st1 to increase sequential throughput and have it handle the database's random I/O as well.

exam-soa-c02-63.explanation: The correct answers are checking the BurstBalance metric to confirm credit exhaustion and changing to gp3 with Elastic Volumes. The baseline performance of a 200 GiB gp2 volume is 600 IOPS, and when it bursts to 3,000 IOPS the credits run out within a few tens of minutes, so performance drops in a batch that lasts more than an hour, and BurstBalance shows the remaining credit balance. gp3 consistently provides a 3,000 IOPS baseline without bursting and lets you provision more if needed, and Elastic Volumes makes the change without interrupting the instance. st1 does not suit a database with a lot of random I/O. Stopping the instance and replacing the volume with io2 interrupts the service and violates the constraint. Reducing the size would actually reduce credit accrual and baseline IOPS.

exam-soa-c02-64.prompt: A retail company has a Site-to-Site VPN connecting its headquarters to a VPC, but only one tunnel is configured on the on-premises firewall. Each time AWS performs maintenance on a tunnel endpoint, the connection drops for several minutes and affects the business. The customer gateway device is a model that supports configuring a second tunnel, and BGP is already in use. Introducing Direct Connect is not possible under the current budget. The customer gateway device supports dual-tunnel failover, and the company's network team is comfortable with routing changes. How can the company reduce such interruptions with the LEAST change, without creating a new VPN connection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the tunnel options, extend the Phase 1 lifetime to the maximum so that tunnel renegotiation does not occur and the session stays up during maintenance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Replace the on-premises firewall with a model that has greater processing capacity to improve throughput so that the connection does not drop during maintenance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Also configure the second tunnel provided by the VPN connection on the customer gateway device so that both tunnels can be used.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Switch to an accelerated Site-to-Site VPN so that the tunnel termination point moves to the AWS edge and the effect of VPC-side maintenance disappears.

exam-soa-c02-64.explanation: The correct answer is to configure the second tunnel on the customer gateway device. According to the documentation, a Site-to-Site VPN connection provides two tunnels, each with its own public IP address, and when one tunnel goes down for maintenance, traffic automatically switches to the other configured tunnel; AWS recommends configuring both tunnels for redundancy. Changing the Phase 1 lifetime only changes the renegotiation interval and does not prevent a tunnel from going down because of AWS-side maintenance. Increasing firewall capacity does not change the interruption as long as there is only one tunnel. Accelerated VPN is a performance improvement feature and does not address the lack of redundancy of a single tunnel.

exam-soa-c02-65.prompt: A fintech service must accept connections from a partner using a small number of fixed IP addresses that can be registered in the partner's firewall allow list. The service uses a TCP-based protocol rather than HTTP and runs behind Network Load Balancers in the Seoul and Frankfurt Regions. If one Region fails, traffic must fail over to the other Region immediately, without waiting for the clients' DNS caches to expire. Most clients are mobile apps that often cache DNS responses for a long time, and the partner takes several days to change its allow list. The mobile apps use a DNS cache of up to a few minutes, the service port is a single TCP port, and preserving the client IP address is not required. What is the MOST suitable configuration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Register the NLBs in both Regions as endpoints of an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator, and give the partner the accelerator's static anycast IP addresses.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower the TTL of the Route 53 failover records to 5 seconds, and instruct the partner to register the NLBs' current IP addresses in the allow list.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Register the NLBs in both Regions as an origin group behind a CloudFront distribution, have the partner register the CloudFront edge IP ranges in the allow list, and fail over to the other origin when an origin fails.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assign Elastic IP addresses to the NLB in each Region and respond with the two addresses by using Route 53 latency records, and have the partner allow both addresses.

exam-soa-c02-65.explanation: The correct answer is a Global Accelerator standard accelerator. This service provides static anycast IP addresses associated with the accelerator and reacts immediately to health changes by sending traffic to healthy endpoints, and the whitepaper also explains that it avoids DNS caching issues, so it meets both the fixed IP and immediate failover requirements. With DNS methods, even a low TTL cannot prevent some resolvers from caching responses, and the allow list is tied to changes in the NLB addresses. CloudFront is for HTTP and HTTPS content delivery, so it does not fit a TCP-based service, allowing the edge IP ranges is a broad scope, and origin failover works on a per-request basis. Responding with Elastic IP addresses through DNS has the same limitation of waiting for cache expiry.
